q: How many planets are in our Solar System?
e: Count them on your fingers: exactly eight marvelous planets dance in big, sweeping loops around our sun.

q: What does LASER stand for?
a: Life antimatter by standing entry of range
Light amplifier by standby energy of radio
Light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation
e: It stands for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation, meaning light gets boosted into one zippy beam.

q: Igneous rocks are formed by excessive heat and pressure.
e: This is false because igneous rocks are born from cooling melted lava, not from squishing pressure.

q: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
e: Light zooms at an incredible 299,792,458 meters per second, winning the universe's ultimate race every time.

q: Which type of rock is created by intense heat AND pressure?
e: Metamorphic rocks are the great shape-shifters, baked by deep heat and squished by heavy pressure until they totally transform.

q: The asteroid belt is located between which two planets?
e: Mars and giant Jupiter share a wild cosmic backyard between them, packed with millions of tumbling, rocky asteroids.

q: Which Apollo mission was the first one to land on the Moon?
e: Apollo 11 was the brave rocket mission that carried the first human boots onto dusty lunar soil.

q: What is the standard SI unit for mass?
e: Scientists choose the kilogram as their trusty standard unit whenever it is time to measure mass.

q: What is the standard SI unit for time?
e: Tick, tock! The second is the official base unit of time, measuring every little heartbeat and ticking moment.

q: How many moons does Pluto have?
e: Tiny Pluto is not lonely at all, with five loyal moons dancing alongside it in the freezing dark.

q: What is the official name of the star located closest to the North Celestial Pole?
e: Polaris perches right above Earth's chilly northern tip, shining like a trusty cosmic nightlight for nighttime travelers.

q: Who discovered the Law of Gravity?
e: Sir Isaac Newton unlocked gravity's secrets after watching an apple tumble, realizing an invisible tug rules everything.

q: The Sun is considered a star.
e: That big, warm buddy in our sky is actually a star, just snuggled up much closer than the twinkling ones!

q: The Earth and the Moon roughly have the same mass.
e: This is false because Earth is a heavyweight champion, packing over eighty times more mass than our Moon!

q: What is the largest planet in the Solar System?
e: Mighty Jupiter is the giant of our cosmic family, puffing out its striped belly bigger than every other planet combined.

q: How many planets make up our Solar System?
e: Ever since Pluto became a dwarf planet, our sun has eight loyal planetary pals spinning around it.

q: All planets in the Solar System orbit the Sun.
e: With its giant gravity hug, our sun keeps every single planet twirling around it in a grand cosmic carousel.

q: How many planets are there in the Solar System?
e: From speedy Mercury to chilly Neptune, eight official planets share our cozy neighborhood around the sun.

q: What is the unit of electrical resistance?
e: When zooming electricity bumps into resistance, we measure that gentle stubborn push in ohms.

q: What lies at the center of our galaxy?
e: Right in our galaxy's swirling heart sits a supermassive black hole, pulling billions of stars into a grand cosmic dance.

q: What is the standard SI unit for temperature?
e: Scientists love measuring heat with Kelvin, because it starts counting from the coldest, freeze-your-toes stillness possible in the universe.

q: What does the letter 'S' stand for in 'NASA'?
e: The letter S stands for Space, where these daring explorers send rockets to meet the stars.

q: What is the hottest planet in the solar system
e: Venus wraps itself in thick blanket-like clouds, trapping so much heat that it sizzles hotter than any other planet.

q: In general, an object's de Broglie [da-BROY] wavelength is inversely proportional to which of the following of its properties?
e: The more momentum a zooming particle packs, the shorter and tighter its tiny de Broglie wavelength becomes.

q: What would be the effect on an x-ray passing through a region containing crossed electric and magnetic fields?
a: The x-ray will be deflected by the electric field but not by the magnetic field
The x-ray will be deflected by the magnetic field but not by the electric field
The x-ray will be unaffected by both the electric field and the magnetic field
The x-ray will be deflected by both the electric field and the magnetic field
e: Because an x-ray has zero electric charge, it happily zips right past both fields without getting nudged at all.

q: In which of the following parts of the Milky Way is the solar system located?
e: We cruise along like cozy passengers tucked safely inside one of the Milky Way's glowing, curved spiral arms.

q: Approximately what percent of Earth's water is in the form of ice?
e: Most water fills deep oceans, leaving only about 1.6 percent locked away as shimmering glaciers and frozen polar caps.

q: Which of the following best approximates the ratio of the volume of Olympus Mons to that of Mauna Loa?
e: Mars's giant volcano is so huge that you could pack about one hundred Mauna Loas inside it!

q: Einstein concluded that E = mc2, where m is mass and c is speed of light. According to this formula, which of the following statements is true?
a: All objects have energy only if they are moving at the speed of light
An object at rest cannot possess an amount of energy due to its mass
All objects have energy of being, or rest mass energy
Small relativistic objects all propagate at the speed of light
e: Even when an object sits totally still, its mass means it is secretly packed with resting energy.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Laboratory are studying spintronic devices. Which of the following is a difference between electronics, which relies on electric charge, and spintronics, which relies on the quantum-mechanical spin of electrons?
a: Spintronics can only be used in quantum computers
Electronics produces less heat than spintronics
Electrons do not need to move for spintronics
e: Instead of tiny electrons zooming through traffic like regular electricity, spintronics lets them stay put and twirl like tops to pass messages.

q: Approximately what percentage of energy used by an incandescent lightbulb is converted to light?
e: Old bulbs are mostly little heaters, leaving only about ten percent of their power to actually shine as light.

q: A modern camera allows light to hit its sensor through a circular opening called an aperture. Assuming the amount of light per area is uniform; by what factor must the radius of the aperture be multiplied to double the amount of light hitting the sensor?
e: Because a circle's area squares its radius, widening the radius by the square root of two lets in exactly double the light.

q: A student observes her weight on a scale as she rides an elevator down 3 stories. What happens to her observed weight during the ride?
a: Her weight stays the same, but it is less than her weight on the ground
Her weight stays the same, and it equals her weight on the ground
First she weighs less, then the same, then more than her weight on the ground
First she weighs more, then the same, then less than her weight on the ground
e: The elevator floor drops at first, cruises steadily, and then pushes to stop, making you weigh less, the same, and then more.

q: Which of the following sediment types would make the best aquiclude?
e: Tiny clay grains hug together so tightly that water gets trapped and simply cannot slip through.

q: The capacity factor for a power plant is defined as the amount of electric energy generated over a given time period, divided by the amount of electric energy that would have been generated had that plant operated at 100% for the entire time period. Which of the following would be a typical capacity factor for a solar photovoltaic [photo-vawl-TAY-ik] power plant?
e: Because the sun sleeps at night and clouds visit, solar panels only make about twenty percent of their full potential power.

q: As a swing rises in the air, which of the following types of energy increases in the rider?
e: As you swoop toward the sky, your body stores up potential energy, just waiting to dive back down!

q: White dwarfs are found in which of the following regions of the H-R diagram?
e: These tiny retired stars are super hot but quite dim, so they tuck themselves snugly in the bottom left corner of the star chart.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are making biomimetics [bio-mih-MEH-tiks] that imitate glycoproteins. These biomimetics are peptoids covered with what?
e: Natural glycoproteins wear cozy jackets made of sugars, so scientists coat these copycats with sugars too.

q: Which of the following is a typical quality factor for a tuning fork?
e: This little metal singer holds its chime so cleanly that its ringing quality score reaches about one thousand!

q: Pressure is defined as:
a: Force divided by mass of air above the object
e: Pressure is just a push sharing its strength across a surface, measured by dividing that force by the area.

q: A person can get sunburned on a cloudy day.
e: It is true because sneaky ultraviolet rays can slip right through fluffy clouds to kiss your cheeks.

q: Which of the following quantities is zero for a falling object that has reached terminal velocity?
e: Air rushes up to hug the falling skydiver, perfectly balancing gravity's pull so the net force drops to zero!

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab have made inorganic crystals of germanium sulfide that are arranged in a helical stack of thin sheets. How did they determine the structure of these crystals?
a: By shooting a beam of neutrons at the crystals
By accelerating charged particles and beaming the emitted radiation toward the crystals
By using an electron microscope with ultra-relativistic electron beams
By using a tiny probe to visualize the surface of the crystals
e: Scientists raced charged particles around a track, creating brilliant light beams to peek inside the crystal's secret spiral shape.

q: Which of the following is the most common and likely source of exposure to harmful radiation for most people?
a: Discovering a piece of abandoned equipment from the nuclear industry
Exposure to a spent fuel rod
Living near a nuclear power plant
e: Naturally occurring radon gas sneaks up through rock into our homes, making it the most common radiation we meet each day.

q: To maximize solar energy absorption in the northern hemisphere, the front of a building constructed for passive solar should face what direction?
e: Up in the north, the sun arcs across the southern sky, so facing south catches the sunniest, coziest warmth.

q: The planet Mars has two moons orbiting it.
e: It is true because red planet Mars has two tiny, potato-shaped moon buddies named Phobos and Deimos.

q: Assuming the potential difference remains constant, if the resistance of a circuit is doubled, which of the following will happen to the power dissipation?
a: It will decrease by a fourth
e: When a wire makes electricity work twice as hard to squeeze through, the power flowing through gets cut right in half.

q: What is the source of the northeast trade winds in the North Atlantic?
e: Warm, restless air spinning off the sun-baked coast of North Africa begins an epic, breezy journey across the vast Atlantic Ocean.

q: Which of the following household appliances uses the least amount of energy over the course of a year?
e: While the fridge hums day and night, the polite dishwasher sleeps quietly until dinner, using the least power all year!

q: Which of the following is the effect of a low pass filter on the output power of a circuit?
a: The circuit resonates and the power is maximized
The circuit resonates diminishing the power to zero
e: At its cutoff edge, this gentle gatekeeper politely blocks half the incoming energy, neatly cutting the circuit's power in half.

q: High level clouds that are composed of ice crystals and can give the Sun or Moon a "halo" are called which of the following?
e: Cirrostratus clouds are thin ice blankets high in the sky, bending sunlight like tiny glass gems to make a glowing halo!

q: Which of the following types of light has the longest wavelength?
e: Infrared waves stretch out long and lazy, carrying cozy heat waves that ripple farther apart than visible colors or snappy X-rays.

q: In thermodynamics, the change in enthalpy [EN- thal-pee] of a process can be equated with heat transferred if which of the following quantities is held constant?
e: When pressure stays steady like a calm room, heat slipping in or out perfectly matches the change in enthalpy.

q: Why is it winter in the northern hemisphere when it is summer in the southern hemisphere?
a: The manner in which the Earth rotates regulates the seasons on Earth
The northern hemisphere is tilted away from the Sun when the southern hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun
Because of the Earth's revolution, each hemisphere experiences summer when it is closest to the Sun and winter when it is further away
Because of the Earth's rotation, seasons are regulated by photoperiods
e: Earth tilts like a leaning top, so when the northern half points away from the warm sun, it chills into winter.

q: The power generated by a hydroelectric dam is proportional to all except which of the following?
e: Heavy water falling fast spins the giant turbines, but the water's temperature doesn't change how hard it pushes.

q: Peridotite [PER-i-doh-tyt] and dunite have which of the following compositions?
e: Deep under Earth's crust, these heavy green rocks are called ultramafic because they are packed with iron and magnesium!

q: A research project called Cosmic plans to use GPS satellites for weather forecasting to give data on temperature, pressure and water vapor in the atmosphere. Today, these data are typically gathered by which of the following:
e: Radiosonde balloons float high into the clouds carrying tiny weather kits, bravely whispering temperature and pressure secrets back home.

q: About how far away is the closest star to the Earth?
e: Our faithful Sun is our closest star neighbor, shining ninety-three million miles away across the quiet sea of space.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the solar tower, Solar Two?
a: It generated steam directly from water in its receiver
It could supply electric power on demand to the local utility company
Nearly 2000 heliostats reflected sunlight onto a receiver located at the top of the tower
Concentrated sunlight heated molten salt to temperatures as high as 1000 Fahrenheit
e: Solar Two caught the blazing sunlight using molten salt first, rather than boiling water directly into steam inside its tower receiver.

q: A ball is swinging in a circle on a string in the absence of gravity. When the string length is doubled at the same velocity, the force on the string will be:
e: On a longer leash, the swinging ball makes a wider, gentler curve, so the pull on the string is halved!

q: What is the term used to describe someone who draws maps?
e: A cartographer is an explorer with a pen, turning winding rivers and giant mountains into handy maps so nobody gets lost.

q: What component of the Milky Way galaxy is comprised of a roughly spherical collection of stars and star clusters with almost no gas or dust?
e: The halo wraps around our galaxy like a giant, starry bubble, holding ancient clusters without any messy dust clouds.

q: Angular momentum can be expressed in which of the following combinations of SI units?
e: When things spin in circles, their mass, reach, and speed multiply into kilogram meters squared per second of dizzy angular momentum.

q: Except for birds, dinosaurs became extinct after which of the following periods:
e: The mighty dinosaurs ruled the world until a giant space rock ended the Cretaceous period with a truly massive bang.

q: What is the primary reason for irradiating food?
a: To make the food taste better
To increase the shelf life of food
To kill pathogens in the food
To make the food more interesting visually
e: Helpful rays zap away sneaky bad germs hiding in your food, keeping every delicious bite safe and healthy.

q: Imagine evenly spaced radial lines emanating from a point source that represents the Earth. If 9 force lines pass through a plane x meters from the source, how many force lines pass through a plane of the same size 3x meters away?
e: As lines fan outward, stepping three times farther away spreads them nine times thinner, leaving just one line passing through.

q: Which of the following sound wave frequencies in hertz would a human be most likely to hear?
e: Our ears are built best for middle pitches, making a bright one-thousand-hertz hum delightfully easy for us to hear.

q: The purpose of a generator in a power plant is to convert one type of energy into another type. What are these two types of energy?
e: Spinning parts use their moving mechanical energy to stir up buzzing electrical power for our homes.

q: Andrew has two conducting spheres, A and B, that are in contact with each other. He brings a negatively-charged rod close to sphere A and immediately separates the two spheres. Which of the following best describes the resulting charges on the spheres once the rod has been removed?
a: Sphere A is positive, while sphere B is negative
Sphere A is negative, while sphere B is positive
e: The negative rod scares electrons away from sphere A into sphere B, leaving sphere A happily positive and sphere B negatively charged.

q: If you double the mass of a cart while it is undergoing a constant unbalanced force, the acceleration will be:
e: Stuffing twice the weight into the cart makes it twice as stubborn, cutting its pickup speed right in half!

q: Which of the following is closest to the distance, in megaparsecs, from Earth to a galaxy that has an apparent radial velocity of 910 kilometers per second?
e: The expanding universe adds seventy kilometers per second for each megaparsec, which puts this galaxy thirteen megaparsecs away!

q: Which of the following is the name for the fault in which displacement of the hanging wall is downward with respect to the footwall:
e: Gravity naturally pulls the hanging wall downward like a sleepy rock sliding out of bed, making this a normal fault.

q: If the work input remains the same and there is an increase in the output of a simple machine, there would also have to be an increase in the machine's:
e: A machine that gives you more helpful work from the exact same push is simply wasting less energy, boosting its efficiency!

q: Which of the following is the inverse of electrical resistance:
e: While resistance acts like a stubborn wall stopping electricity, conductivity measures how easily those little sparks can dance right through.

q: Researchers at Idaho National Lab are working to improve nuclear reactor safety by preventing lanthanides [LAN-tha-nides] from causing damage. What atomic orbital generally contains the highest energy electrons for neutral lanthanide atoms?
e: In busy lanthanide atoms, the most energetic electrons hang out in the outer, flower-shaped f orbitals where all the action happens!

q: Researchers at Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility recently completed the 12 giga-electron-volt upgrade of the Continuous Electron Beam Accelerator Facility. To which of the following does the 12 giga-electron-volts best correspond?
a: Number of electrons in the beam
e: Gigantic electron-volts measure the crazy kinetic energy of these speedy little particles as they zoom along like microscopic race cars.

q: Which of the following is NOT a moon of Jupiter?
e: Giant Titan is already busy circling ringed Saturn, so it cannot be one of Jupiter's loyal moon companions.

q: If you see part of the moon one night, then three nights later you can see more of it, you know that the moon is:
e: Whenever our glowing moon smiles a little bigger each night, it is waxing as more sunlight lights up its dusty face.

q: Earth reflects approximately 30% of the light it receives from the Sun back into space. Which of the following components of Earth is responsible for the predominant portion of this reflectivity?
e: Fluffy white clouds act like giant mirrors floating in the sky, bouncing most of Earth's reflected sunlight straight back into space.

q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Tampa Bay desalination plant?
a: It can produce up to 25 million gallons of drinking water per day
It uses the process of reverse osmosis to produce drinking water from saltwater
Concentrated seawater is directed back to the power plant, where it is mixed with cooling water and returned to the Bay
Increased salinity in Tampa Bay is a proven environmental hazard of this operation
e: The plant safely dilutes its leftover salty water, so extra saltiness has never actually been proven to harm the bay's happy fish.

q: What is the standard SI unit for electric current?
e: Just like counting water in a rushing river, we measure the flow of zooming electrons in amperes.

q: Which of the following is true about sound and light waves transmitted through the air?
a: Sound waves are longitudinal while light waves are transverse
Sound waves are transverse while light waves are longitudinal
Both sound waves and light waves are compression waves
Both sound waves and light waves are shear waves
e: Sound shoves forward in longitudinal squeezes, while light waves dance up and down in transverse wiggles through the air.

q: The Intertropical Convergence Zone is the low-pressure zone of rising, warm air found in what atmospheric circulation cell?
e: In the warm Hadley cell near the equator, toasty air floats upward like a balloon, creating this calm, rainy zone.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of the Kuiper [KYE-pur] belt?
a: It is smaller in size and mass than the asteroid belt
It exists in a region of the solar system beyond the eight planets
The second Kuiper belt object was discovered in 1992
Pluto is its largest known member
e: That icy junkyard past Neptune is actually way bigger and heavier than the rocky asteroid belt, not smaller at all!

q: Which of the following nutrients is most likely to benefit photosynthesizers in an upwelling region?
e: Deep ocean water bubbles up carrying yummy nitrate, giving hungry plant plankton the perfect fertilizer to grow strong.

q: The rings of Saturn are mostly made of which of the following substances?
e: Saturn's glittering halo is mostly made of billions of icy snowballs dancing together in space.

q: What is the process of comparing a property of an object to a well-defined and agreed-upon referent?
e: Measurement lets us see how an object stacks up against a trusted standard, like using a trusty wooden ruler!

q: Hubble's law relates the distance to a galaxy to what other characteristic?
e: The farther a galaxy wanders into deep space, the faster its velocity as it zooms away from us!

q: Which of the following gives glacial meltwater a quality which is commonly described as glacial milk:
e: Tiny bits of crushed rock stay suspended in the icy meltwater, clouding it up like a glass of milk.

q: A ball travels a distances of 10 meters around a circle with a radius of 40 meters. Which of the following is its displacement in meters?
a: 40sin(/4)/sin(3/8) [40 sine of, open parenthesis, pi over 4, close parenthesis, over sine of, open parenthesis, 3 pi over 8, close parenthesis]
40sin(/8)/sin(7/16) [40 sine of, open parenthesis, pi over 8, close parenthesis, over sine of, open parenthesis, 7 pi over 16, close parenthesis]
e: Displacement is the straight shortcut between where the ball started and stopped, which this neat sine formula calculates perfectly.

q: Why do many bridges have expansion joints?
a: To reduce the vibration of cars traveling across the bridge
To permit quick disassembly in case of flooding or other disasters
To increase resistance to UVB-induced photo-degradation
To prevent buckling when the bridge expands and contracts with temperature changes
e: Bridges stretch in the summer heat and shrink in winter, so these clever joints keep them from buckling!

q: Which of the following processes could NOT take place in the active site of an enzyme?
e: Glycolysis is a whole busy ten-step pathway, far too huge to fit inside just one single enzyme's cozy pocket.

q: Coulombic repulsion is about how many times as strong as Newtonian gravitational attraction?
e: Electric repulsion is mind-bogglingly mighty, beating gravity's tiny pull between particles by a factor of 10 to the 40th power!

q: Which of the following is an ore of zinc?
e: Deep underground, sparkly sphalerite hides a shiny secret, holding onto lots of zinc inside its rocky little pockets.

q: Which of the following properties characterizes a water mass?
e: Every ocean water mass carries its own special fingerprint: its unique temperature and how much salty salinity it holds.

q: In the summer, why is it best to do high energy consumption tasks, such as laundry and dishwashing, after 8 pm?
a: It will increase the reliability and accessibility of electricity for critical needs in the electrical grid
It takes more energy to run a dishwasher during the day
More energy is produced at night
Hot water heaters are programmed to operate at maximum efficiency after 8 pm
e: Waiting until night lets the tired power grid rest, saving precious energy for important places like hospitals when they need it most.

q: Two objects have the same size and shape but one is twice as heavy as the other. If air resistance is negligible, what happens when they are dropped simultaneously from a building?
a: The heavy one lands on the ground before the light one
They land on the ground at the same time and have the same speed
They land on the ground at the same time but the heavy one has more speed
They land on the ground at the same time but the heavy object has a lower acceleration
e: Without air getting in the way, gravity pulls on both objects equally, letting them zip down and land together like twins!

q: To maximize the concentration of energy from the Sun, heliostats must do which of the following?
a: Track the zenith angle of the Sun
Track the solar declination of the Sun
Track the azimuth angle and the altitude of the Sun
Keep the panel facing up at all times
e: These clever mirrors track the Sun's azimuth angle and altitude, following it across the sky like sunflowers to catch every ray.

q: Which of these two plates are best know for forming earthquakes and tsunami's?
e: When heavy ocean plates crash together at convergent boundaries, they shove water upward, waking up giant tsunamis and rumbling quakes.

q: What is the SI base unit of temperature?
e: Scientists everywhere pick Kelvin as their grand champion base unit to measure how warm or chilly things are.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are studying the physical properties of B mesons and their antiparticles. Which of the following pairs of quarks would make up a meson that has negative electric charge?
e: A bottom quark pairs with an anti-charm partner, adding their negative electric charges together to make a negative meson!

q: Which of the following is the final phase of stellar evolution for our Sun and stars of similar size?
e: When our cozy Sun grows old, it gently puffs away its blankets, leaving behind a tiny, glowing white dwarf core to snooze forever.

q: Which of the following can transfer heat through a vacuum:
e: Empty space has no air for heat to hitchhike on, so warm sunlight travels as radiation, surfing smoothly all by itself.

q: Most of the matter that makes up the Sun is in what phase?
e: The Sun is so sizzling hot that its atoms dance apart into a wild, glowing soup called plasma!

q: Which of the following is an example of a radiation detector?
e: A Geiger counter acts like an eager little watchdog, cheerfully clicking whenever it sniffs out invisible bits of radiation nearby.

q: At which of the following latitudes in the Northern Hemisphere will the Sun be directly overhead at solar noon on the summer solstice?
e: Earth leans toward the Sun in June, shining noon's brightest spotlight right along the northern belt called the Tropic of Cancer.

q: Two charged particles, X and Y, are 1 meter apart. X has a charge of 2 coulombs and Y has a charge of 1 coulomb. Which of the following is TRUE of the magnitude of the force of X on Y?
a: It has twice the magnitude of the force of Y on X
It has half the magnitude of the force of Y on X
It has the same magnitude as the force of Y on X
It has four times the magnitude of the force of Y on X
e: Even though particle X is bigger, both particles push each other with the exact same force, like two polite dancers pushing apart.

q: Which of the following is closest to the maximum efficiency of a DC/DC converter?
e: These clever gadgets are superstar helpers, passing along ninety percent of their electrical energy without spilling much heat.

q: The Sun shines on a lake at an oblique angle. Compared to your view on the shore, in which of the following ways does a fish see the Sun?
a: The same location in the sky
Total internal reflection blocks the appearance of the Sun
e: Water bends incoming sunlight like a magic trick, tricking a happy little fish into seeing the Sun higher in the sky.

q: A psychrometer is used by meteorologists to most directly measure which of the following?
e: By watching how fast water evaporates from a wet thermometer, this clever tool sniffs out the air's relative humidity.

q: Which of the following is used to focus sunlight to a specific point in solar panels?
e: Giant robotic mirrors called heliostats play team tag, turning all day to bounce bright beams onto one single target.

q: The transfer of energy from the Sun across space is accomplished primarily by:
e: Across the quiet void of space, solar energy journeys directly to our cheeks through radiation, carried by zooming waves of light.

q: Concentrated solar power stores the sun's radiation in what form of energy?
e: Mirrors gather hot sunshine into tanks of molten salt, keeping that sunny power tucked away as toasty thermal heat.

q: If in a given circuit with a 4.0 ohm resistor, the potential difference across it is 12 volts, what is the current traveling through it, in amperes?
e: When twelve volts push against four ohms of stubborn resistance, exactly three amps of current get to zip through.

q: As of 2014, which of the following countries generates the largest percentage of its electricity using nuclear power?
e: Among these nations, snowy Sweden relied on nuclear power for about forty percent of its electricity, taking the crown in 2014.

q: What is the current explanation for the formation of the asteroid belt?
a: There was too big of a gap between Mars and Jupiter to form a planet
Mars had two moons and planetesimals [plan-i-TES-uh-muhls] in that location were not large enough to form another moon
The planetesimals in that location were moving too slowly to accrete to form a planet
After Jupiter was formed, planetesimals in that location were perturbed by Jupiter's gravity and could not form a planet
e: Giant Jupiter was such a gravitational bully that it kept stirring up nearby space rocks, preventing them from ever building a planet.

q: In which of the following cases will the displacement of the object be the least?
a: A 1.2-kilogram object moving 4 meters up an incline of 45 degrees
A 3.1-kilogram object moving 3 meters on a flat surface
A 0.5-kilogram object moving 6 meters along a circle with circumference 6 meters
Cannot be determined from the information given
e: Traveling all the way around a circle brings you right back where you started, making your final displacement zero!

q: During the month of January, the Earth moves along its orbit at a rate that is which of the following?
a: The same rate as any other month of the year
Slower than during March or September
The same rate as it is in June
e: In January, Earth snuggles closest to the Sun, feeling a stronger gravitational pull that makes it whip along faster than in July.

q: Which planet in the Solar System is the closest to the Sun?
e: Speedy little Mercury gets the front-row seat, orbiting closer to the glowing Sun than any other planet.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT part of the standard model of frictional force assumptions?
a: Frictional force is independent of contact area
Frictional force is proportional to normal force
Frictional coefficient is proportional to force between objects
Frictional force is independent of velocity
e: How slippery two surfaces are depends only on what they are made of, not on how hard they press together.

q: Which of the following is a measure of linear stiffness?
e: Young's modulus measures an object's stubbornness, telling us how strongly it fights back against being stretched in a straight line.

q: Emma puts a thermometer into a glass filled with hot water. Why does the mercury inside the thermometer rise?
a: Heat from the water makes it expand
Heat from the water makes it contract
Air pressure above the water pulls it up
e: When warm water shares its cozy heat, the mercury particles spread out and expand, cheerfully climbing up the narrow tube.

q: Light water reactors are an example of which of the following?
e: Water slows speedy neutrons down to a gentle jog, making this a thermal neutron reactor where atoms split nice and steady.

q: Gamma rays released during the Sun's fusion would take thousands of years to reach the Sun's surface from which of the following solar layers?
e: Deep in the Sun's crowded core, tiny rays of light play bumper cars with matter for thousands of years before finally escaping!

q: In a transmission line, the voltage coming from the generator is increased from 25,000 volts to around 400,000 volts. Why must the voltage be raised so high?
a: Higher voltage increases the power lost
Higher voltage reduces the amount of power lost
Transformers raise the voltage to protect the generator from overcurrents or overvoltages
e: Super-high voltage lets electricity zip down the wires using less current, so precious energy does not escape as heat.

q: What is the general term for an erosional or non-depositional surface between strata of different ages?
e: An unconformity is like a missing diary page in Earth's rock history, where old layers eroded away before new ones formed.

q: Which of the following is NOT considered part of a beach's foreshore environment?
e: While waves wash over the foreshore, a sandy berm stays high and dry on the backshore where towels love to rest.

q: Which of the following is the basic unit of energy:
e: Every time you jump or a lightbulb glows, scientists measure that lively burst of energy in friendly units called joules!

q: SLAC [slack] National Accelerator Lab scientists are studying trimethylamine [try-methil-ah-MEEN] with photo-dissociation [photo-disso-see-AY-shun] spectroscopy. When they excite trimethylamine with 200 nanometer light, which of the following atomic orbitals is the excited electron most likely to occupy?
e: That light packs the exact energy needed to bump the electron right up into the roomy 3p orbital!

q: A chisel would represent what type of simple machine?
e: With its sharp, slanted edge sliding in to split things apart, a trusty chisel is doing the clever job of a wedge.

q: What is the primary method used by a reactor operator to reduce the power level in a boiling water nuclear reactor?
a: Addition of water to the reactor vessel
Removal of water from the reactor vessel
e: Sliding control rods into the reactor snatches up zooming neutrons, quietly tucking the runaway heat into a gentle nap.

q: Scientists at Princeton Plasma Physics Lab are studying B fields in plasma. What is the more common term for a B field?
e: Scientists use 'B field' as their shorthand name for a magnetic field, which invisibly guides plasma like a winding roller coaster.

q: Which NASA Space Shuttle broke apart during atmospheric re-entry on February 1, 2003?
e: The brave shuttle Columbia tragically broke apart high in the sky while heading home after a proud journey among the stars.

q: Which of the following would be the most appropriate for providing power for water pumping?
a: Wind turbine connected to a utility power grid
Wind turbine combined with a photovoltaic system
e: A cheerful, lone wind turbine can spin in the breeze and pump well water anywhere, without needing big city power lines.

q: Reverse and normal faults are both examples of what general type of fault?
e: Dip-slip faults let rock slabs slide up or down an inclined slope, just like normal and reverse faults love to do.

q: At the most basic level, wind is caused by differences in atmospheric pressure. When there is a difference, air moves in which of the following directions?
a: Area of low friction to area of high friction
e: Squished air in high-pressure spots rushes toward roomy low-pressure spaces to breathe, creating a breezy wind!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about Jupiter's moon Europa?
a: Its atmosphere is primarily composed of methane
It orbits Jupiter every 3 and a half days
It has a deep salty ocean which is frozen over
e: Europa surrounds itself with a whisper of oxygen rather than methane, keeping the air above its icy ocean sparkling clean.

q: Which of the following is farthest from the Sun?
e: Way past Neptune and icy dwarf worlds, the giant Oort Cloud floats farthest away, like a snowy bubble wrapped around our solar system.

q: Which of the following is the underlying cause of most volcanoes on Jupiter's moon Io?
e: Giant Jupiter constantly squeezes and stretches little Io like a rubber ball, heating its belly until fiery volcanoes burst out!

q: In hydrothermal vent communities, energy production in the food web is based on which of the following?
e: Without any sunlight down deep, chemosynthetic bacteria turn vent chemicals into dinner, feeding the whole bustling underwater neighborhood.

q: Which of the following is true about the water table?
a: It is deeper in summer than winter
It does not vary under high pumping rates
It varies due to precipitation amounts
It is constant throughout the year
e: Underground water acts like a giant sponge, rising happily when rain pours down and sinking during long, thirsty dry spells.

q: A spaceship starts at rest at the origin. Later, the spaceship is at coordinate (2000 meters, 0) with a velocity of 200 meters per second in the positive x direction. If the spaceship accelerated uniformly, what was the magnitude, in meters per second squared, of its acceleration during this interval?
e: To reach top speed across two thousand meters, our plucky rocket had to steadily gain ten meters per second every single second.

q: The United States imports most of its crude oil from what country?
e: Our friendly northern neighbor Canada pipes over more crude oil to the United States than any other country.

q: Why are exhaust fans energy efficient cooling mechanisms in early summer months?
a: Electricity rates are lower in the summer
Exhaust fans physically pull hot air out of the home
Exhaust fans create a cooling breeze
Exhaust fans create a vacuum that prevents hot air from leaking inside the home
e: An exhaust fan simply whisks stubborn hot air right out the window, ushering cooler breezes inside without wasting power.

q: Why do the planets Uranus and Neptune appear blue?
a: Their atmospheres absorb blue light very efficiently.
The wind speeds are very high and so show a strong blue shift.
Their surfaces are covered with water and their clouds are very thin.
Their atmospheres absorb red light very efficiently.
e: Methane gas in their skies hungrily gulps down red sunlight, leaving only lovely, icy blue rays to bounce back to our eyes.

q: Which of the following wave types has the longest wavelength?
e: Radio waves are the gentle giants of light, stretching out into long, lazy ripples far wider than any other wave type.

q: A photovoltaic cell converts between two different kinds of energy. Which of the following are the input and output forms of energy, respectively?
e: Solar cells catch radiant sunshine beaming from the sky and transform that bright warmth into electric power for our gadgets.

q: To the nearest minute, how long does it take for light to travel from the Sun to the Earth?
e: Sunbeams embark on a speedy ninety-three-million-mile sprint, reaching your eyes in just eight bustling minutes.

q: Which of the following blows from west to east over Kansas and Tennessee?
e: The prevailing westerlies blow faithfully from west to east, sweeping fresh breezes right across America's heartland.

q: Oil components are separated using what process?
e: Fractional distillation warms up gooey crude oil so each part boils at its own temperature and separates into tidy groups.

q: Halley's Comet, a famous short-period comet, was last visible from Earth in 1986. In which of the following years will it be visible from Earth again?
e: This snowy space traveler takes seventy-five years to loop around the sun, meaning its next glowing visit arrives in 2061.

q: Researchers at Argonne National Lab are developing tools to assign functions to sequence data that are being generated at a faster and faster pace. Most of the diversity in these data comes from what classification of organisms?
e: Invisible but mighty, tiny prokaryotes rule the microscopic world, packing more genetic variety than all plants and animals combined!

q: One kilogram of which of the following has the most energy?
e: Steam at one hundred degrees holds the most energy because water absorbs a huge burst of extra heat just to become gas.

q: The Coriolis effect causes southern bound currents in the southern hemisphere to do which of the following?
a: Move in a less circular pattern
e: As Earth twirls, it nudges southward currents in the south toward their left, gracefully curving the water toward the east.

q: The last two stars in the bowl of the big dipper point to which of the following?
e: Those two faithful bowl stars act like a cosmic flashlight, beaming straight across the dark sky to guide you toward Polaris.

q: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of a drought?
a: Increased electricity due to wind generation
Snake migration and increases in snake bites
e: A drought dries up water and soil, but it does not magically summon wind to make extra electricity.

q: Identify which of the following forces has the weakest relative strength.
e: While gravity hugs entire planets together, it is secretly the weakest force, easily defeated whenever you hop off the ground.

q: Which of the following triples of quantum numbers n, l, m are NOT allowed?
e: When an electron's energy level is one and its shape is zero, its tilt cannot be minus one because only zero is allowed.

q: Particle Man is attacking a video game hero with gamma rays. A shield made from which of the following would be most effective in protecting our hero?
e: Heavy, super-dense lead packs its atoms so tightly that zippy gamma rays smack right into a wall and stop cold.

q: A component of a solar energy system is the charge controller. What is its function?
a: To provide electrical protection to the system
To regulate the amount of power that goes into energy storage for later use
To store the energy for later use
e: The charge controller acts like a watchful crossing guard, regulating the flow of power so batteries store energy safely for later.

q: About how many watts does the average human generate over an 8 hour period, if not doing additional exercise or other activities?
e: Even while snoozing, your cozy body radiates about 100 watts of heat, glowing quietly just like a warm living room lamp.

q: During which of the following months will the Sun rise exactly in the east to an observer at mid-northern latitudes:
e: In March, the spring equinox balances our tilted planet so the morning Sun peeks up perfectly due east!

q: DOE researchers at Idaho National Lab are developing practical methods to reduce the cost of biodiesel production. From which of the following stocks is biodiesel made?
e: Instead of sizzling french fries, leftover vegetable oil can be cleaned up to fuel giant buses on green adventures.

q: Scientists at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory are studying new ways to measure the Hubble constant. Which of the following best describes what the Hubble constant represents?
a: Rate of expansion of the universe
Number of stars in the Milky Way
Velocity required to enter Earth orbit
e: The Hubble constant clocks how fast our whole universe stretches outward, like a giant balloon blowing up into space.

q: What quantity represents the ratio of charge to potential difference between conductors?
e: Capacitance works like a bucket's size, measuring how much electric charge it can hold for each push of voltage.

q: When an airplane's ailerons move in opposite directions they usually cause a plane to:
e: When wing flaps wiggle in opposite directions, one side dips while the other lifts, making the airplane happily roll.

q: Which type of radiation has the greatest ability to penetrate matter?
e: Gamma rays pack so much mighty punch that they zip right through thick walls that stop other rays cold.

q: What happens to a light wave that passes from air into water?
a: Its speed increases and its frequency remains constant
Its wavelength increases and its speed decreases
Its frequency increases and its wavelength remains constant
Its speed decreases and its frequency remains constant
e: Diving into water slows the speedy light beam down, but its rhythm frequency keeps ticking at the exact same pace.

q: Of the following choices, where would one most likely find a charge-coupled device?
e: Inside a digital camera, a charge-coupled device acts like a tiny electronic eye, catching light to capture your smile forever.

q: A flat-topped plateau bordered on all sides by cliffs is called a:
e: Standing proud in the desert, a butte is a flat-topped rock tower with cliff sides carved by patient winds.

q: Which of the following will produce ions when dissolved in water?
e: When friendly ethylamine jumps into water, it snatches a partner from water molecules to create charged, dancing ions.

q: Which of the following MUST be the case for a more massive object versus a less massive object if both are at the same temperature and pressure:
a: the more massive object will have more thermal energy
the more massive object will have a greater specific heat
the more massive object will lose heat faster than the smaller object
the more massive object will have less inertia
e: With way more tiny particles jiggling inside, the heavier object packs more total thermal energy than its smaller friend.

q: The time required for the Moon to return to the same position relative to the background stars (as seen from Earth) is about how long?
e: Our faithful Moon takes about a month to dance entirely around the sky and return to the very same twinkling star.

q: Argonne National Lab researchers are studying colloids using high- powered microscopes. Which of the following is an example of a colloid?
e: Milk is a colloid because microscopic fat droplets stay floating playfully in the liquid, never sinking to the bottom.

q: A 100 watt light bulb is on for 10 hours in the U.S. What is the average approximate cost in electricity for that one hour?
e: Running that bulb uses one kilowatt-hour of power, costing only about ten cents on average to light your room.

q: Which of the following best describes why objects dropped in a vacuum on Earth will all fall with the same acceleration?
a: The balance of air resistance with gravity imposes a terminal velocity
Gravitational force does not depend on mass
Buoyancy balances the force of gravity
Gravitational force is proportional to mass while acceleration is inversely proportional to mass
e: Heavier things get pulled harder by gravity, but being heavier makes them harder to budge, so everything drops equally!

q: Which of the following is NOT an important component of the hydrologic cycle?
e: Clouds, rain, and soil carry Earth's giant water highway, making our personal breathing, called respiration, too tiny to be a main part.

q: Which of the following factors does NOT affect solar panel performance?
e: Solar panels only care about the bright sky and sunshine. They do not know or care how much money energy costs!

q: Which of the following approximates the world's total annual power demand in terawatts?
e: Every toaster, train, and gadget on Earth together sips about fifteen terawatts of power to keep our world buzzing!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about arch bridges?
a: Its structure distributes compression through its entire form
Weight is diverted onto its abutments
The curve of the arch reduces the effects of tension
Each half-arch has its own structural integrity
e: Arch bridges need both halves leaning together to stand tall, so a half-arch simply tumbles down without its partner!

q: What is the major component of crude oil, by weight?
e: Deep underground, crude oil is mostly made of ring-shaped molecules called naphthenes, giving this thick liquid its heavy weight.

q: A unit of voltage multiplied by a unit of charge results in a unit that measures which of the following quantities?
e: When volts give little electric charges a spirited push, together they create pure energy, ready to do some wonderful work!

q: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) classifies physical constants into various categories. Which of the following is NOT considered a universal physical constant?
a: Speed of light in a vacuum
e: Universal constants never change anywhere, but an alpha particle is just a tiny bundle of parts, not a fundamental cosmic constant.

q: Which of the following units is used to measure electric current:
e: Amperes measure the lively river of electric charge marching through a wire, telling us how much electricity is zooming by.

q: Which of the following is not a primary energy source?
e: Nature doesn't hand us electricity ready-made like wind or sunlight; we have to make it ourselves from other sources.

q: What property of waves allows them to bend around the edges of obstacle:
e: Waves love to squeeze through tight gaps and bend right around corners, an adventurous spreading trick called diffraction.

q: Which of the following best explains why the Northern and Southern Hemispheres of the earth have different seasons?
a: The same face of the moon is always pointed towards the Earth
The orbit of the moon is tilted 5 with respect to the Earth's solar orbit
The Earth's rotational axis is tilted 23 with respect to its solar orbit
The moon orbits the Earth in a direction opposite to the Earth's rotation
e: Earth leans sideways on a 23-degree tilt, letting each hemisphere take turns basking in direct, cozy sunlight.

q: What was the name of the first U.S. satellite put in orbit around the Earth?
e: Explorer I became America's very first little traveler to reach orbit, bravely circling Earth to uncover cosmic secrets!

q: Who is considered the originator of alternating current in electricity transmission systems?
e: Nikola Tesla dreamed up alternating current, letting electricity dance back and forth so it could travel safely across giant distances!

q: What property of protostars or protoplanets leads to accretion [ah-KREE-shun]?
e: The more mass a baby planet has, the stronger its gravity pulls, greedily scooping up dusty space snacks to grow bigger.

q: A vector of magnitude 14 is added to a vector of magnitude 2. The magnitude of the resulting vector is which of the following?
e: Pulling together reaches sixteen and fighting apart leaves twelve, so any other angle lands right between twelve and sixteen.

q: Andrew has a scale, which he decides to calibrate using a one- kilogram mass. Which of the following sets of measurements in kilograms reflect the most accurate calibration?
e: Being accurate means hitting the true mark, and these three numbers average out to exactly one kilogram, right on target!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true of buckminsterfullerene [buhk-min-ster-FOOL-uh-reen]?
a: It can be found in soot
e: These soccer-ball carbon cages are clever semiconductors instead of insulators, letting tiny electric currents dance right through them.

q: Which of the following best describes why horizontal axis turbines produce more power than vertical axis turbines?
a: Horizontal turbines are facing the wind at all times
The power coefficient for a horizontal turbine is twice the power coefficient of a vertical turbine
Vertical turbines are placed at lower heights
The Betz limit specifies that power extracted from the wind for vertical axis turbines is limited to 57%
e: Spinning like giant pinwheels, horizontal turbines boast twice the power coefficient of vertical ones, happily snatching double the breeze's energy!

q: Astronauts in the space shuttle are about 100 miles above the earth's surface. What is true about the effect of gravity on these space shuttle astronauts?
a: The astronauts are far outside the earth's gravitational field
The astronauts have some mass, but it is less than their mass would be on the earth's surface
The astronauts experience "apparent weightlessness" because they are constantly falling around the earth
The astronauts have no mass as they are orbiting the earth
e: Astronauts float because they are actually in a nonstop, magical free fall around Earth, with gravity gently tugging them along.

q: Which of the following MUST be true of an H-two region?
a: It contains large specks of dust
It is close to one or more hot stars
It is close to one or more cold stars
e: These glowing clouds need sizzling-hot neighbor stars to shine bright ultraviolet light that warms and energizes the hydrogen gas.

q: Which of the following appliances typically uses the most electricity per unit time?
e: Turning electricity into a fierce blast of super-hot air takes serious muscle, making that hair dryer the biggest power-gobbler around!

q: A colleague explaining the results of an experiment tells you that a plot of position as a function of time is a straight line. Which of the following can you deduce from this information?
e: A straight path across the chart means cruising at a perfectly steady speed, so there was zero acceleration speeding it up!

q: The upper limit of the zone of saturation is the:
e: The water table is like the top surface of a giant underground puddle where every speck of dirt is completely soaked.

q: The Doppler effect occurs:
e: Whether traveling through water, air, or empty space, every single kind of wave stretches or squishes with the Doppler effect.

q: Which of the following ground-level forms of precipitation results when supercooled water droplets collide with ice pellets and they freeze together:
e: Up in storm clouds, ice pellets scoop up freezing water droplets, growing layer by layer like icy snowballs into hail!

q: Which of the following wavelengths of light best passes through Earth's atmosphere and thus is frequently observed using telescopes on Earth's surface?
e: Radio waves are giant and gently glide right through our air, letting dishes on Earth easily hear the universe whisper.

q: Meteor showers are caused by periodic comets. These comets are periodic for which of the following reasons?
a: They are being ejected by the same source
Areas of Earth's orbit are more comet-dense than others
They orbit the Sun in elliptical paths
They occur when Earth and Jupiter are on opposite sides of the Sun
e: Comets travel along giant oval loops around the Sun, always returning on schedule to leave dusty trails for our meteor showers.

q: A team of physicists and engineers at DOE's Brookhaven National Laboratory has tested a 20-ton cylindrical magnet that could form the heart of an upgraded particle detector at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider. Which of the following would the magnet do?
a: Bend the trajectories of charged particles emerging from proton and ion collisions
Form new ions in the collider
Heat charged particles in the collider
Cool charged particles in the collider
e: This giant magnet gently curves the zooming paths of charged particles, helping scientists track their dance after energetic collisions.

q: Mars is observed to have a very thin atmosphere compared to Earth. Which of the following statements does NOT help explain this difference?
a: Mars is further from the Sun than Earth
Mars has less geothermal activity than Earth
e: Being farther from the sun keeps gases colder and easier to hold, so distance does not explain Mars's thin atmosphere.

q: Argonne National Lab scientists are using machine learning to predict the structures of molecules that can behave as carbon-based wires. Given that metal wires transport electrons via d-orbitals, what orbitals are these organic wires expected to use to transport electrons?
e: In these clever carbon wires, electrons hop across p-orbitals like cheerful frogs leaping between stepping stones.

q: Which of the following is an example of a class three lever?
e: When you pinch tweezers in the middle to grab something at the tip, your helpful fingers make it a class three lever!

q: Scientists at the Joint BioEnergy Institute are studying plants that produce poly-hydroxy-butyrate [BYOO-tur-ate]. What type of polymer is this?
e: Because plants link these sweet little building blocks together using ester bonds, they create a natural polyester.

q: Which of the following is the effect of reactive power on the efficiency of a circuit?
e: Reactive power bounces back and forth without doing real work, which drags down a circuit's overall efficiency.

q: Photovoltaic [foh-toh-vol-TAY-ik] solar trackers can track which of the following in order to further increase power production?
e: Solar trackers follow the azimuth angle to swivel smoothly east to west, catching every golden ray as the sun parades across the sky.

q: In order for a star to enter a supernova phase, it must be which of the following?
e: A star needs a truly gigantic, heavyweight body to trigger that final, dazzling blast called a supernova!

q: Which of the following statements best describes a vehicle traveling at 60 miles per hour on a uniform circular track, assuming the vehicle stays on the track?
a: The vehicle experiences zero net acceleration, as it continually travels at a speed of 60 miles per hour
The vehicle experiences zero net acceleration because the circular track does not move
The vehicle experiences a forward acceleration as it must speed up to continue moving in a circle
The vehicle experiences an acceleration toward the center of the circle
e: Even at a steady speed, turning in a circle means your car is constantly pulled toward the center to stay on track.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter?
a: The transit time from Earth to Mars was about seven months
It has a camera that can spot Martian objects that are as small as a dinner table
It discovered carbon dioxide snow falling on Mars
When it is at its closest range to Earth, it can send data to Earth faster than a cable or DSL home internet connection
e: This orbiter snapped sharp pictures and sent speedy data, but other explorers got credit for catching falling snow on Mars.

q: Which of the following percentages is closest to the typical efficiency of a steam turbine for electricity generation?
e: Steam turbines spin with great power, but only thirty-five percent of their heat becomes electricity while the rest warms the air.

q: Which of the following is true of the Great Red Spot of Jupiter?
a: It does not vary significantly in latitude
It varies significantly in latitude within the Northern Hemisphere
It varies significantly in latitude within the Southern Hemisphere
It frequently migrates between the Northern and Southern Hemisphere
e: Jupiter's great red storm stays trapped between two mighty jet streams, keeping it swirling at the very same latitude for centuries.

q: In meteorology, what is another name for a region of high pressure?
e: An anticyclone is like a giant, happy bubble of heavy air, gently pushing clouds away to bring sunny skies.

q: You installed a brand new Energy Star-rated range in your kitchen, and you discover that it has an induction cooktop. Which of the following cookware materials would best function on an induction cooktop?
e: Induction stoves use magnetic magic to cook, so heavy cast iron pans heat right up because magnets love sticking to iron!

q: Maximum sunspot activity occurs at regular intervals of about how many years?
e: Like clockwork, our lively Sun throws a big freckle party every eleven or twelve years, showing off its sunspots!

q: A long straight shoreline faces northeast. Waves approach the beach from the north and wave refraction bends the waves to the shore. In what direction will the resulting long shore current flow?
e: Because northern waves hit the tilted shoreline at an angle, they push the water along the coast toward the southeast.

q: Which of the following does NOT represent a type of electromagnetic radiation?
e: Light waves can dance through empty space, but sound is physical, needing cozy air molecules to bump together to travel.

q: Which of the following would be the most damaging kind of light pollution for an astronomer using a telescope at an observatory?
a: Everyone on a street leaving on their porch light
A car dealership using a spotlight for advertisement
Everyone in town leaving their living room lights on after they go to bed
e: A giant spotlight shoots super-bright beams straight up into the night sky, completely blinding telescopes trying to see distant stars.

q: What happens to the amount of light reflected as the angle of incidence increases when light passes from air to water?
e: Like a flat stone skipping across a pond, light glancing in at a wider angle bounces off the water instead of diving in!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about Mercury?
a: Mercury is the second densest planet in the solar system
Mercury travels around the Sun faster than any other planet
Mercury has been visited by spacecraft
e: Even though tiny Mercury is scorched and quiet, it surprised scientists by having its very own invisible magnetic shield!

q: What is the amperage in the following circuit: 14 volt power source and four 7-ohm light bulbs in series?
e: Four seven-ohm bulbs team up into twenty-eight ohms of resistance, slowing the fourteen-volt battery down to a gentle half-amp.

q: In grams per milliliter, which of the following is closest to the density of ice:
e: Ice stretches out as it freezes, leaving it at about 0.99 grams per milliliter so it can bob happily near water's top.

q: During winter in the northern hemisphere, what is the northernmost latitude at which the Sun is visible above the horizon?
e: In deep winter, the snowy Arctic Circle is the very last northern line where our sleepy Sun peeks over the horizon.

q: Researchers at Ames Lab are examining flexible solar cells using electron paramagnetic resonance, a technique that allows examinations of unpaired electrons. Which of the following structures can be studied using this technique?
e: Free radicals have lonely, unpaired electrons looking for friends, making them the perfect little puzzle pieces for scientists to study.

q: A typical pair of scissors would be considered:
e: Scissors have their pivot pinned right in the middle, between your squeezing fingers and the snipping blades, making them classic first-class levers!

q: Which of the following is most closely related to the frequency of a wave?
e: Frequency counts how many wave crests roll by, which directly matches how long each individual wave stretches out.

q: The speed needed to put a satellite into orbit does NOT depend on which of the following?
e: Whether a satellite is tiny or gigantic, gravity loops it around at the exact same speed, completely ignoring its mass.

q: Which of the following quantities related to a light wave increases with increasing energy carried by each photon?
e: When light gets super energetic, it wiggles with excitement! That faster frequency means each tiny photon is packed with punch.

q: Cow Power farms in Vermont have more than 500 cows on each farm. These farms use the cows' manure to generate approximately how many kilowatt hours of electricity each year?
e: Five hundred busy cows produce heaps of poop, creating a whopping 3.5 million kilowatt hours of bright electricity every single year!

q: Approximately where on a Hertzsprung-Russell diagram could you find a star like our Sun?
e: Our cozy Sun is neither too hot nor too cold, sitting happily right near the center of the giant star map.

q: Which of the following is NOT a baseload power source?
e: Baseload power needs to run day and night, but solar energy snoozes whenever the nighttime sky rolls in.

q: Which of the following is NOT a passive electrical component?
e: Unlike quiet passive parts, a transistor is active, bossing electrical signals around by switching or boosting them.

q: If the kinetic energy of a non-rotating rigid object is nonzero, which of the following must also be non-zero?
e: To have kinetic energy, something has to be a real object with mass that is actually moving with velocity!

q: Researchers at Fermi National Accelerator Lab are designing a new kind of qubit [Q-bit]. Which of the following best describes the difference between a qubit and a classical bit?
a: Qubits use quantum tunneling to move data more quickly
Qubits can exist in a superposition of classical states
Qubits exploit quantum interference to become more energy efficient than classical bits
Qubits use quantum decoherence to simulate multiple classical bits
e: Unlike normal bits that choose one or zero, playful qubits can dance between both numbers at the very same time.

q: According to the Energy Information Administration, as of 2009, approximately what percentage of U.S. crude oil production took place in the Gulf of Mexico?
e: Back in 2009, nearly a third of all American crude oil bubbled up from deep beneath the warm waves of the Gulf.

q: Scientists at Fermi National Accelerator Lab working on the Dark Energy Survey have measured a cosmological quantity to be 0.776, with a standard error of 0.017. Assuming normality, which of the following best describes their claim?
a: The value of the quantity definitely lies between 0.759 and 0.793
Throughout the universe, the value of the quantity fluctuates between 0.759 and 0.793
With a probability of 68%, the value of the quantity lies between 0.759 and 0.793
Their instruments recorded a value of 0.776, but they know the instrument can make errors of up to 0.017
e: With a classic bell curve, scientists can be 68 percent confident that the true cosmic secret hides within that one-step range.

q: An object is placed between the focal point and curvature center of a concave mirror. How does the image compare to the object?
e: Standing in this sweet spot bends the light so it stretches out, flipping your picture upside down and larger than life!

q: Which of the following NASA missions has a primary objective to map variations in Earth's gravity field?
e: Two friendly satellites named GRACE chased each other through space to map Earth's hidden, playful tugs of gravity.

q: Researchers at Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility are studying ways to polish niobium superconducting cavities without hydrofluoric acid. Which of the following best describes the problem with using hydrofluoric acid?
a: It is extremely dangerous to human health
It is not a strong acid, so it cannot polish very well
Very high pressures are required to keep it in liquid form
It interferes with the superconducting properties of niobium
e: Hydrofluoric acid is so fiercely toxic to our bodies that scientists want a safer buddy to polish their shiny machines.

q: Which of the following accurately describes the structure of the Sun?
e: The Sun shines light straight through its glowing radiative core, while boiling currents bubble across its outer convective envelope.

q: Ames National Lab scientists have developed a method for cheaply synthesizing materials, such as sodium hydride and potassium hydride. These can be classified as which of the following?
e: Sodium and potassium belong to the alkali metal family, so when they buddy up with hydrogen, they become alkali metal hydrides!

q: Which of the following SI units can be used to measure weight?
e: Weight is secretly gravity pulling down on you like an invisible tug, and we measure forces like that in newtons!

q: Which of the following distinguishes fermions from bosons?
e: Tiny particles show their true family colors through their spin, which tells friendly bosons apart from shy fermions.

q: Which of the following is the most common term for the small particles of salt, dust or smoke from which cloud formation begins:
e: Floating water drops need tiny dust specks to hug so they can condense together, making those specks condensation nuclei!

q: What is radiation measured in?
e: When matter soaks up invisible radiation energy, scientists measure every absorbed bite using a unit called the gray.

q: Which of the following is the BEST example of a suspension:
a: water with 10% ethanol added to it
table sugar completely dissolved in water
e: In pulpy juice, juicy little fruit bits drift around without dissolving, creating a classic suspension that settles if you wait.

q: Which of the following is used to describe a thrust fault?
e: A thrust fault happens when giant slabs of rock squeeze together at a convergent boundary, like two friendly bears hugging too tightly.

q: Which of the following spacecraft never touched the moon?
e: Mariner 4 had bigger travel plans, zooming past the red sands of Mars instead of touching the Moon.

q: Centripetal force is an apparent force that acts outward on a body moving around a center, arising from the body's inertia.
e: That is false because centripetal force actually pulls inward, hugging you toward the center like an invisible leash on a spinning ride.

q: Which of the following constants relates the temperature of a particle to its most probable energy?
e: Boltzmann's constant is the handy bridge that tells us how warm particles are by tracking how energetically they jiggle!

q: Which of the following has the highest kinetic energy?
a: A 35-gram bullet traveling at 1.20 X 103 meters per second
A 35-kilogram cheetah running at 30 meters per second
An 875-kilogram car traveling at 5 meters per second
A 148-gram pitched baseball moving at 45 meters per second
e: That tiny bullet zooms so blisteringly fast that its incredible speed gives it far more moving energy than even a leaping cheetah.

q: Which of the following types of maps would show the most accurate representation of the entire surface of the Earth?
e: Flat maps squish and stretch our world, but a round globe shows Earth's true shape without any funny tricks!

q: Which of the following is at the base of the hydrothermal vent community food chain?
e: In the pitch-black ocean, tiny chemosynthetic archaea make food from hot vent chemicals, kicking off the entire undersea food chain!

q: Which of the following types of organism obtains energy primarily from inorganic compounds?
e: With a name meaning rock-eater, chemolithotrophs are clever little microbes that get their energy from inorganic minerals!

q: Which of the following could be a likely location for a salt mine?
e: When desert lake water evaporates under the blazing sun, it leaves behind a flat playa coated in thick, mineable salt.

q: Which of the following processes involves the scattering of a photon off of an electron?
e: Like a tiny game of pool, Compton scattering happens when a light photon bumps into an electron and bounces away!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about Antarctica?
a: It has long periods of constant darkness
Much of the sunlight it receives is reflected back to space
Cold air masses are continuously flowing off of the Antarctic ice cap
A great amount of snow falls in Antarctica
e: Even though it is icy white, Antarctica is actually a super-dry desert where very little fresh snow ever falls!

q: Highly energetic objects, such as binary pulsars, can be best observed on Earth through measuring which of the following forms of electromagnetic radiation?
e: These super energetic celestial pairs shoot out powerful X-rays, letting astronomers catch their brilliant cosmic show.

q: Which of the following characteristics are exhibited by biota that occur early in the succession of a region?
e: The first brave little plants to settle empty land grow super fast, showing high productivity as they turn sunlight into life.

q: Which of the following provides a measure of the amount of matter in a substance?
e: Mass counts up every single atom inside you, measuring all your stuff no matter what planet you bounce on.

q: Laser A has a wavelength of 400 nanometers, and laser B has a wavelength of 800 nanometers. Which of the following is NOT true?
a: Light from laser A is blue, and light from laser B is near infrared
Photons from laser A have half the energy of those from laser B
Light from laser A has twice the frequency of laser B
Light from lasers A and B travel at the same speed in vacuum
e: Shorter waves actually pack more punch! Laser A's tighter waves give it twice the energy of Laser B, not half.

q: Saturn's moon Titan has a dense atmosphere composed primarily of what gas?
e: Titan wraps itself in a cozy, thick blanket made mostly of nitrogen, just like the air hugging you right now!

q: The San Andreas Fault in California is what type of fault?
e: These two giant rock plates don't crash head-on; they slide right past each other sideways in a strike-slip fault!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the Grand Coulee Dam?
a: It is the largest U.S. hydropower producer
It is part of the Columbia Basin Project, which irrigates more than 600,000 acres of land
It contains nearly 12 million cubic yards of concrete
e: This colossal giant is actually a straight concrete gravity dam, holding back rivers with pure weight instead of a curved arch!

q: Which of the following types of radiation has the lowest energy?
e: Microwaves stretch out into long, lazy ripples, making them carry the lowest energy of the whole bunch.

q: Which of the following statements regarding electricity is LEAST accurate:
a: resistance generally increases with increasing temperatures
superconductors have essentially no resistance to current
resistance is often likened to electrical friction
the heater wires in an electric heater or toaster are designed to have very low resistance
e: Toaster wires actually need high resistance, making electrons work hard and create cozy heat to brown your breakfast bread!

q: Which of the following components of the solar irradiance falling on a solar collector is affected directly by the incidence angle?
e: Direct beam sunlight travels straight like a flashlight, so tilting your solar collector changes how squarely that beam hits it.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of typical Jurassic vegetation:
e: Hungry Jurassic dinosaurs never saw a single daisy, because bright flowering plants hadn't blossomed into the world yet.

q: Most of the rain that reaches the ground is from which of the following clouds?
e: Whenever dark, grumpy nimbus clouds roll in, they open their soggy pockets and pour out almost all our rain!

q: Water ice is NOT thought to be present on which of the following celestial bodies?
e: Venus is an absolute furnace, sizzling so fiercely that ice melts and boils away instantly.

q: Name the circuit element that stores energy in the form of a magnetic field.
e: An inductor wraps wire into a cozy coil, storing electric energy inside its own invisible magnetic field.

q: An ant is walking on the ground following a curving path. The magnitude of its velocity remains constant. John is tracking its speed in the x direction, while Poorvi is tracking its speed in the y direction. Which of the following functions of John and Poorvi's measurements will remain constant?
a: The absolute value of the sum
e: Just like a triangle, the sum of the squares of their speeds always matches the ant's steady pace!

q: El Niño pushes warm water to the coasts of the Western Pacific during winter.
e: This is true because El Niño stirs up the Pacific like a warm bath, shifting tropical currents when winter arrives.

q: Matilda plays an instrument which produces a higher pitch than the instrument her friend Matt plays. What can we say about the sound waves of Matilda's music?
a: Matilda's wave peaks are farther apart than Matt's
Both Matilda and Matt's sound waves have the same wavelength, but Matilda's travel slower
Matilda's wave peaks are closer together than Matt's
Both Matilda and Matt's sound waves have the same wavelength, but Matilda's travel faster
e: Squeaky high notes zip by faster, squishing Matilda's sound wave peaks much closer together than Matt's deeper notes.

q: In the world of circuits and electronics, it is possible to add, subtract, multiply, and divide signals by the use of:
e: An operational amplifier acts like a tiny math wizard inside circuits, cleverly adding and multiplying electrical signals!

q: Solar dryers do which of the following?
a: Harness the power of the Sun to dry clothes by means of a special solar alternator to reduce electricity consumption
Harness the power of the Sun to provide a way of storing food for underdeveloped communities
Use the Sun's heat to convert water into steam through a solar collector and a turbine
Use the Sun's heat and wind to evaporate water and then condense it to be able to dry fruits through steam
e: By soaking up sunshine to dry crops, solar dryers help communities keep tasty food saved for the future!

q: Scientists at Sandia National Lab are testing to see if electrical stimulation can improve working memory and reasoning skills. What cortex of the brain are they stimulating?
e: Your prefrontal cortex acts like the wise captain behind your forehead, steering your thoughts, memories, and clever choices.

q: A comet's gas tail points in which of the following directions?
e: The sun breathes out a fierce solar wind, blowing the comet's glowing gas tail straight away like hair in a giant fan.

q: Which of the following best describes quantum tunneling?
a: A particle crosses a potential barrier without surmounting it
A particle rests at equilibrium in a potential well
A particle switches quantum numbers spontaneously
A particle disobeys the exclusion principle
e: Imagine a tiny particle too tired to climb a giant hill, so it sneakily pops right through the wall instead!

q: Argonne National Lab scientists are utilizing lasers and levitation to improve the creation of refractory oxides such as hafnium (IV) oxide. These refractory materials are useful because of which of their properties?
e: These tough materials are real heat heroes, standing strong and refusing to melt even inside blistering, fiery ovens.

q: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of electricity consumption in the US that is currently met by geothermal energy?
