e: Even with Earth bubbling with underground heat, it currently powers just a tiny sliver—less than one percent—of American electricity.

q: Hydroelectric energy accounts for which of the following approximate proportions of the total energy consumed annually in the United States?
e: Rushing river water spins mighty turbines to power our homes, supplying about eight percent of all the energy our country uses.

q: What is the amperage in a circuit with a 14 volt power source and three 6 ohm light bulbs in parallel?
e: Three bulbs side by side drop resistance to two ohms, letting a lively current of seven whole amps dash through!

q: A psychrometer (read as: sigh-KROM-meter) is used to measure:
e: A psychrometer acts like a weather detective, using two thermometers to sniff out how much invisible water vapor is floating around.

q: What law describes the relationship between voltage, current, and impedance in an electric circuit?
e: Ohm's law is the clever rulebook that shows how pushy voltage, flowing current, and stubborn resistance all dance together.

q: Which of the following requires the greatest percentage of energy in a household?
e: Keeping your home cozy and warm takes a lot of hard work, gobbling up more energy than anything else inside.

q: Which of the following is true of the gravitational force between two point masses?
a: When two masses are half as far apart, the force exerted on one by the other will be two times as large
When one mass is twice as large as the other, the force exerted on the smaller mass is twice as large as the force exerted on the larger mass
The absolute value of the universal gravitational constant is not known with high accuracy relative to other natural constants
The universal gravitational constant of the Earth is larger than the universal gravitational constant of the Moon
e: Gravity is surprisingly shy, making its special number much trickier for scientists to measure accurately than other cosmic constants.

q: Which of the following best describes what occurs to the solar wind as it approaches close to the planet Earth:
a: it is absorbed by the troposphere and significantly heats the upper atmosphere
it forms cosmic rays that create the Van Allen belts
it is largely deflected by the Earth's magnetosphere
it causes a shock wave to form, creating what is called a termination shock in the Earth's ionosphere
e: Earth wears an invisible magnetic shield called the magnetosphere, safely bouncing wild solar winds away into space.

q: In years, which of the following is closest to the age of the solar system?
e: Our cozy planetary neighborhood has been dancing around the Sun for about five billion grand birthdays.

q: What moon is known for its thick nitrogen atmosphere and methane lakes?
e: Titan is a wild world wrapped in cozy nitrogen air, where chilly methane rains down into giant, slushy lakes.

q: On which mission did the Space Shuttle Columbia break up upon re-entry?
e: The brave crew flew aboard STS-107, traveling on a science adventure before their tragic journey home.

q: According to the US Energy Information Administration, in cents per kilowatt-hour, which of the following is closest to the average cost of electricity for an American household in 2014?
e: Back in 2014, powering a home was a bargain, costing about twelve little cents for each kilowatt-hour of electric magic.

q: Which of the following is true of tension?
a: It is the same as stress
Its magnitude is independent of mass
It can be defined as the opposite of compression
e: While compression squishes things like a giant hug, tension does the exact opposite by pulling them tight and stretching them out.

q: Which of the following is coherent light?
a: Polarized light that has passed through a coherent filter
Light of one wavelength, traveling in one direction, with crests and troughs aligned
Light of one wavelength, spreading out in all directions, and vibrating in several planes
Light made up of waves that vibrate in only one plane
e: Coherent light is like a team marching in perfect harmony, with every single wave stepping in line together.

q: Which of the following is the same for all electromagnetic waves traveling in a vacuum?
e: Out in empty space, every light wave races at the exact same record-breaking speed, no matter its color or energy.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are studying gases composed of bosons. Which of the following is an example of a boson?
e: Photons, the speedy little packets of light, are bosons that love sharing space and hanging out in big friendly bunches.

q: Which of the following does NOT affect the pressure of an incompressible fluid in a container at a specific point?
a: The depth of the point in the fluid
The width of the container at the point
e: Water pressure only cares about how deep you dive, not how skinny or wide the swimming pool happens to be!

q: Which of the following best describes the direction in which a comet's gas tail points?
e: The Sun breathes out a fierce solar wind, blowing the comet's glowing gas tail straight away like hair in a storm.

q: Which of the following sets of laws describes how planets orbit stars?
e: Kepler figured out the cosmic dance rules, showing us how planets gracefully glide in oval paths around their star.

q: The energy saved from recycling one aluminum can is enough to run a TV set for about how long?
e: Giving just one aluminum can a second life saves enough electric spark to watch television for three whole hours!

q: Researchers at Fermi National Accelerator Facility are constructing DUNE, the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment. In this experiment, neutrinos will travel 800 miles before being detected. How will the neutrinos travel the 800 miles?
a: Neutrinos will travel through underground electrical wiring
Neutrinos will be routed over land by a series of superconducting magnets
Neutrinos will be fired through an 800 mile linear accelerator
Neutrinos will be fired underground and pass through Earth
e: Tiny, ghostly neutrinos can zip straight through solid ground, so scientists shoot them right through the Earth without needing tunnels.

q: Territorial waters are defined as extending how many nautical miles from a shoreline?
e: A country's ocean backyard stretches exactly twelve nautical miles from shore, giving coastal nations their very own watery kingdom to look after.

q: The effect of physiological ions binding to G protein-coupled receptors that transmit information is being studied by researchers at Los Alamos National Laboratory using nuclear magnetic resonance. Which of the following could NOT be an ion they are studying?
e: While metals like calcium happily turn into positive ion helpers, sulfur is a nonmetal that simply cannot play that role.

q: The energy used in our households comes through electrical lines originating from which of the following locations?
e: A generation station is the buzzing powerhouse where electricity is made before it travels through wires right into your home.

q: The r- and s-processes can occur in the cores of massive stars, enabling them to do what?
a: Create more protons to support the core
e: These giant starry ovens capture fast neutrons to forge heavyweight atomic treasures that are heavier than plain iron.

q: Nuclear power plants in the United States typically either generate power at their full rated capacity, or not at all, even though they have the capability to vary power output. Researchers at Argonne National Lab recently conducted a study that demonstrated the benefits of varying power output to help grid operators rebalance supply and demand in response to unexpected power events. Which of the following alternative energy sources, if attached to the grid, would be most likely to result in unplanned surpluses or shortfalls?
e: The playful wind blows whenever it feels like it, making giant turbines spin fast one minute and sit quietly the next.

q: Work is done on the box in all of the following scenarios except:
a: A boy raising the box above his head
A boy holding the box still above his head
A boy pushing the box up a ramp
A boy kicking the box from rest across a frictionless floor
e: Even if your arms get tired, science says work only happens when things move, so holding a box still counts as zero work.

q: Which of the following is an example of the Doppler effect:
a: the higher a sound pitch the slower it travels through a dense medium
light emitted from a galaxy that is moving away from Earth is shifted to the red wavelengths
sound is louder the closer it is to an observer
light intensity falls off with the cube of the distance from an observer
e: When a speeding galaxy rushes away, its light waves stretch out behind it like taffy, glowing redder to our eyes.

q: If one holds a piece of notebook paper vertically in front of and below the mouth and blows strongly over the paper, the paper rises in the direction that the air is flowing. This illustrates what principle of physics:
e: Bernoulli's law shows that fast air whooshing over the paper drops its pressure, letting still air push it up!

q: Which of the following is not true of seawater?
a: Seawater is denser than fresh water
The freezing point of seawater decreases as salt concentration increases
Seawater is uniformly saline throughout the world
The thermal conductivity of seawater decreases with increasing salinity
e: Our big blue oceans mix constantly, so saltiness varies from place to place rather than staying uniformly the same everywhere.

q: What is peculiar in the rotation of the planet Uranus?
a: It is much slower than is typical for Jovian planets
It is much faster than is typical for Jovian planets
The equator rotates much faster than the poles
It rotates on its side with its axis is nearly parallel to the plane of its orbit
e: While other planets spin like upright tops, sleepy Uranus rolls along on its side as it orbits the Sun.

q: Which of the following elements is commonly reduced from its oxide with electricity?
e: Aluminum clings tightly to oxygen, so makers use a powerful zap of electricity to pull the pure, shiny metal free.

q: A spring lies flat on a frictionless table and oscillates with a mass attached to the end of it. Which of the following is NOT true regarding this system?
a: Kinetic energy is greatest at the equilibrium position
Potential energy is greatest at two different displacements
Potential energy is least at the equilibrium position
Increasing the mass of the attached object will increase the magnitude of the spring force
e: The spring only cares how far you stretch it, so adding extra mass won’t change the strength of its snappy pull!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about Tesla coils?
a: They take DC current and step it up to extremely high voltages
Voltages are discharged in the form of electrical arcs
They can create powerful electric fields
Some Tesla coils can wirelessly light up fluorescent lights up to 50 feet away
e: Tesla coils actually run on wiggling AC power, not steady DC, to unleash their dancing sparks!

q: Which of the following terms best describes Earth's magnetic field?
e: Earth acts like a giant magnet with two ends, north and south, which makes its magnetic field dipolar.

q: Which of the following best describes the relationship between the velocity of a galaxy with its distance from the Earth?
e: The farther a galaxy wanders, the faster it zooms away, following a neat and tidy linear pattern through space.

q: Which of the following best explains why most discovered meteorites are composed of iron?
a: They are more common in the solar system
They are more likely to cross Earth's orbit
They are brighter when falling to Earth
e: Rocky space stones crumble away in the weather, but tough iron meteorites survive Earth's rain and wind long enough to be found.

q: Almost everywhere across the entire planet, the layer of ground at a depth between 3 and 100 meters is a relatively constant temperature. In degrees Celsius, which of the following temperatures is it?
e: Deep underground, Earth wears a cozy blanket of soil that stays at a nice, steady ten degrees Celsius all year round.

q: Which of the following devices would an astronomer most likely use to detect electromagnetic radiation entering the Earth's atmosphere?
e: A bolometer is a super-sensitive thermal gadget that senses faint space radiation by feeling the tiny bit of warmth it brings.

q: The tails of comets always do which of the following?
a: Point away from their direction of travel
Point in their direction of travel
e: The Sun breathes out a powerful solar wind, blowing the comet’s dusty hair so it always streams away from the Sun!

q: An observer is watching a train pass. As the train approaches the observer, in what way will the frequency of the sound emanating from the train appear to change relative to the observer?
e: As the speedy train rushes toward you, it squishes its sound waves together, making the whistle sound higher and brighter to your ears!

q: A resistive AC circuit supplied by a voltage of 120 root mean squared dissipates 120 watts of power. A secondary resistive circuit, identical to the first one, dissipates 180 watts of power. What is a possible reason the second circuit dissipates more power than the first one?
a: The power factor for circuit #2 is not equal to 1
The voltage source from circuit #2 contains harmonics
The higher power dissipation for circuit #2 occurs only during the transitory period
Parasitic losses are present in circuit #2
e: Extra ripple waves called harmonics hitched a ride on the voltage, pumping bonus electrical energy into the circuit to create more heat.

q: Which of the following types of energy is associated with the reservoir behind a dam?
e: That still water waiting high up behind the dam is packed with potential energy, just waiting for its turn to tumble down.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Laboratory are studying particle-collision processes that create pairs of Higgs bosons. Which of the following pairs of particles could form from a single photon?
e: A burst of light energy can magically split into matter twins: a tiny electron and its opposite pal, a positron!

q: Which of the following is the reason that a lunar eclipse does not occur during every full moon?
a: The Moon's orbit is inclined relative to the Earth's
Lunar eclipses only occur during an equinox
Lunar eclipses only occur during a solstice
Lunar eclipses only occur during a new moon
e: The Moon’s path is slightly tilted, so it usually dodges right over or under Earth’s shadow during its monthly dance.

q: Which of the following is most closely associated with a cold front?
e: Heavy cold air bulldozes warm air upward, unleashing quick, dramatic downpours before sweeping across the sky.

q: In most geothermal applications, what substance is used to rotate the generation turbines?
e: Earth's underground heat boils water into energetic, hissing steam that happily pushes giant turbine blades around.

q: Which of the following statements about a wave is incorrect regarding refraction?
a: Its wavelength may increase or decrease
Its frequency may increase or decrease
Its speed may increase or decrease
e: When a wave bends into a new home, its speed changes, but its ticking frequency stays stubbornly the same.

q: An object traveling from Earth to Venus experiences equal gravitational pull by Earth and Venus when which of the following occurs?
a: It is closer to Earth's surface
It is closer to Venus's surface
It is exactly halfway between Earth and Venus
e: Earth is heavier than Venus, so a little spaceship must snuggle closer to Venus to feel an equal pull.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Laboratory are searching for bound states of gluons. Which of the following particles are bound together by gluons?
e: Gluons act like super-sticky cosmic tape, holding tiny quarks tight inside every proton!

q: The largest voltage drop would be measured across which of the following circuit components?
a: Conduction loop with 7 amp current and 2 ohm resistance
Individual circuit component with 2 amp current and 8.5 ohm resistance
Conduction loop with 4 amp current and 4.5 ohm resistance
Individual circuit component with 5 amp current and 3 ohm resistance
e: Voltage is current times resistance, and multiplying four amps by four-point-five ohms delivers the biggest punch at eighteen volts.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the six main crystal systems?
e: While nature builds crystals in six neat family shapes, prismatic is just an everyday shape style, not an official system.

q: About what percentage of efficiency can an OTEC system currently achieve?
e: Because warm and cold ocean waters are close in temperature, these giant ocean engines only squeeze out about three percent efficiency.

q: Which of the following elements required to support life on Earth lacks a significant atmospheric cycling component?
e: Unlike gases that ride the winds, shy phosphorus prefers staying grounded, traveling through rocks and soil instead of the air.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of the troposphere:
a: the air is much dryer above the troposphere
the troposphere is 78% nitrogen gas and 21% oxygen gas
the troposphere extends from the Earth's surface up to an average of 27 miles
the troposphere ends where temperature no longer varies with height
e: Our weather blanket is surprisingly thin, reaching only about seven miles high rather than a massive twenty-seven miles.

q: Two physics students can push on a box of mass M and give it acceleration A. How many students would be required to give a box of 0.5M an acceleration of 3A?
e: Pushing half the weight three times faster takes one and a half times the strength, meaning three helpful students.

q: Which of the following does NOT correctly describe force in the context of a moving object?
e: Pushing a wagon faster takes real muscle, meaning force always depends directly on acceleration to get things moving.

q: Which of the following is not one of the Big-Five mass extinctions?
e: Earth survived five legendary bad days, but the Mid Carboniferous was just a smaller hiccup where ancient swamp creatures kept right on dancing.

q: Ring galaxies and tidal tails are both thought to result from what galactic phenomena?
a: Formation of a supermassive black hole
e: When giant galaxies crash into each other, gravity splashes their stars out into cosmic ripples and long, swirling tails like spilled glitter.

q: Which of the following is the fastest growing source of energy in the world since 1990?
e: Giant spinning wind turbines sprouted across the globe faster than any other power source, happily catching breezy gusts to light up our towns.

q: A 16.8 kilogram boy is riding in a 4.5 kilogram wagon. A 12 kilogram girl pushes the wagon and exerts a constant force of 2.6 newtons over a distance of 3.5 meters. How much work in joules is done by the girl pushing the wagon?
e: Work is just push multiplied by distance, so multiplying 2.6 newtons by 3.5 meters gives exactly 9.1 joules of energetic fun!

q: The color of a star is most closely related to which of its other properties?
e: Just like hot fire shifts from red to sizzling blue, a star's color tells us exactly how hot its surface is baking.

q: Which of the following nuclear reactions is the dominant source of energy in the Sun?
e: Deep inside the Sun, tiny atoms squeeze together through fusion, hugging tight to release all the warm, golden sunshine we feel every day.

q: The Solar System is believed to have formed following the collapse of which of the following?
e: Long ago, a giant, chilly molecular cloud of gas collapsed under its own gravity, cozying up to build our entire sunny neighborhood.

q: About what percentage of the Earth surface is covered by water?
e: Look from space and you will see a big blue marble, because oceans and seas happily blanket 71 percent of our home.

q: Pluto is the farthest planet from the sun during most, but not all, of its 249-year orbit. For about 20 years, what planet is actually the farthest from the Sun?
e: Pluto has a quirky, oval path that dips inside, briefly leaving chilly Neptune as the farthest official planet from the warm Sun.

q: What part of the Sun's atmosphere can be seen during a total eclipse of the Sun?
e: When the Moon covers the Sun's bright face, its wispy, pearly outer atmosphere—called the corona—finally gets to shine like a magical crown.

q: Which of the following is true every year when the United States experiences winter solstice?
a: Earth is at its maximum distance from the Sun
The Southern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun
The Moon is a waning crescent
e: While we bundle up in northern winter, Earth's Southern Hemisphere leans toward the Sun to enjoy bright sunshine and warm summer days.

q: Which of the following types of sediment deposits are formed primarily by wind processes?
e: Whenever playful winds scoop up dust and sculpt swirling desert dunes, geologists call those breezy sand piles eolian deposits.

q: You want to design an experiment to measure the moment of inertia of a hollow spherical ball, or at least to theoretically calculate the ball's moment of inertia. Which of the following would NOT be sufficient to do so?
a: Observe that the ball is actually an extremely thin shell, and measure its mass in grams and its outer radius in meters
Measure the ball's mass in grams, its inner radius in meters, and its outer radius in meters
Suspend the ball from a wire oscillating in simple harmonic motion with a known torsional restoring constant K, and measure the velocity of the ball at the lowest point of its oscillation
Suspend the ball from a wire oscillating in simple harmonic motion with a known torsional restoring constant K, and measure the period of the ball
e: Just measuring speed at the bottom leaves out how far the ball twisted, hiding the secret clues needed to calculate its spin.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab recently published a study on the distribution of dust in the Milky Way. Which of the following best explains how they can detect the dust?
a: Interstellar dust easily scatters red light, so stars seen through it appear bluer than expected
Interstellar dust easily scatters blue light, so stars seen through it appear redder than expected
The gravitational effects of the dust are measurable
e: Dusty space clouds scatter away bouncy blue light, leaving starlight looking cozy and red as it sneaks past to say hello.

q: Which of the following is a physical change?
e: In sublimation, dry ice skips melting and leaps straight into vapor, changing its outfit without ever becoming a brand-new chemical.

q: Which of the following statements about heating air is true?
a: Air over land is heated faster than air over water at the same location
Air over a light colored sandy beach is heated to a higher temperature than air over the black asphalted parking lot
Air over water is heated faster than air over land at the same location
Air over ice is heated faster than air over water at the same location
e: Land warms up like a cozy pancake, heating the air above it much faster than patient, slow-to-warm ocean water.

q: As water freezes it often supercools, which means that it:
a: Remains liquid below the freezing point
Becomes a solid above the freezing point
e: Sometimes very quiet water forgets to freeze, staying a liquid even below its normal freezing point!

q: An eclipse of the moon occurs when:
a: The moon passes directly between the Earth and the sun
The Earth passes directly between the sun and the moon
The moon's dark side faces the Earth
The sun passes directly between the Earth and the moon
e: A lunar eclipse happens when Earth steps right between the Sun and Moon, casting its giant shadow over our nighttime buddy.

q: The prevailing westerlies converge and are caused to rise at which of the following latitudes:
e: Around sixty degrees latitude, warm rushing winds bump into icy polar air, giving them nowhere to go but up.

q: The mass of most distant stars is estimated by astronomers by measuring which of the following?
a: The speed at which a star is rotating on its axis
The distance between Earth and the star
The gravitation attraction of the star and nearby planetary objects
The speed of light traveling from that star to Earth
e: Astronomers watch how a star's invisible gravitational hug pulls on nearby orbiting objects to figure out just how heavy it is.

q: Extensional boundaries are typically associated with what type of faulting?
e: When Earth's crust stretches like warm taffy, rock blocks slide smoothly downward along normal faults.

q: The moons, Miranda, Ariel, Umbriel, Titania and Oberon orbit which planet?
e: Tipped on its side, chilly Uranus rolls along with a playful family of moons named after classic fairy-tale spirits.

q: A sound wave hits a wall, causing a reflection. Which of the following statements about this reflection is NOT correct?
a: The wave will bounce off the wall
The speed of the wave may change
The frequency of the wave will not change
The amplitude of the wave may change
e: Since the sound bounces right back into the same air, it keeps traveling at the exact same speedy pace.

q: Which of the following sources of radiation is most commonly used to irradiate food?
e: Friendly beams from cobalt-60 zap away sneaky germs on our food so berries and apples stay delightfully fresh.

q: Which of the following rates, referring to costs for peak hour cost versus off-peak hour cost, respectively, would most incentivize a homeowner for running their large appliances during off-peak hours rather than peak hours?
a: $2 per kilowatt and $0.10 per kilowatt hour
$1 per kilowatt and $0.10 per kilowatt hour
$1 per kilowatt and $0.12 per kilowatt hour
$3 per kilowatt and $0.10 per kilowatt hour
e: A huge peak price of three dollars makes waiting for the cheap ten-cent hours feel like finding a giant discount!

q: Belt-zone circulation is a feature of which of the following groups of planets?
e: Huge, gas-filled Jovian planets wear swirling, colorful striped belts of clouds that race around like merry-go-rounds.

q: About how many watts does a 10 horsepower lawn mower engine produce?
e: Each mighty mechanical horse packs 746 watts of push, so ten of them roar together at 7,460 watts!

q: For an object placed in front of a lens with a negative focal length, which of the following could be true?
a: The image is virtual and the lens is plano-concave
The image is virtual and the lens is plano-convex
The image is real and the lens is plano-convex
The image is real and the lens is plano-concave
e: A curving plano-concave lens bends light outward, tricking our eyes into seeing a neat little virtual picture.

q: Mary has a scale, which she decides to calibrate using a one- kilogram mass. Which of the following sets of measurements in kilograms reflect the most precise calibration?
e: Precision means repeating nearly the same number, so tightly clustered readings like 2.1 and 2.0 win the prize.

q: The temperature in the stratosphere increases with altitude due to absorption of what type of radiation?
e: High above us, ozone soaks up sizzling ultraviolet rays from sunlight like a warm blanket, heating the stratosphere.

q: Researchers at Ames National Lab discovered a zinc-platinum catalytic particle that achieves what desirable pairing of physical properties?
e: Like a crinkled leaf, these particles have high surface area to touch things quickly while keeping their volume small.

q: Scientists using the Advanced Photon Source have solved the structure of the glucagon [GLUE-kah-gon] receptor, providing a potential therapeutic target for what disease?
e: Glucagon helps control the body's sweet sugar levels, so understanding it gives doctors a powerful key to treat diabetes.

q: Which of the following diatomic bonds is most polar?
e: Chlorine is a greedy tug-of-war champion, pulling electrons away from tiny hydrogen to make the most unbalanced, polar bond.

q: The typical thunderstorm clouds of summer, sometimes referred to as hammerheads or thunderheads, are called:
e: Towering cumulonimbus clouds puff up tall like giant anvil castles in the sky, brewing up dramatic rumbles of thunder.

q: Which of the following is the adiabatic lapse rate of a dry air parcel for every kilometer it rises?
e: As dry bubbles of air float a kilometer upward, they stretch out and cool down by 10 Celsius.

q: Which of the following quantities measures the amount of friction between two layers of a fluid moving at different velocities?
e: Viscosity is the sticky friction that makes sluggish honey crawl slowly over itself instead of splashing like water.

q: The strength of the gravitational force between the earth and an airplane flying above its surface is NOT dependent on which of the following?
e: Earth's pull only cares about mass and distance, completely ignoring how fast a plane zooms through the sky.

q: As a part of the DESI [DEH-zee] collaboration, Lawrence Berkeley National Lab scientists seek to explain differences in the heterogeneities [hetero-jeh-NAY-ih-tees] in the cosmic microwave background and the matter distribution in the universe. Which of the following best describes these differences?
a: The cosmic microwave background is more heterogeneous [hetero-JEE-nee-us] than the matter distribution
The matter distribution is more heterogeneous than the cosmic microwave background
The cosmic microwave background and the matter distribution are perfectly homogeneous
The matter distribution is more homogeneous than the cosmic microwave background
e: Matter clumped up into chunky galaxies, making it much more uneven and patchy than the smooth early cosmic glow.

q: The Chandrasekhar [chun-dra-SHAY-kar] limit sets a theoretical maximum on which of the following properties of a white dwarf star?
e: A tired white dwarf star can only pack on so much mass before gravity crushes it completely.

q: With over 10,000 different species, grasses are the most widespread plant on the planet. Which of the following makes them different from, and more successful than, flowering plants?
a: Flowers taking the form of leaves
e: When hungry critters nibble the tops off, clever grasses cheerfully keep growing from the very bottom.

q: Which of the following was a storm observed on Saturn - a large, bright, convective storm that appeared in Saturn's southern hemisphere?
e: Saturn brewed a bright, crackling tempest called the Dragon Storm, named because its fierce shape looked like a mythical beast.

q: A falling leaf eventually stops accelerating towards Earth because of wind resistance. Potential energy of the leaf, however, is still decreasing as the leaf falls. Into which of the following forms of energy is the remaining potential energy converted?
e: Since the leaf coasts without speeding up, air friction turns all its leftover falling energy into thermal heat alone.

q: Which of the following characteristics of water best explains why the flow from a faucet gets narrower as it falls?
e: Because water cannot be squished, falling faster means the stream must stretch thinner to keep the same amount flowing.

q: According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, which of the following encompasses the least portion of energy usage in the modern American home?
e: Even during sweaty summer heatwaves, running the air conditioning actually uses the smallest slice of your home's total yearly power.

q: Which of the following is not a type of heat pump?
e: Heat pumps love moving warmth from air, water, or soil, but radiant systems just glow heat straight from cozy floors instead of pumping it.

q: Which of the following countries generates the highest percentage of its electricity by nuclear power?
e: France decided to power its bakeries and glowing cities by relying on nuclear energy for over two-thirds of its electricity.

q: What is the term for small distinctive groups of stars within constellations?
e: Asterisms are those fun little star pictures, like the Big Dipper, hiding inside bigger constellations like secret connect-the-dot puzzles.

q: Suppose your weight is A newtons. If M is the mass of the Earth, which of the following expressions equals the magnitude of the gravitational force that you exert on the Earth?
e: Gravity is a two-way street: since Earth pulls on you with force A, you pull right back on Earth with force A!

q: Which of the following energies is harnessed by floating generators?
e: Floating generators bob happily on rolling ocean waves, turning every bobbing splash into clean, usable electricity.

q: What is the approximate air pressure at the surface of the Earth in pascals?
e: The heavy blanket of air above us presses down with about 100,000 pascals of pressure, but our bodies push back comfortably!

q: Which of the following types of drainage is formed as streams flow toward a central depression?
e: In centripetal drainage, eager streams rush inward from every direction, meeting at the center like water gathering in a giant bowl.

q: What is the name of the Supermassive Black Hole in the centre of the Milky Way?
e: Right in the bustling center of our galaxy sleeps Sagittarius A*, a supermassive black hole quietly spinning like a cosmic whirlpool.

q: Which of the following types of force occurs between two parallel wires carrying currents in the same direction?
e: When electricity zooms the same way down both wires, their friendly magnetic fields gently pull them toward each other.

q: The velocity-time graph of a body that starts from rest and moves away from the origin with constant positive acceleration appears as:
a: A straight line with positive slope
A straight line with negative slope
A curved line whose slope is increasing in time
e: Starting from zero and speeding up steadily makes your graph climb as a neat, straight line with positive slope.

q: Where on an Hertzsprung-Russel diagram would one find a red supergiant?
e: Because red supergiants are cooler yet fantastically bright and huge, they shine proudly in the chart's top right corner.

q: Which of the following star masses, given in solar masses, is closest to the minimum amount of mass needed to form a black hole?
e: A tired star needs a heavy core about three times our Sun's mass to collapse completely into a mysterious black hole.

q: If you shine unpolarized light through a polarizing filter, the light that exits the filter is:
e: Light wiggles every which way, but the filter blocks half the light waves, leaving the beam half as intense.

q: Which of the following is a key characteristic of a protostar?
a: It is surrounded by an opaque envelope
It is at least one solar mass
e: Before a baby star can shine brightly, it stays cozy inside an opaque envelope of dust, hidden like a sleeping chick in an egg.

q: Which of the following is an example of laboratory equipment that is specifically designed to mix fluids without spilling:
e: With its cone body and narrow neck, the Erlenmeyer flask lets scientists swirl bubbly liquids without spilling a drop.

q: Which of the following best explains why door knobs are located on the edge of the door away from the door's hinges?
e: Placing the knob far from the hinges gives your push extra twisting power, called torque, making the heavy door swing open effortlessly!

q: Which of the following materials yields the greatest percentage reduction in energy to manufacture when it is made from recycled material rather than from raw materials?
e: Melting an old soda can takes ninety-five percent less energy than digging brand-new aluminum out of the earth!

q: Which of the following is NOT used in calculating acceleration?
e: Acceleration only cares about how fast you started, finished, and the time between, happily ignoring average speed!

q: What is the major source of energy for protostars?
e: Before a baby star can spark its nuclear engine, gravity squeezes all its cosmic dust together, powering it with gravitational energy!

q: A Newtonian telescope uses which of the following as its primary device for gathering light?
e: Instead of bending light through thick glass lenses, this clever telescope uses a curved mirror to bounce starlight into your eye!

q: What geologic dating technique measures radioactive decay caused during the shattering of a nucleus by cosmic rays on the surface of an exposed rock?
e: Cosmogenic dating clocks the secret sunburn rocks get when tiny cosmic rays from outer space zap their surface atoms.

q: Which of the following materials is an electric conductor?
e: Electricity loves zooming through metals, so steel happily opens the door and lets electric charges race right across!

q: Scientists at the Joint BioEnergy Institute are using CRISPR/Cas9 technology on fungi. Which of the following best describes what they are trying to do to the fungi?
e: Think of CRISPR as tiny scissors snipping and rewriting the fungi's DNA recipe books to edit their genomes!

q: A lunar eclipse can only happen during which of the following?
e: Earth can only cast its shadow on the moon when they face each other directly during a bright full moon!

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a turbidite?
a: Found in alkaline bodies of water
e: When underwater avalanches settle, the heaviest pebbles sink first and tiny grains rest on top, leaving behind neat graded bedding layers.

q: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has a shorter wavelength than visible light?
e: Ultraviolet waves squeeze closer together than rainbow colors, carrying extra energy beyond what our eyes can see.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are studying the carboxysome [car-BOX-ih-sohm], a bacterial microcompartment containing RuBisCO [roo-BIS-koh]. The function of the carboxysome is most analogous to the function of what eukaryotic organelle?
e: Just like a plant cell's chloroplast, this tiny compartment grabs carbon from the air to help build tasty sugars.

q: The Doppler effect occurs in which of the following?
e: Whether it is sound, light, or water ripples, every kind of traveling wave squishes or stretches when things are moving.

q: Bob can either raise a crate 4 feet using a pulley or push a crate up a 4 foot tall ramp. If using the pulley takes 5 seconds and using the ramp takes 10 seconds, which method requires greater average power?
a: Both methods take the same amount of average power
It depends on how steep the ramp is
e: Bob does the same lifting work in half the time with the pulley, and speed means more power!

q: Assuming no friction, in order to accomplish a specific task, using simple machines can change all of the following except:
e: Simple machines can make lifting feel easier, but the total energy you must spend always stays the exact same!

q: Which of the following components of the interstellar medium is typically the least dense?
e: Blasted by exploding stars, scorching coronal gas puffs outward so thin that its particles are lonelier than anywhere else!

q: Which of the following is the hottest region of planet Earth:
e: Deep down under the weight of the whole world, Earth's squished inner core burns as hot as the sun!

q: Scientists at SLAC [slack] are using the Linac [LIH-nak] Coherent Light Source to study protein crystal structures. Which of the following best describes a main challenge to this approach?
a: Some proteins crystallize into structures too large to study
e: Some wiggly proteins are just too floppy to freeze into neat crystal blocks for their big science photo shoots.

q: A car rounds a curve on a level road. What most directly provides the centripetal force on the car?
a: Friction between the tires and the road
The force applied to the steering wheel
e: As you turn, your sticky rubber tires grip the pavement, using friction to pull the car safely around the curve.

q: The impact crater located beneath the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico is implicated in causing an extinction event that happened between which of the following two periods:
e: A giant space rock crashed down, ending the dinosaur-filled Cretaceous period and welcoming the brand-new Tertiary world!

q: Approximately which of the following percentages of U.S. electric power is generated by nuclear reactors?
e: Nuclear power quietly supplies nineteen percent of America's electricity, glowing behind nearly one out of every five lightbulbs.

q: When calculating the efficiency of a solar collector, it is very important to know the incident angle. The angle depends directly on which of the following?
a: Solar altitude and the orientation of the collector
e: To catch the most sunshine, it all depends on how high the sun climbs and which way the panel tilts its face.

q: Most sounds are point sources or line sources. Which of the following is true of a line source?
a: The sound produces spherical spreading and noise level decreases by 3 decibels when distance is doubled
The sound produces spherical spreading and noise level decreases by 6 decibels when distance is doubled
The sound produces cylindrical spreading and noise level decreases by 3 decibels when distance is doubled
The sound produces cylindrical spreading and noise level decreases by 6 decibels when distance is doubled
e: Busy highways stretch out sound like a long tube, spreading in a cylinder where noise drops three decibels every time distance doubles.

q: Which of the following modes of heat transfer is responsible for the heating of Earth's surface by the sun?
e: Since space is totally empty, sunlight must travel as radiation, beaming warm energy directly to Earth like an invisible hug.

q: It is impossible for a sound wave to travel through which of the following?
e: Sound needs friendly air particles to bump together, so it cannot travel across an empty, silent vacuum where nobody is home.

q: Which of the following sectors in the United States consumes the most energy yearly?
e: Giant factories and humming mills in the industrial sector work day and night, using more energy than our homes or cars.

q: The first scientist to propose the hypothesis of the past existence of the supercontinent Pangea was:
e: Curious scientist Alfred Wegener looked at Earth like a giant puzzle and first imagined the mighty supercontinent Pangea.

q: Clementine, Lunar Prospector, and LCROSS were all space probes sent to verify the presence of what feature on the Moon?
e: Robot explorers peered into dark, frosty Moon craters to hunt for hidden water ice waiting in the shadows.

q: Which of the following is TRUE regarding mixing pigments:
a: violet is typically considered a primary color for pigments
only primary pigment colors can be mixed to give other colors
as more pigments are mixed, the darker the resulting mixture becomes
magenta and cyan are complementary pigment colors
e: Each pigment gobbles up its own share of light, so mixing more colors together steals away brightness and leaves a darker shade.

q: Which of the following types of mirrors is curved outward?
e: A convex mirror puffs outward like a gentle round belly, giving you a wider peek at the world around you.

q: In a 24 hour period, when does the coldest temperature of the day typically occur:
e: The ground leaks warmth all night long, making the air shiver at its coldest right after sunrise.

q: Which of the following types of wind turbine will produce the most power?
e: Horizontal axis turbines spin like giant airplane propellers, facing the wind head-on where fast breezes generate the most power.

q: If you travel toward a loudspeaker playing a sound at 500 hertz, which of the following may be the frequency of sound you hear, in hertz?
e: As you rush toward the speaker, you bump into sound waves faster, squishing them together so the pitch rises to 600 hertz.

q: Scientists at Argonne National Lab have been studying the drinking mechanisms in mosquitoes. They watched liquid flow through the proboscis [pro-BOSS-is] using synchrotron X-rays to penetrate the exoskeleton, which is made of what material?
e: Mosquitoes wear tough little suits of armor made of chitin, a sturdy shell that protects their tiny bodies.

q: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of the total power radiated by the Sun incident on the Earth's atmosphere that is reflected or scattered before reaching the surface of the planet?
e: Our shiny clouds and air act like a shield, bouncing about 34 percent of incoming sunlight straight back into space.

q: What highly efficient technology is currently employed to allow satellites to maintain their orbits without carrying large quantities of fuel?
e: Ion thrusters gently puff out glowing, charged particles to push satellites along on whisper-quiet space journeys with almost no fuel!

q: Scientists at Argonne National Lab are studying liquid crystals that can be found in which of the following devices?
e: Those handy liquid crystals line up like tiny window blinds, shaping the dark, boxy numbers on your digital bedside clock.

q: Which of the following quantities is always conserved in an inelastic collision?
e: Even when squishing cars lose bouncing energy during a messy crash, their total moving punch, called momentum, is never lost.

q: Scientists at Los Alamos National Lab are using terahertz radiation for short-range communication. Which of the following is closest to the wavelength of this terahertz radiation?
e: Terahertz waves are tiny wiggles measuring right around one millimeter, which is about as thin as a plastic credit card.

q: Which of the following layers of the Sun has the lowest density?
e: The corona is the sun's wispy outer crown, stretched out so thin and ghostly that it has the lowest density around.

q: Which of the following devices exemplifies a reverse heat engine?
e: Instead of turning heat into motion, a busy refrigerator works backwards, cleverly scooping heat out of your milk to keep it chilled!

q: In the Northern Hemisphere, when is the Earth the greatest distance from the sun:
e: Earth wanders farthest from the sun during northern summer, but we stay toasty because our home tilts toward the sunshine.

q: The acceleration of a stone thrown upwards is which of the following?
a: Greater than that of a stone thrown downward
The same as that of a stone thrown downward
Less than that of a stone thrown downward
Zero until it reaches the highest point
e: Gravity is an eager puppy pulling down on every tossed pebble with the exact same tug, no matter which way it flies!

q: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of using biosolids in compost?
a: They generate bioaerosols which add additional nutrients into nearby soils
e: Drifting compost dust doesn't feed the soil; those tiny floating puffs can actually spread unwanted germs instead.

q: As a ball rolls down an inclined plane in free motion, what is the normal force acting on the ball?
a: Depends on the volume of the ball
e: Because the ramp is tilted, it only props up part of the ball's weight, letting gravity roll the rest away!

q: Which of the following can NOT be a direct source of energy for living organisms?
e: Thirsty plants and puppies love water, but it holds zero calories of energy to power their little engines!

q: Which factor does not influence the speed needed to put a satellite into orbit?
e: Space is wonderfully fair, so whether a satellite is light as a toaster or heavy as a bus, gravity guides it at the same speed.

q: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of mass in our Solar System belonging to the Sun?
e: Our blazing sun is such an enormous heavyweight that it hogs ninety-nine percent of our solar system's entire mass.

q: The spectrum of electromagnetic energy emitted by a black body is determined by which of the following?
a: A combination of material and size
e: A black body does not care what it is made of; only its temperature decides what colorful light it glows!

q: If you see the Moon in the western sky just above the setting Sun, what is the Moon's phase?
e: Peeking right above the sunset, the moon shows off just a tiny sunlit sliver, smiling like a brand new waxing crescent.

q: Which planet did the "Viking 1" spacecraft send surface images of, starting in 1976?
e: Viking 1 touched down on Mars, sending back our very first clear postcards from its dusty red plains.

q: Which of the following is NOT an SI unit?
e: While liters measure your morning juice, scientists chose the cubic meter as their official SI unit for volume instead.

q: Lawrence Berkeley National Lab researchers are studying the structure of PRC2, an enzyme that silences genes. Which of the following best characterizes PRC2?
e: Enzymes like PRC2 are hardworking proteins folded into clever little machines to do important jobs inside cells.

q: The mass of a brick is measured on Earth, then transported to the Moon and measured again. Compared to its mass on Earth, the brick's mass on the Moon will be which of the following?
a: Impossible to determine without further information
e: Even after a wild rocket trip, the brick still holds all its original stuff, so its mass stays exactly the same!

q: Which of the following symptoms is LEAST likely to occur during an astronaut's long-term stay in the International Space Station?
e: In floating zero gravity, spines actually stretch out and relax, so astronauts grow a little taller rather than shrinking in height!

q: According to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, construction of communications towers may negatively impact migratory birds. Which of the following is LEAST dangerous to migrating birds ?
a: Lighted towers with a height greater than 199 feet
Unlighted towers with a height greater than 199 feet
Lighted towers with a height less than 199 feet
Unlighted towers with a height less than 199 feet
e: Short towers without confusing, glowing lights stay out of the birds' way, letting feathered travelers zoom safely through the night!

q: Which of the following does the slope on a distance- time graph represent?
e: The steepness of that little hill shows velocity, revealing just how fast our traveler is zooming along!

q: Which of the following is an example of a well-known group of extinct marine arthropods that existed in abundance during the lower Paleozoic?
e: Long before dinosaurs walked the land, little armored crawlers called trilobites scurried happily across ancient ocean floors.

q: Harmonics, an issue of power quality, causes which of the following effects?
a: Distorts the voltage and current waveforms of a circuit
Power interruption for more than one minute
e: Harmonics are like mischievous echoes in the wires, twisting and distorting the clean, smooth waves of electricity flowing through a circuit.

q: Which of the following is the most common type of galaxy in the universe?
e: Smooth elliptical galaxies shape up like giant, glowing cosmic footballs, and they outnumber every other kind of galaxy in our starry universe.

q: Given that middle C is 261.63 hertz, then, in hertz, what is the frequency of the next overtone of C?
e: Musical notes love leaping up an octave by vibrating twice as fast, doubling that sound right to 523.26 hertz!

q: Which of the following describes a region within a magnetic material that has uniform magnetization?
e: Inside a magnet, tiny magnetic domains act like friendly neighborhoods where all the atoms proudly point their compasses in the exact same direction.

q: Which of the following is an example of Newton's second law of motion?
a: When a block is traveling at velocity v, it will continue unless acted upon by a force
Angular momentum cannot be created or destroyed
When the same force is applied to a block of mass M as is applied to a block of mass 2M, the block with a greater mass accelerates more slowly
When a block collides with another block, energy is transferred
e: Giving two sleepy boxes the same push means the heavier one speeds up much slower, proving Newton's rule that mass resists acceleration.

q: According to thermodynamics, whenever energy is converted from one form to another then:
a: the net useful energy remains the same
the net useful energy must decrease
the total energy of the system increases
the total energy of the system decreases
e: Whenever energy swaps costumes into something new, a little bit gets lost as useless heat, so the amount of useful energy always shrinks.

q: What phenomenon is responsible for the shimmer that rises from cement on a hot day?
a: Refraction of light off dust particles
Changing light refraction from mixing cool air with warm air
e: Toasty rising air mixes with cooler air, bending light rays like a wiggly funhouse mirror to make the ground shimmer.

q: According to the American Wind Energy Association, wind energy is currently on pace to meet which of the following percentages of U.S. electricity production by 2020?
e: Spinning pinwheels were blowing along so fast that experts found wind power was ready to provide a whole ten percent of America's electricity.

q: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of the Moon's surface that is illuminated by the Sun during Third Quarter?
e: Just like Earth, the Sun always bathes half the Moon in warm light, keeping fifty percent glowing bright even when hidden from our view.

q: The escape velocity from the event horizon of a black hole is which of the following?
a: Greater than the speed of light
e: Right at that cosmic edge, gravity pulls so hard that even light must dash at its absolute top speed to escape.

q: Two resistors of equal resistance R are in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance of this circuit?
e: When two twin resistors share the electrical path side by side, current flows twice as easily, cutting the total resistance in half.

q: Which of the following correctly describes Sputnik I?
e: A little metal beach ball named Sputnik leaped into the sky in 1957, becoming Earth's very first human-made satellite to circle the globe!

q: Solar boilers and solar disinfectors both utilize which of the following concepts to raise the temperature of water?
e: As water warms, it floats up like a happy hot-air balloon, naturally circulating heat without needing any electric pumps at all.

q: Which of the following are the highest of the clouds in the troposphere and are composed entirely of ice crystals:
e: High up where the air is freezing, delicate cirrus clouds brush the sky like feather dusters spun from pure ice.

q: Galvanometers [GAL-van-AW-meh-tur] and ammeters are used to most directly measure which of the following quantities?
e: These clever little meters act like tiny toll booths for wires, measuring the bustling parade of electric current zipping along.

q: According to VSEPR [VESS-pur] theory, what is the molecular geometry of water?
e: Unshared electrons push water's two hydrogen arms downward like a stubborn little boomerang, giving the molecule its famously bent shape.

q: Which of the following is an asterism as opposed to a constellation?
e: The Big Dipper is an iconic spoon in the sky, but it is just a friendly pattern called an asterism tucked inside a constellation.

q: Which of the following BEST explains why a concrete floor feels colder than a wooden floor if both are at 21C:
a: wood is not as dense as concrete
concrete conducts heat better than wood
wood is alive and concrete is not
concrete is much less elastic than wood
e: Concrete is a speedy heat thief, whisking warmth right out of your bare feet much faster than cozy wood can.

q: Starch is made of what simple sugar?
e: Plants link sweet little glucose sugar blocks together in a long, happy chain to store up all their yummy starch.

q: Which of the following is NOT a simple machine?
e: Unlike basic tools like wedges and pulleys, toothy gears combine wheels and levers together, making them too complex to be a simple machine.

q: Which of the following is a primary issue associated with harnessing solar power via panels?
a: Overheating the foundation under the panels
Rain damage to the solar panels
e: Even our best solar panels can only catch a modest fraction of the sunlight pouring over them, limiting their efficiency.

q: Which of the following stars can someone in North America see year-round?
e: Polaris sits faithfully above our spinning North Pole, shining bright all year long without ever dipping beneath the horizon.

q: Feet per minute is a unit for which of the following quantities?
e: Counting how many feet you travel in a single minute tells the world your speed, whether you are strolling or zooming along!

q: Relative humidity is calculated using what two quantities?
a: Water vapor pressure and total atmospheric pressure
Water vapor pressure and saturation vapor pressure
e: Relative humidity compares the air's actual water vapor pressure against the saturation vapor pressure it could possibly hold.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Laboratory are planning to use the High Luminosity Large Hadron Collider to study the Higgs boson. In this context, which of the following best describes the meaning of luminosity?
e: In particle physics, luminosity measures how often speeding particles smash together, like a super-busy cosmic demolition derby.

q: Which of the following is an extensive property of a material?
e: Volume is all about how much room something takes up, so adding more clay to your sculpture makes its volume grow bigger!

q: Which of the following does water possess that most directly allows it to absorb large amounts of energy with a relatively small change in temperature:
e: With its high specific heat, water acts like a patient sponge, soaking up lots of heat energy before warming up even a bit.

q: Which of the following substances likely has the strongest odor?
e: Unlike solid salt or metal, ammonia is a gas with busy molecules that escape easily to tickle your nose with a sharp stink!

q: Using current technologies, which of the following sources of energy is nonrenewable?
e: Nuclear power uses up rare fuel hidden inside the Earth, and once those special rocks are gone, nature cannot remake them anytime soon.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a direct-use application of geothermal energy?
e: Making electricity needs turbines and generators, so it is indirect, unlike simply soaking your toes in toasty underground hot springs.

q: Which of the following is a major component of marine snow?
e: Deep ocean critters welcome a blizzard of marine snow, which is mostly tiny bits of drifted plankton poop falling like flakes!

q: Researchers at Lawrence Livermore National Lab are working to develop new reflective optics for use with X-ray imaging. Which of the following wavelengths would be considered X-ray?
e: X-rays are super tight waves of light, and four nanometers is just the right microscopic squeeze to fit right in.

q: Which of the following can form when calcium ions precipitate from solution?
e: When wandering calcium settles out of water, it happily locks together to build a sparkling mineral called calcite.

q: When a ball rolls downhill, the gravitational potential energy of the ball is transformed into what type of energy?
e: As the ball tumbles down the hill, its stored waiting energy joyfully turns into kinetic energy, the wonderful energy of motion!

q: Which of the following is the type of moderator used in the reactor in Chernobyl, Ukraine?
e: Heavy blocks of graphite sat inside the reactor, stepping in to slow down those zippy, bouncing neutrons.

q: An object that keeps the same speed while changing direction is:
e: Even at a steady speed, steering around a curve is called accelerating because your direction of travel is changing every second!

q: Scientists at Argonne National Lab have been using Bragg coherent diffraction imaging to probe the structures of nanometer-sized crystals. What part of the electromagnetic spectrum is used for this imaging?
e: Tiny crystal treasures are so microscopic that only super-short X-ray waves can squeeze in to take their picture.

q: Barium hydroxide and ammonium nitrate are mixed in a 2 to 1 ratio in an Erlenmeyer flask and stirred together at room temperature. Within 30 seconds, the odor of ammonia is evident. The Erlenmeyer flask is then placed in contact with a small amount of liquid water. Which of the following will happen to the water?
a: It will completely turn into steam
Part of it will remain liquid and part will turn into steam
e: This hungry reaction steals heat from everything nearby, chilling the wet spot underneath so quickly that the water shivers into solid ice!

q: Which of the following choices is NOT a condition required for the formation of a thunderstorm?
a: Humid air in low- to mid-troposphere
e: Thunderstorms are cozy heat-lovers, so they crave warm air to cook up giant storms instead of low, chilly temperatures!

q: A star's spectral type is most related to which of its following properties?
e: Just like a campfire glows blue when sizzling hot and red when cooling, a star's spectral type reveals its temperature.

q: The Arctic Circle lies at which of the following latitudes:
e: At sixty-six degrees north, this frosty line marks the magical place where the summer sun refuses to go to bed.

q: The product of mass and velocity would most commonly be described as:
e: Momentum is an object's rolling oomph, multiplying its heavy mass by its speedy zoom to show how hard it is to stop!

q: The Doppler effect applies to light.

q: Which of the following sectors of American society uses the greatest amount of freshwater?
e: Thirsty crops love a big drink, so agriculture gulps down way more freshwater than our homes and factories combined!

q: What causes skin to sunburn after prolonged exposure to sunlight?
e: Sunbeams carry invisible ultraviolet light packed with secret energy that can sting your skin cells and leave a pink sunburn.

q: Which of the following equations represents Dalton's law?
a: V1/n1 = V2/n2 [V 1 over n 1 equals V 2 over n 2]
e: Dalton showed that mixed gases share their room politely, simply adding up each little push to make the total pressure!

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Laboratory are colliding fully-ionized gold atoms. Which of the following is true regarding ionization energies on the periodic table?
a: They decrease from left to right
They increase from top to bottom
They are greatest for alkali metals
They are greatest for noble gases

q: Real images produced by a single lens are always:
e: When light rays cross to paint a real image, they always flip upside down, making the picture playfully inverted.

q: Potential energy is most synonymous with:
e: Think of potential energy like a coiled toy spring waiting to bounce. It is simply stored energy, ready to leap into action!

q: The kinetic energy of an object is proportional to which of the following?
e: If you double an object's speed, its energy of motion squares, multiplying its zoom power by four!

q: In October 2011, astrophysicists announced surprising findings from the Crab pulsar. Which of the following statements is NOT true?
a: They used the VERITAS array to make the discovery
They detected gamma-ray emissions far beyond what was expected
They can explain their results based on curvature radiation
They hope to test the Lorentz invariance in the future
e: This spinning star surprised scientists with wild energy beams, so curvature radiation could not explain what happened at all.

q: If you drop a tennis ball from the first-story window of a building, as it falls it has increasingly less of which of the following forms of energy?
e: As the little ball zooms closer to the floor, it loses its high-up perch, so its stored gravitational energy drains away.

q: Disregarding the effects of convection and evaporation, 100 kilograms of which of the following substances in the same container will take longer to cool to room temperature if the initial temperature for each is 97 Celsius?
e: Water loves hugging heat tight, stubbornly refusing to cool down as quickly as sand or concrete.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the jet stream?
a: It is found at the altitude at which winds are the strongest
It is strongest when there is a large temperature contrast between two air masses
It is usually composed of easterly winds
It is caused by a combination of the Earth's rotation on its axis and atmospheric heating

q: The man-made satellites at the lowest orbits generally orbit at a distance of 150 kilometers above Earth. Which of the following best explains why?
a: At this distance, they feel minimal gravitational attraction to Earth
At this distance, they feel minimal air resistance from Earth's atmosphere
It is impossible to travel fast enough to maintain an orbit below this altitude
This is the height at which geostationary orbits can be maintained
e: High up at 150 kilometers, the air is so whisper-thin that satellites can glide smoothly without friction slowing them down.

q: In the U.S., the frequency of alternating current is which of the following cycles per second?
e: Electricity does a lightning-fast dance inside your walls, switching directions sixty times every second to power your favorite toys.

q: Earth's perihelion [peh-ree-HEEL-yun] is closest in time to which of the following?
a: Vernal equinox in the Northern Hemisphere
Vernal equinox in the Southern Hemisphere
Winter solstice in the Northern Hemisphere
Winter solstice in the Southern Hemisphere
e: Earth sneaks closest to the sun in early January, just a tiny hop away from the Northern winter solstice.

q: Fiberglass insulation is one option for home insulation. It can be placed in attics, within outside walls, under floors, over unheated garages, and in other locations. Which of the following is NOT an advantage of fiberglass insulation?
a: It reduces heat flow in and out of the home, so less energy is used for heating and cooling
It can reduce transmission of sound from one room to another or from the outside
It is entirely made from recycled materials
e: While fluffy fiberglass uses plenty of recycled glass, it still mixes in new sand, so it is not entirely recycled.

q: When at half of its flow capacity, the typical percent efficiency range of a modern wheel micro-hydropower system is which of the following?
e: Even when the creek slows to half speed, this clever wheel still captures 50 to 70 percent of the water's energy!

q: Ariah is holding a bowling ball and Robert is holding a tennis ball on the roof of their school. Ariah and Robert drop these objects off the roof at the same time. Neglecting air resistance, what will happen?
a: Ariah's bowling ball will hit the ground first due to its greater mass
Robert's tennis ball will hit the ground first due to its faster acceleration
The tennis ball and the bowling ball will hit the ground at the same time
The result can't be determined without knowing the ball's density
e: Gravity pulls on every falling friend equally, so without air in the way, both balls hit the ground together!

q: Which of the following is characteristic of a cold front?
a: Boundary between air masses has a gentle slope
Associated with moderate amounts of precipitation
It moves faster than a warm front
e: Cold air is heavy and bullies its way forward like a speedy snowplow, racing much faster than lazy warm fronts.

q: Scientists in the Biosciences Division at Argonne National Lab are studying lignin, a structural polymer. Where can one find lignin?
e: Lignin acts like tough natural glue inside plant cell walls, giving wood the mighty strength to stand tall.

q: Most mammals are able to eat both plants and animals. Therefore, most mammals are considered:
e: Creatures that happily feast on both crunchy greens and delicious meats are known as omnivores.

q: When a fighter pilot fires a machine gun on a plane directly in front of her, the momentum of the fighter pilot and her plane changes in what way?
e: Shooting heavy bullets forward pushes the plane backward, so its forward momentum decreases.

q: A stream is dammed, raising its base level. Which of the following is most likely to happen?
a: The stream deposits sediment upstream of the dam
The gradient of the stream increases
e: When a dam blocks the way, the sleepy stream slows down and drops its heavy load of sandy sediment upstream.

q: Which of the following compounds has the highest boiling point?
e: Magnesium oxide's atoms cling together with super-strong electric charges, so it needs blistering heat to finally boil!

q: Why is a sinusoidal waveform used to transmit power to homes when the shape does not maximize efficiency in the circuit?
a: The shape is distorted when capacitors and inductors are present in a circuit
The shape is preserved when capacitors and inductors are present in a circuit
The need for capacitors and inductors is eliminated, making the power factor very close to 1
The shape guarantees that no power outages will occur
e: This smooth rolling wave keeps its curvy shape without getting bent out of place by circuit parts.

q: What is the term for the maximum slope angle that a pile of loose sediment can sustain without falling or rolling downward?
e: The angle of repose is a sandcastle's tipping point, showing how steep loose grains can pile before tumbling down.

q: Which of the following is a correct pairing of a layer of the Sun's atmosphere and its effective temperature?
e: The Sun's glowing golden surface, the photosphere, warms our solar system at a toasty six thousand kelvins.

q: A metal coin and a plastic coin are heated to the same temperature. The two coins have the same size and shape, are dropped into the same tub of cold water at the same time, and are left for 30 seconds. Which coin will have the lower temperature?
a: Both coins will have the same temperature
e: The metal coin quickly dumps its heat into the cold water much faster than plastic, chilling down first!

q: Which of the following is a simple instrument often used to demonstrate electrostatic induction:
e: An electroscope uses lightweight little metal leaves that flutter apart to show invisible electric charges at play.

q: Which of the following countries generates the greatest share of its electricity from wind power?
e: Denmark catches mighty ocean breezes with giant white windmills, making a bigger share of its electricity from wind than anyone else.

q: What rock type would you not expect to find on the Moon?
a: Rock similar in composition to Earth's mantle
Rock similar in composition to a metallic meteor
e: Layered sedimentary rock needs flowing rivers or gentle breezes to slowly build up, and the Moon has neither.

q: What is the metric unit for mass?
e: When the metric system weighs a heavy backpack or a playful puppy, it measures their mass in kilograms.

q: The Tropic of Cancer lies at which of the following latitudes:
e: The Tropic of Cancer wraps around Earth's sunny top half at twenty-three degrees north of the equator.

q: Which of the following is the shortest amount of time?
e: At just one billionth of a second, a nanosecond zips by faster than two thousand picoseconds or microseconds!

q: Which of the following moons has the highest surface albedo?
e: Blanketed in clean, sparkling ice, the moon Enceladus acts like a bright mirror reflecting nearly all sunlight.

q: Which of the following is true of Coulomb's law?

It is independent of the separation distance between the two points of charge
It measures the total energy in an electric field
e: Electric charges do not just push or pull with strength; they aim in specific directions, making this rule a vector function.

q: A low-e window will have greater performance in comparison to a standard home window in what regard?
a: It will allow more infrared energy into the home
It will allow less ultraviolet energy into the home
It will emit less radiant energy from the home
It will allow more visible light into the home

q: Which of the following best describes a Plesiosaur that lived during the Late Triassic Period?
a: the largest herbivore of the Triassic Period
e: Plesiosaurs were not land dinosaurs, but magnificent giant marine reptiles that paddled gracefully through ancient ocean waters.

q: Which of the following is the term for the phenomenon in which light striking a metal ejects electrons from its atoms?
e: In the photoelectric effect, energetic light beams give shy electrons a playful push, knocking them right out of their metal homes.

q: On Earth, Billy weighs 980 newtons. On Planet X, the acceleration due to gravity near the surface is half that of Earth. How much does Billy weigh in newtons on Planet X?

q: Complex carbohydrates are called:
e: Think of polysaccharides as giant conga lines of tiny sugar friends holding hands to store lots of energy!

q: Scientists at Argonne National Lab are refining the SIR model. This model is meant to predict what?
e: Like watching a game of tag, this clever math map tracks how sneaky germs hop from person to person through a neighborhood.

q: Which of the following distances is NOT approximately equal to one light year?
e: Light zips through a year in thirty-two million seconds, so billions of light-seconds is far too huge!

q: Which of the following statements about elastic and inelastic collisions is true?
a: Elastic conserve momentum and kinetic energy; inelastic conserve only momentum
Elastic conserve only kinetic energy; inelastic conserve momentum and kinetic energy
Elastic conserve only momentum; inelastic conserve only kinetic energy
Elastic conserve only kinetic energy; inelastic conserve only momentum

q: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of the electricity in the United States that is generated from wind?

q: The only way for a bird to receive an electric shock when touching power lines at the same voltage and phasing is to:

q: Which of the following does NOT affect the porosity of a material?

A model of wave propagation through space by formation of spherical fronts

Because when it is summer in Finland it is winter in Africa

e: Earth sneaks just about two percent closer to the warm Sun, like taking one tiny, cozy step toward a campfire.

Reversing the direction of the current
Turning the current through the coil on and off

The final velocity and the displacement of the object
