a: They protect the areas near them from space weathering
They merge to create a very weak global magnetic field
They only cover the polar caps
e: These patchy magnetic fields act like tiny umbrellas, shielding the red Martian rocks beneath them from harsh space weather.

q: Which of the following types of stars has the weakest hydrogen Balmer lines?
e: Type G stars are a bit too cool to excite hydrogen strongly, giving them the weakest Balmer lines here.

q: In which of the following units would capacitance most likely be given:
e: Capacitors act like tiny buckets storing electric charge, and we measure that holding power in units called farads.

q: A hypothetical spaceship is traveling toward the Earth at a speed that is 20% of the speed of light. The space ship shines a beam of light at the Earth and an observer on the Earth measures the speed of the beam of light. The Earth-bound observer would determine the speed of light to be:
a: increased by the speed of the space ship
decreased by the speed of the space ship
increased by the speed of the space ship minus the speed of the Earth moving in its orbit around the sun
unaffected by either the motion of the ship or the Earth
e: Light marches to the beat of its own drum, zipping through space at the exact same speedy pace no matter who is moving.

q: A neon light does NOT produce which of the following?
e: Neon lights love to glow and beam out happy, colorful light, not soak it up like an absorption spectrum does!

q: A particle is moving along a circular path with a constant speed. What is the term for the force that pulls the particle inwards towards the center of the circle?
e: Centripetal force is the invisible tether pulling an object toward the center, keeping it twirling in a neat circle instead of flying away.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of an electromagnetic wave?
e: While light zips through empty space, sound waves must bump real air particles to travel straight to your ears.

q: As the spring constant (k) of a spring increases, what happens to its energy storage potential?
e: Double a spring's stiffness and you double its bounce, meaning its stored energy increases linearly.

q: The crew of a fishing vessel on the equator notices that their nets, hanging several meters below the ship, are drifting in the opposite direction of their boat. This is a result of which of the following currents?
e: Beneath the surface, the equatorial undercurrent sneaks backward like a secret underwater river, quietly tugging the deep fishing nets along!

q: Mammoths and mastodons became extinct around the end of the:
e: Shaggy mammoths tromped through the frosty Pleistocene ice age before finally waving their trunks goodbye.

q: Lawrence Berkeley National Lab is utilizing deep learning techniques to analyze health records. Deep learning is a type of which of the following?
e: Deep learning is a clever machine learning technique that trains computers to learn on their own, just like curious kids.

q: A Keplerian [kep-LEER-ee-uhn] orbit is a description of an orbiting body considering the gravitational interaction of two point masses. Which of the following is NOT a Keplerian orbit?
e: Gravity swoops planets into smooth ovals and circles, never a strange, guitar pick shape like a Reuleaux curve.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about solar dish- engine systems?
a: Direct-beam energy is concentrated at a focal point on a dish made of mirrors
The concentrated solar beam is converted to heat that is transferred to an engine
Mercury or copper are commonly used as heat transfer media
The engine uses heat to create mechanical power that drives a generator
e: Solar dishes prefer friendly gases like hydrogen to carry heat, never toxic mercury or heavy copper metals.

q: Who, from the Western history of science, first proposed the heliocentric model of the solar system?
e: Long ago in ancient Greece, clever Aristarchus first imagined that our giant, glowing Sun sits at the center.

q: If a system expends a 2 newton force over a 3 meter distance, then the energy state of the system does which of the following?
e: By spending two newtons of push across three meters, this little system proudly gives away six joules of its energy.

q: Which of the following stars is located closest to the north celestial pole?
e: Polaris stays steady in the night sky, sitting almost perfectly above Earth's North Pole to guide wandering travelers home.

q: If you were to build a pond in your back yard, which of the following materials should you use to line the bottom of the pond?
a: A mixture of sand, silt, and clay
e: Sticky clay packs together so tightly that sneaky water cannot leak through, keeping your backyard pond happily full.

q: If a wind turbine produces 400 kilowatts of electrical power at one wind speed, how much power, in kilowatts, will be produced if the wind speed decreases to one-half the original value?
e: When the playful breeze slows to half speed, turbine power tumbles down by eight times, leaving just 50 kilowatts turning.

q: What is the name of the point directly overhead for an observer viewing the night sky?
e: If you tip your chin straight up toward the tippy-top of the night sky, you are staring right at the zenith!

q: Of the following choices, which one best describes the way snowflakes form?
a: Water vapor freezes onto ice crystals inside clouds
Ice attaches to dust particles in the air
e: Floating water vapor hugs tiny ice crystals in chilly clouds, growing into beautiful, delicate frozen stars.

q: Which of the following forms of electromagnetic radiation has the highest energy?
e: Gamma rays pack the mightiest cosmic punch in the whole light family, fizzing with the absolute highest energy.

q: Which of the following standard units is defined in terms of a physical object?
e: Scientists defined the kilogram using an actual, shiny metal cylinder kept super safe inside a secret glass vault.

q: A heat engine operates between temperatures of 100 and 400 degrees Celsius. The maximum possible efficiency of the engine is closest to which of the following?
e: Because heat engines can never be completely perfect, the temperature difference here caps this engine's top efficiency near forty-five percent.

q: The frictional force acting on a moving object is most directly proportional to which of the following quantities?
e: The harder two surfaces squish together, creating normal force, the more friction grabs on and resists sliding.

q: Hydraulic lifts utilize Pascal's principle and an increased surface area on the lift to do which of the following?
a: Multiply the force of the object
Multiply the force of the operator
Decrease the weight of the object being lifted
Decrease the force of the operator
e: You give a tiny push, and the clever liquid multiplies your force to lift a giant car with ease!

q: What wattage of light bulb is closest to the energy used by the human brain?
e: Your brilliant brain does all its daydreaming using only about ten watts of power, just like a cozy little nightlight.

q: What kind of spectrum would you expect to see when observing a hot gas through a spectrograph?
e: When hot gas atoms get excited, they glow and show off an emission spectrum full of bright, colorful lines.

q: What SI unit measures the same quantity as the US measure of weight, the pound?
e: A pound measures gravity pulling down on you, and a newton measures that very same downward force in science.

q: Which of the following is closest to the ratio of the surface temperature of Aldebaran, a red giant, to that of the Sun?
e: Even though the giant star Aldebaran is huge, its cooler surface is only about half as hot as our Sun!

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are working on methods to increase the recyclability of PET, a common material in plastic. Which of the following terms best describes PET?
e: PET plastic is made of carbon atoms holding hands in long, repeating chains, which makes it an organic polymer.

q: What is the unit of electrical capacitance?
e: The farad measures how much electric charge a cozy little capacitor can store up before letting it burst out.

q: Which statement best describes the conditions under which a cone of depression forms?
a: The water table rises in a local area
e: If you slurp up groundwater faster than rain can refill it, the water table dips into a cone of depression.

q: Which of the following is the name for the last of 4 glacial episodes recognized in North America:
e: The very last great blanket of ice that crept across North America is called the Wisconsinan glacial episode.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about hummingbirds?
a: They have the highest metabolic rates of any animals
They may become torpid at night
At their active metabolic rate, they can survive without food for about three days
They have to consume about their body weight in nectar daily
e: Tiny hummingbirds burn energy so fast that skipping meals for three days would starve them in mere hours.

q: The Pleistocene [PLAY-stuh-seen] megafauna is a set of species of large animals that lived on Earth during the Pleistocene epoch. Which of following is not part of the Pleistocene megafauna?
e: Pterodactyls soared with dinosaurs and vanished millions of years before the furry Ice Age megafauna ever arrived.

q: Two objects have the same size and shape, but one is twice as heavy as the other. They are dropped simultaneously from a building. If air resistance is negligible, which of the following is true?
a: The heavy one lands on the ground before the light one
They land on the ground at the same time but the heavy one has more speed upon impact
They land on the ground at the same time and have the same speed upon impact.
The land on the ground at the same time but the heavy object has a lower acceleration
e: Gravity gives every falling object the exact same downward pull, so both racers zoom toward the ground together at the very same speed!

q: At what point in an inferior planet's orbit will it appear largest in the sky?
e: At inferior conjunction, a planet sneaks right between Earth and the Sun, coming closest so it looks biggest!

q: What is the name of the collection of galaxies that contains the Milky Way, M31, M33 and the Magellanic Clouds [maj-uh-LAN-ik]?
e: Our Milky Way lives in a cozy cosmic neighborhood called the Local Group, sharing space with Andromeda and dozens of galactic friends.

q: Which of the following countries produces the greatest percentage of its electricity from nuclear energy?
e: Hungary relies on busy atom-splitting power plants for about half of all its electricity, beating out the other nations in percentage.

q: Which of the following is NOT a true statement about the angular momentum of an isolated system?
a: It is determined by dividing moment of inertia by angular velocity
e: To find a spinning object's angular momentum, you multiply inertia by speed, so dividing them is completely backwards.

q: Which of the following must increase for the particles in a closed container of a constant volume if the temperature in the container increases:
e: Turning up the heat makes those tiny trapped particles bounce around faster, which boosts their kinetic energy!

q: The mass of a quantity of matter divided by its volume provides which specific property?
e: Dividing how much stuff an object has by the space it fills reveals its density, showing how tightly packed it is.

q: Which type of current is the Gulf Stream?
e: Hugging the western edge of the Atlantic Ocean, the Gulf Stream is a warm western boundary current speeding northward like an ocean river.

q: An object suspended above the ground by a string is acted upon by:
e: To keep a dangling toy floating still, the string pulls upward with tension that exactly matches its downward weight.

q: Some devices use electricity even after they are turned off. What is the term for this phenomenon?
e: Like sneaky little ghosts, sleeping gadgets still sip electricity in secret, which is why we call it a phantom load.

q: About what percent of aluminum soda cans were recycled in 2010?
e: In 2010, exactly half of all soda cans—a whopping fifty percent—were saved from trash heaps to be remade into brand new treasures!

q: A mass is held at 20 meters above the ground. Given that g is 10 meters per second squared, how fast in meters per second is it moving after it has been dropped and half of its potential energy has been converted into kinetic energy?
e: Gravity speeds the falling mass up to ten times the square root of two, which this math puzzle wrote down as 102.

q: Hooke's law is most directly related to the behavior of what?
e: Springs love to bounce right back when stretched, and Hooke's law explains how that playful stretch and pull works!

q: Which of the following states would have the least amount of mass wasting based on the state's topography?
e: Rocks need steep, wild slopes to tumble, so flatter South Dakota avoids the messy landslides other mountain states face.

q: A collaboration between Harvard University and Argonne National Lab researchers is studying peptidoglycan [peptihdo-GLY-can] breakdown. Which of the following enzymes catalyzes this process?
e: Lysozyme acts like a helpful pair of scissors, chopping up the tough peptidoglycan walls that protect bacteria.

q: Researchers at SLAC [slack] National Accelerator Facility are using the Linac Coherent Light Source to demagnetize a magnet extremely quickly. Which of the following processes would also likely demagnetize a magnet?
a: Attaching the magnet to a 9-volt battery
Running an alternating current through the magnet
Submerging the magnet in aqueous solution
Cooling the magnet with liquid nitrogen
e: An alternating current rapidly switches directions, jumbling up a magnet's neat little team until its stickiness disappears.

q: Which of the following determines the size of the image formed by a telescope?
a: The focal length of the main lens or mirror
e: A longer focal length gives light more room to spread out, painting a much bigger picture for your curious eyes.

q: Relative to the Sun, in which of the following directions is Sirius located on a Hertzsprung-Russell diagram?
e: Because Sirius burns hotter and shines brighter than our Sun, it sits up and to the left on the cosmic star map.

q: The efficiency of a solar water heater collector depends directly on solar irradiance and which of the following?
a: Collector temperature and efficiency of the heat exchanger
Efficiency of the heat exchanger and temperature of the water
Tilt angle of the collector and collector temperature
e: A heater's efficiency depends on how warm it gets compared to the chilly outside air trying to steal its heat away.

q: Beta Pictoris has a mass about 2 times that of the Sun. In this star, how is hydrogen turned into helium?
e: Being twice as hefty as our Sun, this scorching star uses carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen in the speedy CNO cycle to brew helium.

q: Which of the following BEST describes the term static:
e: When something is static, like a sleepy statue, it stays completely stationary and refuses to budge an inch!

q: On which day does daylight last for 24 hours at the Arctic Circle?
e: On the summer solstice, Earth tilts its northern cap toward the sun, giving the Arctic a bright day that never goes to sleep!

q: Researchers at Los Alamos National Lab are building long-range radio networks for real-time sensors. Which of the following could be the wavelength of a radio wave?
e: Radio waves are the gentle giants of light, easily stretching ten meters long, just like a big school bus!

q: An example of a source region for continental arctic air is:
a: Northern Great Plains of the United States
e: Vast, frozen Siberia acts like a giant freezer, chilling massive blankets of dry arctic air before sending them on a frosty journey.

q: Which of the following best explains the relative lack of hydrogen in our atmosphere in spite of its abundance in the Universe:
a: most of it is tied up in the water molecule
most of it is consumed in photosynthesis
most of it escaped into space long ago because of its low mass
most of it was an unstable isotope that decayed into helium
e: Hydrogen atoms are so feather-light that Earth couldn't hold on, letting them escape into outer space long ago.

q: Which of the following best describes the difference between resistance and resistivity?
a: Resistivity is intrinsic, while resistance is extrinsic
Resistivity is used for fluids, and resistance is used for solids
Superconductors have zero resistance but nonzero resistivity
e: Resistivity is an intrinsic quality built right into the material itself, while resistance depends on the wire's actual size and shape.

q: Which of the following quantities would have the same units as pressure?
e: Pressure is just a push spread over a surface, like footsteps on snow, so it is measured as force per area.

q: Which of the following is true about sound perception?
a: The intensity of sound is independent of loudness
The frequency of sound is logarithmically related to the intensity
The loudness of a sound is logarithmically related to the intensity
Sounds measured in decibels are independent of the threshold of hearing
e: Our ears hear loudness on a special curved scale, meaning sound intensity must leap by multiples to sound twice as loud.

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of appliances labeled under the Energy Star logo?
a: They consume 10-15% less energy than required by federal standards
They consume 20-30% less energy than required by federal standards
They convert 30% of the electrical energy into mechanical energy
They have an energy loss of around 20-30%
e: Friendly little Energy Star gadgets politely sip power, using twenty to thirty percent less electricity than regular government rules demand!

q: Which of the following is closest to the number of astronomical units from the Earth to Proxima Centauri?
e: Visiting our nearest neighbor star takes a trek across about 3 times ten to the fifth astronomical units!

q: Electrodes are NOT found in which of the following?
e: A permanent magnet has its own natural pull without using electric currents, so it never needs electrodes.

q: A bob of mass m is attached to a string, forming a pendulum. If the bob is replaced with one of mass 4m, what effect does it have on the period of the pendulum?
a: There is no effect on the period
e: Gravity pulls heavier things harder while mass resists moving, so changing the bob's weight has no effect on its period.

q: Which of the following clouds has little vertical development:
e: Wispy cirrus clouds drift high up like gentle brushstrokes, staying thin and flat instead of puffing tall into the sky.

q: A stone of mass m is tossed directly above to a height h. If the acceleration due to gravity is g, what is the net gravitational force acting on the stone?
e: Earth gives the stone a steady downward tug that always equals its mass times gravity, keeping the net force at mg.

q: What era is also known as the Age of Mammals?
e: After dinosaurs bowed out, furry critters finally got their turn in the spotlight during the grand Cenozoic era!

q: According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, which of the following sectors consumes the most energy in the U.S.?
e: Big busy factories in the industrial sector work around the clock, gobbling up more energy than anywhere else.

q: Which of the following planetary characteristics is estimated based on observations of abundance, size, and distribution of craters on the surface of other planets?
e: Craters are like birthday candles on a rocky world, where counting more bumps reveals an older age.

q: Which of the following best describes the intercloud medium in space?
e: The space drifting between deep clouds is spread thin and baked by starlight, making it hot with low density.

q: Which of the following demonstrates Bernoulli's principle?
e: When a rushing fluid hurries up, it pushes outward less, meaning faster speed brings delightfully lower pressure.

q: On a summer night you notice that the zenith is in the constellation Cygnus [SIG-nus]. Which of the following constellations would be highest above the horizon?
e: Because Lyra is cozy neighbors with overhead Cygnus, it sits highest above the horizon on that summer night.

q: What is a meteorite?
a: A natural particle from space that vaporizes upon entering Earth's atmosphere
A natural particle from space that survives impact with the Earth's surface
e: A meteorite is a brave space rock that survives its fiery trip through the sky to touch Earth's ground!

q: What parameter of a planet's orbit is a measure of how closely the orbit approximates a perfect circle?
e: Eccentricity measures how stretched out an orbit is, showing whether a planet loops in a tidy circle or a squished oval.

q: An object is placed 10 centimeters from a double convex lens with a focal length of 20 centimeters. Which of the following types of image will be produced?
e: Because the object sits inside the focal point, the lens creates an upright, virtual image, just like looking through a magnifying glass.

q: Which of the following is a dark gray, low cloud associated with continuous falling rain:
e: Nimbostratus clouds spread out like a heavy gray blanket, gently raining all day long without stopping.

q: Imagine you are playing a game on your Nintendo Wii and all of a sudden the TV and Wii turn off unexpectedly, then turn back on 5 seconds later. This indicates a power quality problem; there was a voltage:
e: When the power takes a quick little dip, like a tired yawn, that momentary drop in electricity is a sag.

q: Which of the following materials could potentially be found directly underneath a perched water table?
e: Sticky clay packs together so tightly that sinking water cannot slip past, catching it like a bowl to make a perched water table.

q: According to the Department of Energy, as of 2014, which of the following is closest to the percentage of U.S. energy used for transportation that is provided by oil?
e: Nearly our whole bustling travel world relied on oil, which fueled a whopping 92 percent of America's transportation.

q: A swing converts energy between which two forms?
e: A playground swing trades height for zoom, endlessly swapping stored potential energy with speedy kinetic energy!

q: According to the U.S. government, the BP oil spill was responsible for the release of approximately how many million gallons of oil into the Gulf of Mexico?
e: In a sad, messy disaster, about 210 million gallons of dark oil poured into the Gulf's blue waters.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of a lahar?
a: It can occur long after the eruption that caused it
It must involve material at high temperatures
It contains more water than a pyroclastic flow
e: A lahar is a giant volcanic mudslide that can actually be freezing cold, so it does not have to be hot at all.

q: Most of the photons emitted by our sun fall in which pair of ranges of the electromagnetic spectrum?
e: Our cozy Sun showers us mostly with visible light to brighten our day and gentle infrared to warm our cheeks.

q: Which of the following statements about sound energy is true?
a: Sound energy is produced by vibrations, not by discrete particles
Sound energy can easily be used for production of electrical power
Sound energy is a form of thermal energy
Sound energy is related to chemical changes
e: Sound is just invisible wiggles dancing through the air, traveling as rhythmic vibrations instead of flying little particles.

q: Which of the following is the nearest large spiral galaxy to Earth?
e: Andromeda is our giant, glittering spiral neighbor spinning across deep space, swirling closer to us than any other big spiral!

q: Which of the following best describes the shape of the Milky Way galaxy?
e: Our home galaxy twirls like a giant pinwheel, with a straight bar of bright stars right across its middle!

q: A recipe calls for 5 cups of flour. A baker measures and adds a quantity of flour to a mixing bowl 5 times. Afterward, the quantity of flour in the bowl is measured and determined to be 5 cups. If the same thing happens on repeated attempts to make the recipe, which of the following is a correct description of the baker's measurements?
e: Hitting five cups exactly right is accurate, and repeating that perfect bake every single time makes it wonderfully precise, too.

q: The horse latitudes are zones primarily characterized by:
e: Sinking air presses down so gently here that the breeze falls asleep, leaving ocean waters with almost no wind at all.

q: There are two groups of planets, terrestrial and Jovian, in our Solar System. Terrestrial planets have which of the following characteristics?
a: Few moons, located near the asteroid belt, no solid surfaces, extremely cold
Located relatively far from the Sun, gaseous, largest planets in the Solar System
Rich in rock, relatively very large in size, many moons, extremely high temperature at the surface
Located relatively close to the Sun, relatively small in size, iron-rich, solid, few or no moons
e: Terrestrial planets are rocky, compact neighbors huddled close to the Sun, packed with heavy iron and having barely any moons.

q: The kinetic energy of an object is which of the following?
a: Directly proportional to the square of the velocity
Independent of the speed at which it is moving
Independent of the mass of the object
e: When you zoom twice as fast, your energy of motion skyrockets by four times, matching the square of your speed.

q: Which of the following major cities is located next to a major subduction zone?
e: Beautiful Victoria sits right beside a giant ocean plate sliding sleepily underneath the continent.

q: Which of the following is true about the forces acting upon the system of you and a bicycle as you pedal the bike at a constant velocity in a horizontal straight line?
a: The force you are exerting on the pedal is greater than the resisting forces
All forces are in balance, with the net force equal to zero
The resisting forces of air and tire friction are less than the force you are exerting
The resisting forces are greater than the force you are exerting
e: Cruising at a steady speed means your pedal pushes and the breezy drag cancel out completely, balancing every force to zero.

q: What size of particle is loess [LOH-es]?
e: Loess is fine, powdery silt, like baking flour carried across the land on the breezy wings of wind.

q: What prevents most of the consequences of a solar flare from reaching the Earth's surface?
a: Nothing - it all reaches the Earth's surface
e: Earth wraps itself in an invisible magnetic field, acting like a giant protective bubble that deflects wild solar storms away safely!

q: Consider a plot showing the temperature of water on the x-axis and its density on the y-axis. At what temperature, in degrees Celsius, does the diagram have a local maximum?
e: Water plays a funny trick by squeezing into its tightest, densest huddle right at four degrees Celsius before expanding into ice!

q: In which of the following years did the U.S. have the highest energy consumption per person?
e: Back in 1979, folks used heaps of power, reaching America's all-time record peak for energy consumed by each person!

q: In the most common type of geothermal power plant, what rotates the turbines?
e: Deep underground heat boils water into whistling steam that rushes up to spin giant electric turbines.

q: In a circuit diagram, two parallel lines of equal length with a gap in between represents which of the following circuit components?
e: Those two matching parallel lines show a capacitor, two flat plates ready to store up electric charge across the tiny gap.

q: Which of the following is the crystal habit of halite?
e: Halite, or common rock salt, loves tidy patterns and builds itself into cute, perfect little microscopic cubes.

q: Gannymede is the largest moon of which planet?
e: Giant Jupiter is so grand that its prized moon, Ganymede, is actually bigger than the entire planet Mercury!

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are using supervised learning to classify genetic data. "Supervised learning," in this case, means which of the following?
a: A researcher must classify the training data, which the model then learns
A researcher must watch the model as it is classifying the data
There is no distinction between training and hold-out data
The hold-out data is gathered under supervision
e: Like a teacher showing flashcards, a scientist labels the examples first so the computer can study and learn the right answers.

q: In the modern American home, what represents the largest portion of energy usage?
e: Keeping a cozy house toasty warm takes huge effort, which is why heating gobbles up the biggest slice of energy.

q: Which of the following is NOT a true statement about electric and gravitational fields?
a: Both can act in a vacuum
Both are proportional to the product of the quantity that causes the field
e: Gravity only hugs things close, but electric charges can push away like grumpy magnets, so they are not both only attractive.

q: When an object reaches terminal velocity, the net force on the object becomes zero and the object will do which of the following?
e: When falling air pushes back just as hard as gravity pulls, you glide down at a steady speed and stop accelerating.

q: Scientists at Fermi National Accelerator Lab have measured the magnetic moment of the muon to high precision. Their value exceeded the prediction of theorists by 3.3 standard deviations. Which of the following percentages is closest to the probability of obtaining a value at least this large by chance, assuming that the theoretical value is in fact correct and the measurement error is normally distributed?
e: That surprise muon measurement was so rare that getting it by pure luck happens only about 0.05 percent of the time.

q: How many Btus are needed to raise the temperature of 5 pounds of water from 45 Fahrenheit to 65 Fahrenheit?
e: Warming five pounds of water by twenty whole degrees needs five times twenty, or exactly one hundred energetic heat units.

q: What happens to a 180 watt solar panel's power output when the solar irradiance is lower than the one specified at standard temperature and pressure?
a: The power is converted from AC to DC
The power is converted from DC to AC
e: Solar panels crave bright sunshine. When clouds dim the light, the panel catches less energy and makes less than 180 watts.

q: Pluto and Charon are which of the following?
e: Pluto and Charon are locked in a cosmic waltz, forever facing each other because their spins match their orbits.

q: Which of the following planets has an orbital period less than one Earth year?
e: Because Venus hugs the Sun closer than Earth does, its racetrack is shorter, letting it finish a year in less time!

q: In the northern hemisphere, in what direction should your solar panels face if you want peak energy production to mostly coincide with peak energy use?
e: Pointing panels west catches the setting afternoon sun, right when families get home and turn on all their gadgets!

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are studying particles called neutral pions. Which of the following best explains why they are called neutral?
a: They do not interact with other particles
They form from the decay of neutrons
They have no net electric charge
e: These tiny particles are called neutral because they carry no electric charge at all, keeping things perfectly peaceful.

q: Fermi National Lab scientists studied the creation of a top quark by a collision of a proton and an anti-proton. Which of the following particles is created concomitantly [Kon-koh-MIT-ent-lee] in order to obey conservation laws?
e: Nature loves perfect balance, so whenever a heavy top quark pops into existence, its anti-top twin must appear beside it!

q: What will occur if a wave strikes a medium boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle?
e: Tilted past that special angle, a wave cannot escape across the border, so it bounces backward in a reflection!

q: Which of the following kinds of power plants is BEST suited for peak load demands?
e: When everyone turns on lights at once, gas turbines can fire up in minutes like speedy race cars to meet the sudden peak demand.

q: Which of the following is NOT a key step in the nitrogen cycle:
e: Busy soil bacteria handle nitrogen's journey, while evaporation is just water's special trick for floating up into the clouds.

q: Which of the following elements would one be likely to find in a catalytic converter?
e: Hidden inside cars, clever palladium acts like a hardworking sponge, trapping dirty exhaust fumes to keep our air cleaner.

q: The objects that Carl Seyfert [say-fert] observed are examples of what?
e: Carl Seyfert looked deep into space and spotted magnificent swirling galaxies, each spinning with a super-bright, glowing center.

q: Approximately how many years ago was the last magnetic pole reversal?
e: Earth's giant magnetic compass last flipped upside down around 780,000 years ago, long before humans built their very first cities.

q: Which of the following is an example of a longitudinal wave?
e: A pressure wave squeezes and stretches forward like a playful slinky, making it a true longitudinal wave.

q: For residential cooling equipment, such as ground source heat pumps, the seasonal energy efficiency ratio can be calculated. What is the typical value for a ground source heat pump with good performance?
e: A rating of seventeen means this clever underground system runs smoothly and saves tons of energy while keeping your home cozy.

q: Which of the following countries produces over 90% of its energy through geothermal resources?
e: Sitting right on bubbly volcanic ground, Iceland taps the Earth's natural underground steam to make almost all its energy!

q: You accidentally drop a drinking glass. After the glass left your hand:
a: The inertia of Earth pulled the glass down
Gravity caused the glass to fall at a constant rate
Gravity caused the glass to fall faster and faster
The equal and opposite forces of gravity and air resistance acted upon it
e: Gravity gives the tumbling glass a relentless hug, pulling it downward so it zooms faster and faster with every single second.

q: What is the SI derived unit used to express power?
e: Watts measure how fast energy zips around doing work, like a cheerful little lightbulb shining with power!

q: Which of the following is not considered a type of wetland?
e: While squishy bogs love muddy ground, a bay is a grand scoop of open, deep water.

q: What will raising water temperature (under pressure) from 100C to 110C do to the cooking time of a potato?
e: Hotter water cooks food twice as fast, cutting the hungry potato's bath time down by 50%!

q: About how long in years do wind turbines typically last?
e: These giant white pinwheels happily spin through breezy skies for about 20 to 25 years before retiring.

q: Which of the following is NOT correct about the gravitational force between two objects?
a: It behaves independently of the law of conservation of energy
It is a form of potential energy
It is directly proportional to the mass of the two objects
It is related to the distance between the objects
e: Gravity always plays by the rules, so saying it ignores energy conservation is simply not true!

q: A line of thunderstoms that can form along or ahead of a cold front is known as which of the following?
e: When chilly air pushes in, stormy clouds line up like a marching band called a squall line.

q: A cubic centimeter of water has a mass of almost exactly one of which of the following?
e: Nature loves neat math, so a tiny sugar-cube size of water weighs almost exactly one gram.

q: Which of the following would be most useful for seeing the lines of force created by the north and south poles of a magnet?
e: Tiny iron filings dance and line up around a magnet, making its invisible force lines magically appear!

q: Which of the following is the typical shape of a charged particle's path in a magnetic field?
e: A magnetic field constantly tugs the speedy particle sideways, bending its path into a neat, looping circular dance.

q: Much attention is being given to solid-state lighting because it can do which of the following?
a: Improve the power factor of power lines
Reduce lighting power consumption by one fourth
Compete, in terms of efficacy, with current lighting technology
e: Solid-state lights glow brightly while sipping tiny sips of electricity, cutting our country's lighting power appetite by a whole one-fourth.

q: In nuclear power plants, the heat released from nuclear fissions is used in which of the following?
e: Splitting atoms creates super-hot water, making a whirlwind of steam that spins giant turbines to create electric power.

q: Of the following locations, where on the Earth's surface are you closest to the center of the Earth?
e: Earth bulges at its middle like a spinning water balloon, leaving the flat North Pole closest to its center.

q: A pencil sitting in a glass of water appears bent because light bends as it passes from water to the surrounding air and vice versa. This is an example of what process?
e: Light bends when it dives into water, which scientists call refraction, playfully tricking our eyes into seeing a crooked pencil.

q: What happens to the wavelength and frequency of a wave when the amplitude of a wave increases?
e: Growing taller just makes a wave bigger, leaving its marching speed and spacing happily unchanged.

q: What state has the largest geothermal power generation capacity?
e: California tops the charts by brewing the most electricity from the sizzle of deep underground heat.

q: How fast does the Sun rotate?
e: Our giant, glowing Sun takes about 27 days to finish one big, slow spin like a lazy dancer.

q: Which of the following is closest to the average orbital period, in Earth years, of an asteroid in the asteroid belt?
e: These rocky space travelers take about five Earth years to finish one grand loop around the Sun.

q: Which of the following covalent bonds is most polar?
e: Greedy fluorine pulls electrons away from tiny hydrogen harder than any other pair, making H-F the most polar.

q: Which of the following units is not used to measure atmospheric pressure?
e: Pounds only measure weight, so air pressure needs special units that measure pushing force across an area.

q: Crater counting is a method that can be used to estimate what feature of a moon or planet?
e: Space rocks leave scars over time, so counting old craters is like counting planetary birthday candles to find its age!

q: The darker portion of the Moon that faces the Earth in a crescent phase often appears somewhat lighted with a faint grayish glow. Which of the following BEST describes why this happens:
a: sunlight reflected off the Earth's surface onto the Moon
afterglow of the Moon's lighted surface
e: Earth acts like a giant mirror, bouncing sunshine right back to give the Moon's shadowy side a cozy nightlight.

q: Why is the equator warmer than the poles?
a: The angle of sunlight is more direct at the equator
The angle of sunlight is more direct at the poles
The seasons are shorter at the equator
The seasons are shorter at the poles
e: The equator catches sunlight beaming straight on like a warm spotlight, instead of tilted and spread out like at the poles.

q: Which of the following types of radiation has the greatest ability to penetrate matter?
e: Energetic gamma rays zip straight through matter like unstoppable ghosts, piercing much deeper than chunkier particles ever could.

q: Commercially available photovoltaic [photo-vawl-TAY-ik] cells are primarily made of what element?
e: Solar panels love silicon, a trusty element found in sand that catches sunshine and turns it into electric power.

q: When a reptile is cold, it will do which of the following?
a: Lie perpendicular to the Sun's rays
Lie parallel to the Sun's rays
e: A chilly lizard turns sideways to the sunbeams, soaking up as much toasty warmth across its back as possible!

q: What does the prefix "alto" indicate when describing clouds?
e: The word alto comes from Latin meaning high, describing lofty clouds drifting way up in the sky.

q: What is the frequency of a wave with a velocity of 10 meters per second and wavelength of 20 meters?
e: With waves twenty meters long moving ten meters each second, only half a wave rolls past, making the frequency 0.5 hertz.

q: Which of the following solar system objects are made up of mostly dust and ice?
e: Comets are like giant, dusty snowballs zooming across the dark sky, leaving glowing tails behind them!

q: If you break a bar magnet with a north pole and a south pole in half between the poles, which of the following will result?
a: One north magnet and one south magnet
Two smaller magnets, each with a north and south pole
e: Snap a magnet in half and each piece instantly grows its own north and south pole, creating two new little magnets!

q: A 2-pound ball traveling to the right collides elastically [ee-LASS-tik-lee] with a stationary 1-pound ball. Which of the following is most likely to occur as a result of the collision?
a: The 2-pound ball will travel to the left while the 1-pound ball will travel to the right
The 1-pound ball and the 2-pound ball will move to the right at the same speed
The 1-pound ball and the 2-pound ball will move to the right at different speeds
The 1-pound ball will move to the right while the 2-pound ball remains stationary
e: The heavier ball shoves the little one forward fast while rolling right behind it at its own slower speed.

q: Which of the following BEST describes the air circulation pattern above the Bermuda or Azores high in the northern hemisphere in August:
a: air spiraling into the center in a clockwise direction
air spiraling out from the center in a clockwise direction
air spiraling into the center in a counter-clockwise direction
air spiraling out from the center in a counter-clockwise direction
e: High-pressure systems push air outward from their center, spinning clockwise like a giant, swirling pinwheel.

q: Which of the following elements was NOT produced in the Big Bang?
e: The young universe only cooked up tiny lightweight atoms, leaving heavier carbon to bake inside giant stars much later.

q: Which of the following is closest to the speed of light in kilometers per second?
e: Light is the universe's fastest traveler, zooming across space at nearly 300,000 kilometers in just one single second.

q: Which of the following areas of the United States has the most potential for geothermal energy?
e: The Northwest sits right over bubbly underground volcanic heat, making it the perfect steamy kitchen for geothermal power.

q: Researchers supported by the Department of Energy are developing quantum dots that emit visible light. In order to do this, they are irradiated with what type of light?
e: Tiny dots drink up energetic ultraviolet light and happily transform that invisible energy into bright, colorful glows.

q: Cadmium and boron are used for control rods in a nuclear power plant because they do which of the following?
e: These clever control rods act like thirsty sponges, soaking up wandering neutrons to keep the reactor calm and safe.

q: What layer of the Sun's atmosphere is hidden during totality?
e: The Moon slides right in front of the blindingly bright photosphere, finally letting the Sun's faint outer crown shine.

q: Which of the following is NOT a carbonate?
e: Labradorite is a glittery silicate mineral made of silica, not a carbonate built from carbon and oxygen buddies.

q: Which of the following is true about constellations?
a: They are made up of stars that not only appear close together but that are actually physically close together in space
They are all visible throughout the year from all points on Earth's surface
They may serve as reference points in the night sky
The locations of the stars in the constellations have changed significantly since the times of ancient Greeks
e: Sky gazers use these twinkling starry patterns like friendly cosmic signposts to help find their way across the dark night sky.

q: Which of the following is a unit of pressure?
e: Whenever air or water squeezes down on something, scientists use the pascal to measure that gentle little squish.

q: What is the shape of the surface of the secondary mirror in a Newtonian telescope?
e: This little mirror is completely flat, catching starlight and bouncing it sideways into your eye without bending the picture at all.

q: Force is equivalent to mass times the acceleration of an object. How could you guarantee a decrease in the acceleration of an object?
a: Increase the mass and decrease the force
Increase the force and decrease the mass
e: Pile heavy rocks onto a wagon and give it only a tiny, gentle push, and it will barely speed up at all.

q: Which of the following is TRUE of the apparent path of the Sun across the sky in the United States in June?
a: The Sun rises North of East and sets North of West
The Sun rises North of East and sets South of West
The Sun rises South of East and sets North of West
The Sun rises South of East and sets South of West
e: In joyful June, our Sun wakes up north of east and tucks itself in north of west to give us extra daylight!

q: Lunar terrae are another name for what surface feature?
e: Lunar terrae are the bright, rocky highlands that stand tall like glowing white mountains across the moon.

q: A star with a declination of 23.5 degrees and a right ascension of 6 hours will be eclipsed by the Sun on what day of the year?
e: On the sunny summer solstice, the Sun climbs to its highest spot in the sky, perfectly hiding that starry neighbor!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about hydropower?
a: The first hydropower plant was built at Niagara Falls in 1879
The U.S. is the largest producer of hydropower
The amount of electricity generated depends on how far the water drops and how much water moves through the system
It provides about one fifth of the world's electricity
e: Even though America loves rushing water, China actually splashes ahead as the world's biggest maker of hydropower.

q: Which of the following is the emission source for microwaves in a typical microwave oven:
a: cadmium disk bombarded with a soft x-ray source
e: A clever little tube called a magnetron whirls with energy, sending out invisible waves that dance your food warm.

q: To maintain beaches that are rapidly losing sand to erosional processes, barriers are built at right angles to the beach to trap sand that is moving parallel to shore. What are these barriers called?
e: Low walls called groins reach out into the ocean like sturdy fences, catching wandering sand before the waves can carry it away.

q: Government agencies and utilities offer various incentives to encourage people to improve the energy efficiency of buildings and vehicles. Which of the following is NOT a typical incentive?
e: While programs happily offer tax breaks or cash back, they rarely send workers to do the actual hardware installation for you.

q: Which of the following types of clouds would be most predictive of heavy rain?
e: Towering cumulonimbus clouds puff up like giant, shadowy castles, holding tons of heavy rain ready to pour down.

q: Which of the following best explains why the moon appears red during a total lunar eclipse?
a: Scattering by dust in lunar orbit
e: Earth's atmosphere bends red sunset light around our planet through refraction, bathing the eclipsed Moon in a warm, cozy glow.

q: A particular gem has no refraction at angles above 40.7, there is only total internal reflection. Therefore, 40.7 corresponds to which of the following for this gem?
e: That special tipping point is called the critical angle, where escaping light gives up and bounces totally inward instead.

q: If the radius of a wheel is 6 centimeters and the radius of the axle is 2 centimeters, what is the mechanical advantage?
e: Dividing the big wheel's six-centimeter radius by the axle's two gives you three, giving your turning effort triple the muscle!

q: Soundtracks of space movies frequently have sounds of ships exploding or whizzing through space. Why is this an inaccurate depiction of space?
a: Sound waves are distorted in space so everything would sound like it was under water
Sound cannot travel through a vacuum
Everything would have a very high pitch in space
Space vibrations would muffle the explosions
e: Space is an empty vacuum with no air molecules to bump together, leaving rocket zooms completely, beautifully silent.

q: You graph a series of equipotentials between two point charges of equal but opposite charge. Which of the following would NOT be true?
a: The equipotentials cross all lines of force at right angles
If you graphed all possible equipotentials, there would be no straight lines
If you graphed all possible equipotentials, the potentials would be mirrored across an axis perpendicular to the line that runs through the two charges
The voltage is the same at any point along one of the equipotential lines
e: Right down the middle between the two charges, there actually is a perfectly straight line where the voltages balance out!

q: Which of the following types of asteroids is most abundant in our solar system?
e: Dark, carbon-filled C-type asteroids are the most common rocky travelers out there, outnumbering all other space pebbles in our solar neighborhood.

q: A geomagnetic storm adds heat to a part of Earth's atmosphere called the thermosphere. As the atmosphere rises, the density in low Earth orbit increases. Which of the following might this subsequently increase on a satellite?
e: When the cozy atmosphere puffs up higher into space, satellites bump into more air particles, creating extra drag that slows them down.

q: Sound can travel through a vacuum.
e: That is false because sound needs friendly air particles to bump together, and an empty vacuum has none.

q: Which of the following is true about the Moon?
a: It crosses our sky along the same path every night
It always rises in the west
It changes size in our sky as it passes from horizon to zenith to the other horizon
It gives off no light of its own
e: The moon cannot make its own glow; it simply borrows warm sunlight and bounces it back to us!

q: Which of the following is closest to the frequency corresponding to a radio wave with a wavelength of 30 centimeters?
e: When light waves zip along, a thirty-centimeter radio wave wiggles up and down one billion times every second, making it one gigahertz!

q: Sarah launches a projectile over flat ground at 10 meters per second at an angle of 15 degrees. If Jake wants to launch a projectile the same horizontal distance, which of the following launch parameters would be appropriate?
e: Launching at seventy-five degrees uses the matching twin angle to fifteen, sending the ball on a sky-high arch that lands in the exact same spot.

q: Which of the following materials has a Moh's hardness between 3 and 4?
e: A copper penny is tougher than your fingernail, but softer than an iron nail, putting its hardness right between three and four.

q: When a car turns a corner on dry pavement, the wheels do not slide sideways and the car completes the turn due to what interaction between the tires and the pavement?
e: Sticky friction grabs hold of the road, keeping tires from sliding sideways so the car hugs the turn safely.

q: Assume the acceleration due to gravity is 10 meters per second squared, and you are holding a 5 newton weight hanging from a relatively weightless string. You pull up on the string, causing both the string and mass to accelerate upwards at a rate of 4 meters per second squared. How many newtons of tension exist in the string during this motion?
e: Pulling the weight upward takes extra muscle, adding two newtons of acceleration to its five-newton weight for seven newtons total.

q: An object of weight 2.5 pounds is dropped from a height such that by the time it hits the ground it is moving at a speed of 8 feet per second. From what height, in feet, was the object dropped?
e: Gravity speeds falling things up fast, so a tiny one-foot drop is all it takes to reach eight feet per second!

q: When designing a solar panel field in the northern hemisphere, in what cardinal direction should the panels tilt to collect the greatest solar energy collection?
e: Because the sun arcs across the southern sky up north, solar panels tilt south to catch every golden ray.

q: Where is the water along a stream's meander expected to move most quickly?
e: Like a race car swinging wide around a bend, water rushes fastest along the outside bank to make the turn.

q: Suppose a basketball is thrown upward by a student standing on Earth, with a velocity of 10 meters per second. Which of the following must also be TRUE at this instant?
a: Earth recoils at 10 meters per second downward
Earth recoils at 10 meters per second upward
Earth recoils at an imperceptibly slow speed downward
Earth recoils at an imperceptibly slow speed upward
e: Every upward push pushes back down, but because giant Earth is so heavy, its tiny downward nudge is impossible to feel.

q: Which of the following best describes the way an air mass would flow?
a: From an area of high to an area of low pressure
From an area of low to an area of high pressure
Perpendicular to a line drawn between a maximum and minimum pressure
e: Air loves to share space, so it naturally breezes away from crowded high-pressure spots toward roomier low-pressure areas.

q: Compressive forces that result in brittle deformation yield what formation?
e: When rocks get squeezed until they snap, one block climbs upward over the other, creating a reverse fault.

q: Two ores of iron are hematite and magnetite. They can be identified on the basis of the streak test. What color is the hematite streak and what color is the magnetite streak, respectively?
e: When scratched like chalk, rusty hematite leaves a reddish orange scribble, while magnetic magnetite draws in bold black.

q: What is the largest known natural satellite in the solar system?
e: Ganymede is the undisputed champion of moons, so gigantic it is even bigger than the planet Mercury!

q: Which of the following groups contains the most stars on a Hertzsprung-Russell diagram?
e: Cozy little red dwarfs might be dim, but they vastly outnumber all their flashier stellar cousins in our galaxy.

q: Thermodynamics tells us that we cannot reduce entropy in a closed system; it will always increase. Of what does entropy serve as a measure?
e: Entropy is just nature's scorekeeper for messiness, measuring the wild disorder of busy particles that never clean up their rooms.

q: Which of the following margins is considered active?
e: The northeastern Eurasian edge actively collides with tectonic plates, shaking with volcanoes and earthquakes along a restless active margin.

q: Which of the following regions of the electromagnetic spectrum has a longer wavelength than visible light?
e: Microwaves stretch out into much longer ripples than visible light waves, carrying cozy heat across wider spaces.

q: The potential energy stored in a spring is proportional to which of the following?
a: The square of the spring constant
The square root of the spring's mass
The spring's height from Earth's surface
The square of the spring's stretch from equilibrium
e: Stretchy springs store energy that jumps up fast, multiplying by the square of how far you pull them!

q: The circumstellar habitable zone, or "Goldilocks Zone", refers to the range of distances from a star within which what substance can exist on an orbiting planet's surface?
e: This sweet spot is neither too hot nor too cold, letting liquid water flow happily without freezing or boiling away.

q: The jet stream separates major air masses over the central continental U.S. The high pressure air mass to the north of the jet stream has which of the following characteristics in winter?
e: Born over frozen northern lands, this winter air is chilly and holds very little moisture, keeping it cold and dry.

q: Plasmas are typically described as glowing substances that are which of the following?
e: Packed with zippy free electrons, glowing plasma lets electric currents dance right through it, making this fiery stuff super conductive!

q: Which of the following numbers represents apatite on Moh's scale of hardness?
e: On a scratch test from softest to hardest, friendly apatite scores right in the middle at number five.

q: Which of the following optical devices produces a real image:
e: A convex lens curves outward to focus wandering light beams together, creating a real picture you can project on a wall!

q: Argentite is an ore of what element?
e: Deep underground, the dark, lumpy rock called argentite hides shiny silver waiting to burst out and sparkle!

q: A cubic meter is a measure of which of the following?
e: Imagine a giant block: a cubic meter measures volume, which is all the roomy space that fits inside.

q: Which of the following situations requires the most power?
a: Lifting a 60 newton weight 50 meters in 3 minutes
Lifting a 60 newton weight 70 meters in 5 minutes
Lifting a 70 newton weight 50 meters in 3 minutes
Lifting a 70 newton weight 70 meters in 5 minutes
e: Power is all about how fast you work, and hoisting that heavy load in just three minutes takes the biggest burst.

q: The MOST catastrophic mass extinction event in Earth's history occurred about how many million years ago:
e: Earth faced its greatest extinction 250 million years ago, sweeping away almost all life long before dinosaurs appeared.

q: Which of the following is not a potential environmental concern related to concentrating solar plants?
e: Solar plants use giant sunny mirrors instead of spinning wind turbines, so birds never have to dodge whirring blades there.

q: Which of the following regions of the EM spectrum is most energetic?
e: Ultraviolet waves vibrate with tons of pep, carrying far more energy than lazy radio waves or gentle visible light.

q: Which of the following is a simple device that can be used to show that the Earth rotates on its axis:
e: A swinging Foucault pendulum seems to turn because our big, round Earth is quietly spinning underneath it.

q: Which of the following celestial objects has the closest chemical makeup to the planet Jupiter:
e: Jupiter and the Sun are cosmic twins, both whipped up from giant swirling clouds of hydrogen and helium gas.

q: Which of the following scientists did NOT study electricity and its properties?
e: While other thinkers chased electric sparks, John Dalton was busy dreaming up tiny building blocks called atoms.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the 10 major cloud types:
e: You can watch the sky all day and never spot a cirronimbus, because that made-up cloud doesn't exist!

q: Lawrence Berkeley National Lab scientists are studying the ability of a pill, originally designed to treat radiation poisoning, to remove MRI contrast dyes from the body. Which of the following lanthanide [LAN-tha-nide] elements used in these dyes are they hoping to remove?
e: Doctors use a heavy metal named gadolinium to brighten hospital scans, and this helpful pill sweeps it away.

q: What type of nebula consists primarily of hot, ionized gas that radiates light?
e: An emission nebula is like a giant cosmic neon sign, glowing with its own colorful light as hot gas gets excited.

q: At the surface of the Earth, the acceleration due to gravity is g. At an elevation of twice the Earth's radius, which of the following best represents the acceleration due to gravity?
e: Being two planet heights up puts you three steps from Earth's center, so gravity's pull gets divided by three squared, leaving just g/9.

q: Which of the following characteristics is NOT related to sound?
e: Sound is just wiggly energy dancing through the air, not physical stuff you can weigh with mass.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about modern evaporative coolers?
a: They cool the air through the evaporation of water
They produce an odor of algae
They are well suited for climates where the air is hot and the humidity is low
They provide little thermal comfort in highly humid climates
e: Modern coolers simply chill parched air using clean water pads, so they do not make any smelly algae odors.

q: What class of mollusks [MOL-uhsks] includes modern day clams?
e: Clams keep their soft little bodies safe inside two matching shell doors, which makes them proud bivalves!

q: As seen from Earth, which of the following stellar objects has the most similar angular diameter to the Sun?
e: By a happy cosmic coincidence, the Moon looks like a perfect twin in size to our giant Sun when viewed from Earth.

q: The ratio of the amount of water vapor in the air to the amount required to saturate the air is:
e: Relative humidity tells us how full the thirsty air is compared to the absolute most water it could hold.

q: At what specific angle of incidence should the irradiance hit a solar panel in order to produce maximum power?
e: Sunlight works best when it dives straight down at zero degrees, looking right into the panel's face for the biggest, brightest high-five!

q: Which of the following types of friction are you experiencing as you push a book across a table?
e: Once your book goes sliding across the desk, kinetic friction is the busy, rubbing force that tickles its belly to slow it down.

q: Randy was precise in his lab experiment but he was not accurate. Which of the following best describes his measurements:
a: his data was close to the true value but not reproducible
his data was close to the true value and reproducible
his data was not close to the true value but reproducible
his data was not close to the true value and reproducible
e: Randy hit the exact same wrong spot over and over, making his data nicely reproducible, but far from the true target.

q: By our current estimations, the Earth is approximately how many billions of years old:
e: Our lovely Earth has been spinning through space for 4.6 billion years, collecting rocks and stories along the way!

q: The Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) satellite was launched in 1997 with the primary mission of measuring rainfall from space using passive microwave and active radar sensors. Which of the following is NOT a benefit of TRMM?
a: Increased understanding of the water cycle
Increased understanding of the heat release associated with rainfall
Better likelihood of accurate climate models
e: This storm-watching satellite focused on tropical rain clouds down below, not the wispy airplane exhaust trails known as contrails.

q: The temperature outside is 85 F and the air is holding a maximum amount of moisture. If the temperature drops rapidly to 65F, which of the following will MOST likely happen:
a: the relative humidity is lowered by about 25%
e: When chilly air gets too full of water to carry it all, it has to let go as rain!

q: On a rolling bicycle wheel, which of the following parts of the wheel has the highest instantaneous speed relative to the ground?
a: The forward-most edge of the wheel
e: As a wheel rolls, its top zooms forward twice as fast as the bike itself, while the bottom briefly hugs the ground!

q: A light-year is a unit for measuring what?
e: Even with year in its name, a light-year actually measures the giant distance a beam of light travels in twelve months.

q: What type of unconformity is created when shale is deposited on top of an eroded sandstone layer?
e: Since both rocks are flat sedimentary layers sharing an eroded gap between them, geologists call this missing chapter a disconformity.

q: Which of the following is the BEST description of the thermodynamic term entropy:
a: a measure of the disorder of a system
the amount of heat in a system
heat moving from a warm system and generating work
e: Think of entropy as nature's messy bedroom, measuring how wild, scrambled, and disordered everything has become.

q: In watts, how much power is consumed by a circuit that has a resistance of 10 ohms at a current of 3 amperes?
e: When three amps square up to nine and push through ten ohms, they create ninety watts of crackling electrical power!

q: The penultimate fate of most low mass stars is which of the following?
e: After puffing away its outer blanket, a small star shrinks into a cozy, glowing white dwarf that slowly cools down.

q: Who was the first scientist to be awarded two Nobel Prizes for science and did extensive research on radioactivity?
e: Brilliant Marie Curie unlocked the glowing mysteries of radioactivity, winning two shiny Nobel Prizes for her ground-breaking discoveries.

q: Which of the following will save the most energy per load of laundry using an electric washing machine?
a: Using the cold water setting on the washer
e: Heating bathwater takes an enormous amount of electricity, so washing clothes in cold water saves the biggest chunk of energy.

q: Field lines can be difficult to represent in a drawing because they are actually three-dimensional. Which of the following is a common mistake you might make when drawing field lines?
a: Starting on a negative charge and ending on a positive surface
Placing lines close together for stronger fields
Drawing the lines going out to infinity for an isolated charged body
Drawing shorter lines when further from the source charge
e: Electric field lines always blossom outward from positive charges toward negative ones, so starting them backwards on negative charges is a mistake.

q: Given a parcel of air that is saturated with water, which of the following statements is NOT correct?
a: Its dew point is equal to the current temperature
If you raised the temperature, its relative humidity would decrease
If you lowered the temperature, its relative humidity would decrease
e: Chilly air holds less moisture, so cooling saturated air would never decrease humidity; it just squeezes out rain!

q: Which of the following occurs as a bottle of milk falls from the edge of a table until just before it strikes a floor:
a: all the bottle's potential energy is lost to heat and friction
the potential energy of the bottle decreases
the potential energy of the bottle increases
the total potential energy of the bottle remains the same
e: As the bottle tumbles toward the floor, its height drops, trading its stored potential energy for rushing falling speed!

q: X-ray diffraction is a technique typically used to study the structure of what phase of matter?
e: X-rays love bouncing off solids because their neat, orderly rows of frozen atoms stand still for a picture!

q: A 10 kilogram block is suspended from a thick cord of negligible mass attached to the ceiling. Given that g is 10 meters per second squared, What is the force on the ceiling by the cord, in newtons?
e: Gravity pulls that ten-kilogram block with ten meters per second squared, tugging the ceiling with a force of one hundred newtons.

q: Which of the following is NOT a method by which heat travels?
e: Heat loves to travel by touching, floating, or glowing, but a convention is just a busy meeting for people!

q: Why is it best to hit a baseball on the sweet spot of a bat?
a: There is less friction on the sweet spot
The sweet spot is the widest part of the bat so it easier to hit the ball
When the ball hits the sweet spot more force is imparted to it
Less energy is lost to bat vibrations when the ball hits the sweet spot
e: Hitting the sweet spot stops the bat from buzzing in your hands, sending all that energy into the ball instead of vibrations!

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are developing new polymerizable [paw-lim-ur-EYE-zah-bul] linkages to produce plastics that can be recycled. What type of linkage is present in proteins?
e: Inside your cells, proteins link their building blocks together using tough amide bonds, making them natural polyamides hugging like a cozy chain.

q: Argonne National Lab researchers are developing techniques to better annotate genomes [JEE-nomes] of organisms. In this case, to what does annotation refer?
a: Adding information about the functions of different sequences
Adding information about similar genes in other organisms
Converting the genome to amino acid code
Converting the genome to RNA code
e: Annotating is like sticking cheerful little notes on DNA, explaining the special job each secret code does for the body.

q: Electricity used to power a home in the United States is sold by what unit?
e: Power companies measure your home's sparky adventures in kilowatt hours, tracking how much electricity you use over time.

q: Which of the following methods of electricity generation use the kinetic energy of steam to turn a turbine?
e: Deep inside a nuclear plant, splitting atoms heats water into powerful steam that spins giant wheels to make electricity.

q: Specific gravity is a measure of what?
e: Specific gravity compares an object's density to water, showing how tightly its tiny building blocks are packed together.

q: A ball is thrown into the air with a velocity of 3 meters per second to the east and 4 meters per second away from the Earth. At the top of its arc, what is the velocity of the ball in meters per second?
e: At the tippy-top, the ball pauses its climb for a tiny second, leaving only its three-meter-per-second eastward drift.

q: Non-storm wave action can move fine sand particles in depths of up to how many meters?
e: Even gentle everyday waves reach their watery fingers down twenty meters deep to tickle and slide fine sand across the seabed.

q: Transformers are based on the principle of electromagnetic induction, stated by which of the following laws?
e: Faraday discovered how magnetic fields gently coax electric currents into flowing, the clever trick that makes transformers work.

q: Which of the following is not a star in the summer triangle?
e: Vega, Deneb, and Altair form the starry triangle, while Draco is actually a whole winding dragon constellation!

q: Which of the following MUST change if constructive interference occurs between two light waves:
e: When two light waves team up constructively, their peaks stack together to create a taller wave, boosting its amplitude.

q: Which of the following cosmic phenomena gave rise to most of the iron found on Earth?
e: Giant dying stars burst in spectacular supernovae, blasting showers of freshly made iron out across the universe!

q: The Moon is full on September 7, 2006. On which of the following days that month will a last quarter Moon occur:
e: The moon loves a steady rhythm, taking about one week to shrink from full to a last quarter, landing right on the 14th.

q: The Archimedes [ark-ih-MEE-deez] Principle is most related to which of the following concepts?
e: Archimedes solved the secret of buoyancy, showing how water happily pushes upward to keep your favorite rubber duck afloat.

q: Bok globules are visible in the Orion Nebula. What does this imply is occuring in the star?
e: These dusty cosmic clouds are like cozy nurseries, quietly squishing together to form bright, brand-new baby stars.

q: Which north or south latitude experiences the greatest variation in sun exposure over the course of the year?
e: Right at ninety degrees, the poles swing between months of endless summer sunshine and pitch-black, frozen winter nights!

q: Ultrasound is acoustic energy in the form of waves with a frequency above the human hearing range. Which of the following statements does NOT reflect a use of ultrasonic energy?
a: To observe the condition of a fetus before birth
To detect motion in the immediate vicinity of a vehicle
To make iPod sound quality better
e: Ultrasound is way too high-pitched for human ears, so it could never help an iPod play music better!

q: Which of the following is the approximate age of the Universe in years?
e: Our universe had a dazzling birthday party fourteen billion years ago, giving stars and galaxies plenty of time to grow!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about magnets?
a: As two magnets move apart, the repelling force increases
If you break a magnet you have two new magnets
Compasses are affected by magnetic fields
e: When magnets drift apart, their push gets sleepy and weaker, so their repelling force definitely does not increase.

q: A man stands in front of a concave mirror with a focal length of 200 centimeters and sees an upright image of his face at twice its actual size. How far, in centimeters, is he from the mirror?
e: Standing 100 centimeters away puts you halfway to the mirror's focal point, ballooning your happy face to twice its normal size!

q: A compact car and a large SUV are both driving down the freeway at 60 miles per hour. They both must stop to avoid an obstacle 0.3 miles in front of them. What does the SUV require more of relative to the car in order to stop in time to avoid hitting the obstacle?
e: That big, heavy SUV carries way more heft, so the brakes need a lot more stopping force to tame its roll.

q: Which of the following types of stars is expected to last for the longest time in its current stage of stellar evolution?
e: Tiny red dwarf stars sip their fuel so gently that they can keep glowing for trillions of peaceful years.

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are studying piezoelectricity, which is a phenomenon typically demonstrated by what type of material?
e: Certain special ceramics love being squished, happily turning a firm squeeze into a tiny burst of electric power.

q: Aerobraking is a method that can be used to slow a spacecraft down by having it drag through a planet's atmosphere. Why couldn't NASA use this method for the MESSENGER spacecraft?
a: Mercury is too close to the Sun
Mercury's atmosphere has too much corrosive methane in it
Mercury has little to no atmosphere
Mercury has insufficient gravity to permit it
e: You cannot use air brakes if there is no air! Mercury is so bare that the spaceship had nothing to brush against.

q: If the Earth were to suddenly gain mass, it would need to do which of the following in order to maintain its current distance from the Sun?
a: Increase the eccentricity of its orbit
e: Earth needs to do nothing at all! Its cosmic orbit only cares about the Sun's giant pull, not our planet's extra winter weight.

q: How is energy transported in the layer of the Sun just below the photosphere?
e: Deep inside, hot gas bubbles upward like a giant pot of soup, using convection to carry warmth toward the surface.

q: Which of the following types of quantities appears in a free-body diagram?
e: These clever little sketches draw arrows to show every single push and pull, or force, nudging an object around.

q: Which of the following most directly contributes to the actual mechanical advantage always being less than the ideal mechanical advantage:
a: the basic design of any machine
the input distance always being less than the output distance
e: Friction is the sneaky party crasher that rubs moving parts together, stealing away a bit of a machine's push.

q: Which of the following explains why the same side of the Moon always faces the Earth?
a: The Moon is tidally locked to the Earth
The Moon rotates around its axis once every 12 hours
The Moon rotates around its axis once every 24 hours
The Moon is gravitationally uncoupled from the Earth
e: Earth's gentle gravity slowed the Moon's spin until it matched its orbit, locking its smiling face toward us forever.

q: When the nickel-iron crystals in iron meteorites cool very slowly it often causes them to:
a: be exceedingly brittle with a flake-like appearance
have a soft outer layer and a dense hard inner core
e: Given millions of quiet, chilly years in deep space, those metal atoms had plenty of time to grow into large crystals.

q: Doing a given amount of work at different rates always involves a different amount of:
e: Power measures how fast you work, so finishing a big chore in a zippy flash takes much more power than creeping along.

q: A photon of red light and a photon of green light are traveling in a vacuum. Which of the following is identical for the two photons?
e: In empty space, all light beams race side by side at the exact same speed, no matter their flashy rainbow colors.

q: Which of the following is a widespread and long-lived, violent convectively- induced straight-line windstorm that is associated with a fast-moving band of severe thunderstorms usually taking the form of a bow echo?
e: A derecho is a ferocious storm engine that charges across the map in a straight line, howling for hundreds of miles!

q: Why is the angle of incidence of sunlight important for solar panels?
a: It helps the panel remain cooler, but decreases the power output
It helps the panel remain hotter, and increases the power output
The closer the angle is to normal, the more power produced by the panel
The further the angle is from normal, the more power produced by the panel

q: Which of the following laws most directly limits the ability of a simple machine to an efficiency of 100% or lower:
a: the law of conservation of energy
e: The law of conservation of energy says you cannot create new energy from nowhere, so no machine can ever give over 100%.

q: In years, which of the following is closest to the age of Earth?
e: Our cozy home planet has been spinning around the Sun for about 4.5 billion years, making it an extraordinarily wise old rock!

q: With regard to water heaters, which of the following options presents energy savings of up to 30%?
a: Replacing the tank water heater by an on-demand water heater
Insulating pipe lines up to 6ft away from the heater
Insulating the surroundings of the water heater
e: An on-demand heater warms water only when you turn the faucet, saving energy instead of babysitting a giant hot tank all day.

q: Which of the following prevailing wind belts is most affected by El Nio?
e: El Nino disrupts the ocean's rhythm by weakening the trusty trade winds that normally blow across warm tropical waters.

q: Greenhouse gases heat the atmosphere by allowing sunlight to pass through while trapping heat. Which of the following planets does NOT have an atmosphere that contains greenhouse gases?
e: Mercury has practically no atmosphere at all, so it lacks any cozy greenhouse blanket to trap daytime heat.

q: Just before a lightning strike, how is charge distributed in a rain cloud?
a: Negative at the base and top, positive in the center
Positive at the base and top, negative in the center
Negative at the base, positive at the top
Positive at the base, negative at the top
