q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are studying matter whose properties can be described using the Dirac [dih-RAHK] equation. In that sense, this matter is similar to which of the following elementary particles?
e: The Dirac equation describes true matter particles that spin, making the tiny up quark a perfect match.

q: For an ideal simple pendulum [PEN-juh-luhm], where is the position of maximum speed of the pendulum bob located?
a: At the points corresponding to maximum displacement
At a point corresponding to a displacement of twice the amplitude
At the points corresponding a displacement of one third of the amplitude
e: As the pendulum swoops down like a swing, it zooms fastest right through the bottom at its equilibrium point.

q: Soils that have an abundance of which of the following generally have the greatest rate of permeability?
e: Sand grains are chunky and leave wide-open spaces between them, letting water zip through much faster than tight clay or silt.

q: Scientists at SLAC National Accelerator Lab are studying stishovite [STISH-oh-vyte]. What process is thought to produce stishovite on the surface of Earth?
e: When a speedy meteorite crashes into Earth, its monstrous smash squeezes plain old quartz so hard that it turns into stishovite.

q: How old is the universe?
e: Our grand universe has been sparkling, expanding, and telling stories for an astonishing 13.8 billion years.

q: Utilities distribute electrical power at high voltage from generating plants to industrial and residential customers through a network of wires. Which of the following is the term for these wires?
e: Tall transmission lines act like giant highway lanes, zooming energetic electricity across miles right into our cozy neighborhoods.

q: Kirchhoff's voltage law states that which of the following is true?
a: The sum of voltages in a closed path is equal to zero
The power produced by sources must be equal to the power used by appliances
The sum of currents in a node is equal to zero
The voltage in a resistor is equal to the current times the value of the circuit's resistance
e: If electricity goes on a complete loop around a circuit, every bit of push it gains equals what it loses, balancing out to zero.

q: What is the primary element in today's commercially available solar cells?
e: Silicon is the busy worker inside solar panels, soaking up bright sunshine like a sponge and turning it into clean electricity!

q: Which of the following occurs for you to witness a partial solar eclipse?
a: The umbra passes over you, but the penumbra does not
Both the penumbra and umbra pass over you
The penumbra passes over you, but the umbra does not
Neither the penumbra nor the umbra pass over you

q: A photon of what wavelength carries the most energy?
e: Tiny ultraviolet light waves squeeze together so tightly that their little packets carry more punch and energy than visible colors do!

q: Your teacher asks you to draw a free body diagram of a box being moved by a rope and pulley system. Which of the following should be included?
a: All forces acting on the box
All forces exerted by the box on itself
All forces exerted by the box on other objects
Both forces for all action-reaction pairs
e: Picture the box as the star of the show; you only draw the pushes and pulls acting directly on it.

q: During which of the following periods were coals generally lignite deposits still containing significant volatile material?
e: Because Tertiary coals are the youngsters of the coal family, they haven't been cooked long enough to lose their smoky, trapped gases.

q: The best evidence for the model of Earth's interior comes from the study of:

q: The ability of a water strider to float and travel on the water surface is an example of what property?

q: Scientists at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory are using new imaging modalities [moh-DAHL-ih-teez] to study DNA damage. In particular, they are studying damage to DNA caused by what region of the EM spectrum that is divided into A, B, and C ranges?

q: Compared to cooler air, warm air can hold:

Less water vapor, depending upon the humidity

q: Which of the following has the highest energy photons?

q: A dry steam geothermal power plant produces electricity in which of the following ways?

Using heat to boil a working fluid that is vaporized through a heat exchanger and drives a generator
Using water at high temperatures to convert ground water into steam
Using steam from underground wells to rotate a turbine, activating an electricity generator
e: Earth acts like a giant teapot, shooting underground steam straight into spinny turbines that power an electrical generator!

q: Wind turbines use which of the following principles of fluid mechanics when producing energy?
e: As breezy air squeezes past giant blades, the law of continuity makes it speed up and push, just like water rushing through a garden hose!

q: Which of the following items, commonly found in most American households, represents significant energy input if made from its common ore; however, recycling this item saves enough energy to run a TV for 3 hours.

q: Which of the following is not a contributor to increased power generation from a wind turbine?

q: Operational amplifiers can be used in combination with inductors and capacitors and their energy storage abilities to create:

q: Which of the following separation techniques utilizes a moving phase and a stationary phase to separate the components of a mixture?
e: Chromatography separates sneaky mixtures like a fun race, letting moving liquids carry parts forward while a stay-at-home paper slows others down!

q: Which of the following do ideal machines MOST directly assume:

q: The Moon orbits the Earth due to which of the following characteristics of the Earth?

Energy from the surrounding water is given off to the forming ice

the wavelength will shorten and frequency decreases
the wavelength will increase and frequency increases
the wavelength will increase and frequency decreases

e: Plants reach out their leaves like tiny solar catchers, soaking up golden light energy to cook sweet sugars for their fruit.

e: When the speedy objects crash and stick together, they stop completely. Stopping that one-kilogram object at twenty meters per second takes an impulse of twenty!

q: Which of the following is characteristic of all plankton?

q: What is the number one tip the Department of Energy has for homeowners to save money on energy bills?

Use a power strip for your electronic equipment
Use natural lighting rather than artificial
Install and set a programmable thermostat
e: A programmable thermostat acts like a smart little buddy, turning down the heat while you sleep so your house saves the most energy.

The speed of the solar wind has increased significantly
e: When the Sun wakes up for its active season, its fiery face breaks out with lots of dark, magnetic freckles called sunspots.

It has two reservoirs instead of one
Its generators rotate a series of magnets inside coils of wire to create an electric current

q: What was the heaviest element produced during the big bang nucleosynthesis?

q: What is the energy efficiency range of a typical photovoltaic solar panel in production?

e: When you spin three times faster, the circular force multiplies by nine because speed gets squared.

e: Gravitational energy loves mass! If you double an object's weight, its stored climbing energy happily doubles right along with it by two.

A higher coefficient of performance on the compressor

q: Polaris is the brightest star in the northern hemisphere night sky.

q: In the mid-nineteenth century, the English physicist James Joule created a device in which falling weights rotated paddles immersed in a barrel of water. Which of the following results did he observe?

The potential energy of the weights transferred entirely into elastic energy to drive the paddles

The water in the barrel cooled slightly

You shine a laser beam onto the surface of the black film and you notice the film is deflected away from the laser and hangs at a slight angle relative to the vertical. This observation shows that light has which of the following?
e: Even without any weight, light gives a tiny push when it hits, proving those traveling rays carry momentum.

q: If light is passed through two pin holes and the patterns allowed to overlap on a wall, the pattern produced by the intersection of waves is called:
e: When beams of light overlap and ripple into each other, they paint stripes called an interference pattern.

q: What type of fault is the San Andreas fault in California?
e: Giant slabs of Earth shuffle sideways past each other like dancers bumping shoulders, making this a strike-slip fault.

q: What astronomical term is used to describe the high-luminosity end of the observed main-sequence stars in a given cluster?
e: The turnoff point is where aging stars run out of fuel and peel away from the main-sequence pack.

q: Scientists at the Joint Genome Institute recently conducted epigenetic sequencing of fungi [fun-ji]. Which of the following is primarily measured in epigenetic analysis?
e: Epigenetics studies the tiny chemical tags, called methylation, that attach to DNA bases to switch genes on or off.

q: Radiometric dating of the oldest meteoroids of the solar system would produce ages closest to which of the following?
e: Space rocks are nearly as old as our solar system itself, making five billion years the closest match for these ancient cosmic travelers.

q: The principle asserting that processes operating in the present world can be used to interpret events of the past, i.e., "the present is the key to the past," is called which of the following?
e: Uniformitarianism means nature plays by the same rules today as long ago, letting the present unlock ancient secrets.

q: Amy is pulling a heavy cart. It is harder to start pulling the cart than to keep the cart in motion, because kinetic friction:
a: Is zero once the cart is moving
Is only present when the cart is first pulled
e: Once wheels start rolling, kinetic friction grips the ground less than stubborn resting friction, letting the cart glide along much easier.

q: Researchers at Los Alamos National Lab are using direct numerical simulations to study the interaction of shock waves with fluid flow. Which of the following equations or sets of equations is most relevant in modeling the motion of fluids like water?
e: The Euler equations give scientists the clever math recipe to track how swirling water and rushing fluids glide along.

q: While driving down the freeway, a bug splatters on your windshield. Which of the following is true?
a: The bug experiences more of an absolute change in momentum
The car experiences more of an absolute change in momentum
Both the car and the bug experience the same absolute change in momentum
Neither the car nor the bug experiences a change in momentum
e: Even though the poor bug goes splat, Newton's rules say the speeding car and tiny insect trade the exact same amount of momentum.

q: The Sun's tide-generating force is about:
e: The Sun is gigantic, but because it sits so far away, its tidal tug is only about half as strong as the closer Moon's.

q: Which of the following are the two parts of sunspots?
e: Every sunspot wears a dark, cozy center called an umbra, wrapped in a lighter, shaded blanket called the penumbra.

q: Marcellus shale occurs in the subsurface under several states. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
e: While this underground rock blanket stretches across nearby states, it stops short before ever tucking under Indiana.

q: A beam of light passes through a material A, with a refractive index of 1.5, to material B with a refractive index of 1. Which of the following is the critical angle of the light?
e: Light gets trapped at a magical tipping angle, found by taking the inverse sine of one over one point five, which equals two-thirds.

q: Which of the following best describes the composition of polycrystalline silicon solar panels?
a: A piece of semi-conducting material with a thin silicon film over the top
One continuous sheet of silicon with a backing of metal-conducting material
Lots of individual PV cells that have a backing of metal-conducting material
Strips of silicon form the PV cells that have a backing of metal-conducting material
e: These panels gather lots of little silicon cells over a metal base, teaming up together to catch golden sunshine.

q: Which of the following is a type of dune that forms at right angles to the wind when there is abundant sand, a lack of vegetation, and a constant wind direction?
e: Constant winds push across bare, sandy ground to sculpt barchan dunes right across the breeze, curving like giant crescent smiles.

q: Models are frequently employed in science. Which of the following is not true of scientific models?
a: They cannot be changed once formalized
They are patterned after items or events in the natural world
They offer a means of testing predictions
e: Science is a growing adventure, so when curious researchers find new clues, they happily update their models instead of freezing them forever.

q: Which of the following is made of microcrystalline quartz and is very hard and compact:
e: Packed tight with microscopic quartz crystals, chert is a rock so tough and sharp that ancient people shaped it into trusty arrowheads.

q: What type of telescope uses convex lenses to bend light?
e: Refracting telescopes work like giant reading glasses, using curved lenses to bend and focus starlight straight into your curious eyes.

q: What is the name for a strong ground-level wind system that emanates from a point source above and blows radially from the point of contact at ground level?
e: When a stormy cloud drops a heavy pocket of air, it crashes down and splashes outward in all directions as a fierce downburst.

q: Which of the following forms of winter precipitation is most likely to cause downed power lines and broken tree limbs:
e: Freezing rain glazes trees and wires in thick, heavy coats of shiny ice until the branches snap under all that extra weight!

q: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has a shorter wavelength than visible light waves?
e: Ultraviolet light ripples with shorter, tighter waves than visible colors can, packing invisible energy that gives us sunny tans.

q: Which of the following quantities has the same units as angular momentum per time?
e: Just like a shove changes straight motion, a twist called torque is what changes spinning angular momentum as time ticks by.

q: Which of the following is the main disadvantage of hydroelectric dams?
a: They increase the potential for flooding
They consume more energy than they produce
They add pollutant byproducts to the water
e: While giant dams make clean energy, flooding the land drowns habitats and blocks swimming fish, upsetting the river's living ecosystem.

q: Which of the following sets of two locations have the most similar latitudes?
a: New York City, New York and London, England
Death Valley, California and Boston, Massachusetts
e: Sunny Tampa and snowy Kathmandu sit on nearly the same line across our spinning globe, sharing matching latitudes like faraway neighborhood twins.

q: What is the approximate mass of the largest stars?
e: Space's grandest heavyweights are true monsters, packing the mighty heft of about one hundred suns all rolled into one giant star!

q: Which of the following areas of the United States accounts for approximately half of the total hydroelectric power generation in the United States?
e: With roaring rivers tumbling through rainy mountains, the Northwest captures all that rushing water to generate about half of our country's hydropower.

q: Which of the following describes when flooding is most likely to occur as the result of a slow moving, relatively long term, moderate rain event?
a: After it has been raining for about an hour
After it has been raining for a few hours
At the beginning of the rainstorm
e: The ground drinks slowly, so rainwater takes hours to creep into rivers and cause flooding only after the storm finishes.

q: Which of the following forces always causes a loss of energy in a mechanical system?
e: Friction is a sneaky little force that rubs surfaces together, stealing their moving energy and turning it into heat.

q: The property of water which permits an insect to "walk" on water is:
e: Water molecules hold hands tightly at the surface, creating an invisible, stretchy trampoline called surface tension that lets tiny bugs tiptoe across.

q: Which of the following phenomena describes a beam of light entering a glass of water and bending from its original path?
e: When a beam of light dives into water, it slows down and stumbles, bending its path in a little dance called refraction.

q: A red ball has a mass of 2 grams and a volume of 8 cubic centimeters. A yellow ball has a mass of 5 grams and a volume of 2 cubic centimeters. When both balls are placed into a bucket of water, which of the following is true?
a: The yellow ball floats and the red ball sinks
The red ball floats and the yellow ball sinks
Both the red and yellow ball float
Both the red and yellow ball sink
e: The airy red ball is lighter than water so it floats, while the packed yellow ball sinks right to the bottom!

q: Why is copper one of the most common materials used to make wires that carry electricity?
a: Because of its perfect insulating properties
Because it has both conducting and dielectric properties
Because it is a good conductor
e: Electricity loves zipping through copper because it is a wonderful conductor that lets electric energy slide right on through!

q: Most of Earth's deserts in the northern hemisphere are located near which of the following latitudes:
e: Dry air loves to tumble downward near latitude thirty, baking the land into sunny, sandy deserts.

q: Which of the following enables scientists to estimate the strength of the magnetic field associated with sunspots?
e: Strong magnetic fields cleverly split the sun's light, and this Zeeman effect lets scientists measure just how mighty sunspots really are.

q: Which of the following can occur with light but NOT sound?
e: Light waves can do a special dance called polarization by lining up their wiggles, but sound waves simply cannot.

q: In a vacuum, all photons have the same:
e: In the quiet empty of space, every single beam of light zooms in a perfect tie at top speed.

q: Which of the following is the process by which water vapor changes directly into rain:
e: When cozy floating vapor gets chilly, it snuggles together into heavy liquid raindrops through a magical change called condensation!

q: What is the densest layer of the Sun's atmosphere?
e: Down at the bottom of the sun's sky sits the photosphere, packed so tightly with glowing particles that it makes the densest layer.

q: Which of the following explains why white light entering a prism exits and projects a rainbow?
a: The prism's crystal lattice colors the white light, like stained glass
Different parts of the prism absorb different colors of light
The prism separates the white light into its component parts
The prism acts as a polarizing filter
e: White light is secretly packed with every rainbow color, and the prism gently separates them so each can take a bow!

q: Which of the following ores is NOT a sulfide?
e: Barite hugs oxygen along with sulfur, which makes it a sulfate rather than a true sulfide like its rock cousins.

q: Ultrasonic sound frequencies are typically considered to be:
e: Ultrasonic sounds vibrate way faster than our ears can catch, zooming above twenty kilohertz into the secret world of bats.

q: Electromagnetic radiation is carried by photons. The speed of photons through vacuum does which of the following?
a: Varies depending on the amount of energy they carry
e: Through the empty quiet of space, every single photon zips along at the exact same cosmic speed, never slowing down.

q: Which of the following is the Epoch name given to the last approximately 10,000 years of Earth's history:
e: Our cozy modern chapter of Earth's story is the Holocene, a warm ten thousand year epoch where humans built farms and cities.

q: Meteor showers are composed of:
a: dust and other debris from comets
e: Comets are messy travelers that shed trails of dusty crumbs, lighting up our sky whenever Earth swoops through their leftover litter!

q: Enthalpy is a measure of the energy that is not available for work during a thermodynamic process.
e: That is false because entropy tracks unavailable, messy energy, while enthalpy measures the total heat locked inside.

q: A 10 kilogram mass hangs from a string in an elevator that is accelerating upwards at 2.0 meters per second squared. What is the tension in the string in newtons?
e: The elevator floor pushes up while gravity pulls down, teaming up so the string feels a tight pull of 118 newtons.

q: In an average home, which of the following end uses would be most likely to use three-phase power?
e: Big, hungry clothes dryers need a gigantic gulp of electricity to spin and heat, making them perfect for mighty three-phase power.

q: Windows can be rated on the rate at which heat flows through them through which of the following measures?
e: The U-factor measures how easily sneaky heat slips through glass, showing whether your window keeps your cozy room warm.

q: Researchers at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory have developed a new electron gun that uses a superconducting chamber made from niobium [nye-OH-bee-um] metal. How did the scientists lower the electrical resistance of the niobium to nearly zero?
a: Subjected the niobium to intense pressures
Heated the niobium to 1000 degrees Celsius
e: Chilling niobium to a super-frosty four kelvins turns it into a frictionless ice rink where electricity can glide freely.

q: Which of the following is a force that will always decrease the efficiency of a mechanical system?
e: Friction is like a sneaky thief, rubbing parts together and stealing useful energy away as heat.

q: In a parallel circuit with constant voltage, if a branch was added, which of the following would happen to the total equivalent resistance and the total supplied current?
a: The resistance would increase and the current would decrease
The resistance would decrease and the current would increase
e: Opening a new path is like adding a highway lane; electricity meets less resistance, so more total current rushes happily through!

q: What term describes the height of an object in the sky?
e: Altitude tells stargazers exactly how high an object sits above the horizon in our vast night sky.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about Michael Faraday's experiment demonstrating electromagnetic induction, which featured a permanent magnet and a galvanometer connected to a coil of wire around a paper cylinder?
a: When a permanent magnet is left stationary inside the wire coil, no current is induced
A permanent magnet produces stronger current when it is moved quickly in and out of the wire coil
When the north end of the permanent magnet enters the coil, a current that travels in a clockwise direction is induced
When the north end of the permanent magnet enters the coil, a current that travels in a counterclockwise direction is induced
e: An incoming north magnet pushes current counterclockwise to resist it, so saying the electricity spins clockwise is simply untrue.

q: A crystal's habit that is plant-like in shape is called which of the following?
e: A dendritic crystal branches out like tiny frozen tree limbs or fern leaves painted across stone.

q: Which of the following is the SI unit of mass?
e: Scientists across the globe chose the trusty kilogram as their official measuring champion for how much stuff an object holds.

q: Which of the following scientific principles is most directly used in a stationary hand-held radar gun to determine the speed of a car?
e: The Doppler effect spots speeders because bouncing radar waves get squished or stretched as a car zooms past!

q: Why aren't birds electrified when standing on power lines?
a: Because there is no difference in potential energy when they stand on top of power lines
Because the kinetic energy remains the same
Because there is a differential in potential that allows the flow of energy through them
e: Electricity only flows when there is a difference to jump across. Because a bird's feet share the same energy level, the current safely skips them!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about incandescent lamps?
a: They have the least expensive initial purchase price
They typically can last over one million hours
e: Old-fashioned incandescent bulbs work hard, but their delicate glowing wires burn out way before reaching a million hours.

q: Lawrence Berkeley National Lab scientists have developed ReACT, a new amino acid labeling technique. This technique can be used to study which of the following biomolecules?
e: Amino acids are the tiny building blocks that snap together to make proteins, so tagging them reveals the whole structure!

q: A person applies for a patent on an engine that is 100% efficient. This application would be rejected because the engine would violate the:
e: The laws of thermodynamics rule our universe, insisting that every working machine must lose a little energy as heat.

q: Which of the following is CLOSEST to the estimate of how many million years ago the first bacteria appeared on Earth:
e: Way back, about 3,800 million years ago, tiny bacteria became Earth's very first living pioneers.

q: When ingested, which of the following provides the greatest number of calories per gram?
e: Gram for gram, fat packs the most fuel, storing giant bursts of energy for our adventures!

q: A particular material absorbs violet, blue, and green light. Which of the following colors will NOT be observed when light strikes the material?
e: If an object swallows up all the blue and green light, blue-green can never bounce back into your eyes!

q: A wave travels through air and hits the surface of water at an angle of 90. Which of the following will be true about the wave?
a: Its angle of incidence will increase
Its angle of incidence will decrease
Its angle of incidence will not change, and its speed will not change
Its angle of incidence will not change, and its speed may increase or decrease
e: Plunging straight into the water, the wave keeps its angle, but diving into a new home changes its speed.

q: Which of the following can be said about a single, unchanging mass M that is moving at a constant speed?
a: The object's kinetic energy is a constant
No outside forces act on the object
The object's potential energy is a constant
No internal forces act on the object
e: Because neither its mass nor speed changes, the object's kinetic energy stays happily constant the whole way.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the properties of forces?
a: Forces can cause a change in motion
Forces can cancel each other out
Forces in opposite directions always result in an unbalanced net force
e: In an even game of tug-of-war, equal forces pulling in opposite directions perfectly balance each other out.

q: Electrical current is best conducted through which of the following substances?
e: Copper has friendly, loose electrons that pass electric sparks along in a super-fast relay race, making it a wonderful conductor.

q: Light passes through a rectangular slit in a box and produces a small spot of light on a screen at the back of the box. What is located between the slit in the box and the screen?
e: A curvy convex lens acts like a friendly guide, bending scattered light rays inward until they meet as one bright, tidy spot.

q: Which of the following is NOT a component of the solar wind?
e: The solar wind is a gust of tiny charged particles, while light travels as photons, making photons completely different travelers.

q: Shortly after its formation, Earth's moon was:
a: Closer to Earth than it is now
Farther from Earth than it is now
The same distance from Earth as it is now
Oscillating between further from and closer to Earth
e: When our young moon was first born, it snuggled much closer to Earth before slowly drifting farther out into space.

q: Solar panels commonly possess a blocking diode. What is its function?
a: To prevent the panel from draining the energy storage system
To protect the panel from excessive voltage levels
To protect the panel from excessive current levels
To store energy to be used for the circuit later
e: Think of a diode as a tiny one-way door. It stops your battery from accidentally feeding its precious power back to sleepy nighttime panels!

q: A longitudinal mechanical wave causes particles of a material to move:
a: Back and forth in the same direction the wave is moving
Perpendicular to the direction the wave is moving
In a circular motion parallel to the direction the wave is moving
In a circular motion perpendicular to the direction the wave is moving
e: Like a playful spring, the particles bump forward and back along the very same path the wave travels!

q: In millions of years, how long ago are the lunar maria thought to have solidified?
e: Those dark lunar seas were once glowing lava that finally cooled and hardened into solid rock about 3,000 million years ago.

q: Rounding your answer to the nearest tenth, a difference of one in the apparent magnitudes of two stars means that the brighter star appears how many times as bright as the dimmer one?
e: On this starlight scale, climbing one brightness level means the happier, shinier star beams about 3.2 times as bright.

q: Which of the following components corresponds to the pitch of a sound wave:
e: Pitch tells you how high a whistle sounds, and that depends on frequency, which is just how quickly sound waves wiggle!

q: Middle C on a piano is 256 hertz. Given that the speed of sound in air is 330 meters per second, which of the following is closest to the wavelength of middle C in meters?
e: Dividing sound's speedy travel of 330 meters per second by its 256 musical wiggles leaves each wave stretching 1.3 meters wide.

q: Which of the following is a unit for sound intensity level?
e: Whether it is a tiny mouse squeak or a roaring rocket, decibels measure just how loud sound energy can be!

q: To what crystal system does halite belong?
e: Halite is salty rock whose tiny atoms love stacking together like square blocks to build perfect, shiny cubes.

q: Which of the following is closest to the temperature, in kelvins, at which hydrogen fusion will commence in a young star?
e: A baby star must squeeze its core until it hits a sizzling 10 million kelvins, hot enough to spark hydrogen into starlight!

q: Which of the following best demonstrates the mass continuity of fluid flow?
a: Water flows fastest through the narrowest piece of a long pipe
Water flows slower after having moved further from Earth's center
Pressure is lower in water moving at high speed
A small force can be used on a small tube to lift a large object sitting on a large tube
e: Water cannot just vanish, so when a pipe gets skinny, the crowded liquid must zoom faster to push everyone through.

q: Which of the following is true of a step-down transformer?
a: The number of turns in the primary coil is less than the number of turns in the secondary coil
The number of turns in the primary and secondary coils are the same
The number of turns in the primary coil is greater than the number of turns in the secondary coil
The action of a step-down transformer does not depend on the number of turns in the primary and secondary coils
e: To step down high voltage into a gentler flow, electricity enters through a coil with more wire loops than the exit coil.

q: Which of the following BEST describes how the SI unit called the Newton is derived:
a: the product of force times time
the energy in one kilogram traveling at one meter per second
the force needed to accelerate 1 kilogram at one meter per second squared
the power needed to accelerate 1 kilogram at one kilometer per hour
e: A single newton is the exact friendly shove needed to speed up a one-kilogram mass by one meter per second squared!

q: What quantity is a measure of the amount of light that a star emits that reaches the Earth?
e: Apparent magnitude measures how bright a distant star looks to our eyes on Earth, no matter how far away it lives.

q: If an object experiences a change in its velocity, which of the following statements must be TRUE about its acceleration?
e: Acceleration measures any change in how something moves, so whenever velocity shifts, that acceleration is always non-zero.

q: As of 2008, which of the following states consumed the most energy, including residential, commercial, industrial, and transportation sectors?
e: With its giant oil refineries, sprawling cities, and humming power grids, Texas used the most total energy back in 2008.

q: Which of the following best illustrates the particle nature of light?
e: Light behaves like tiny ping-pong balls here, knocking electrons loose from metal one direct hit at a time.

q: Which of the following is closest to the number of commercial nuclear reactors currently operating in the United States?
e: Across the country, about one hundred busy nuclear reactors hum day and night to keep our cities glowing bright.

q: What is the name for the bands of ions from the solar wind and cosmic rays that have become trapped in Earth's magnetic field?
e: Earth wears giant magnetic hula hoops called the Van Allen belts, happily catching zooming space particles before they reach us.

q: Why does the same side of the Moon always face the Earth?
a: The Moon rotates about its axis about once per month
The Moon rotates about its axis about once per year
The Moon and the Earth rotate about their axes at the same rate
The Moon does not rotate about its axis
e: The Moon takes about a month to spin around once, perfectly matching its dance around Earth so we always see its smiling face.

q: Cepheid variables are most useful for determining which of the following?
e: Like faithful cosmic lighthouses, Cepheid stars blink in a steady rhythm that helps astronomers measure the distance to another galaxy.

q: By 2050, what is projected to be the world's approximate total annual power demand in terawatts?
e: By 2050, our busy planet will need about thirty terawatts of power to keep every gadget and light humming along happily.

q: The radius of Planet C is close to half that of Earth, and both have the same average density. Compared to Earth's gravitational acceleration at the surface, approximately what will Planet C's gravity be at its surface?
e: Being half as wide with the same density, this little world hugs you down with just half of Earth's gravity, or g/2.

q: For a projectile that is accelerating only due to gravity, where is its speed the lowest?
a: Just before it hits the ground
At the top of its arc
At the bottom of its arc
e: At the very top of its arc, a tossed ball pauses its climb, moving slowest before gravity pulls it back down.

q: A student is standing in an elevator that is moving. Taking upward to be positive and downward to be negative, which of the following could NOT be true?
a: The student has a velocity equal to zero and a positive acceleration vector
The student has an acceleration equal to zero and a positive velocity vector
The student has a positive acceleration vector and a negative velocity vector
The student has a negative acceleration vector and is slowing down
e: If the elevator is actively moving, the student cannot have a velocity of zero, no matter how it accelerates.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about honeybee flight?
a: They flap their wings very quickly
Their wings beat over a very short arc
When they want to generate more power, they increase the arc of their wing strokes
Their flight muscles are physiologically very similar to those of fruit flies
e: Busy honeybees flap with their own special mechanics, so their flight muscles are actually not very similar to fruit flies at all!

q: The heat energy stored in water while it flows through a tube has been studied by which of the following scientists?
e: Bernoulli loved watching water swoosh through pipes, discovering the playful way flowing liquids carry their stored heat energy.

q: Which of the following purification techniques is most appropriate for separating a mixture of sand and water?
e: Filtration lets water slip right through a tiny sieve while trapping gritty sand behind, keeping everything neat and tidy!

q: Which of the following is NOT true of humidity:
a: relative humidity is a description of the water vapor content in air
humans feel uncomfortable when the relative humidity is high because cooling from sweating is less effective
dew points normally occur when the relative humidity of an air mass is 100%
the dew point is measured in percent along with the relative humidity
e: While humidity loves percentages, dew point is actually a temperature, proudly wearing degrees like your morning forecast.

q: Touching hot objects with oven mitts relies on insulation that slows heat movement from the hot pan to your hand. However, the air in the oven mitt is only a good insulator if convection is not able to happen. That means that the air must be:
e: Trapped air in an oven mitt must stay totally still, or stagnant, so sneaky heat cannot wander over to your fingers.

q: Which of the following statements regarding Saturn is NOT true?
a: It has a 29-year orbit around the Sun
Its rotational axis is tilted 27 with respect to the orbital plane
Its seasons are about twice as long as corresponding seasons on Earth
Its rings are aligned with its equator
e: Because Saturn takes twenty-nine years to circle the Sun, its giant seasons last over seven years, not just twice Earth's!

q: The Energy Star program was created by which of the following agencies?
e: The Environmental Protection Agency created Energy Star to help friendly appliances sip power gently and keep our planet green.

q: When the lunar surface is bombarded with solar wind, which of the following resources may be exploited from the Moon's surface?
e: Sunbeams shower the Moon with helium, creating a buried treasure that future astronauts could scoop up for clean nuclear fusion power.

q: Argonne National Lab researchers are using X-rays from the Advanced Photon Source to study the self-healing properties of nanoparticles. Which of the following techniques are they using to image these particles?
e: Argonne scientists use coherent diffraction imaging, bouncing X-rays off tiny particles to watch them cleverly heal their own wounds.

q: A star has a temperature of 2500 kelvins. Which of the following best categorizes the peak emission wavelength of the star?
e: At a cool twenty-five hundred kelvins, this cozy star shines brightest in infrared light, hiding its glow just beyond human eyes.

q: Which of the following is NOT a standard characteristic of a laser:
e: Lasers need a kick to start shining, but they lack a distinctly identifiable pumping turn-off, fading whenever energy dips.

q: Researchers at SLAC National Accelerator Lab have developed a new electron-gun that produces near-continuous high-energy electron beams. The electron gun uses a chamber of niobium cooled to 4 kelvins, which has what property?
e: Chilled to freezing temperatures, niobium unlocks superconductivity, letting electricity glide through without losing a single drop of energy!

q: What Galilean [gal-ih- LAY-en] moon is the closest to Jupiter, and subjected to intense tidal heating that drives prolific volcanism?
e: Jupiter squishes its moon Io like a rubber ball, heating it up inside until fiery volcanoes blast across its surface!

q: Native to Asia, the Burmese python was brought to the United States for sale as a pet. Owners released their Burmese pythons into the wild of the Florida Everglades, creating ecological problems in that habitat. Which best describes the Burmese Python?
e: When these giant snakes moved in from far away and bullied the local wildlife, they became an invasive species wrecking swamp harmony.

q: A gust of wind causes the blades of a wind turbine to begin rotating. Which of the following is an accurate description of the blades?
a: They are out of static equilibrium because the wind provides a net horizontal force
They are out of static equilibrium because the wind provides a net torque
They are in static equilibrium because the forces are balanced
They are in static equilibrium because their center of mass remains in place
e: The breeze gives the blades a mighty twisting push called torque, knocking them out of static equilibrium to start spinning!

q: Which of the following is a consequence of the exclusion principle?
a: Electrons bound in an atom can only occupy orbits for which the angular momentum is quantized
An electron in a stationary state emits no radiation
No two electrons in a single atom can have an identical set of quantum numbers
Only when an electron jumps to a lower state does it emit a photon
e: Electrons are tidy roommates who refuse to dress alike, so no two can ever share the exact same quantum numbers inside an atom.

q: The wavelength shift of light from a quasar gives the recessional speed v 2.18 108 meters per second. If the Hubble constant is 21.8 millimeters per second per light year, what is the approximate distance of the quasar in light years?
e: Dividing how fast this cosmic beacon zooms away by the universe's growth rate puts it ten to the tenth light-years away.

q: In which of the following regions would one most likely find the oldest stars?
e: Globular clusters are like glittering retirement homes for stars, packed tight with the most ancient, grandfatherly lights in the whole galaxy.

q: The interstellar medium is primarily composed of two components, a warm ionized phase and a cool neutral phase. Which of the following is approximately the temperature in Kelvin of the cool phase?
e: Deep in space, this chilly gas rests at about one hundred Kelvin, cold enough to freeze water into hard cosmic ice.

q: Which of the following best describes how the kinetic energy of ejected electrons depends on the frequency and the intensity of light in the photoelectric effect?
a: Increases linearly with intensity, inversely proportional to frequency
Increases linearly with frequency, inversely proportional to intensity
Increases linearly with intensity, independent of frequency
Increases linearly with frequency, independent of intensity
e: Light with higher frequency kicks electrons harder, while extra brightness only changes how many jump, not their speedy energy.

q: Which of the following is the dominant cooling mechanism in a core-collapse supernova?
e: Trillions of speedy ghost particles called neutrinos zip away into space, carrying off almost all the giant star's blazing heat.

q: Scientists at Argonne National Lab are studying how Lepidopterans [leh-pid-OP-tur-anz] drink liquids. Which of the following types of animals are part of Lepidoptera?
e: With their colorful, powdery wings and straw-like tongues, lovely fluttering butterflies belong to the grand insect family called Lepidoptera.

q: What is the equivalent resistance, to the nearest tenth of an ohm, of a circuit containing 3 resistors in parallel, with resistance values of 5 ohms, 3 ohms, and 6 ohms?
e: Because electricity gets three paths to scurry through at once, the total pushback drops neatly down to just one point four ohms.

q: A clothes dryer can be a high consumer of household electricity. Which of the following options is NOT a way in which to reduce energy consumption when using your clothes dryer?
a: Purchase a dryer model that has an ENERGY STAR label
Use the moisture sensor option, if you have one
Clean the lint filter to improve the efficiency of the dryer
Scrub the lint filter if you use dryer sheets
e: Shopping for an Energy Star model happens at the store, not while you are actually at home spinning your wet socks!

q: Which of the following most directly addresses that a gas of low density, when excited, will emit light of a certain wavelength:
e: Kirchhoff's second law reveals that warm, thin clouds of gas glow with their very own colorful fingerprint lines of light.

q: Photons and gluons are classified as which of the following types of particles?
e: These force-carrying particles love to crowd together and share energy, making them part of the friendly family called bosons.

q: An elevator is moving downward with decreasing speed. What are the directions of its velocity and acceleration?
a: Velocity is upward and acceleration is downward
Velocity is downward and acceleration is upward
e: The elevator is sinking downward, but upward braking forces tug to slow it down, pointing its acceleration straight toward the sky.

q: During the formation of a neutron star, protons and electrons will combine to form neutrons and neutrinos. This reaction is mechanistically similar to what mode of radioactive decay?
e: A proton snatches an electron to become a neutron, mirroring the cozy nuclear hug known as electron capture.

q: What is one way in which power can be calculated?
a: Subtracting the relative vectors F and v
The time derivative of work performed
The strength of the force times g
e: Power measures how quickly energy does a job, which mathematicians find by taking the time derivative of work performed.

q: Spectroscopic binaries are easiest to detect when
a: The stars are of the same spectral class
e: When the stars circle edge-on, they rush directly toward and away from us, making their wobbling light shifts easiest to catch.

q: Researchers at Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility are using Monte Carlo methods to evaluate integrals in very high dimensional spaces. Which of the following best explains the advantage of Monte Carlo techniques in these settings?
a: Direct integration techniques are too computationally intensive in high dimensions
Monte Carlo integration is known to be more accurate than direct integration
Monte Carlo techniques are easier to combine with machine learning methods
Direct integration techniques are susceptible to numerical overflow in high dimensions
e: Regular math grids get overwhelmed in giant spaces, making direct calculations far too slow and heavy for computers to solve.

q: An outflow of charged particles from the sun that escapes the sun's outer atmosphere is called:
e: Like a continuous breath blowing from our star across space, this breezy river of charged particles is the solar wind.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of hydrogenous sediments?
e: Siliceous ooze comes from the tiny glassy shells of sea critters, not water chemicals, making it biological instead of hydrogenous.

q: Pure water would conduct electricity if we added to it which of the following?
e: When salt dives into water, it breaks into tiny charged helpers that happily carry electrical sparks along.

q: What is the challenge with regard to wind energy and transmission line capacity?
a: Not enough transmission lines connect cities to the windiest parts of the country
Transmission lines only have the capacity to transfer wind energy from small turbines
We have more transmission lines than our power plants can currently support
e: Mighty winds blow across open fields, but we simply lack enough power lines to carry all that breezy energy home to big cities.

q: What type of image is produced by a concave spherical mirror when an object is placed outside its focal point?
e: The cozy curved mirror bends light beams until they cross, projecting a real picture that flips your smile upside down!

q: What is the unit of electrical inductance?
e: Coils resist changes in current with a magnetic hug, measured by a polite unit called the henry!

q: Researchers using Los Alamos National Lab facilities have found higher- than-expected nucleosynthesis yields for nuclei with masses between 60 and 90 atomic mass units. Which of the following elements do they predict having higher yields?
e: Arsenic has an atomic weight near seventy-five, fitting snugly right into that cosmic sweet spot between sixty and ninety.

q: Which of the following principles of fluid dynamics does an airplane use to create an upward force?
e: Bernoulli's principle shows that speedy air rushing over curved wings creates low pressure, gently lifting the airplane up into the clouds!

q: A fully-charged capacitor is connected to a circuit with a resistor. Which of the following describes how the charge in the capacitor will change with time?
e: Electric charge rushes out fast at first, then slows down, draining away on a gentle exponential curve until it hits zero.

q: The radiation emitted by T Tauri stars primarily comes from which of the following?
e: Before baby stars can start true fusion, gravity squeezes them tight, warming them up through the Kelvin-Helmholtz mechanism.

q: Which of the following terms does NOT uniquely apply to the description of magnet properties?
e: Anisotropy just means having different traits in different directions, a trick shared by crystals and wood, not just magnets.

q: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe was specifically designed to:
a: map all matter in the universe down to a resolution of 1 arc second
map the cosmic background radiation to much greater accuracy and precision than previous instruments
map the size and locations of the Local Group
map the exact location of the active galactic center of the Milky Way
e: This clever space probe took the sharpest baby picture ever of ancient microwave glow left behind from the very beginning.

q: Andrew connects a vacuum pump to a long tube and dips the other end of the tube into a swimming pool directly below him. In meters, which of the following distances is closest to the maximum height he could pump water up the tube?
e: Earth's cozy blanket of air can only push water about ten meters up before the heavy water pushes back too hard.

q: Which of the following was the big surprise in the classic gold foil experiments of Rutherford, Geiger and Marsden:
a: electrons would not penetrate the nucleus
the atom was mostly space as supported by the finding that most alpha particles continued on a straight path and hit the rear of the detection screen
some alpha particles left evidence of having returned almost straight back to hit the front part of the detection screen
e: Scientists expected tiny particles to zip right through, so seeing a few bounce straight backward was a jaw-dropping surprise!

q: In a series-connected string of holiday lights, which of the following is most likely to occur if one bulb gets shorted without breaking the filament?
a: All other bulbs will go out
The current in the string will increase
The current in the string will decrease
The current in the string will remain unchanged
e: Skipping past that faulty bulb lowers the path's resistance, letting more electric current rush happily through the string.

q: A chinook wind causes which of the following?
e: As this wind tumbles down mountain slopes, the air gets squeezed, turning warm and dry like a giant hairdryer.

q: How much work must be done, in joules, on a 15 kilogram mass in order to increase its speed from 7.5 meters per second to 11.5 meters per second?
e: Boosting the object's energetic speed takes five hundred seventy joules of work to pay for that extra motion.

q: Which of the following conditions is common to both warm and cold fronts?
a: Lifting of warm air over a cold air mass
e: Warm air is light and floaty, so whether meeting hot or cold weather fronts, it always gets pushed up over chilly air.

q: Which of the following circuit laws is a direct consequence of the conservation of charge?
e: Because electric charges never vanish, every bit entering a wire crossroad must leave, perfectly matching Kirchhoff's junction law.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of what occurs during an equinox:
a: equal length of day and night except at the poles
the Earth is not tilted with respect to the ecliptic
the Sun is directly overhead at the equator
the Moon is directly overhead at the poles
e: While the Sun balances day and night, the wandering Moon follows its own path and does not sit directly over the poles.

q: Lobate scarps on the surface of Mercury are a result of which of the following processes?
e: As tiny Mercury cooled down inside, it shrank like a drying apple, wrinkling its rocky crust into giant cliffs called scarps.

q: A small rubber duck is held underwater at a depth of 10 meters, then released. When the duck reaches a depth of 5 meters, how much has the buoyant force on the duck changed?
e: Water pushes up with the same friendly force because the duck pushes aside the exact same amount of water everywhere underwater.

q: Which one of the following terms is used to indicate the natural tendency of an object to remain at rest or in motion at a constant speed along a straight line?
e: Inertia is an object's stubborn habit of staying cozy on the couch, or coasting forever until something pushes it!

q: Which of the following clouds develops at the highest altitude?
e: Cirrocumulus clouds are the sky's highest little fleecy sheep, drifting way up near space where the air is freezing cold.

q: Ignoring air resistance, wind velocity, and the rotation of the Earth, if a projectile is fired directly upwards, the horizontal component of the projectile's velocity:
e: Because the ball shoots straight up toward the stars, it has zero sideways speed pushing it left or right.

q: Roberto lives in Florida. Which of the following is NOT a way that he could use less energy at home?
a: Close the window curtains during the day in the summer
Open the curtains on south-facing windows during the day in the winter
Hang his wet clothes on clotheslines outside when it is sunny
Turn thermostats to a colder temperature during the summer
e: Cranking the thermostat extra cold makes the cooler work overtime, guzzling up way more power instead of saving it!

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of alpha decay?
a: Alpha decay occurs in heavy nuclei where the electrostatic repulsion between the protons in the nucleus is large
The mass of a nucleus that undergoes alpha decay will be changed by only a small amount
Neither the mass number nor the atomic number is changed
e: Heavy atomic cores get so packed with repelling protons that they kick out an alpha particle to relieve the squeeze.

q: Which of the following characteristics makes Xenon-135 an effective neutron poison in nuclear reactors?
a: Cherenkov radiation from beta decay of Xenon-135
e: Xenon-135 acts like a giant catcher's mitt, easily snatching up wandering neutrons before other atoms can even touch them.

q: Which of the following is the most common usage of syngas?
e: Most of this gas gets burned in big power plants, happily spinning turbines to generate bright electricity for homes.

q: Which of the following power types demonstrates large scale temporary storage of energy?
e: Hydroelectric dams store energy by pumping water uphill like a giant liquid battery, ready to rush down when needed!

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are studying explosive compounds like TNT. What is the preferred IUPAC name of TNT?
e: The official name reveals a benzene ring neatly decorated with one methyl group and three explosive nitro groups.

q: What percentage of the world's production of rare earth metals is produced by China?
e: China digs up a whopping ninety-five percent, supplying almost all the world's rare metals for our shiny gadgets.

q: Approximately what percentage of water on Earth is fresh water?
e: Earth is a giant blue puddle, but only three percent is sweet fresh water we can actually drink.

q: Which of the following quantities is defined as the rate of change of angular momentum?
e: Torque is the twisting muscle that gets things spinning faster, changing their turning momentum over time.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the current electricity system in the United States?
a: It consists of more than 9,000 electric generating units
It has more than 1,000,000 megawatts of generating capacity
e: America's electricity is tied together into massive interconnected regional grids, rather than being decentralized into separated parts.

q: Eccentricity of an orbit describes:
a: Its deviation from a circular orbit
Its time difference from a standard day
e: Eccentricity measures how much a planet's orbit stretches out from a perfect circle into an oval shape.

q: In electricity transmission, at consistent current and resistance, which of the following changes over long distances?
e: As electricity travels across miles of wire, its pushing strength, called voltage, slowly drops along the way.

q: Which of the following is a type of telescope technology that uses mirrors whose shapes can be deformed:
e: Adaptive optics uses bendy mirrors that shift like flexible clay to instantly unblur twinkling starlight!

q: Which of the following thermodynamic properties is not a state function?
e: Heat isn't a fixed property an object keeps inside, but energy flowing on a journey from hot to cold.

q: What is the name for a particle that carries a half-integer spin?
e: Fermions are the shy building blocks of matter that spin in half-steps and refuse to share their space.

q: Amy is pulling a heavy cart. It is harder to start pulling the cart than to keep the cart in motion because the kinetic frictional force:
a: Is zero once the cart starts moving
Is only present when the cart is first pulled
Is less than the static frictional force
e: Once the heavy cart is rolling, moving friction puts up less resistance than the stubborn grip holding it still.

q: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory's National Ignition Facility is using what technology to further nuclear fusion energy research?
e: Scientists fire giant lasers to crush tiny fuel pellets, trapping the heat so fast that fusion sparks to life!

q: On July 4, under modern conditions, the planet is at which of the following in relation to the Sun?
e: In July, Earth swings out to aphelion, the farthest point in its yearly dance around the Sun.

q: The displacement-time graph of a body that starts from rest and moves away from the origin with constant acceleration appears as which of the following?
a: A curved line whose slope is increasing in time
A curved line whose slope is decreasing in time
A straight line with zero slope
A straight line with non-zero slope
e: When something speeds up faster and faster, its graph curves upward, growing steeper with every ticking second.

q: An object is placed 17 centimeters to the left of the vertex of a concave spherical mirror with a radius of curvature of 30 centimeters. Which of the following pairs of properties describe the image formed?
e: Standing just past the mirror's sweet spot makes the bouncing light flip upside down into a real, inverted picture.

q: In a compound gearing arrangement where a 40-tooth gear drives an 80-tooth gear which is directly connected to a 50-tooth gear that drives a 100-tooth gear, the total reduction is a factor of:
e: The first gear pair cuts the speed in half, and the next pair halves it again, making a reduction of four!

q: Brain computer interfaces can measure minute differences in the voltage between neurons, amplify and filter the signal, and then a computer interprets it. All of the following are current applications of brain computer interfaces, except:
a: Controlling a computer cursor via mental commands
Interpreting brain signals for movement for someone who can't physically move
Providing a communication link for people who suffer from "locked in" syndrome
e: Computers can listen to our brain's whispers, but they cannot mend or repair damaged neurons just yet.

q: Which of the following is closest to the percent of the world's electricity that is supplied by nuclear power plants?
e: Nuclear plants quietly hum along, providing about 15 percent of all the electric power that lights our world.

q: Which of the following describes the purpose of the ground connection on a common power outlet?
a: Remove excess heat from the transmission system
Give a low resistance path for short circuits to travel through
Act as a small current source to prevent corrosion
e: The ground wire is a trusty escape hatch, giving runaway electricity a safe, low-resistance path straight into the dirt.

q: What is the largest size of sediment you would expect to find near the headwaters of a stream?
e: High up where energetic mountain streams begin, the rushing water is mighty enough to tumble giant boulders.

q: Which of the following is the primary characteristic of the Jovian planets:
e: Giant gas worlds like Jupiter are mostly puffy atmosphere, giving them a surprisingly low density like cosmic cotton balls.

q: The principle constituent of most granites is:
e: Granite rocks are packed with tiny mineral crystals, and sturdy feldspar is the biggest ingredient in the recipe.

q: You are traveling west by jet and cross three time zone boundaries. If your watch reads 3:00 p.m. when you arrive, to what time should you reset it?
e: Flying west chases the sun backward, so you turn your clock back three whole hours to 12:00 noon.

q: According to the location in the H-R diagram, which of the following stars has the highest absolute visual magnitude and is also the hottest:
a: one located in the upper left of the diagram
one located in the upper right of the diagram
one located in the lower left of the diagram
one located in the lower right of the diagram
e: The hottest, brightest stars shine proudly in the upper left corner of the chart, blazing with dazzling energy.

q: Which of the following mathematical representations is commonly used to model AC voltages and currents as a rotating vector in the complex plane?
e: A phasor is like a little arrow spinning around in circles to track alternating electric waves.

q: Which of the following changes with the local acceleration due to gravity?
e: Your body stays the same everywhere, but your weight changes whenever gravity gives a harder or softer tug!

q: In a science lab, a sphere rolls on a horizontal flat surface until it eventually comes to rest, but not as a result of a frictional force. Which of the following is the best explanation of why the sphere comes to rest?
a: The spherical shape and/or flat surface must not be ideal and the sphere will stop where a defect makes that location a minimum potential-energy position
Some other force, like fluid friction, must be acting on the sphere
Angular momentum between the rolling sphere and the spinning Earth must be conserved
The force of gravity must not be constant even though the surface is flat
e: No surface is perfectly flat, so the rolling ball rests in a tiny dip with the lowest potential energy.

q: Which of the following is the equivalent resistance, in ohms, of a circuit in which a 5 ohm resistor is connected in series to two 4 ohm resistors which are connected in parallel?
e: The two parallel resistors combine into two ohms, and adding the five-ohm resistor gives seven ohms in total.

q: In response to the development of incandescent lights, gas lights were vastly improved by soaking the mantles in what substance to help convert heat and UV energy into visible light:
e: Soaking mantles in thorium oxide helped old gas lamps glow with a brilliant, cheerful white light.

q: Which of the following does not occur after the passage of a cold front?
e: Once a chilly front swoops by, heavy cool air settles in, causing the air pressure to rise, not drop.

q: Which of the following BEST explains why gravitational acceleration on Earth varies from one place to another:
a: the Sun's gravitational pull varies irregularly
the Earth is not a uniform sphere
the Moon and the Sun exert a complex combination of gravitational pulls on the Earth
the changing angular momentum of the Earth varies during its yearly orbit
e: Earth is not a perfect, smooth marble, so its lumpy shape tugs on you slightly differently from place to place.

q: An object sits in front of a spherical mirror with a focal length of 20 centimeters. The image produced by the mirror is upright and has a height one-third that of the original object. Which of the following is true?
a: The image is real and the mirror is convex
The image is real and the mirror is concave
The image is virtual and the mirror is convex
The image is virtual and the mirror is concave
e: A curved convex mirror bends outward like a bubble, shrinking your reflection into an upright, virtual picture.

q: Free neutrons decay to protons, electrons, and antineutrinos. What fundamental force is responsible for this decay?
e: Deep inside tiny particles, the weak nuclear force quietly nudges a restless neutron, transforming it into a brand-new little family of particles.

q: Which of the following is NOT an accurate description of the dominant airmass effecting America's Pacific Northwest?
e: Ocean breezes love bringing soggy, misty hugs to the Pacific Northwest, making dry the absolute last word you would use for its air.

q: In which of the following locations would there typically be more Population Two stars than Population One stars:
e: Globular clusters are cozy cosmic retirement homes, packed with ancient Population Two stars that have been twinkling since the universe was young.

q: Which of the following conditions must be true for Hooke's law to apply:
a: the spring must be within its proportional elastic limit
the spring must me made of cold formed steel coils
the deflection of the spring must be less than one tenth the spring's free length
the carbon content of the metal must be over 0.023 percent
e: A spring happily bounces right back to shape only if you stay within its elastic limit, without stretching it so far it breaks!

q: If an object immersed in water experiences a buoyant force of 19.6 x 103 newtons, assuming that the density of water is 1000 kilograms per meter cubed, what is the immersed volume of the object?
e: To push up with that mighty water force, the object must push aside two cubic meters of water, matching its exact immersed size.

q: Which of the following is a glacial feature that is NOT caused by the deposition of sediments:
e: While melting ice drops piles of dirt elsewhere, a bergschrund is just a giant, icy crack ripped open where moving glaciers pull away.

q: From mid-northern latitudes, during which of the following months would the constellation Orion be most prominent in the southern sky at about 10 PM:
e: When chilly December winter nights arrive, Orion straps on his glittering belt to march proudly across the southern sky before bedtime.

q: Planets A and B are in circular orbits about the same star. Planet A's orbital radius is three times as large as Planet B's. Which of the following is the ratio of Planet A's orbital period to Planet B's?
a: 33/2 [three to the power of the quantity three over two]
32/3 [three to the power of the quantity two over three]
e: Because planets take longer strolls on wider paths, tripling the orbit stretches its travel time by three to the three-halves power.

q: The proportionality [proportion-AL-ih-tee] constant in the ideal gas equation turns out to be almost equal for all real gases in which of the following conditions?
e: With plenty of heat to zoom around and low pressure giving them breathing room, gas particles act like an ideal, happy family.

q: Scientists at Argonne National Lab are studying supernova nucleosynthesis. Which of the following elements on Earth primarily originates from supernova nucleosynthesis?
e: When giant stars explode in dazzling supernovas, they blast out brand-new cosmic treasures into space, including Earth's supply of arsenic.

q: Which of the following is LEAST accurate:
a: most stars visible to the unaided eye are part of the Milky Way galaxy
there are 88 constellations officially recognized by the IAU
a red supergiant has a hotter surface than our Sun
the constellation Leo is located within 9 of the ecliptic
e: Red supergiants are enormous glowing giants, but their red color gives away their secret: their surfaces are actually cooler than our Sun!

q: Which of the following products has the same units as power?
e: Multiplying how hard you push by how fast you move gives you pure power, showing how quickly work gets done!

q: A 20 kilogram mass is suspended from the end of a spring with a spring constant of 5 newtons per meter. If the mass is displaced 10 centimeters from equilibrium [ee-kwuh-LIB-ree-uhm], what is the maximum speed of the mass in meters per second?
e: That heavy weight moves at a gentle crawl, reaching its peak speed of point zero five meters each second at the center.

q: Which of the following is the BEST reason why the Sun's corona primarily emits x-rays:
a: it has a high-strength magnetic field
it is where most of the neutrinos escape to outer space
e: The Sun's glowing crown sizzles at millions of degrees, and being so incredibly hot makes it glow with energetic X-rays.

q: Which of the following is characterized by the lack of a distinct melting point?
a: Stainless steel of a known composition
e: Without tidy crystal rows, glass simply softens into gooey taffy as it warms up instead of melting at one exact temperature.

q: Two loudspeakers, A and B, are placed 4 meters apart and facing each other. The loudspeakers produce sound at 171 hertz in phase with one another. A microphone is moved with varying speed along a straight line that joins A and B. Which of the following statements is true?
a: The microphone detects sound with no amplitude fluctuations as it moves
The microphone detects sound with amplitude fluctuations that increase as its speed decreases
The microphone detects sound with amplitude fluctuations that increase as its speed increases
e: As you dash faster through the quiet and loud spots of sound, your ears hear those volume wobbles happen much more quickly!

q: Which of the following types of electromagnetic radiation possesses the greatest amount of energy per photon?
e: Zipping through space with super-tight waves, X-rays pack way more punch and photon energy than gentle rays like light or microwaves.

q: Which of the following types of magnetometers needs to be cooled to very low temperatures due to reliance on the Josephson effect?
e: SQUID sensors must stay shivering in deep cold so their superconducting quantum loops can sniff out the tiniest magnetic whispers.

q: Comet McNaught visited in 2007 but is now on a path to leave the solar system forever. Which of the following best describes its orbit?
e: Flying too fast to ever turn back, this runaway comet zooms along an open, hyperbolic curve straight out into deep space!

q: Fermi National Lab scientists demonstrated the accuracy of lattice quantum chromodynamics, which is a theory that, among other predictions, predicts which of the following experimental observations?
e: Tiny quarks are glued together so tightly by color confinement that not a single one can ever break free and wander alone.

q: What forces maintain neutron stars against gravitational collapse?
e: Mighty nuclear forces act like tiny superhero muscles, shoving packed neutrons outward so gravity cannot crush the star any further.

q: The Peter Auger cosmic ray observatory is operated by DOE scientists from Fermilab. Which of the following statements is TRUE of how cosmic rays are detected by this observatory?
a: The observatory detects cosmic rays by measuring the local electric field
The observatory directly observes cosmic rays interacting with water
The observatory detects the shower of energetic particles produced by a cosmic ray
The observatory uses interferometry to detect cosmic rays
e: When an energetic cosmic ray hits our atmosphere, it shatters into a giant shower of energetic particles that detectors catch like confetti.

q: Scientists at Los Alamos National Lab are generating radioactive radium for cancer therapy. Given that radium concentrates in hydroxyapatite [high-drox-ee-AP-ah-tite], what type of tumor will radium be most useful for treating?
e: Since bones are made of hydroxyapatite, radioactive radium journeys straight to the skeleton to zap dangerous bone tumors.

q: In electrostatics, which of the following must be true of a conductor?
a: It can only carry negative charge
The electric field on its surface is zero
The electric field inside it is zero
e: Inside a conductor, mobile charges quickly push each other outward to the surface until the inner electric field drops to zero.

q: Scientists at Pacific Northwest National Lab are exploring gene therapy to improve drug delivery while minimizing toxic side effects. Which of the following is LEAST likely to be effectively treated with gene therapy?
e: Gene therapy fixes broken human instruction manuals, but tuberculosis is caused by an invading bacterium, not a faulty gene.

q: Which of the following is the term for the phenomenon by which a changing magnetic field creates a current in a circuit?
e: When a magnet dances past a wire, it magically coaxes electricity to flow through a phenomenon called induction!

q: Which of the following statements is not true regarding lighting and lighting technology?
a: Incandescent lights emit most of their energy as heat
LED lights are based on a pn-junction diode
Halogen light bulbs use tungsten filaments just like incandescent bulbs do
e: Organic LEDs shine with their own little glow, so they never need a separate backlight behind them to light up.

q: Which of the following is the term for the hygroscopic [hy-gruh-SKOP-ik] atmospheric particles that are precursors to clouds?
e: Tiny floating specks called cloud condensation nuclei act like cozy landing pads where water vapor gathers to form fluffy clouds.

q: A jet engine gets its thrust by taking in air, heating and compressing it and then ejecting it at a high speed. If a particular engine takes in 20 kilograms of air per second at 100 meters per second, and ejects it at 500 meters per second, what is the thrust of the engine in newtons?
e: By speeding up twenty kilograms of air by four hundred meters every second, the engine blasts forward with eight thousand newtons.

q: Which of the following BEST describes Fermat's principle:
a: light disperses in a specific medium depending on the medium's refractive index
light follows the path of least time between two points
the angle of incidence can be greater than the angle of reflection
light always travels in the same medium at the same speed
e: Clever rays of light are always in a hurry, naturally choosing the path of least time between two points.

q: Which of the following is a cloud type that, by definition, produces precipitation?
e: With a name born from rain, dark nimbostratus clouds wrap the sky like a giant, dripping blanket to pour down precipitation.

q: Which of the following types of thermometer is based on the difference in the voltage induced by a temperature gradient in two metals?
e: Joined together, two different metals create an electrical voltage when heated, letting a thermocouple measure temperature with a spark of genius.

q: During positron emission, which of the following most likely occurs:
a: a proton changes to an electron
a proton changes to a neutron
a neutron changes to an electron
a neutron changes to a proton
e: In a busy atomic nucleus, a restless proton can shed its positive charge and magically transform into a calm neutron.

q: One component of a solar energy system is the charge controller. Its function is to:
a: Provide electrical protection to the system
Regulate the amount of power that goes into energy storage for later use
Store the energy for later use
e: Acting like a gentle traffic cop, a charge controller regulates the flow of solar electricity into storage so batteries stay safe.

q: Which of the following is TRUE of the wave model of atomic theory?
a: Electrons orbit the nucleus in circles
Electrons have a well-defined position and momentum at all points in their orbit
Electrons compose most of the mass of the atom
Electrons can absorb photons to transition between states
e: Electrons act like playful acrobats, happily absorbing little light packets called photons to leap upward into higher energy states.

q: Which of the following colors of light will have the shallowest penetration in the marine water column?
e: Thirsty water molecules quickly soak up red light right near the surface, stopping it from diving deep into the sea.

q: Which of the following has the lowest refractive index at STP:
e: With nothing to bump into, light races fastest through an empty vacuum, giving it the lowest refractive index of all.

q: An object is placed 20 centimeters in front of a thin convex lens of focal length 10 centimeters. What must be the image distance in centimeters?
e: Placed at twice the focal distance, light bends evenly through the lens, painting an identical copy exactly twenty centimeters behind it.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab recently captured images of a Type one-A supernova in a galaxy four billion light-years away that appeared 50 times brighter than normal and in four different places in the sky. Which of the following did the scientists discover?
a: A Type-one-A supernova with a progenitor that was 20-50 times more massive than normal
An anomalous type-two supernova with a light curve resembling type Ia
A light echo of a type-one-A supernova
A type-one-A supernova whose image was strongly gravitationally lensed
e: A heavy galaxy warped space like a giant magnifying lens, gravitationally lensing that one exploding star into four bright images.

q: A wireless router transmits an 802.11a Wi-Fi radio signal at 5 megahertz with a speed up to 54 megabits of data per second. What is the wavelength of the router's signal in meters?
e: Light speed divided by five million wave pulses each second stretches each radio wave to exactly sixty meters long.

q: Which of the following best explains why power transmission lines use high voltage?
a: Substation equipment used to transmit power at high voltage is cheaper than equipment for low voltage
Power loss decreases as the square of the voltage increases
Power loss decreases linearly as the voltage increases
It is safer to transmit power at high rather than low voltage
e: Cranking up the voltage helps electricity zoom through wires with far less wasted heat, because energy loss drops by the square of that boost!

q: According to Betz's Law, wind turbines cannot capture more than what approximate percentage of the kinetic energy present in wind?
e: Wind needs room to sneak away after pushing the blades, so turbines can only catch about fifty-nine percent of its breezy energy.

q: Scientists at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory are studying ways to use gravitational-lensing data to measure the Hubble constant. Expressed in SI units, what are the units of the Hubble constant?
e: Because distances cancel out when watching the universe stretch, this cosmic speed is measured in simple units of one over seconds.

q: An -particle [alpha particle] and a proton, both initially at rest, are accelerated through a potential difference of 105 kilovolts. Find the ratio (K/Kp) [k alpha over k proton] of their final kinetic energies.
e: With twice the electric charge of a proton, the mighty alpha particle gets pulled twice as hard, scooping up double the kinetic energy!
