q: For a given time interval, when is the average velocity of an object equal to the instantaneous velocity for every time in the interval:
a: only when the velocity is changing at a constant rate
only when the velocity is constant
e: If a cheerful little scooter never speeds up or slows down, its speed at any single moment always matches its overall average.

q: Which of the following is MOST closely related to the movement of charge in non-ceramic superconductors:
e: Chilly electrons buddy up into friendly Cooper pairs, gliding through the wire without bumping into anything at all!

q: Which of the following does a Carnot engine convert?
e: This clever imaginary engine takes cozy, flowing heat and neatly turns it into useful work to push things along.

q: If a beam of white light passes through a prism, which of the following colors color will emerge on the other side at the lowest angle with respect to the incident beam:
e: Orange light has longer waves that stroll right through the glass, bending at the lowest angle among these colorful friends.

q: Kate is tuning her cello's A string by producing an A note on a string that is already tuned and comparing the sounds. Which of the following beat frequencies, in hertz, would indicate that the strings are closest to having the same pitch?
e: A tiny beat frequency of two means the strings are wobbling almost in perfect unison, like two hummingbirds singing together.

q: A poorly designed fishing bob does not float in a sucrose solution. Which of the following actions could be taken so the fishing bob would float?
a: Increase the volume of the solution
Decrease the volume of the solution
Increase the concentration of the solution
Decrease the concentration of the solution
e: Stirring in extra sugar increases the solution's concentration and density, giving the sleepy bobber the buoyant push it needs to float.

q: Saltwater desalination is a very energy-intensive process when practiced at large scale. What technology is predominantly used for saltwater desalination in the United States?
e: Squeezing ocean water through super-tight filters leaves the salty bits behind, making reverse osmosis our favorite way to clean seawater.

q: What is the name for a stream that is similar to a braided stream but the mid- channel bars are much more stable than those found in a braided stream?
e: Anastomosing streams weave around tough, plant-covered islands that stay firmly anchored in place rather than washing away.

q: Scientists at Argonne National Lab are studying the force that holds nuclei together. What is this force?
e: The strong force acts like invisible superglue, hugging protons and neutrons so tightly inside the nucleus that they never escape.

q: Which of the following statements is correct about the behavior of black bodies?
a: At high enough temperatures, black bodies will stop emitting in the microwave region
The Stefan-Boltzmann law relates the power radiated by a black body to temperature squared
Approximating a human as a black body shows that most of a person's energy is radiated away as ultraviolet light
Wien's law can be used to predict the color of a black body
e: Wien's law reveals how hot an object is just by looking at its glowing color, from warm red to blazing blue!

q: The largest supermassive black holes are found in
e: Giant elliptical galaxies love gobbling up smaller neighbors, feeding the absolute biggest supermassive black holes in the universe.

q: The TEX86 paleothermometer (read as: pay-ley-e- thehr-MOH-meh-tehr), measured from the abundance of crenarchaeal (read as: kren arr kee ah tah) lipids in marine sediments, depends on the relative abundance of which class of lipids?
e: Ancient microbes adjusted the tetraethers in their fatty jackets to stay cozy, leaving behind clues about past ocean temperatures.

q: The external presence of which of the following would result in the forward bias of a p-n junction?
a: Electric field directed toward the p region
Electric field directed toward the n region
Magnetic field directed toward the p region
Magnetic field directed toward the n region
e: Aiming an electric field toward the n region pushes charges across the barrier, opening the gate so current can flow forward!

q: What hazardous material enables compact fluorescent light bulbs to be more efficient while also requiring special disposal methods?
e: A pinch of mercury helps the bulb glow brightly using less energy, but this hazardous liquid needs careful disposal.

q: Which of the following particles does NOT correspond to one of the four basic types of radiation?
e: While electrons, photons, and helium nuclei are classic radiation travelers, the chunky lithium nucleus is not one of them.

q: What thermodynamic cycle describes a jet turbine?
e: The Brayton cycle describes how jet engines gulp air, squeeze it, and blast it out to send planes soaring!

q: Which of the following is NOT true of satellites in geostationary orbits?
a: They are in the line-of-sight of more than one third of the Earth's surface
They are useful for weather monitoring and communications
They provide excellent views of the polar regions
They can receive transmissions from free-floating balloons, buoys, and remote automatic data collection stations
e: Hovering high above Earth's waistline, these watchful helpers cannot peek around the curve to see the snowy polar regions.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Livermore National Lab are exploring how to 3D- print mechanical logic gates. What logic gate has the following behavior: zero and zero become one; zero and one become one; one and zero become one; one and one become zero.
e: A NAND gate is a contrary little switch that happily says yes, unless both of its incoming friends say yes too.

q: The Marcellus shale gas formation is located in which of the following states?
e: Deep beneath Pennsylvania's rolling hills lies a giant, ancient rock blanket holding huge pockets of trapped natural gas.

q: Which of the following is the BEST explanation for what causes zodiacal light:
a: reflection of moonlight off the Earth's surface
dispersion of the Earth's radiant heat off the troposphere
sunlight reflected off interplanetary dust particles
radiation from the Van Allen belts
e: Tiny specks of cosmic dust floating in space catch sunlight like glitter, making the night sky softly glow before dawn.

q: Power companies estimate the over-time cost of designing, building, operating, and decommissioning a power plant in order to calculate which of the following?
e: Levelized cost bundles every penny spent from a power plant's birth to its retirement, smoothing them into one steady price tag.

q: Which of the following cooking pot materials is most useful for an induction cooktop?
e: Induction stoves cook with magnetic magic, and trusty cast iron pans have plenty of iron to catch that invisible dance and sizzle.

q: Which of the following mechanisms transfers angular momentum in accretion disks?
e: Viscosity acts like cosmic sticky honey, rubbing swirling gas layers together so momentum can drift outward while matter falls inside.

q: You have just crystallized a new compound. You shine light through it and observe the internal reflection as the light attempts to pass into the air on the opposite side of the crystal. You measure the critical angle of the crystal to be 45 degrees. Taking the index of refraction of air to be 1, what is the index of refraction of the crystal?
e: Light bends at a neat forty-five-degree tilt, and doing the math reveals the crystal's light-bending power is the square root of two.

q: The motion of an underdamped harmonic oscillator can be written as the real part of an exponential of a product of time with a constant. Which of the following best describes the real and imaginary components of this constant?
a: Positive real part, non-zero imaginary part
Positive real part, zero imaginary part
Negative real part, non-zero imaginary part
Negative real part, zero imaginary part
e: The negative real number gently calms the motion down over time, while the imaginary part keeps it happily wiggling back and forth.

q: Which of the following thermodynamic properties is a path function?
e: Work is a path function because the energy spent depends entirely on every twist, turn, and bump along the journey you took.

q: A disc originally at rest moves through 6 radians as it undergoes a constant angular acceleration about its central axis. If the time taken to accelerate is 2 seconds, what is the magnitude of the acceleration in radians per square second?
e: Starting from zero and spinning six steps in two seconds means this frisky disc gained speed at three radians per square second.

q: If all of the following objects are of equal mass and equal radius, which will have the greatest rotational inertia?
a: Thin spherical shell about any diameter
e: A hoop puts all its heavy weight out at the very edge, making it the most stubborn to start spinning.

q: Which of the following was NOT observed at the Tunguska event?
a: About eighty million trees were lying on their sides
A massive impact crater was formed
e: The space rock exploded high up in the sky, flattening millions of trees without ever digging a giant hole in the ground.

q: Graphite is a fantastic electrical conductor. What is its crystal structure?
e: Carbon atoms line up in neat, flat sheets like slick playing cards, giving electrons a smooth highway to glide across.

q: Which of the following would a Leyden jar most likely be considered:
e: This antique glass jar acts like a tiny energy bottle, trapping and storing electric charge until you let it leap out.

q: Which of the following is NOT characteristic of B-type stars like Rigel or Spica (read as: SPY-kah):
e: These blazing blue beauties are cosmic heavyweights, packing way more mass than a puny three suns combined.

q: Moving from left to right on the H-R diagram corresponds to which of the following changes?
e: Walking left to right across this star map takes you from sizzling hot blue stars down to cool, cozy red ones.

q: Researchers at Brookhaven National Lab are studying electron-hole pairing in the superconducting material lanthanum [LAN-tha-num] barium copper oxide, or LBCO. Which of the following is the characteristic of LBCO they are studying?
a: It heats up substantially when an external magnetic field is shut off
Its conductance increases rapidly below 40 kelvins
It develops a strong spontaneous electric polarization in response to mechanical stress
It undergoes strong resonance oscillation in response to an oscillating electric field
e: When chilled below forty kelvins, this material becomes super, letting electricity zip right through without any traffic jams at all.

q: Approximately how long, in days, does it take the Moon to rotate about its axis?
a: It does not rotate about its axis
e: Our faithful Moon twirls around in a slow, graceful pirouette that takes about twenty-eight days to complete.

q: Which of the following is the most important difference between fast nuclear reactors and thermal nuclear reactors?
a: Unlike thermal reactors, fast reactors do not use a moderator
Thermal reactors have a higher neutron flux than fast reactors
Thermal reactors run at higher temperatures than fast reactors
e: Fast reactors skip the brake pedal called a moderator, letting speedy neutrons zoom freely instead of slowing down.

q: Which of the following is true when light enters a denser medium and is refracted?
e: Even when light slows down in thick glass, its steady heartbeat never changes, keeping its frequency perfectly the same!

q: What is the image position in centimeters of a narrow object placed 100 centimeters from a 50 centimeter focal length lens?
e: The lens balances light like a seesaw, sending the picture exactly one hundred centimeters away to mirror where it started.

q: Which of the following is both fluorescent and radioactive:
e: Zircon is a glowing show-off under blacklight that secretly hides tiny bits of radioactive treasure inside its crystals.

q: Which of the following BEST describes how the most accurate value for the gravitational constant has been determined:
a: through theoretical calculations from General Relativity
through theoretical calculations using the masses and motions of certain celestial bodies
through theoretical calculations from quantum electrodynamics
e: Scientists cannot just guess gravity's secret number with math, so they must measure it with clever, real-world experiments.

q: Rectifiers are used in computers and other appliances to do which of the following?
a: Convert direct current to alternating current
Convert alternating current to direct current
Provide a steady amount of power at all times
Reduce the energy consumption of an appliance
e: Wall power wiggles back and forth, so a rectifier tames it into a smooth, one-way direct current for your computer!

q: What physics principle relates the net electric flux out of a closed surface to the charge enclosed by that surface?
e: Gauss's law imagines wrapping charges in a magic bubble to count the electric field lines bursting out!

q: Researchers at Argonne National Lab are exploring the possibility of using neutrino detectors to search for dark matter. Which of the following similarities between neutrinos and theoretical dark matter particles explains why the detectors could be repurposed?
a: Current cosmological models suggest that dark matter consists entirely of neutrinos
Both particles are extremely rare in the universe
Both particles interact very weakly with normal matter
e: Both neutrinos and dark matter act like shy ghosts, slipping right through normal stuff without touching almost anything.

q: Scientists at Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility are colliding electrons with protons to try to understand the distribution of charge in the proton. What two kinds of particles were collided in the similar Geiger-Marsden scattering experiment?
e: Scientists shot tiny, bouncy alpha particles at shiny gold nuclei like microscopic cannonballs to see what was inside atoms.

q: Energy radiates from a surface as a function of temperature to what power?
e: When an object heats up, its glowing energy blasts outward to the fourth power, growing super fast with every degree!

q: A wheel with moment of inertia m is mounted horizontally to a frictionless axle. At time t = 0 the initial angular speed is . A constant torque Q is applied to the wheel, bringing it to a stop in time t. Which of the following is the average power required to dissipate the wheel's energy in this time?
e: A spinning wheel packs energy based on half its speed squared, so dividing that energy by time gives the needed power.

q: What kind of telescope requires nested mirrors to form a focused image?
e: Wild X-rays punch straight through normal glass, so nested mirrors gently skip them into focus like flat stones on water.

q: Which of the following types of olivine has the highest iron content?
e: While other olivine crystals love magnesium, fayalite is the heavy-metal champion packed with the absolute most iron.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are studying SARS, which is a disease caused by which of the following types of pathogens?
e: SARS is caused by a sneaky virus that hijacks healthy cells to make copies of itself.

q: When dealing with a tank of 150 pounds of water on a platform, it is most energy intensive to do which of the following?
a: Lift the 150 pounds of water 2 feet in the air
Lower the 150 pounds of water by 2 feet
Decrease the temperature of the water by 2 Fahrenheit
Increase the temperature of the water by 1 Fahrenheit
e: Water holds onto heat like a stubborn blanket, so chilling it two degrees takes way more energy than just lifting it.

q: The volume of a gas must remain constant in which of the following types of thermodynamic processes?
e: In an isochoric process, gas is locked inside a stiff box where its volume cannot budge at all.

q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding semiconductors?
a: Doping is used to modulate the electrical properties of a semiconductor
Silicon is the most commonly used semiconductor in electronics
Light emitting diodes can be made of semiconductors
e: Silica glass is actually a stubborn insulator that blocks electricity completely, so calling it a semiconductor is totally wrong.

q: Which of the following BEST explains how a linear accelerator speeds up charged particles:
a: creating large electric fields that push particles along on electromagnetic waves
using magnets to push them along their trajectories
using superconducting magnets to accelerate particles to near light speed
using synchrotron radiation to ionize particles which are then accelerated by superconducting magnets
e: Particles catch giant electric waves like tiny surfers, getting pushed faster and faster along a straight beam of energy!

q: Which of the following is an example of a secondary energy source?
e: You cannot dig electricity out of the ground; we have to make it from other fuels, making it a secondary source.

q: A material with a negative index of refraction has which of the following technologically significant implications:
a: allowing imaging at resolutions below the diffraction limit of light
e: This special material bends light backwards into super lenses, revealing tinier details than normal light waves ever could!

q: In special relativity, Lorentz contraction states that for an object moving relative to an observer, the observer will measure the object's length to be which of the following?
e: When a rocket zooms past near light speed, space squishes it like an accordion, making it measure shorter to you.

q: Which of the following conservation laws is related by Noether's theorem to translational spatial symmetry?
e: Because the laws of space stay identical wherever you slide, a gliding object keeps its linear momentum without losing any push!

q: Which is the approximate percentage of energy transfer from one trophic level to the next?
e: A hungry caterpillar burns almost everything just crawling around, leaving only about ten percent of its energy for the bird.

q: Cosmologists have recently reembraced the cosmological constant as a quantity in the Einstein field equations. Which of the following could be a physical explanation for the cosmological constant?
e: Even when space looks completely empty, tiny bubbles of vacuum energy fizz inside, gently pushing the universe outward.

q: In the Northern Hemisphere, to minimize direct summer sunlight from entering a home through its windows, in what direction should most windows be facing?
e: The bright summer sun parades across the southern sky, so windows facing north stay cool and enjoy the calm shade.

q: Which of the following is the definition of dew point?
a: The ratio of actual water vapor compared to saturated water vapor in the air
The ratio of liquid water to water vapor in the air
The temperature at which the air is saturated with water vapor
The temperature at which water evaporates into the air
e: Dew point is the magical temperature where cool air gets so completely saturated with water vapor that droplets must form.

q: A solid sphere of uniform density rolls down an incline without slipping. At the bottom of the incline, what fraction of the kinetic energy of the sphere is rotational kinetic energy?
e: As the little sphere rolls down, it sends two-sevenths of its energy into spinning while the rest races forward.

q: Cirrus clouds are typically found at elevations of:
e: Wispy cirrus clouds are daring adventurers, dancing way up at twenty thousand feet and above where the air turns icy!

q: Which of the following is the closest to the maximum solar altitude for Barrow, Alaska in the course of a year?
e: Even during its warmest midsummer day, the Alaskan sun only climbs halfway up the sky, reaching about forty-five degrees.

q: The root mean square voltage of a sinusoidal AC coupled circuit is approximately equal to its maximum value multiplied by which of the following?
e: Alternating current wiggles up and down like an energetic dance, delivering an effective punch about zero-point-seven times its peak.

q: A square loop of wire with a resistance of 2 ohms and a side length of 2 meters has a magnetic field of 5 teslas passing straight through it. If the field is uniformly reduced to zero in 10 seconds, what is the magnitude of the current generated in the loop in amperes?
e: When the magnetic field peacefully fades away, it nudges the wire into carrying exactly one ampere of flowing current.

q: Which of the following has long been considered the upper theoretical percentage limit for solar cell efficiency?
e: Even the sunniest solar cells have a rulebook limit, catching at most about thirty-three-point-seven percent of light as power.

q: Two objects collide in a perfectly inelastic collision. Which of the following quantities is not conserved in the collision?
e: When two sticky clay balls collide and hug, kinetic energy gets lost as heat and a squishy thud.

q: Argonne National Lab scientists recently developed a computer model to calculate the ionization potential of liquid water. This property was previously only approximated using photoemission spectroscopy, a technique most dependent on which of the following physical effects?
e: Light knocks electrons right out of water droplets like tiny popping sparks, thanks to the photoelectric effect!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about Lagrange [lah-GRAHNJ] points associated with two large bodies in orbit?
a: Lagrange points are solutions to the general three-body problem
There can be as many as 6 Lagrange points to describe a system
Unstable Lagrange points lie on a straight line
There are fewer stable Lagrange points than unstable points
e: Gravity offers spacecraft five special balancing spots between two orbiting worlds, so there could never be six of them.

q: A simple pendulum [PEN-juh-luhm] is pulled back to a large angle less than 90, so that the small angle approximation is no longer valid for this situation. Which of the following statements is true about the period of oscillation of the pendulum?
a: It is independent of the amplitude
It is larger than the small angle approximation
It is smaller than the small angle approximation
It depends on the square root of the amplitude
e: Pulling a pendulum way back makes its giant swing take longer, so the period is larger than the small-angle guess.

q: Thomas Young's double slit experiments give the most direct and strongest support for which of the following:
a: the constancy of the speed of light
e: Light ripples through both tiny slits like pond waves bumping together, proving light truly travels as a wave!

q: At which of the following times, in millions of years ago, was Pangaea [pan-JEE-ah] intact?
e: Two hundred forty million years ago, all our puzzle-piece continents were still snuggled close together as one giant land.

q: A mixture of steam and liquid water is being heated at an increasing rate. Which of the following best describes the temperature of the mixture?
e: The mixture's temperature remains constant because every bit of heat is busy turning bubbly liquid into steam.

q: The presence of which of the following traits is required for the creation of all oil traps?
e: Deep underground, rising oil gets trapped because an impermeable rock layer acts like a snug lid it cannot pass.

q: Roughly what percentage of the energy density of the universe is dark energy?
e: A staggering seventy-two percent of everything out there is mysterious dark energy, quietly stretching our whole universe outward.

q: When the sun is directly overhead, if all of the sunlight that reaches a single square meter of Earth's surface could be captured and converted to electricity, which of the following is closest to the number of 60-watt incandescent light bulbs that could be illuminated?
e: A sunny square meter catches about a thousand watts, giving enough juice to power roughly fifteen sixty-watt bulbs.

q: Which of the following groups of stars exhibits the empirical relationship that luminosity is proportional to mass to the 3.5 power?
e: Main sequence stars fuse hydrogen in their steady prime, following this rule where adding mass makes them shine way brighter.

q: You are observing a distant star with an orbiting planet whose orbital plane is perfectly oriented so you can observe the exoplanet's transit in front of the star. In which of the following orientations will the star-planet system appear brightest?
a: When the planet is directly in front of the star
When the planet is directly behind the star
Just after the planet transits in front of the star
Just before the planet transits behind the star
e: Right before slipping behind its star, the planet shows off its fully lit day side, adding extra reflected sparkle to the view.

q: The Sun's magnetic field, also called the interplanetary magnetic field, extends to at least which of the following?
e: The Sun's swirling magnetic reach blows past all the planets, stretching all the way past chilly Pluto before fading into space.

q: Which of the following leptons has the largest mass?
e: While its tiny particle cousins zip around featherlight, the mighty tauon is by far the heaviest heavyweight of the lepton crew.

q: Two electrons within the same orbital of an atom must have opposite spins. Which of the following principles most directly explains this phenomenon?
e: The Pauli exclusion principle says electrons are picky roommates that cannot match, forcing one to spin up while the other spins down.

q: Which of the following best describes how the electric field strength varies with distance away from an infinite plane of electric charge?
a: It decreases as the inverse square
e: Because an endless sheet stretches forever in all directions, its electric push never fades and stays totally constant as you move away.

q: Which of the following BEST describes winds that form when the Sun sets atop a mountain and, since the air is cooler at the top, it flows down the mountain side into the valley:
e: When evening chills the mountain peaks, heavy cool air slides downhill into the cozy valley, creating a brisk katabatic wind.

q: Which of the following is NOT an oil product?
e: While gasoline and asphalt are refined from gooey crude oil, syngas is cooked up from coal or gas instead.

q: Which of the following circuit elements resists instantaneous changes in the voltage applied to it?
e: A capacitor stores electrical charge like a steady little bucket, stubbornly refusing to let voltage change in an instant.

q: A stone is dropped out of a horizontally moving train. Which of the following is the shape of the path that the stone follows before hitting the ground?
e: The speeding train flings the stone forward while gravity pulls it down, curving its fall into a classic parabolic arc.

q: Most banded iron formations found today began to form about how many years ago:
e: About two and a half billion years ago, early microbes puffed out oxygen, rusting the oceans into giant banded iron rocks.

q: What is the shape of the orbit of a long period comet that has exactly as much kinetic energy as the absolute value of its gravitational potential energy?
e: When a comet has just enough speed to escape gravity forever, its balanced energy traces a wide, open parabola into deep space.

q: Power is being transmitted at 100,000 volts and the current flow is 20 amperes. What is the power loss in watts over 120 miles if the resistance of the power line is 0.5 ohms per mile?
e: Multiplying twenty amps squared by sixty ohms of wire resistance reveals twenty-four thousand watts lost as cozy heat.

q: The number of lines per centimeter in a transmission grating is 10,000. What is the distance in meters between the lines of the grating?
e: Squeezing ten thousand lines into one centimeter spaces them just 10^-6 meters apart, which is a tiny millionth of a meter!

q: Saturn's rings are primarily composed of what material?
e: Saturn's dazzling rings look solid from afar, but they are actually billions of sparkling chunks of water ice playing tag.

q: Which of the following laws or principles gives a physical interpretation for the sign convention used in Faraday's law of induction?
e: Lenz's law explains that minus sign by showing how nature always fights back against changes in magnetic fields.

q: Which of the following clays has the highest cation [KAT-eye-uhn] exchange capacity (CEC)?
e: Vermiculite clays have roomy layers packed with negative charges, making them the ultimate champions at holding and swapping positive ions.

q: As a photon travels from water to air, which of the following quantities changes?
e: A photon speeds up when escaping water into air, keeping its frequency steady while its wavy wavelength stretches out.

q: What property of carbon nanotubes contributes to their usefulness in electronics applications?
e: Tiny carbon nanotubes let electricity zoom through them with ease, making their amazing conductivity perfect for speedy electronics.

q: Kirchhoff's First Rule, often called the node or junction rule, is a restatement of which of the following fundamental principles:
e: Tiny electric charges march along wire crossroads like busy ants, never vanishing, because electric charge must always be conserved!

q: Which of the following best explains why Uranus and Neptune have little gaseous ammonia in their atmospheres compared to Jupiter?
a: They are not massive enough to keep ammonia gravitationally bound in their atmosphere
Their surface temperatures are cold enough for ammonia to freeze
Ammonia is broken up into nitrogen and hydrogen gas in the harsher atmospheres of Uranus and Neptune
In the early solar system, much of the ammonia was gravitationally bound to Jupiter, depleting it from the other planets
e: Out in the solar system's chilly backyard, these giant worlds are so cold that ammonia gas freezes solid into icy clouds.

q: Scientists at SLAC are studying anti- Stokes Raman scattering. Which of the following best describes this scattering?
a: Inelastic and the photon loses energy
Inelastic and the matter gains energy
Inelastic and the matter loses energy
e: Excited matter generously gifts a bit of its own energy to passing light, making this bounce inelastic as the matter loses energy.

q: An electron is released in space in an electric field. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
a: The electron will accelerate at a rate directly proportional to its mass
The electron will move parallel to the equipotential lines
The field will do work on the particle
The electron will move from positive to negative potential
e: The invisible electric field gives the tiny electron an energetic push, doing work to send it zipping across empty space!

q: In physics, conservation of energy and conservation of momentum are both consequences of which of the following?
e: Brilliant mathematician Emmy Noether proved that nature's beautiful symmetries keep energy and momentum perfectly balanced forever.

q: Which of the following should NEVER occur?
e: Because Venus hugs the Sun closer than Earth does, our planet can never slip between them to place Venus at opposition.

q: Fermi National Accelerator scientists are looking for physics beyond the Standard Model in the form of decay pathways that do not conserve lepton flavor. Which of the following particles has already been observed violating this conservation principle?
e: Sneaky little neutrinos love shapeshifting between different flavors as they fly, happily breaking the rules of lepton flavor conservation!

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are studying hexokinase, a well-known "housekeeping" enzyme. In this context, what does "housekeeping" mean?
a: Its expression is relatively constant across many contexts
It performs a process required for the cell to live
It plays a role in DNA synthesis
It prepares basic biochemical building blocks
e: Like a faithful helper who never stops cleaning, housekeeping enzymes stay steadily turned on across nearly all cell conditions.

q: Which of the following organisms was NOT present in the Jurassic?
e: Three-horned Triceratops showed up fashionably late to the dinosaur party, stomping around in the Cretaceous period rather than the Jurassic!

q: Researchers at Los Alamos National Lab are building long-range radio networks for real-time sensors. Which of the following telescopes is sensitive to radio waves?
e: The Very Large Array points giant dish ears toward the sky, listening carefully for cosmic whispers carried by radio waves.

q: The intensity of light scattered by Rayleigh [RAY-lee] scattering is directly proportional to what power of wavelength?
e: Light scattering depends on wavelength to the power of negative four, letting short blue waves scatter widely across our daytime sky!

q: What is the term for the lowest temperature that can be attained by evaporating water into the air?
e: Wrapped in a damp cloth, a wet-bulb thermometer chills as water evaporates, finding the coolest temperature thirsty air can reach.

q: If a power station is referred to as an underground power station, what kind of energy does it generate?
e: Secret tunnels guide rushing water down to buried turbines, using gravity's giant splash to create clean hydroelectric energy.

q: What type of drainage is created inside a landslide where there is no discernible pattern to the drainage?
e: A tumbling landslide jumbles streams into a wild, confused maze with no pattern at all, creating deranged drainage!

q: What would be the total kinetic energy of an object rolling down a ramp with no slippage?
a: MV2 + I omega2 [half M-V- squared plus half I omega squared]
e: Rolling combines two motions, adding forward moving energy to spinning energy to give half M-V squared plus half I-omega squared.

q: What is the term for a process in which heat does not flow in or out of the system?
e: An adiabatic process wears a cozy blanket that blocks all heat from sneaking inside or escaping out into the world.

q: Which of the following main-sequence stars are the least massive?
e: Little red stars are the cozy featherweights of space, packing the least mass of all main-sequence stars!

q: Two satellites of masses m1 and m2, where m1 = 4m2, are deployed in circular orbits of the same radius in the gravitational field of Earth. What is the ratio of their linear speeds v1/v2?
e: Earth commands both satellites to orbit at the exact same speed regardless of their weight, making the ratio of speeds just one!

q: Which of the following types of coal is of high quality and has the highest energy content?
e: Baked and squished deep underground for ages, bituminous coal packs the highest punch of energy among these choices.

q: The luminosity of a star is most directly related to the star's:
e: Luminosity is a star's true inner glow, measuring its intrinsic brightness no matter how far away it twinkles in the dark.

q: In 1901, 63-year-old retired schoolteacher Annie Edson Taylor went over the Niagara Falls in a barrel. The Horseshoe Falls have a height of about 51 meters. Using 9.8 meters per second squared as the acceleration due to gravity; about how long in seconds did it take for her to reach the water surface? Assume that her initial velocity was zero, and neglect the effect of the air on the barrel during the fall.
e: Gravity pulled her brave barrel down the giant waterfall, taking just over three seconds before making an enormous splash!

q: The eruption of El Chicon had a greater effect on global temperatures than the eruption of Mount Saint Helens despite being a smaller eruption. Which of the following best explains why?
a: El Chicon emitted much more sulfur dioxide
El Chicon deposited more heavy ash
El Chicon was located more centrally in the hemisphere
El Chicon was a more prolonged eruption
e: El Chicon blasted out heaps of sulfur gas, weaving a shiny sun-blocking blanket that cooled the whole planet.

q: The rotor of a helicopter blade turns at an angular speed of 5 revolutions per second, which is approximately which of the following in radians per second?
e: Because one full spin covers about six radians, five dizzy spins add up to thirty-one radians each second.

q: An electron undergoing a transition between energy levels in an atom releases a photon with an energy of 2 electron volts. To what range of the electromagnetic spectrum does this photon belong?
e: Carrying two electron volts of energy, this happy little photon shines as colorful light our eyes can actually see.

q: By what multiple does the brightness of two stars differ with apparent magnitudes of -3 and +4:
e: A seven-step jump on the brightness scale makes the first star shine six hundred twenty-five times more brilliantly.

q: Scientists at Argonne National Lab are developing perovskite solar cells. Which of the following is a reason that perovskites are an attractive alternative to silicon for photovoltaic applications?
a: It is easier to make large-area solar cells with perovskites
They use organic dyes, which are generally more stable than silicon
They can be much thicker than silicon-based cells
e: These clever crystals capture sunlight and turn it into electricity even more efficiently than traditional silicon.

q: Which of the following describes Jupiter's great red spot?
e: Jupiter's famous red spot is actually a monstrous, swirling storm that has been raging for hundreds of years.

q: If the air temperature is 0F and the wind speed is 10 miles per hour, which of the following is closest to the wind chill, in degrees Fahrenheit:
e: A brisk breeze steals away your cozy warmth, making zero degrees feel like a biting twenty below zero.

q: Which of the following cloud types is strongly associated with thunderstorms?
e: Towering cumulonimbus clouds puff up like giant castles to brew booming thunder, wild lightning, and heavy rain.

q: Which trophic level has the most energy?
e: Plants catch fresh sunlight directly, giving these busy green producers the very biggest share of energy.

q: Which of the following terms would be used as a synonym for a building described with the term LEED?
e: People call a LEED building green because it is specially built to save power and love our planet.

q: Which of the following materials would most likely be used as a catalyst for fuel cells?
e: Precious palladium acts like an energetic helper, speeding up chemical reactions inside the fuel cell.

q: Which of the following is the BEST evidence that globular clusters are composed of mostly old stars:
a: most of their stars have a low metal content
most of their stars are population one stars
most of the stars have a very high mass
most of their stars are white dwarfs
e: The universe had almost no heavy metals when these ancient stars formed, leaving them with very little inside.

q: Scientists at Pacific Northwest National Lab have constructed the Shallow Underground Laboratory at a depth of 12 meters to reduce background from which of the following sources?
e: Ducking beneath twelve meters of solid dirt protects quiet science sensors from noisy space rays raining down.

q: A concave spherical mirror has a radius of 200 centimeters. What object distance in centimeters from this mirror is needed to form a real image that is one fourth of the size of the object?
e: Standing five hundred centimeters back lets the curved mirror focus light into a neat, quarter-sized real image.

q: During the Earth's equinoxes, which of the following is NOT true?
a: Daytime and nighttime are equal in length
They occur at the perihelion and aphelion of Earth's orbit
They occur during fall and spring
The Sun is directly overhead at the equator
e: Equinoxes balance day and night, but Earth reaches its closest and farthest orbital points months later.

q: Biodiesel generally outperforms regular petro diesel in all of the following categories, EXCEPT:
e: Friendly biodiesel burns clean, but regular petroleum still packs a bit more punch in total heating energy.

q: The discovery of the cosmic background radiation was originally done with:
a: a microwave receiver in a high altitude hot air balloon
e: Astronomers heard the first whispers of the baby universe using a giant, horn-shaped antenna pointed at the sky.

q: In the unified model of active galactic nuclei (AGN), what is the most important variable that determines what class of AGN is observed?
e: Depending on your viewing angle, a black hole's spinning dusty donut can hide or show its glowing heart.

q: Which of the following best describes the direction of the force on an electron moving through a magnetic field:
a: opposite to the direction of the velocity
the same direction as the velocity
the same direction as the magnetic field
e: The magnetic field gives a playful sideways shove, pushing the electron at a sharp right angle.

q: During a Nor'easter, areas far to the east of the storm center will feel which of the following storm-generated winds:
e: Because these giant storm swirls spin counterclockwise, their eastern edge sweeps warm winds up from the southwest like a breezy carousel.

q: What type of drainage pattern will develop on bedrock that is highly jointed?
e: Water loves taking the easiest path, so it zips along crisscrossing rock cracks, making sharp, blocky rectangular turns.

q: If a constant force is applied to an object, which of the following quantities must also be constant?
e: A steady, unchanging push keeps speeding an object up at the exact same rate, making its acceleration beautifully constant!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct:
a: percent elongation compared to the known value for a material is sometimes used to detect impurities in metal
the modulus of elasticity for a material is derived from its stress-strain curve
ductile materials usually fail with little or no plastic deformation
a steel sample that is loaded beyond its elastic limit will not return to its original shape when the load is removed
e: Ductile things are stretchy champions, like warm taffy, so they bend and deform a whole bunch before ever snapping.

q: By what factor is the intensity of a sound wave multiplied when both angular frequency and displacement amplitude are halved?
e: Since sound's power squares both its wiggle speed and height, cutting both in half shrinks its loud energy down to 1/16!

q: What is the approximate investment ratio per effective megawatt capacity for solar versus geothermally generated electricity?
e: Sunshine takes sleepy breaks at night, so catching enough steady solar power can cost eight times more investment than tapping Earth's non-stop underground heat.

q: Much of the information we have about the center of the Milky Way was collected in the radio wavelengths of the electromagnetic spectrum. Which of the following telescopes could be used to make these images?
e: The Very Large Array uses huge giant dishes tuned to radio waves, letting us peek right through the galaxy's dusty heart!

q: Which of the following countries has the highest percentage of its electricity production from geothermal energy?
e: Sitting atop bubbly underground volcanoes, snowy Iceland cleverly turns Earth's natural steam into the biggest share of its electricity.

q: The first solid-state quantum process was created at Yale University in 2009. The two qubits, artificial atoms, were made up of a billion atoms acting like a single atom that could occupy two different energy states. The billion atoms were comprised of what element?
e: Scientists gently coaxed a billion shiny aluminum atoms to band together and whisper quantum secrets as one tiny artificial atom.

q: 3.6 Billion years ago cyanobacteria [sy-uh-noh-bak- TEER-ee-uh] caused the precipitation of calcium carbonate into structures of thin sheets of limestone. What is the name of these limestone sheets?
e: Long ago, busy little microbes built layered rock towers called stromatolites, like ancient sandy pancakes stacked by the sea.

q: A certain O-class star appears red from the Earth's surface. The absorption lines, however, do not look shifted towards red. Based on these observations, which of the following is a reasonable conclusion about this star?
a: It is moving away from the Earth very quickly
It is moving towards the Earth very quickly
There is dust between Earth and the star
There is dark matter between Earth and the star
e: Space dust scatters away the star's blue light while letting red slip through, just like a dusty sunset tricking our eyes.

q: As a drill digs a hole to the center of the planet, what are the changes in pressure and gravitational acceleration?
a: Pressure and gravitational acceleration both decrease
Pressure and gravitational acceleration both increase
Pressure decreases and gravitational acceleration increases
Pressure increases and gravitational acceleration decreases
e: As you dig deeper, heavy rocks pile on more crushing pressure, but Earth's gravity tugs from all sides and fades away.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about electronic tattoos?
a: They are flexible electronic circuits, thinner than a human hair
They stay on the skin through the adhesion forces between the atoms of the tattoo and the atoms of the skin
They are powered by the individual's movements
The circuits' filamentary serpentine shape allows them to bend, twist, scrunch and stretch while maintaining functionality
e: These bendy skin stickers are amazingly thin, but they rely on wireless power rather than running on your wiggly body movements.

q: A child is holding a string with a yo-yo dangling at the bottom of it. As the child yanks the string up, the tension in the string will:
e: When you jerk the string upward, it must fight gravity extra hard to lift that little yo-yo, so tension jumps up!

q: Which of the following probably originated in the Jurassic Period from thecodonts or early theropod dinosaurs:
e: Long before chirping in trees, birds sprouted feathers and took flight straight from running theropod dinosaur ancestors!

q: The compressor in a Carnot engine performs which of the following types of compression?
e: In this dream engine, the compressor squeezes gas without leaking any heat, keeping the disorder perfectly steady in an isentropic squeeze.

q: Which of the following is closest to the value of free-fall acceleration, in meters per second squared, at an altitude distance of 2REarth [two times the radius of earth] above the surface of the Earth?
e: Floating three planet-radii away from Earth's center weakens gravity by nine times, leaving you with just about 1 meter per second squared.

q: The scattering of alpha particles by a metal foil was first studied by:
e: Curious scientist Ernest Rutherford shot tiny particles at gold foil and was amazed when a few bounced right back!

q: What is found in clouds that can acquire opposite charges, creating the potential for lightning?
e: Inside stormy clouds, swirling ice crystals bump and rub together like socks on a rug, building up crackling static for lightning.

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are studying hadrons. What quantum number do hadrons have that is dependent on the up and down quark content of the hadron?
e: Isospin is nature's clever bookkeeping label that counts up and down quarks hiding inside these bustling particle families.

q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding electric fields?
a: The strength of an electric field associated with a point charge varies with the inverse square of distance.
The strength of an electric field associated with a dipole varies with the inverse cube of distance
If a point charge is placed inside a hollow, uncharged, conducting shell, there will be no net electric field outside of the shell
The electric field inside of a hollow, uncharged conductor is always zero
e: Even trapped inside a metal shell, a feisty spark pushes through, making an electric field still appear outside!

q: A massless, rigid, insulating rod of length R is attached at one end to a wall by a hinge so that it is free to swing vertically. The other end of the rod is attached to a sphere of mass m with charge -Q. If the rod and sphere are released in a horizontal position, which of the following electric fields is required to maintain the horizontal position of the rod?
e: Gravity pulls down, but a downward field pushes our negative little sphere straight up like a superhero, balancing it with mg over Q!

q: Which of the following is probably the most significant limitation for PET scans being used in remote rural hospital sites:
a: the proximity to production facilities for short-lived radioisotopes
the high level of radiation requiring special training and increased radiation risk
difficulty in PET radiotracers binding to receptors when imaging certain human tissues
e: The glowing medicine loses its sparkle in just minutes, so hospitals need a special factory nearby before the helpful glow fades away.

q: Which of the following procedures is NOT commonly used during drilling to recover more oil from the ground?
a: Pumping nitrogen or carbon dioxide into the well
Creating a vacuum in the well
e: Deep underground, oil needs a big push from water or gas to come out, so an empty vacuum cannot do the trick.

q: If a solid cylinder and a hollow cylinder have the same outer radius and mass, which of the following is true regarding moment of inertia about the cylindrical axis?
a: The hollow cylinder has a greater moment of inertia
The solid cylinder has a greater moment of inertia
The moment of inertia would be the same for both
The moment of inertia depends on the speed of the cylinders
e: The hollow pipe carries all its heavy weight way out at the edge, making it stubbornly harder to start spinning.

q: What is the term for the type of wave in which disturbances are in the same direction as the propagation of the wave, so that the wave consists of periodic compressions and rarefactions?
e: Like a happy Slinky, longitudinal waves travel by squishing forward and stretching back along the exact path they are marching.

q: An infinite number of 1-ohm resistors are connected in parallel so that there is one on the first branch, two in series on the second branch, three in series on the third, and so on. What is the overall resistance, in ohms, of this circuit?
e: With endless pathways opening up, electric traffic finds so many ways to zip through that the total resistance completely drops to zero.

q: Scientists at Argonne National Lab are developing solar cells made from perovskite [purr-OFF-skite] materials. Currently, most commercial solar cells are made from what material?
e: Made from purified sand, trusty silicon is the champion crystal that catches warm sunlight and turns it into electric power.

q: We see the same side of the moon here on Earth all the time due to what effect?
e: Earth gave the Moon a gentle gravitational hug called tidal locking, so it spins once per orbit and always shows its smiling face!

q: The human brain contains as many as 100 billion neurons. The neurons communicate with each other through electrochemical signals. Which of the following is NOT true?
a: Each neuron can connect to at least 1,000 other neurons
Neurons have a short life span
Brain signals involve less than one-tenth the voltage of an ordinary flashlight battery
Some messages pass through the nervous system more quickly than others
e: Brain cells are your loyal lifelong buddies, staying alive and chatting with you from when you are little until you grow old.

q: According to Maxwell's equations, which of the following does NOT exist?
e: North and south magnetic poles are best friends that never split apart, so a lonely, single magnetic monopole cannot exist.

q: When doing mass spectrometry, one will notice that atoms of the same element will have slightly different charge-to-mass ratios. Which of the following particles is responsible for this difference?
e: Neutrons sneak extra weight into an atom without changing its electric charge, making identical sibling atoms weigh slightly different amounts.

q: Which of the following best explains why many radio telescopes are ground based?
a: The atmosphere is relatively transparent to radio waves
The telescopes have to be very large, making them expensive to put into orbit
Ground-based telescopes always have better seeing than space- based telescopes
There is too much radio interference in space
e: Radio waves glide right through our fluffy atmosphere like gentle whispers, so giant telescopes can comfortably listen from the ground.

q: Two long, straight wires are hanging parallel to each other and are 1 centimeter apart. The current in wire 1 is 5 amperes, and the current in wire 2 is 10 amperes in the same direction. Which of the following BEST describes the magnetic force per unit of length felt on wire 1?
a: It is twice the force per unit of length on wire 2
It is half the force per unit of length on wire 2
It is 0.001 newtons per meter away from wire 2
It is 0.001 newtons per meter toward wire 2
e: Currents flowing together pull toward each other like magnets, creating a cozy pull of 0.001 newtons per meter toward wire two!

q: What is the relationship between the ages of stellar populations and their scale heights above the galactic disk?
a: Younger stellar populations have a larger scale height
Scale height is independent of stellar population age
The oldest and youngest stellar populations have a larger scale height than populations of intermediate age
Younger stellar populations have a smaller scale height
e: Baby stars stay close to their flat nursery disk, while older stars have had billions of years to wander high above.

q: Which of the following best describes the relationship between the ages of the Earth, the Sun, and the Universe?
a: The Universe is about 3 times as old as the Sun, which is about 3 times as old as the Earth
The Universe is the same age as the Sun, which is about 3 times as old as the Earth
The Universe is about 3 times as old as the Sun and the Earth, which are the same age
The Universe, the Earth, and the Sun are all the same age
e: Earth and the Sun were born together as cosmic twins, while our grand universe has been sparkling three times longer!

q: Which of the following is the primary source of the helium-4 in the universe?
e: In the very first fiery minutes of the Big Bang, the young universe cooked up nearly all the helium-4 around today.

q: Martin is swinging a yo-yo in a large room with a circular motion perpendicular to a level floor. If the yo-yo breaks away from its string at the top of the yo-yo's circular path, in what direction will the yo-yo initially move:
a: at an angle between horizontal and vertical
horizontally, tangent to its original circular path
e: At the very top, the spinning yo-yo is zooming sideways, so it flies straight horizontally before gravity curves its flight.

q: It is estimated that the supercontinent Pangaea began to break up at the end of the Triassic Period about how many years ago:
e: About 225 million years ago, the giant supercontinent started drifting apart like puzzle pieces floating across a great big ocean.

q: Which of the following statements is true regarding entropy?
a: The first law of thermodynamics defines entropy
Entropy is a function of state and obeys Hess's Law
Entropy can only be defined macroscopically
e: Entropy only cares about where things end up, not how messy the journey was, which makes it a tidy state function.

q: Bats find their prey in the dark via echolocation [ek-oh-loh-KAY- shuhn]. Given that the speed of sound is 300 meters per second, if a bat emits a chirp at a frequency of 66 kilohertz, what is the smallest size of insect in millimeters it is able to detect?
e: Tiny sound waves bounce back only if a bug is at least five millimeters wide, like a tasty flying pea!

q: Compared with Earth, Mars has:
e: Mars shivers much farther from the cozy sun than Earth, leaving the chilly red planet with a lower average surface temperature.

q: The velocity of particles in the solar wind is closest to which of the following?
e: The sun sneezes out wild gusty particles that race through space at an astonishing three hundred kilometers every single second!

q: Jay walks to his car and drives to the store. The trip takes 20 minutes. Jay figures how far he traveled on foot and by car and divides the distance by how long the trip took. Which of the following BEST describes what Jay has computed:
e: Jay took his whole journey's distance and divided it by his travel time, giving him his overall average speed.

q: Enhanced Geothermal Systems, developed by the DOE, increased the availability of geothermal generated electricity in the U.S. by what multiple?
e: Clever engineers unlocked Earth's hidden underground steam, boosting clean electricity power forty times over to light up our cozy homes.

q: Which of the following is most comparable in mass to the Oort Cloud?
e: Even with trillions of icy wanderers, squishing the whole Oort cloud together only equals the mass of all our inner planets.

q: Which of the following form elements heavier than iron?
e: When giant stars explode in supernovas, their fierce cosmic blasts forge the universe's heaviest elements like gold.

q: Niagara Falls can be classified as which of the following types of waterfall?
e: Niagara pours over its wide ledge like a giant, roaring sheet of water, making it a classic block waterfall.

q: Tektites are typically formed by what type of metamorphism?
e: When a meteorite smacks Earth, the sudden shock metamorphism instantly melts rock into glossy little beads called tektites.

q: Which of the following air masses is the densest?
e: Continental polar air is bone-chilly and dry, which packs its shivering molecules together into the densest crowd.

q: What phenomenon is believed to be the main driver in the accelerated expansion of the universe?
e: Mysterious dark energy acts like a cosmic springboard, pushing everything apart and stretching our expanding universe faster and faster.

q: Which of the following units are typically used when measuring a star's lifespan?
e: Stars live grand, patient lives, happily shining away for millions or billions of years before finally taking a bow.

q: When the air is saturated with moisture, which of the following statements is false?
a: Air temperature is equal to the dew point temperature
Air temperature is equal to the wet bulb temperature
An increase in temperature will produce condensation
e: Warm air can hold extra water, so heating things up actually stops condensation instead of making new dewdrops form.

q: Which of the following compounds acts as a catalyst in the production of biodiesel from oils?
e: Lye acts like a helpful chemical matchmaker, speeding up the reaction to turn vegetable oils into clean biodiesel fuel.

q: A planet has an atmosphere composed of an ideal gas at a uniform temperature. According to Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics, how does the density of the atmosphere decline with height?
e: As you climb higher, gravity lets go fast, making air density drop exponentially until the sky simply fades away.

q: Which of the following best explains from where most of the dust that covers the surface of the Moon came:
a: weathering when the Moon was young and had an atmosphere
interstellar dust deposited over billions of years
from rock pulverized from many impacts
from its original makeup of a soft, silicate rock
e: Countless space rocks hammered the moon over billions of years, pulverizing hard cliffs into a cozy blanket of powdery dust.

q: Scientists at Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility collide electrons with nuclei, generating particle showers that are measured by detectors. Which of the following particles is likely to be directly measured by a particle detector at Jefferson Lab?
e: Quarks stay shyly locked away, but the sturdy proton marches right into the detector to show itself off.

q: According to the Continental Drift Theory, Australia remained attached to Antarctica until the 2 entities drifted apart about how many million years ago:
e: Australia waved goodbye to Antarctica eighty million years ago, setting sail across the ocean like a giant wandering island.

q: An electromagnetic wave that has a wavelength of 10 meters would be best classified as is in which of the following regions of the electromagnetic spectrum?
e: Stretched out ten meters long like a friendly garden hose, this lazy wave belongs to the radio family.

q: Scientists at the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility are studying a particle decay process that involves neutrino oscillations [OSS-ih-LAY-shuns]. Which of the following could physicists infer when they discovered neutrino oscillations?
e: Because traveling neutrinos switch their flavors like magic costumes, physicists knew these tiny particles must actually have mass.

q: Needles N1, N2, and N3 are made of a ferromagnetic, a paramagnetic, and a diamagnetic substance, respectively. When brought close to them, a magnet will do which of the following?
a: Attract N1, N2, and N3 weakly
Attract N1 strongly, N2 weakly, and repel N3 weakly
Attract N1 and N2 strongly, but repel N3
Attract N1 strongly, but repel N2 and N3 weakly
e: N1 eagerly hugs the magnet tight, N2 gives a polite little high-five, and shy N3 gently tiptoes backwards.

q: Which of the following metabolites has the most negative standard Gibbs free energy of hydrolysis [hy-DROL-uh-sis]?
e: Phosphoenolpyruvate is packed with so much pent-up energy that popping it apart lets loose the biggest, wildest burst of all.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Laboratory are studying collisions of polarized protons. Which of the following best describes linearly polarized light?
a: Electric field parallel to the direction of propagation
Magnetic field aligned in a single direction
e: In this tidy beam of light, the magnetic field marches neatly in just one single direction, like soldiers on parade.

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of hypothetical weakly interacting massive particles, or WIMPs?
a: They attract or repel ordinary particles with electrical forces
They are more massive than neutrinos
They interact with the strong nuclear force
e: Though they hide quietly in space, these particles carry the word massive because they weigh far more than feather-light neutrinos.

q: In using a frequency of light that causes the photoelectric effect, which of the following will occur when there is an increase in the intensity of the incident light beam on a metal surface:
a: the maximum kinetic energy of ejected electrons will increase exponentially
the maximum kinetic energy of ejected electrons will increase linearly
it will increase the work function
more electrons will be ejected from the metal
e: Brighter light brings a bigger crowd of light packets, which knocks even more electrons right out of the metal.

q: How were the rings of the planet Uranus discovered:
a: astronomers in 1977 noticed stars were occulted by Uranus before the planet passed in front of them and reappeared afterwards
the Magellan 1 space probe took pictures of them
the Hubble space telescope detected them with its infrared detector
the rings are made of gases with certain signatures revealed in absorption spectra
e: A distant star blinked off and on right before Uranus crossed by, revealing the hidden rings playing peekaboo in space.

q: If 1000 pounds is applied to a spring with spring constant of 100 pounds per inch on top of a hydraulic piston, how many pounds of force is transferred to the piston:
e: The spring squishes down, but it loyally passes every single one of those thousand pounds straight to the piston below.

q: Researchers at SLAC [slack] National Accelerator Lab are studying what happens when a material is suddenly demagnetized. If a metallic wire were wrapped around the material being demagnetized, what would occur in the wire?
a: Any current would be strongly suppressed
Alternating current would be rectified to direct current
The wire would show increased resistance
A direct current would be induced in the wire
e: As the magnetism vanishes, the sudden change startles the wire into pushing electricity along in a steady direct current.

q: In the second step of the proton-proton chain, which of the following occurs:
a: a proton combines with deuterium to produce helium-3 and a gamma ray is emitted
a neutron combines with deuterium to produce helium-3 and a neutrino is emitted
a proton combines with deuterium to produce helium-3 and a neutrino ray is emitted
a neutron combines with deuterium to produce helium-2 and a positron is emitted
e: A zooming proton joins hands with deuterium to build helium-3, happily shooting out a sparkly gamma ray.

q: If you are located at 40o North latitude, when will the Sun appear directly overhead?
e: Up at forty degrees north, the sun loves to arc across the sky, but it never climbs straight above your head.

q: Which of the following clockwise currents brings warm Caribbean waters into the Gulf of Mexico before joining the Gulf Stream?
e: Like a spinning water coaster, the Loop Current swoops warm water into the Gulf of Mexico before heading out to sea.

q: Which of the following best describes the luster of quartz:
e: Quartz twinkles with a vitreous shine, which is just a fancy science way of saying it sparkles like smooth, clean glass.

q: Which of the following is the MAIN advantage of space-based telescopes over typical ground-based telescopes:
a: they are not affected by radiation
their mirrors can be any size because of zero gravity
e: Above Earth's fuzzy blanket of air, space telescopes see crisp, clear starlight without any atmosphere blurring their view.

q: Which of the following is a space observatory, launched in 2004 through the combined effort of Italy, the United Kingdom, and the United States, for the detection and study of gamma-ray bursts:
e: Named SWIFT, this watchful space explorer was built to spin quickly and catch sudden flashes of gamma rays across the cosmos.

q: What is the primary mode of heat transport in a white dwarf?
e: Packed tight with buzzing electrons, a white dwarf passes warmth along by conduction, like heat traveling through a metal spoon.

q: What would happen in the mid-northern latitudes if the tilt of the Earth's axis decreased by 15 degrees:
e: With less tilt, our planet stands up straighter, calming the wild seasons into cooler summers and cozier, warmer winters.

q: The majority of helium originating in the dust cloud that formed the Earth has since evaporated into space. Most present-day terrestrially available helium comes from which of the following?
e: Deep underground, heavy rock elements slowly break down and decay, burping up fresh helium that gets trapped in the earth.

q: Which of the following is true of galaxies that are more distant from us?
e: In our stretching universe, the farther away a galaxy lives, the faster it zooms away from our cosmic neighborhood.

q: A body with a 2 kilogram mass has position vector r = 3i + 2t 2j meters. What is the velocity at t = 1 second?
e: Since the sideways position never changes, only the upward speed grows, reaching four j right at one second.

q: Which of the following properties of a telescope determines its resolving power?
e: A telescope's aperture is its giant eye opening, and the wider it opens, the sharper and clearer its cosmic vision becomes.

q: Hubble's law states that there is a direct correlation between the distance to a galaxy and which of the following quantities:
e: The farther a galaxy roams, the faster it scampers away, making its speedy recessional velocity grow with distance!

q: What is the term for the minimum distance a satellite must orbit from a planetary body without being torn apart by tidal forces?
e: Get too close to a giant planet's hug and tidal forces tear you apart, making the Roche limit a moon's danger zone.

q: A pendulum with a length of 2.0 meters is released when it makes an angle of 25 degrees from the vertical. Given 9.8 meters per second squared as g, what is its velocity in meters per second at the bottom of its swing?
e: As the swing dives downward, gravity trades falling height for pure speed, swooping past the bottom at 1.9 meters per second!

q: Jupiter appears brightest in which of the following configurations relative to the Earth?
e: Jupiter smiles brightest at opposition because it lines up right opposite the Sun, showing Earth its fully lit, closest face!

q: The Leidenfrost effect is what causes water to "skitter" across a hot surface such as a pan and can permit a droplet to persist for longer on the hot surface at higher temperatures. On what is the water floating?
a: An insulating piece of the surface it sublimed
e: A sizzling pan instantly turns a droplet's belly into an insulating layer of steam, letting it ride on its own tiny cloud!

q: Which of the following statements BEST describes specific heat capacity?
a: The amount of thermal energy required to change the temperature of a substance by a certain amount per unit of mass
The amount of thermal energy required to alter the physical state of a given substance
The total amount of thermal energy in a specific system
The average kinetic energy of molecules in a system
e: Specific heat capacity tells us how much cozy thermal energy each scoop of mass must soak up to change its temperature.

q: The typical efficiency of an automobile engine is approximately which of the following percentages?
e: Most car engines lose heat to the chilly air, so only about 25 percent of the fuel actually spins the wheels!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding a system undergoing rotation?
a: Torque is the physical quantity describing a force causing rotation about an axis
Moment of inertia describes the tendency of an object to resist changes in angular momentum
Torque is required to tilt the axis of rotation
Conservation of angular momentum explains why pulsars will never stop spinning
e: Even mighty spinning pulsars slowly tire out from friction and magnetic drag, so angular momentum cannot keep them spinning forever.

q: DOE scientists at SLAC [slack] have been using the Linac Coherent Light Source to study SNARE proteins in the brain. Which of the following processes are SNARE proteins involved with?
e: Like little dock workers tying up boats, SNARE proteins lasso tiny chemical bubble cargo safely in place during vesicle docking.

q: A star is found to have a surface temperature of 20,000 kelvin. Which of the following spectral types is it most likely to be:
e: Blazing blue type O stars are the hottest suns in space, easily sizzling past twenty thousand kelvin!

q: One vector has a magnitude of six meters, and the other has a magnitude of three meters. The magnitude of their vector product is 0.556. Which of the following is true of this system?
a: The angle between the vectors is 33.7 degrees
The angle between the vectors is 146.3 degrees
There is not enough information to determine the angle or the scalar product
e: Since that cross-product leaves two angles hiding in the shadows, there is not enough information to solve the puzzle.

q: How much radiation does a banana emit?
e: Every sweet yellow banana gives off a tiny, harmless tickle of radiation, measuring just 0.1 microsieverts!

q: Los Alamos National Lab scientists are fabricating nanoparticles to produce terahertz radiation. The terahertz band is best described as lying between what two regions of the electromagnetic spectrum?
e: Tucked cozily in the rainbow family, terahertz waves dance right between puffy microwaves and warm infrared rays.

q: A bicyclist goes over the top of a hill with a radius of 50 meters. Which of the following is closest to the maximum speed, in meters per second, the cyclist can have without leaving the ground at the top of the hill?
e: Gravity hugs the wheels downward just hard enough so you can zoom over the crest at 22 meters per second without flying!

q: Which of the following is true for a cyclist applying her brakes while traveling west on a straight path?
a: She accelerates both to the east and the west
e: To slow down westbound wheels, brakes must push backward, tugging the bike with acceleration toward the east.

q: Kepler's second law states that each planet moves so that a line from the sun to the planet sweeps out equal areas in equal periods of time. It is a direct result of the conservation of which of the following physical quantities?
e: As planets orbit, conserved angular momentum keeps their cosmic dance in balance, sweeping out equal areas over time.

q: The triple point of water is nearest which of the following temperatures?
e: At a chilly 273 Kelvin, ice, liquid, and steam can all snuggle together at water's magical triple point!

q: Which of the following explanations is used by scientists to justify the observed accelerating expansion of the universe?
e: Mysterious dark energy fills deep space, acting like a giant balloon pump that pushes the universe apart faster and faster!

q: The compressibility of an object's volume is dependent on which of the following?
e: Bulk modulus measures how stubbornly an object pushes back whenever you try squeezing its whole volume together.

q: A region contains a time-varying magnetic field. Which of Maxwell's equations would be most directly useful for computing the EMF induced in objects within the field?
e: Faraday's law reveals the magic recipe showing how a shifting magnetic field tickles electricity into life inside nearby objects.

q: Which of the following locations in a spiral galaxy possesses the highest rate of star formation?
e: A galaxy's spinning spiral arms squeeze thick clouds of dust together, making cozy cosmic nurseries where bright baby stars burst into life!

q: A galaxy is receding from an observer such that the hydrogen alpha line appears to be at 657 nanometers instead of 656.3 nanometers. Which of the following best describes the changes in the beta and gamma lines for this galaxy?
a: They will both be shifted longer by 0.7 nanometers
They will both be shifted by slightly less than 0.7 nanometers
They will both be shifted by slightly more than 0.7 nanometers
They will both be shifted shorter by 0.7 nanometers
e: Redshift stretches light by a fair percentage, so the naturally shorter blue waves stretch out by slightly less than 0.7 nanometers.

q: Lawrence Berkeley National Lab scientists are studying the teeth of parrotfish due to their unique structure. Parrotfish can be classified best as which of the following?
e: Parrotfish steer through the reef with delicate fins spread out on tiny bony rods, placing them proudly among the ray-finned fish.

q: If a slow-moving warm front is followed by a fast- moving cold front, the cold front will sometimes overtake the warm front. When the cold air lifts the warm air entirely aloft, what atmospheric phenomenon results?
e: A speedy cold front scoops the warm air right off the ground like a giant shovel, trapping it aloft to create an occluded front.

q: How can 2 batteries and three capacitors be arranged to store the maximum amount of energy?
a: Connect the capacitors in parallel and the batteries in series
Connect the capacitors in series and the batteries in parallel
Connect the capacitors and batteries in parallel
Connect the capacitors and batteries in series
e: Teaming the batteries in series boosts total push, while linking capacitors side-by-side in parallel gathers the biggest pool of electric treasure.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are accelerating electrons to energies of 7.8 giga-electron-volts at the BELLA center. Which of the following combinations of SI base units measures the same quantity as an electron-volt?
e: An electron-volt simply measures energy, which scientists tally up in base units as kilogram-meters squared per second squared.

q: A train approaches a station with a velocity of +15 meters per second relative to the ground. If a person on the train is moving towards the rear of the train at a speed of 1.5 meters per second relative to the train, what is the velocity, in meters per second, of the person relative to the ground?
e: Walking backward at 1.5 meters per second gently subtracts from the train's forward rush of 15, leaving you gliding ahead at plus 13.5.

q: According to the Energy Information Administration, which of the following is closest to the net number of barrels of oil per day imported by the United States in 2012?
e: Back in 2012, America welcomed a massive parade of tanker ships carrying about 10 million barrels of oil every single day.

q: Which of the following is closest to the amount of energy, in electron-volts, that a photon of visible light carries?
e: Each tiny sparkle of rainbow light carries just a whisper of energy, landing right around one electron-volt.

q: Which of the following forms of energy does NOT require bulk motion of physical matter through space?
e: Radiant energy travels as pure light beams, soaring freely across empty space without needing physical matter to push along.

q: One of the criticisms of ground-mount solar farms is the amount of space they occupy. A new solar system was recently announced called "floatovoltaics," because it is a floating solar farm. Which of the following is NOT a potential benefit of this system?
e: Floating panels help cool the water, but building them on lakes costs extra money, making short-term profit unlikely at first.

q: Researchers at Lawrence Livermore National Lab are studying the conditions under which planet formation occurs by doing which of the following?
a: Determining the melting point of silica at gigapascal [gih-gah-pass-KAL] pressures
Determining the melting point of silica in ultra high vacuum
Determining the boiling point of silica at gigapascal pressures
Determining the boiling point of alumina at gigapascal pressures
e: Scientists crush rocky silica under giant gigapascal pressures to find its melting point, copying the deep ovens where baby planets form.

q: Which of the following types of electromagnetic energy has the shortest wavelengths?
e: X-rays wiggle with fierce energy, packing their ripples so tightly together that they have the shortest waves of the bunch.

q: Researchers at Argonne National Lab used high-energy x-rays to confirm a model of quantum magnetism. Which of the following facilities did they use?
e: The Advanced Photon Source acts like a giant super-flashlight, firing brilliant X-rays to peer inside tiny magnetic secrets.

q: What cloud type is characterized by a formless cloud layer that is almost uniformly dark gray?
e: Nimbostratus clouds blanket the entire sky in a cozy, shadowy gray sheet, quietly drizzling rain all day long.

q: Which of the following BEST describes the position of the first quarter Moon to an observer in northern mid-latitudes on a clear summer night just after sunset:
e: As the sun sets in the west, the half-lit moon peeks out directly halfway across the sky, shining high in the south.

q: Which of the following types of terrace is carved into bedrock?
e: Strath terraces are tough benches of solid bedrock carved flat by a patient river slicing straight through stone.

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE about the rotation rate of the Sun at its surface?
a: It is the same everywhere on the Sun
It is greatest in two bands at mid-latitude
e: The Sun spins faster at its warm equator, but its rotation gets slower and lazier as you travel toward the poles.
