q: If gE and gM are the accelerations due to gravity on the surfaces of Earth and the Moon respectively, and if Millikan's oil drop experiment could be performed on the two surfaces, the ratio of the electronic charge on the Moon to the electronic charge on the Earth would be which of the following?
e: An electron always carries the exact same fundamental electric charge everywhere in the universe, making the ratio simply one.

q: During which of the following two days is the maximum solar altitude less than 90 at the equator?
e: On the summer and winter solstices, Earth tilts away, so the midday sun never climbs completely overhead at the equator.

q: Which of the following is a consequence of Gauss's law for magnetism?
a: A changing magnetic flux through a loop creates an electric current around the loop
Charges must be moving to produce magnetic fields
A time-varying electric flux acts as a current and produces a magnetic field
e: Magnets always keep their north and south poles joined like best friends, meaning lonely, single poles simply do not exist.

q: The National Energy Technology Lab is leading a project that gasifies coal and coal-biomass blends to form syngas, which is primarily a mixture of hydrogen and what other chemical compound?
e: Syngas is a bubbly team made of hydrogen dancing alongside carbon monoxide to make useful energy.

q: The earliest known single-celled life forms on Earth belong to which of the following taxonomic groups?
e: Long ago, the Monera group welcomed the very first tiny, single-celled creatures to life on our young planet.

q: The International Astronomical Union recently downgraded Pluto from a planet to a dwarf planet. Which of the proposed criteria for a planet does Pluto now fail to meet?
a: It must have the gravitational force to shape itself into a sphere
It must have cleared its orbit of other debris
e: Little Pluto is simply too tiny to sweep away all the messy space rocks sharing its snowy neighborhood path.

q: Which of the following MOST directly determines the permittivity of a material:
a: ability of the material to magnetize
e: A material's electrical susceptibility shows how eagerly it responds to an electric field, which directly sets its permittivity.

q: Which of the following stars is the bluest?
e: Rigel burns with such sizzling heat that it shines with a fierce blue glow, far hotter than its neighbors.

q: A pipe with a 30 centimeter inner radius is connected to a pipe with a 15 centimeter inner radius. If incompressible water flows through the pipes, what is the flow speed in centimeters per second in the smaller pipe if the flow speed through the larger pipe is 10 centimeters per second?
e: Squeezing into a pipe half as wide forces the water to hurry four times faster, rushing at forty centimeters per second!

q: The temperature in the region of the Sun where fusion occurs is about how many degrees Fahrenheit?
e: Deep inside the sun's core, a blistering twenty-seven million degrees Fahrenheit cooks atoms together to make light.

q: In the distant future, the Andromeda Galaxy will collide with the Milky Way. Which of the following would a hypothetical alien presently living in Andromeda observe about Balmer lines from our galaxy?
a: Their wavelengths are shorter than expected
Their wavelengths are longer than expected
Their frequencies are lower than expected
They are not subject to Zeeman splitting
e: Because our galaxies are speeding toward each other, the light gets squished together, making its wavelengths shorter than expected.

q: Name the notable scientist who first devised the mathematical laws governing the motion of planetary orbits.
e: Kepler cracked the secret code of the sky, creating the first math rules showing how planets orbit the sun.

q: Through which of the following materials does sound travel the fastest?
e: Sound zips fastest through aluminum because its tightly packed, springy atoms pass vibrations along in a flash.

q: Which of these is not an example of a Milankovich [mil-AYN- koh-vitch] cycle?
a: Shifting tilt of the Earth's axis
e: Milankovitch cycles track Earth's gentle wobbles, while sunspots are just the sun having its own stormy magnetic day.

q: A total solar eclipse can occur only during what phase of the moon?
e: The moon must step right between Earth and the sun, hiding its bright face as a shadowy new moon.

q: From 2001 to 2011, the installed wind power in the U.S. in megawatts has increased by approximately what factor?
e: Across that breezy decade, wind energy zoomed by a factor of ten as giant spinning turbines sprang up everywhere.

q: The power produced by a wind turbine depends primarily on which of the following parameters?
e: A larger blade radius lets a turbine sweep across a wider circle of wind, capturing heaps more power.

q: If a light ray passes from air (n = 1.00) to acetone (n = 1.36), what is the critical angle?
a: There is no total internal reflection
e: Light only bounces completely backward when speeding up, so slowing down into acetone causes no total internal reflection.

q: Which of the following is NOT a type of vacuum pump?
e: Instead of sucking air out like a vacuum pump, a diaphragm compressor squeezes gases together to build up pressure.

q: At what altitude does the greatest variation in daily temperature occur?
e: Earth's ground bakes under the sun and chills quickly at night, creating the wildest temperature swings right near the dirt.

q: Current accounting of the composition of the universe suggests that dark energy and dark matter together make up about what percent of the energy in the universe:
e: Nearly ninety-five percent of our wondrous universe hides as mysterious dark energy and dark matter waiting to be discovered.

q: At 8:00 AM in early August of 2006 in New York, the Moon could be seen low in the western sky. What phase was it most likely in:
e: Because a full moon sets at sunrise, lingering in the morning western sky means it is a few days past full.

q: A chunk of gold with a density of 19,300 kilograms per cubic meter and volume of 0.3 cubic meters is completely submerged in water. Assuming g = 10 meters per second squared and the density of water is 1000 kilograms per cubic meter, what is the apparent weight of the gold in newtons?
e: Water gives the heavy gold block a friendly upward lift of 3,000 newtons, leaving it weighing 54,900 newtons.

q: A sports car driver slams the brakes and the car slows from 90 miles per hour to a complete stop in 4 seconds. In terms of g, which of the following is closest to the car's acceleration?
e: Slamming the brakes pulls the car backward just as strongly as Earth's gravity pulls down, giving it an acceleration of negative g.

q: Which of the following surfaces has the highest albedo?
e: Fresh snow acts like a giant, sparkly mirror, bouncing almost all of the sun's bright light straight back into the sky!

q: Which of the following drives the volcanism on Jupiter's moon, Io?
e: Giant Jupiter constantly squishes and stretches little Io like silly putty, and those tidal forces heat its belly into fiery volcanoes!

q: A capacitor is charged by applying a voltage that linearly increases with time. Which of the following describes the dependence of the stored electric potential energy with time?
e: Stored energy loves to multiply voltage by itself, so as voltage climbs steadily, the energy zooms up in a quadratic curve.

q: Which of the following is NOT a type of nuclear reactor currently used in the United States?
e: Reactors need cooling fluids that flow, so solid sodium is not used because a frozen chunk of metal cannot carry away heat.

q: Which of the following statements about the moon is NOT correct?
a: Moonquakes are due to tidal stresses from the Earth and meteorite impacts
The moon formed during the late heavy bombardment
Lunar basalts contain fewer volatiles than basalts on Earth
The moon has no global magnetic field
e: Our Moon was already peacefully floating in space long before the Late Heavy Bombardment arrived to pelt it with rocks.

q: Which of the following has the greatest energy content in BTUs?
e: A whole cord of wood is a giant stack of logs, packing way more cozy heat energy inside than the others.

q: Astrophysicists, when referring to interstellar gases, typically use the Roman numeral I to indicate that an atom is:
e: When stargazers write the numeral one, they mean an atom is neutral and still happily holding onto all its little electrons.

q: Which of the following best describes why arches and domes are more stable than flat roofed structures?
a: They transmit compressive forces along their length to the ground, uniformly bearing the load of gravity upon the structure
Each section is under great tension, using the stronger dimension of the components
Torsional resistance to sideways swaying ensures that such structures are stable, even in high winds
The surface tension of the arched shape allows the building components to be hollowed out, saving weight
e: Arches gently squeeze their stones together, passing the heavy weight along their smooth curves safely down to the ground.

q: In millimeters, what must the focal length of the objective lens of a telescope be in order to produce a magnification of 300 when used with a 3-millimeter eye piece?
e: To make things look three hundred times bigger with a three-millimeter eyepiece, the main lens needs a long nine-hundred-millimeter reach.

q: Compounds of bismuth telluride are used in which of the following types of devices?
e: Bismuth telluride is a clever material inside thermoelectric devices that turns heat differences into electricity like magic.

q: Which Landsat Satellite currently has had the longest operational life?
e: Plucky little Landsat 5 kept snapping Earth photos for nearly twenty-nine glorious years, outlasting every other satellite sister!

q: Which of the following is NOT featured in the Bohr model of the atom?
e: Bohr pictured electrons zooming in simple round tracks, not fuzzy cloud-like shapes called atomic orbitals.

q: Pascal's law governs the actions of forces in which of the following?
e: When you squeeze an incompressible fluid, it cannot shrink, so it loyally pushes that pressure out in every direction!

q: Which of the following is NOT true according to the Standard Model of Particle Physics:
a: quarks can be isolated from their hadrons
the carrier particle for the electromagnetic interaction has zero charge
e: Quarks are best friends forever who refuse to be isolated, always sticking tightly together inside their little particles.

q: To reduce total energy consumption in the home, in which of the following locations should insulation with the highest R-value be installed?
e: Since warm air loves to float upward, tucking the thickest insulation in the attic keeps your home cozy like a winter hat!

q: Which of the following is measured by total harmonic distortion, a standard for gauging the quality of power provided to customers?
a: How distorted the waveform is from a pure sinusoidal waveform
How distorted a waveform is from a triangular waveform
The difference between a sinusoidal waveform and a triangular waveform
The maximum value of a sinusoidal waveform with respect to the reference point of the waveform
e: Clean electricity flows in a smooth, pretty sine wave, and this test checks how wobbly or distorted that wave gets.

q: The Clean Air Act Amendments established rules on a variety of pollutants. Since 1990, by what approximate amount have ambient sulfate concentrations decreased in most regions of the U.S.?
e: Thanks to cleaner air rules, pesky sulfate pollution dropped by a wonderful fifty percent, helping skies breathe easier.

q: In a rectifier, which of the following pairs of current types describes the input and output of the device, respectively?
e: A rectifier catches wild, back-and-forth alternating current and straightens it out into calm direct current.

q: Which of the following is a direct corollary of the second law of thermodynamics?
a: Energy cannot be created or destroyed
Real thermodynamic processes are not reversible
Absolute zero is the minimum possible temperature
e: You can drop an egg, but nature won't let it un-smash itself, meaning real processes can never truly run backwards!

q: Areas of low pressure exist over the equatorial regions due to which of the following?
e: The sun bakes the equator like a giant pancake, warming the air so it floats right up and leaves low pressure behind!

q: In what form can excess electrical energy be stored in a flywheel?
e: A flywheel spins like a tireless dizzy top, packing away power as pure spinning motion called rotational kinetic energy.

q: Often, investors in energy projects will use a discount rate to evaluate the net present value of future energy sales. If analysts decided to change the discount rate of a wind project from 3% to 7%, how would the net present value of future energy from the project change given constant supply and market costs?
e: When the discount rate goes up, future money shrinks in value today, so the project's overall worth decreases.

q: Which of the following best describes the concept upon which Kirchhoff's current law or first law is based:
a: all charges flow from the negative to the positive
charge can neither be created nor destroyed
what goes up must come down
e: Little electric charges can never be created or destroyed, so every single spark entering a crossroad must come right back out!

q: In a simple harmonic oscillator system, which of the following is equal to the spring constant?
a: First derivative of potential energy with respect to displacement
First derivative of potential energy with respect to time
Second derivative of potential energy with respect to displacement
Second derivative of potential energy with respect to time
e: If you track how stored energy curves as a spring stretches, its second derivative reveals just how stiff that spring is.

q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding white dwarfs?
a: They shrink in radius as they get cooler
They do not perform nuclear fusion
Their mass is mostly composed of carbon and oxygen
They can have atmospheres of helium
e: White dwarfs are stubborn little stars locked in size, which is why they do not shrink at all as they cool down.

q: Scientists at Pacific Northwest National Lab are studying lipids. In humans, which of the following is a lipid-derived hormone?
e: Cortisol is a helpful stress hormone built directly from oily fats, making it a true lipid-derived messenger inside you!

q: Most solar radiation is emitted in short wavelengths. Visible wavelengths fall in which of the following ranges in micrometers?
e: All the bright rainbow colors our eyes can see wiggle in tiny waves between 0.4 and 0.7 micrometers!

q: Brookhaven National Lab scientists recently made strides on understanding the nature of Cooper pairs. To which of the following disciplines is this discovery most relevant?
e: Cooper pairs are electrons dancing together so electricity glides without friction, making them superstars of superconductor physics!

q: Which of the following is NOT a composite material:
e: While composites mix separate ingredients together, mild steel is a smoothly melted metal blend, so it is not a composite.

q: Which of the following elements has the largest 2nd ionization energy?
e: Lithium happily gives away one outer electron, but guards its second one with all its might, giving it the largest second ionization energy!

q: Which of the following quark compositions does NOT have a total of zero strangeness quantum number?
e: A lonely strange quark brings its own quirky strangeness along, so pairing it with an up quark leaves a non-zero strangeness.

q: While walking down the street, an open wire falls on you and you receive an instantaneous alternating current electric shock. Where did most of the electrons come from that "shocked" you?
e: The wire just shakes the electrons already inside you like a snow globe, so the shock comes from your own body!

q: Which of the following is the MOST reliable measure of the remaining percentage of stored energy in a lead acid battery:
a: voltage remaining in the battery as measured on a voltmeter
e: The battery liquid gets lighter as its stored energy empties, so measuring its density, or specific gravity, tells you the honest truth.

q: Which of the following constants is fundamentally related to the speed of light?
e: The permeability of free space sets how magnetic fields spread out, teaming up with electricity to define the speed of light.

q: Most lignite is used for what purpose in the US?
e: Most of this crumbly brown coal gets tossed into power plant furnaces to make electricity for our homes.

q: Which of the following BEST describes how and why electrical resistance is related to temperature:
a: as temperature increases, resistance decreases because electrons move faster
as temperature increases, resistance decreases because electrons are lost from the conductor
as temperature increases, resistance increases because protons move faster
as temperature increases, resistance increases because atoms vibrate more, increasing electron scattering
e: Hotter atoms wiggle like hyperactive dancers, bumping into passing electrons and creating more resistance to slow them down.

q: The Schmidt telescope would BEST be considered:
a: an advanced adaptive optics telescope with x-ray detection capabilities
e: The Schmidt telescope uses a clever curved lens to capture huge, sweeping views of starry skies as a wide field telescope.

q: How many types of quarks are there in nature?
e: Nature cooked up a cozy family of exactly six different quark flavors to build our wonderful universe!

q: What type of collision occurs when two objects collide and stick together?
e: When two sticky blobs crash and hug together forever without bouncing, scientists call that a perfectly inelastic collision.

q: Which of the following is NOT a type of meteorite:
e: While space rocks tumble from the sky as chondrites or irons, andesite is a homebody volcanic rock born right here on Earth.

q: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of distributed generation?
e: Making power right at home is handy, but cities still have to spend money building and fixing the neighborhood electric lines.

q: Epsilon naught, o, and mu naught, o, are permittivity and permeability constants of free space, respectively. The speed of light is found in terms of these constants as which of the following?
a: 1/00 [1 over the square root of the quantity epsilon naught mu naught]
00 [the square root of the quantity epsilon naught mu naught]
0 [the fraction with numerator mu naught and denominator 4 pi epsilon naught] 40
e: Light zooms through empty space at a speed equal to one divided by the square root of those two cosmic constants.

q: John has twice the mass of Carl. They jump off a cliff into the water below. Just before the splash:
a: John has half as much kinetic energy as Carl
John and Carl have the same kinetic energy
John has twice as much kinetic energy as Carl
John has four times as much kinetic energy as Carl
e: Both friends splash down at the same speed, but heavier John packs twice the mass, giving him twice as much kinetic energy.

q: Which of the following is necessarily true regarding capacitors?
a: For capacitance in parallel, the equivalent capacitance is less than that of any individual capacitor
For capacitance in parallel, the equivalent capacitance is the sum of reciprocals of the individual capacitors
For capacitance in series, the equivalent capacitance is less than that of any individual capacitor
For capacitance in series, the equivalent capacitance is the sum of the individual capacitors
e: When capacitors line up single file in series, their combined room to store charge shrinks smaller than any single one.

q: Which of the following planets has rings?
e: Far-out blue Neptune loves to accessorize, proudly spinning with faint, dusty rings hidden in the cold dark.

q: Scientists at Berkeley National Laboratory are using artificial intelligence to create dark matter simulations. In this system, one neural network learns the training data, while a second neural network tries to fool the first by generating inputs that appear to be from the training set. What is this type of network called?
e: Because the two clever computer brains act like playful rivals trying to outsmart each other, scientists call them adversarial networks.

q: Panning is a simple mining technique that is used for extracting gold deposited in:
e: Rushing river water gently tumbles heavy gold into gravel beds called placer deposits, where lucky miners swirl them clean.

q: NASA's QuickSCAT satellite mapped winds over all of Earth's oceans. Which of the following is NOT true of this satellite?
a: It bounced microwaves off the ocean surface
It retrieved both wind direction and speed
It was powered by solar arrays
e: Instead of hovering frozen over one lonely spot like a geosynchronous satellite, this busy bee circled the entire globe.

q: While waterskiing behind her uncle's boat, Michelle is pulled at a constant speed with a force of 164 newtons by a rope that is nearly horizontal. If Michelle has a mass of 65 kilograms, what is the coefficient of sliding friction between Michelle and the water?
e: Dividing Michelle's pulling force by her heavy weight on the water reveals a slippery friction number of 0.26.

q: Which of the following are characteristics of an ideal voltmeter?
a: Infinitely large resistance and no potential difference between its terminals
Infinitely large resistance and no current diverted through it
Zero resistance and no potential difference between its terminals
Zero resistance and no current diverted through it
e: A polite voltmeter uses giant resistance so it can measure the electric push without stealing any of the flowing current.

q: Which of the following is unlikely, given the Moon's current orbital plane?
a: The Moon passing directly over the poles
Variations in the lunar path across the sky
e: The Moon circles around Earth's tilted waistline, so its path never takes it directly above the freezing North or South poles.

q: Also known as fall-stripes, precipitation falling from the undersurface of a cloud but not reaching the ground is known as:
e: When thirsty air swallows falling raindrops before they can touch the ground, those ghostly sky ribbons are called virga.

q: If Z = atomic number and A = mass number, the radius of an approximately spherical nucleus [NOO-klee-uhs] is proportional to which of the following?
e: Since atomic particles pack together like a round ball of clay, the nucleus radius grows with mass number to the one-third.

q: Scientists at Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility are studying decay processes that could provide insight into physics beyond the Standard Model. Which of the following phenomena is part of the Standard Model?
a: Pion decay into a muon and an anti-muon neutrino
Gravitational waves emitted by in-spiraling black holes
Conversion of axions to photons in electromagnetic fields
Production of stable free up quarks from proton-proton collisions
e: A pion happily decaying into a muon and a neutrino is an everyday trick right inside the standard model rulebook.

q: Which of the following energy generation methods is the BEST source for baseload?
e: While wind rests and the sun sets, mighty rivers keep flowing day and night, making hydroelectric dams the most dependable power.

q: Which of the following BEST describes one of Maxwell's equations that is a mathematical conceptualization of Faraday's law:
a: a magnetic B-field is a solenoid vector field
an EMF induced in a conductor opposes that motion
induced currents are caused by the magnetic field and in opposition to the opposed flux
a time-varying B-field produces an E-field
e: Whenever a magnetic field wiggles and changes over time, it magically swirls an electric field into life all around it.

q: Which of the following will INCREASE the current from a solar panel?
a: Using a lead acid cell in series with the solar cells
Using a wet cell in series with the solar cells
Connecting the solar cells in series
Connecting the solar cells in parallel
e: Wiring solar cells side by side in parallel lets their currents team up into one mighty, flowing electric river.

q: Uranus is unique among the planets in our solar system because:
a: It has a highly elliptical orbit, and is occasionally further from the Sun than Neptune
It is the only outer planet with an icy shell
Its rotational axis is nearly parallel with its orbital plane
It orbits the Sun in a clockwise direction, opposite all other planets
e: Playful Uranus rolls through space on its side, spinning with its axis tilted nearly flat against its sunny racetrack.

q: Which of the following is the BEST description of our Sun:
a: a cool large star similar to Proxima Centauri
a small-sized star about 6 billion years old
a large-sized red giant about 4.7 billion years old
e: Our cozy Sun is a mid-sized yellow dwarf, sitting right in the sweet spot of star sizes to keep Earth warm and happy.

q: Assuming h = 6.63 x 10-34 joule seconds, what is the approximate energy of a photon in joules in a 1000 nanometer light beam?
e: Each tiny packet of light carries a whisper of energy, measuring just two times ten to the negative nineteenth joules.

q: An object is suspended from a spring balance in an elevator. The reading of the balance is 200 newtons when the elevator is at rest. If the balance reading later is 190 newtons, which of the following best describes how the elevator could be moving at that time?
e: When the elevator speeds up downward, the floor drops away slightly, making the scale feel less of your weight.

q: At a latitude of 45 degrees, which of the following is closest to the percentage of astronomical sources that are circumpolar?
e: From halfway up our planet, about thirty percent of the night sky circles endlessly around the pole without ever setting.

q: What is the name of the postulate of quantum mechanics that requires that quantum mechanical systems behave classically as quantum numbers approach infinity?
e: The correspondence principle is nature's bridge, showing how tiny quantum weirdness smoothly turns into the everyday world we can see.

q: If an ideal gas performs work on its surroundings, then which of the following must be true?
e: To push on the outside world and do work, the gas must stretch out its elbows and increase its volume.

q: Which of the following particles are classified as baryons?
e: A neutron is a baryon because it packs a sturdy trio of quarks right in the heart of an atom.

q: In about twelve thousand years, the star Vega will be the North Star, not Polaris, due to which of the following:
e: Earth slowly wobbles like a sleepy spinning top, an axial precession that will eventually point our North Pole toward bright Vega.

q: Which of the following industries has the largest water withdrawal?
e: Thermoelectric power plants withdraw the most water because their fiery machines need giant gulps to stay cool.

q: A 3 kilogram mass, a 4 kilogram mass, and a 5 kilogram mass are placed in a line at positions of 3 meters, 4 meters, and 5 meters, respectively, from the origin. Which of the following is nearest the location of the center of mass of this set of masses in meters from the origin?
e: Because the heaviest mass pulls the balance point closest to itself, their sweet balancing spot lands right at 4.17 meters.

q: In which of the following locations is it possible to find an esker formed during the Pleistocene [PLY-stuh-seen] epoch?
e: Giant ice sheets once slid across Iowa, leaving behind winding gravel trails called eskers where ancient glacial rivers flowed.

q: Evidence of which of the following was gathered from the Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM) and indicates possible low grade subsurface metamorphism on Mars?
e: Alteration clays reveal that warm underground water once gently baked Martian rocks, hinting at heat deep below the surface.

q: Which of the following statements correctly summarizes the zeroth law of thermodynamics?
a: If each of two systems are in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they must be in thermal equilibrium with each other
When energy passes as work, heat, or with matter, into or out of a system, its internal energy changes in accord with the law of conservation of energy
In a natural thermodynamic process, the sum of the entropies of the participating thermodynamic systems increases
The entropy of a system approaches a constant value as the temperature approaches absolute zero
e: If two cozy things each match the temperature of a third buddy, they are all in perfect balance together.

q: If a car is going around a corner, which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship among the speeds of the wheels on the car:
a: the wheels all rotate at the same speed
the wheels on the inside of the corner rotate faster because they have less distance to travel
the wheels on the inside of the corner rotate faster because they have more distance to travel
the wheels on the outside of the corner rotate faster because they have more distance to travel
e: Outside wheels take the long way around the curve, so they must spin faster to keep up with the car.

q: What are the bright outbursts in flare stars due to?
e: Twisted magnetic field lines snap and reconnect like rubber bands, unleashing dazzling fireworks of starlight.

q: Which of the following best describes the graph of position versus time for a damped harmonic oscillator?
e: The motion wiggles back and forth as a sinusoid, gently fading inside an exponentially shrinking boundary as friction slows it down.

q: Two-thirds of the charge is removed from a capacitor without changing its capacitance. The stored energy in the capacitor is now what multiple of the original:
e: Leaving only one-third of the charge squares the drop, shrinking the stored energy down to just one-ninth of before.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding the moon?
a: The dividing line between darkness and light on the moon is called the terminator
The moon is tidally locked to the Earth
Maria are mostly composed of basaltic minerals
Many moon rock samples are sedimentary
e: Without wind or flowing water to pile up layers of sand, the Moon cannot create sedimentary rocks.

q: Which of the following are the most important calibration references that Celsius used to devise his temperature scale:
a: melting point and boiling point of water
ice-point and freeze-thaw point of water
boiling point and steam point of water
e: Celsius cleverly anchored his scale to water, using the melting point where it thaws and the boiling point where it steams.

q: What is the term for the rate at which an object's velocity changes with time?
e: Acceleration is the lively measure of how quickly something speeds up, slows down, or changes its zooming direction.

q: For which of the following is Erwin Schrodinger most famous?
a: Describing how wavefunctions change over time
Discovering that electrons occupy energy levels in atoms
Discovering that atoms contain a positively charged nucleus
e: Erwin Schrodinger wrote the special recipe showing how tiny quantum particle waves ripple and change over time like playful ocean waves.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are studying molecular [moh-LEK- yoo-lur] wires as a potential polymeric replacement for silicon-based technologies. Which of the following polymers could behave as a molecular wire without any other functional groups?
e: With its chain of alternating bonds, polyphenylene vinylene lets electrons zip straight through like cars on an open highway!

q: Which of the following is the most commonly accepted theory for the creation of Earth's moon?
a: The Earth collided with a large proto-planet
The Earth captured a proto-planet due to gravity
The Earth rotated too fast and spun off a large piece
The Earth and the Moon condensed together
e: Long ago, a runaway space rock crashed right into baby Earth, splashing out melted rocks that gathered together to build our Moon.

q: Which of the following is primarily responsible for nucleosynthesis of first-row d-block metals?
e: When tiny, exhausted white dwarf stars go out with an enormous bang, their fiery blasts forge first-row metals like iron for the universe!

q: A nubbin-on-a-spring keeps a door from hitting the wall. If the nubbin is flicked, such that the nubbin passes its rest point more than once before coming to rest, which of the following is true?
e: Because the spring wobbles back and forth past home before stopping, friction has not calmed it down right away, making it underdamped.

q: The catastrophic dust bowl of the 1930's was caused by which of the following processes:
e: Terrible droughts and overplowing dried the fertile soil into powdery sand, turning green farmland into a dusty desert during desertification.

q: With a constant braking force, the stopping distance of a car is proportional to which of the following?
a: The product of the velocity and the mass
The product of the square of the mass and the square of the velocity
e: Double your speed, and your car packs four times the energy! Brakes must work extra hard, stretching the stopping distance with velocity squared.

q: Lawrence Berkeley National Lab scientists are studying the inflammasome, which is a structure that forms around flagellin. This protein is involved in the immune response to which of the following?
e: Many sneaky bacteria swim around using tiny spinning tails made of flagellin, which alerts your body's clever defense team to fight them.

q: Generally, physicists cannot use light to explore the composition of the subatomic world since light wavelengths are too long. Which of the following do they MOST often resort to as a tool of probing the nature of the atomic nucleus:
e: To peek inside tiny atomic hearts, scientists shoot speedy, energetic charged particles like tiny cue balls to scatter clues everywhere!

q: Which of the following is a reasonable conclusion from the observation that particles found in the Sun's chromosphere are more ionized than ions found in the photosphere?
a: The photosphere and the chromosphere are composed of different ions
The chromosphere is hotter than the photosphere
The photosphere is magnetically opposite the chromosphere
The chromosphere is cooler than the photosphere
e: Sizzling heat strips electrons off atoms! Since chromosphere atoms lose more electrons, this outer layer is actually hotter than the glowing surface below.

q: Which of the following effects is primarily responsible for separating the colors in a rainbow?
e: Raindrops act like tiny glass prisms, bending each color by a different amount to spread them into a rainbow during dispersion.

q: A moving coil galvanometer has 150 equal divisions. Its current sensitivity is 10 divisions per milliampere and its voltage sensitivity is 2 divisions per millivolt. In order for each division to read 1-volt, what resistance, in ohms, must be connected in series with the coil?
e: Adding a 9,995-ohm resistor to the meter's five-ohm coil builds ten thousand ohms, letting the needle safely measure every single volt!

q: Consider charges +Q and +4Q, separated by 3 meters. At which of the following points on a line between the two charges can a charge -Q be placed so that it will experience no electrostatic force?
e: The big charge pulls four times as hard, so our little particle stays balanced by sitting one meter from the smaller positive charge.

q: Our solar system formed approximately how many billion years ago?
e: About five billion years ago, a giant cloud of swirling stardust pulled together to create our warm Sun and spinning planets.

q: Which of the following most accurately describes the strength of Mercury's magnetic field at the planet's surface?
a: About the same as that of the Moon
About one-hundreth that of the Earth
About half that of the Earth
e: Mercury's molten core tries its best, but its magnetic shield is quite gentle, measuring only about one-hundredth as strong as Earth's!

q: A spaceship going away from you at a speed 0.2c sends an electromagnetic signal to you. What is the speed at which the signal approaches?
e: No matter how fast a rocket zooms away, light is the ultimate cosmic sprinter and always races toward you at speed c!

q: The overall charge at the top and bottom, respectively, of a towering cumulonimbus cloud during a thunderstorm is:
e: Rising ice crystals give storm clouds a cheerful positive hat up top, while heavier slush piles up negative charges down below.

q: Which of the following statements about surface seawater salinity is true?
a: Salinity is highest at the equator and lowest in the subtropics
Salinity is highest in the subtropics and lowest at high latitudes
Salinity is highest at the poles and lowest in the subtropics
e: Hot sunshine bakes subtropical waters, leaving extra salt behind, while melting polar ice and rainy skies keep high latitudes pleasantly fresh.

q: The majority of moth species forage for food energy during what stage of their life cycle?
e: As hungry larvae, baby caterpillars do all the serious eating and growing before transforming into fluttery moths!

q: Under which of the following conditions is the momentum of a system unchanged?
a: The system is acted upon by multiple forces
The net external forces are zero
The net internal forces are zero
e: When no outside forces push or pull on the system, its total momentum stays locked in and happily keeps on rolling.

q: The word "solstice" means "sunstop." Which of the following does this reference?
a: The Sun's daily change in declination stops and reverses direction
The Sun literally stops in our sky for a brief but measurable time
The Earth reaches the point where the Sun shines directly on the equator, restarting the solar calendar
The ancient belief that the Earth orbited the Sun ROUND 12 Page 12
e: As the sun climbs across our seasons, it pauses at its very highest point before gently turning back around.

q: In inductors, the back EMF generated most directly depends on which of the following properties of the circuit?
e: An inductor hates surprises, so it pushes back hardest whenever the flow of electricity changes quickly over time.

q: Which of the following most accurately describes the dominant air mass over Nebraska in January?
e: Far from any ocean, Nebraska spends January wrapped in chilly, dry land air sweeping down from the frozen continent.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of stellar evolution and the HR diagram?
a: White dwarfs occupy the lower left region of the HR diagram
The sun falls on the main sequence
The instability strip falls below the main sequence
The Hayashi track is a pre-main-sequence phase of stellar evolution
e: Jittery, pulsing stars do not hide at the bottom; their instability strip sits high above the main sequence band.

q: Suppose you compress a gas in a cylinder with a piston by pushing down on the piston. What is the best explanation for why the gas gets warm?
a: The decrease in volume at constant pressure increases the temperature
By compressing the gas, you do work on it, which is converted into heat
By compressing the gas, you increase its entropy, resulting in a negative free energy
The gas will start to condense, releasing energy
e: When you push the piston down, your hard work gives those bouncing gas particles extra energy, heating them right up!

q: At 100 volts, which of the following is closest to the amperage through a circuit that consists of the following in series: resistors of 10 ohms, 15 ohms, and 22 ohms followed by these resistors in parallel: 5, 10, 20, all in the same circuit.
e: All those resistors team up to block fifty ohms of electricity, letting exactly two amps squeeze happily through.

q: A light ray passes from air (n = 1.00) to the cornea (n = 1.33) of the eye. If the angle of incidence is 30, which of the following is true of the angle of refraction?
e: Entering the thicker eye slows the light ray down, bending it inward so its angle shrinks below thirty degrees.

q: The spin quantum number is so named because spin can be expressed in which of the following units?
e: Tiny spinning particles measure their swirling angular momentum in kilogram-meters squared per second, just like a spinning top.

q: America's first satellite, Explorer I, had all of the following technology aboard, EXCEPT:
e: Brave little Explorer One ventured into the dark sky without any solar panels, relying only on chemical batteries.

q: If the circuit breaker in a 110-volt circuit is listed at 30 amperes, how many 100 watt light bulbs could you have on that circuit, which includes a TV with 250 watts, a hair dryer of 1500 watts and a computer of 150 watts?
e: With fourteen hundred spare watts before the switch trips, exactly fourteen glowing light bulbs can join the cozy party.

q: Neglecting the effect of air resistance, a stone dropped off of a 197-meter high building lands on the ground at which of the following approximate times in seconds?
e: Gravity pulls the tumbling pebble faster each moment, carrying it all the way down in about six seconds.

q: Which of the following was the primary instrument used to gather 5 to 35 micrometer spectra data from the Deep Impact mission:
e: Spitzer used its infrared spectrograph to read glowing heat waves and unlock the comet's dusty secrets.

q: Which of the following is the most likely next event in the evolution of Betelgeuse [BAY-tel-jews]?
e: This giant red star is destined to run out of fuel and pop as a mighty type two supernova!

q: Kepler's third law of planetary motion relates what two parameters of the orbiting body?
a: Solar mass and mass of orbiting body
e: Kepler showed that a planet's orbital time neatly pairs with its semi-major axis distance from the sun.

q: Which of the following has a shale protolith?
e: Under intense heat and squishing pressure, ordinary muddy shale transforms into beautiful, banded gneiss rock.

q: The triple alpha process, a fusion-based reaction, results in the formation of what element in the cores of red giant stars?
e: Three helium friends huddle together in the fiery core, fusing into a shiny new carbon atom.

q: What makes arches and domes more stable than flat roofed structures?
a: They transmit compressive forces along their length to the ground, uniformly bearing the load of gravity
Each section is under great tension, using the stronger dimension of the components
Torsional resistance to sideways swaying ensures that such structures are stable, even in high winds
The surface tension of the arched shape allows the building components to be hollowed out, saving weight.
e: Arches squeeze their stones under compression, sending the heavy load of gravity safely down to the ground.

q: At which of the following locations on the HR diagram would one find Betelgeuse?
e: Because Betelgeuse is both super chilly and immensely bright, it perches proudly in the top right corner.

q: In kelvins, which of the following is closest to the radiative equilibrium temperature of Earth?
e: Without any air to trap warmth, our planet balances sunshine and space chill at a brisk two hundred fifty kelvins.

q: If two inductance coils of inductance L are connected in parallel, but are well separated, the equivalent inductance of the system is which of the following?
e: Placing two identical coils side by side gives electricity two paths, cutting their total inductance in half to 0.5L.

q: De novo phasing is a technique that structural biologists at SLAC [slack] use to gather information about a new protein's 3D shape. This technique involves the replacement of a single atom inside the protein with a traditionally non-proteinogenic [pro-teen-oh-JEN-ik] atom with similar chemical behavior. In one example, the researchers replaced a sulfur atom with what?
e: Friendly selenium acts just like sulfur's twin brother, slipping into the protein so scientists can spot its secret 3D shape under bright X-rays!

q: Which of the following factors, if increased, would increase the period of oscillation of a simple pendulum?
e: Give a swing longer ropes, and it takes its sweet time drifting back and forth! A longer pendulum stretches out each lazy tick-tock.

q: When honey is poured from a jar, the flowing honey column gets narrower and narrower as it falls. Which of the following best explains the observed profile for steady flow?
a: Flow rate decreases but speed remains constant with distance
Flow rate remains constant but speed increases with distance
Viscosity increases with distance from the jar
Turbulence increases with distance from the jar
e: As gravity speeds the honey up, it stretches out thinner and thinner so the same sweet amount keeps flowing every second.

q: Which of the following gases is most likely to escape from a planet's atmosphere?
e: Light and bouncy hydrogen is the featherweight champion of gases, zipping fast enough to easily float right off into space!

q: In a gearing arrangement where a 10-tooth pinion drives a 40-tooth gear, what is the gear ratio:
e: The busy little gear must spin four whole times just to turn the giant gear once, making the ratio four to one.

q: What causes clouds of matter to flatten during the development of a protostar?
e: Just like spinning pizza dough flattens into a delicious pie, a rotating cloud spins itself into a flat, whirling pancake.

q: Which of the following did J. J. Thompson use that primarily led him to conclude that electrons were basic particles of atoms and carried electric charge:
e: Thomson shot glowing beams through glass cathode ray tubes, discovering tiny, electrically charged electrons dancing inside the beam!

q: If two simple pendulums have the same oscillation [aw-sih-LAY-shun] frequency but pendulum A has twice the mass of pendulum B, what is the length of pendulum B?
a: Four times that of pendulum A
e: Mass doesn't change a pendulum's rhythm at all, so both must have the exact same length to keep time together.

q: How long is a light-year?
e: In one year, a speedy ray of light zooms across an astonishing 9.461 trillion kilometers of cosmic space!

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are studying a possible critical point in the phase diagram of nuclear matter. Which of the following best describes what occurs at a thermodynamical critical point?
e: At this magical tipping point, the boundary dividing bubbly liquid and floating gas completely vanishes, ending the line between them.

q: A diver jumps out of a plane into free fall without air resistance. Which of the following quantities is the greatest?
e: Gravity keeps piling on more speed every second, so the diver is zooming the fastest right at the two-second mark!

q: Researchers at Argonne National Lab are developing smart materials that can self-assemble and break down in response to external stimuli. They recently demonstrated self- assembly of nickel microparticles in the presence of what?
e: Tiny nickel bits love magnets, so waving a changing magnetic field nudges them into building cool shapes all by themselves!

q: Scientists at SLAC [slack] recently demonstrated that coating the gold tip of an electron gun with nanodiamonds resulted in a higher electron flux through the gun. This is because the diamonds changed what property of the electron gun tip?
e: The shiny diamond coating lowered the tip's work function, making it wonderfully easy for trapped electrons to leap free!

q: Which of the following equations best represents the conservation of energy in fluid systems?
e: Bernoulli wrote the ultimate rulebook for moving fluids, showing how energy stays perfectly balanced as water speeds up or slows down.

q: A granitic pluton is overlain by a sandstone. This relationship is an example of which of the following?
e: When brand-new sedimentary sandstone rests right on top of ancient granite rock, geologists call that mismatched friendship a nonconformity.

q: Given 9.8 meters per second squared as g, how much kinetic energy in joules is lost when a 100-gram ball dropped from a 2 meter height rebounds to 1.5 meters?
e: The ball lost half a meter of bounce height, which neatly equals zero point four nine joules of lost energy.

q: Imagine that you tie a ball on the end of a long string and swing it around your head in a horizontal circle. If you let go of the string, where will the ball go initially?
a: It will hit you in the head
It will fall at your feet
It will fly up in the air
It will continue in the direction in which it was traveling when you let go
e: Once you let go, the ball happily zooms in a straight line, heading whatever way it was already pointing!

q: Triton's retrograde orbit provides the strongest evidence for which of the following hypotheses?
a: It has a deep subsurface ocean
It generates an intrinsic magnetic field
It formed from a collision with another planet
e: Triton orbits backwards like a stubborn runaway, proving Neptune's mighty gravity snatched it up as it wandered by!

q: Gabby has a device capable of pushing objects with an unknown amount of constant force. To determine the magnitude of this force, she makes several measurements by using the device to apply force to objects of varying mass and measuring the resultant acceleration. Which parameters should she choose for her x- and y-axes, respectively, such that the slope of the line of best fit is the force her device applies?
a: One over mass and one over acceleration
e: Graphing one over mass against acceleration gives a line whose slope reveals Gabby's mystery push, because acceleration is force divided by mass!

q: Which of the following is TRUE about the electric field just outside the surface of a charged spherical conductor?
a: It is directed perpendicularly to the surface
It is directed parallel to the surface
e: Tiny charges spread out evenly across the ball, pointing their electric field straight outward, perfectly perpendicular to the surface.

q: A necessary conclusion of Hubble's law is that very-distant galaxies are moving away from us at speeds faster than the speed of light. Which of the following correctly explains this observation?
a: Hubble's law becomes non-linear for very large distances
The Hubble constant was originally miscalculated
Due to the metric expansion of space, faraway objects can recede from us faster than the speed of light
The proper distance to faraway galaxies does not scale linearly with the Hubble constant
e: Space stretches like baking dough, carrying distant galaxies away faster than even light can sprint!

q: There is an electrostatic force of attraction between any two of three metal spheres P, Q, and R. Which of the following is a possible combination for the charges on P, Q, and R?
a: P: positive, Q: negative, R: positive
P: positive, Q: negative, R: neutral
P: positive, Q: positive, R: positive
P: neutral, Q: positive, R: neutral
e: Opposites attract, and a neutral sphere happily hugs both positive and negative neighbors by shifting its charges inside.

q: A 50 gram ball moving to the right at 4 meters per second overtakes and collides perfectly elastically with a 100 gram ball moving to the right at 2 meters per second. Which of the following is true after the collision?
a: Both balls are moving to the left at 1.33 meters per second and 3.33 meters per second, respectively
Both balls are moving to the right at 1.33 meters per second and 3.33 meters per second, respectively
Both balls are moving to the left at 1.66 and 3.00 meters per second, respectively
Both balls are moving to the right at 1.66 and 3.00 meters per second, respectively
e: The bouncy collision pushes both balls forward to the right, cruising at 1.33 and 3.33 meters per second.

q: Which of the following is typically increased in order for electricity to travel long distances through transmission lines?
e: Cranking up the voltage gives electricity extra push, letting it travel far across power lines without wasting its energy.

q: Huygen's principle can be used to most directly derive which of the following:
a: the laws of reflection and refraction
e: Imagining light as marching ripples neatly explains how waves bounce off mirrors in reflection and bend in refraction.

q: During which of the following orbital arrangements can a transit occur for the planet Venus:
e: Venus can only cross the bright Sun when it sneaks right between us and our star, at inferior conjunction.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about the Sun?
a: It vibrates in multiple modes like a bell that is repeatedly struck
Gas near the Sun's higher latitudes rotate more quickly than gas near its equator
It contains about 99% of the mass in the solar system
e: The Sun spins like gooey soup, so its equator actually twirls faster than its higher latitudes, not slower!

q: Capillary action refers to which of the following?
a: The tendency for objects to flee the center of circular motion
The change in frequency of a wave depending on the relative motion of the source
The property by which liquids can flow against gravity
The tendency for fluids to dissipate energy as heat
e: Water loves clinging to tiny spaces so much that capillary action pulls it upward against gravity like magic.

q: In general, there are three types of compensation agreements for electricity generated using distributed generation, such as solar photovoltaic. All of the following are examples, except:
e: People earn money from solar power through special deals, but rate allocation is just about dividing bills, not paying you.

q: Wind can be harnessed to generate electricity via turbines. Which of the following is the greatest challenge to widespread use of wind for electricity?
a: Wind turbines are huge, expensive, and not particularly aesthetic
Wind has major negative ecological and environmental effects
Suitable locations for wind farms with sufficiently constant and fast winds are limited
Wind farms lead to significant loss of agricultural lands
e: Giant turbines crave steady, speedy breezes, but finding places with nonstop wind across the map is surprisingly tough.

q: Plasmas are considered strongly coupled when the ratio of the average distance between the particles to the distance of closest approach is which of the following?
e: When plasma particles crowd together with a small distance ratio, their electric pushes lock hands extra tight.

q: Which of the following events is thought to be the main reason for the development of starburst galaxies?
e: When two galaxies crash together in a cosmic hug, their smashed gas clouds spark a wild burst of brand-new stars!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about quasars?
a: They give off enormous amounts of energy
They can be seen with the unaided eye
Some theorists say that there are black holes in the center of the galaxies in which the quasars are located
e: Quasars blaze with monster energy, but they live so ridiculously far away that our bare eyes cannot spot them.

q: Which of the following is a fine-grained, typically buff- colored sediment deposited by wind?
e: Wandering winds sweep up silky dust and softly pile it into thick, golden blankets called loess.

q: Neglecting air resistance, at what angle above the horizontal would you aim your garden hose nozzle to obtain the greatest horizontal distance if the nozzle is at ground level:
e: Tilting your hose at forty-five degrees gives water the perfect mix of high leap and forward dash to fly farthest.

q: Sinkholes, disappearing streams, and caves are found in which of the following types of regions?
e: Secret underground water nibbles soft rock in karst regions, carving giant caves and swallowing rivers into sinkholes.

q: Which of the following components of a car provides the best example of a damped oscillator?
e: Shock absorbers hush the wild bouncing of a car's springs, gently calming every jiggle into a smooth ride.

q: The red shift in the spectral lines reaching us from other galaxies implies that these galaxies are which of the following?
a: Moving farther apart from one another
e: When galaxies zoom away from one another, their traveling light waves stretch out, shifting into a telltale red.

q: Which of the following is closest to the average pH of marine water?
e: Ocean water stays slightly basic at about 8.16, creating a cozy, balanced salty bath for sea life.

q: The Jurassic period occurred during which era?
e: The Jurassic is the grand middle chapter of the Mesozoic era, when magnificent dinosaurs ruled the Earth.

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE of simple harmonic oscillation?
a: Acceleration is proportional to velocity, but in the opposite direction
Acceleration is proportional to displacement, but in the opposite direction
Velocity is proportional to displacement, but in the opposite direction
Velocity is proportional to displacement and shares the same direction
e: Think of a swing: the farther you pull it away, the harder it yanks back in the opposite direction!

q: Most lignite mined in the United States comes from what state?
e: Deep under the giant state of Texas lies America's biggest stash of crumbly, brown lignite coal, eagerly mined for power.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of smart grid technology?
e: Ground heat pumps simply borrow warmth from backyard dirt rather than communicating across clever digital power grids.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding the planet Mercury?
a: Mercury is more massive than Ganymede
Mercury has a magnetic field generated by a liquid iron core
Mercury is synchronously tidally locked with the Sun
Craters on Mercury's north pole are known to contain water ice
e: Little Mercury pirouettes three times for every two loops around the Sun, proving it is never stuck facing one way.

q: Which of the following is NOT evidence that liquid water was once present on Mars?
e: Whistling winds sweep up those sandy dunes, showing off the breeze's artwork rather than ancient flowing water.

q: Researchers are using the Argonne Leadership Computing Facility to design and model peptide therapeutics. Which of the following is NOT a challenge associated with peptide therapeutics?
a: They are degraded in the circulatory system
e: Peptides are like clever keys that fit their targets with amazing precision, so poor specificity is never their problem!

q: Which of the following methods of determining distances to celestial objects is useful for the greatest distances?
e: As the universe stretches, Hubble's law tracks runaway galaxies across the deepest distances of space.

q: Which of the following is the best estimate of the electricity consumption of a petascale [PEH-tah-scale] supercomputer today?
e: Thinking super-fast takes massive energy, and these digital giants gulp down about eight megawatts, like thousands of busy homes.

q: Which of the following is the term for a pair of stars that are not physically close to each other but appear as a single star when viewed from Earth?
e: An optical double is a cosmic trick where two lonely stars only seem close because they line up from our viewpoint.

q: Assuming the Boltzmann constant k = 1.38 10-23 joules per Kelvin, what is the average translational kinetic energy in joules of molecules of an ideal gas at 127o Celsius?
e: Warming those particles to four hundred Kelvin makes them dance with an average energy of 8.28 times 10 to the minus 21 joules.

q: The Leonid [LEE-ah-nid] meteor shower occurs in what month?
e: Every chilly November, Earth sweeps through a dusty comet trail, lighting up autumn skies with dancing Leonid shooting stars.

q: Assuming that you start with 100% U-238 and the U- 238 decays to Pb-206, how many half-lives are needed to yield 625 atoms of U-238 and 19,375 atoms of Pb-206?
e: Halving five times turns a huge crowd of twenty thousand uranium atoms into just six hundred twenty-five survivors!

q: Which of these atmospheric layers is furthest from the Earth's surface?
e: High above our heads, the sizzling thermosphere perches way up top, farther out than any of the other layers.

q: For the June solstice, which of the following statements is NOT true?
a: The northern hemisphere experiences the day with the longest period of sunlight
There are 24 hours of sunlight in the Arctic Circle
Earth is further from the Sun than it is at the winter solstice
The Sun is directly overhead at noon in the Arctic Circle
e: While the Arctic gets nonstop daylight, the Sun only skims the horizon, never standing directly overhead at noon.

q: Looking down on the Earth in the Northern Hemisphere, which of the following BEST describes the circulation of air above an anticyclone:
a: air spiraling inward in a counter-clockwise direction
air spiraling outward in a counter-clockwise direction
air spiraling inward in a clockwise direction
air spiraling outward in a clockwise direction
e: High pressure pushes air outward, and Earth's spin twists it into a cheerful clockwise swirl.

q: Most of the galaxies in the universe are classified as which of the following:
e: While giant spirals get all the glory, pint-sized dwarf galaxies quietly outnumber everything else in our starry universe!

q: Traditional solar cells have a maximum conversion efficiency of about 34% because many of the captured wavelengths result in the creation of heat, not electrons. Newly published research has shown that cell efficiencies can reach up to 44% by doing which of the following?
a: Using gallium arsenide instead of silicon
Using selenium in one of the layers
e: Blue light packs extra punch, so capturing energetic blue wavelengths stops wasted heat and unlocks way more power.

q: A freely falling object has a constant acceleration of 9.8 meters per second squared. Which of the following is correct?
a: The object's displacement changes by 9.8 meters every second squared
The object's acceleration increases by 9.8 meters per second squared each second
The object travels 9.8 meters each second
The object's speed increases by 9.8 meters per second each second
e: Gravity gives falling things a steady push, adding 9.8 meters per second to their speed every single second!

q: Which of the following are the correct units for Young's modulus?
e: Measuring how stiffly materials push back uses pressure, which neatly breaks down into kilograms per meter second squared.

q: A star is consistently observed to have a 1% dip in brightness lasting for 3 hours every 3 days. Which of the following is the best explanation of this phenomenon?
a: The star is an intrinsic variable
The observation is distorted by parallax
e: A faithful exoplanet playing peek-a-boo blocks a tiny splash of starlight every time it marches across its sun.

q: Which of the following quarks does NOT have negative charge?
e: Like a sunny little spark, the charm quark smiles with positive electric charge instead of a negative one!

q: Of which of the following is the Hubble Law most directly a consequence:
e: As distant galaxies zoom away, their light stretches out just like a fading train whistle, showing off the Doppler shift.

q: The core of the Sun can reach which temperature?
e: Deep at the Sun's fiery heart, temperatures roar up to an unbelievable twenty-seven million degrees Fahrenheit!

q: An RLC circuit consists of a 2 henry inductor, a 1000 ohm resistor, an 8 farad capacitor, and a power supply in series. With what frequency in hertz must the power supply operate in order to establish resonance in the circuit?
e: The inductor and capacitor team up, timing their electrical heartbeat to perfectly match one-eighth of a cycle each second.

q: In a series resonant circuit, the circuit impedance at resonance is always which of the following?
e: At just the right rhythm, opposing electrical pushes cancel each other out, leaving only the simple resistance behind.

q: If the proper energy of 15 grams of matter is 1.35 x 10n joules, what is the value of n?
e: A tiny pinch of matter packs a gigantic punch, releasing energy where the power of ten reaches fifteen!

q: In compact fluorescent light bulbs, conversion of electrical energy into radiant energy occurs due to which of the following?
e: Zippy little electrons bump into gas atoms and share their energy through inelastic scattering, making the bulb glow brightly!

q: A rising parcel of air reaches the lifting condensation level at 2,000 meters at a dew point temperature of 15C. At 3,000 meters, the temperature of this parcel of air will on average be:
e: As the moist cloud rises another kilometer, it chills by five degrees, cooling down from fifteen to ten degrees!

q: The mass of a raindrop is 4 milligrams. Which of the following represents the correct mass in grams of the raindrop?
e: A milligram is one-thousandth of a gram, so our tiny falling raindrop weighs four times ten to the minus three grams.

q: At which of the following locations would an observer find the greatest force due to the Earth's gravity?
e: Because Earth is slightly squished, standing at the North Pole puts you closest to its center, where gravity pulls tightest!

q: Which of the following MOST directly modulates the intensity of incoming solar radiation through the course of a year:
a: the time for 1 orbit of Earth around the Sun
Earth's rapid rotation about its axis
e: Our planet leans on a gentle tilt, tipping us toward the warm sunshine in summer and away in winter.

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are studying semimetals. Which of the following best describes a semimetal?
a: A material with no overlap between the valence band and the conduction band
A material with a complete overlap between the valence band and the conduction band
A material with a slight overlap between the valence band and the conduction band
A material with a reversed ordering of the valence band and the conduction band
e: In semimetals, electron energy bands act like polite neighbors, barely crossing fences with just a tiny, gentle overlap.

q: Which of the following describes how the electric potential due to a point charge scales with distance away from the charge?
e: As you drift away from a charge, its electric potential softly weakens with the inverse of your distance.

q: When do eclipses of the sun occur?
e: A solar eclipse happens during a new moon, when the moon sneaks right between Earth and the Sun to block daylight!

q: The orbit of Mercury has a semi major axis of 0.4 AU and an eccentricity of 0.2. At which of the following distances from the Sun in AU will Mercury move the slowest?
e: Mercury takes a leisurely breath and travels slowest when it wanders farthest from the Sun, out at point-five units.

q: To early astrophysical researchers, the Sun was originally found to emit about one-third of the expected amount of neutrinos. Which of the following BEST explains why:
a: about 66% of the neutrinos were deflected by the Earth's magnetic field
two-thirds of the neutrinos were too energetic to be detected
neutrinos were changing flavor on their way to Earth
original estimations of the numbers emitted by the Sun were incorrect
e: Sneaky little neutrinos played dress-up on their journey, changing flavors before reaching Earth so early detectors missed them!

q: In which of the following types of electrical equipment is high resistance most undesirable?
e: Superconducting magnets want electricity to glide with zero roadblocks, so even a tiny bit of resistance spoils the magic.

q: Which of the following is not a polymorph of silica?
e: While the other crystal cousins are pure silica, wadsleyite is built from different mineral ingredients entirely.

q: Which of the following will double the power dissipated by a resistor?
a: Doubling the voltage across the resistor
Decreasing the voltage to one half of the original value
Increasing the voltage by a factor of the square root of 2
Decreasing the voltage by a factor of the square root of 2
e: Since power squares the voltage, bumping voltage up by the square root of two neatly doubles the energy released!

q: What bright features extending from the Sun's photosphere, often loop-shaped, are composed of relatively cool plasma that emits visible light?
e: Prominences are gorgeous, giant loops of cooler glowing gas that leap high above the Sun like fiery rollercoasters!

q: The Intertropical Convergence Zone is NOT characterized by which of the following?
e: Here at the equator, winds rush together for a giant rainy hug, which means air gathers instead of spreading out or diverging.

q: Which of the following is considered an activator of fluorescence because when present in small concentrations it usually causes a ruby crystal to fluoresce a bright deep red:
e: A tiny sprinkle of chromium sneaks into the crystal, waking up its atoms to glow with a dazzling red sparkle!

q: Of the history of the universe, which of the following best represents the period of time Earth has existed?
e: If the universe were a giant birthday cake, our cozy Earth was only baked during the very last third of the party.

q: Which of the following is true regarding light bulbs?
a: Incandescent bulbs have about one-tenth of the lifespan as compact fluorescent lamps
Compact fluorescent lamps produce light by exciting argon gas
The cost to buy a single incandescent bulb is generally higher than the cost to buy an equivalent CFL
LED lamps are highly stable at high temperatures
e: Old glowing bulbs work so hard making heat that they burn out ten times faster than clever curly lamps!

q: Liquid water can store more heat energy than an equal amount of any other naturally occurring substance because liquid water has which of the following characteristics?
a: It has its greatest density at 4 Celsius
It can be changed into a solid or a gas
e: Water acts like a patient heat sponge because its high specific heat lets it soak up warmth without quickly boiling over!

q: Which of the following is not true regarding electrochemical cells?
a: Concentration cells have a standard cell potential of zero
In a Daniell cell, copper is oxidized
The equilibrium reduction potential of a half cell is related to the standard electrode potential via the Nernst equation
Electrochemical cells using water as a solvent are usually limited to a cell potential of approximately 2.5 volts
e: In this bustling little battery, zinc gives up electrons while copper happily catches them, meaning copper is actually reduced, not oxidized.

q: Which of the following energy sources is most directly derived from the sun?
e: The sun warmly tickles our atmosphere, making rising pockets of warm air dance around as playful wind!

q: Which of the following best estimates the momentum carried by an electromagnetic wave with energy of 30 joules?
e: When you divide energy by light's blazing speed, thirty joules becomes a tiny push of ten to the minus seven.

q: Which of the following most commonly functions to limit current to one direction:
e: A diode acts like a strict one-way door, cheerfully waving electricity forward while refusing to let it go backward.

q: Researchers at SLAC National Lab are studying scattering processes that violate the conservation of helicity [heel-IH-sih-dee] to the maximum possible extent. Which of the following best describes helicity?
a: The projection of a particle's spin onto its momentum
The angle between a particle's magnetic moment and its spin
The angular momentum of a particle with respect to the collision axis
The expectation value of a particle's magnetic quadrupole moment
e: Imagine a flying, spinning baseball; helicity just checks if its spin points the same way it is zooming forward.

q: Which of the following is the term for the set of planets that will exhibit a full range of phases as observed from Earth?
e: Planets closer to the sun than Earth are called inferior, and they show off every glowing phase just like our moon does!

q: Researchers at the DOE's Joint Genome [JEE-nome] Institute recently performed a transcriptomic [trans-krip-TAWN-ik] analysis on mycorrhizal [MY-koh-RYE-zul] fungi [fun- ji] to understand their mechanisms of drought adaptation. Which of the following procedures was integral to this analysis?
a: Measured numbers of RNAs for all of the fungal [FUN-gul] genes
Measured the levels of every fungal protein
Sequenced all of the fungi's [fun-jize] proteins
e: Scientists counted all the RNA messages to hear which survival recipes the thirsty little fungi were secretly reading.

q: In order for a process to have no change in entropy, which of the following properties must it possess?
e: A reversible process is so gentle and tidy that it can neatly rewind backward without creating any messy new disorder.

q: For all collisions, all of the following properties are conserved except:
e: When things go bump and crash, some motion energy sneakily turns into heat or sound instead of being saved.

q: Which of the following best describes Bernoulli's principle?
a: Fluid pressure increases as speed increases
Fluid pressure decreases as speed increases
Fluid pressure is proportional to speed
Fluid pressure is inversely proportional to speed
e: When water or air zooms by really fast, it relaxes its sideways push, making its pressure drop!

q: Aquaculture applications for geothermal energy are particularly promising for all of the following reasons, except:
a: A variety of freshwater or marine organisms can be raised
There is an abundance of geothermal resources at the required temperature range
Consistent water temperatures increase survival rates
Consistent water circulation enables year-round harvesting of consistently-sized fish
e: Earth's deep heat keeps water cozy for swimming fish, but warm rocks do not swirl or circulate the water on their own.

q: A planet orbits a star in an elliptical orbit. When the planet is furthest from the star, which of the following statements is true?
a: The angular momentum of the planet is at a maximum
The angular momentum of the planet is at a minimum
The kinetic energy of the planet is at a minimum
The kinetic energy of the planet is at a maximum
e: Far away from its star, an orbiting world lazily slows down, so its energy of motion drops to its lowest dip.

q: The energy price spikes in the 1970s and in 2008 suggested which of the following about U.S. energy usage?
a: Usage rises in response to rising prices
Usage stays the same when prices rise
Usage drops in response to rising prices
There was no consistent trend about U.S. energy usage
e: When fuel got super pricey, thrifty drivers and families tapped the brakes and used far less power.

q: An electron is moving along the x-axis in the positive direction, within a uniform magnetic field that is oriented toward the positive z-axis. In which of the following directions does the Lorentz [lohr-ENZ] force act?
e: Because electrons carry a mischievous negative charge, the magnetic field flips its push upward into the positive y-axis!

q: Work W is done to extend a spring beyond its natural length by a small distance x. Assuming a spring constant of 1, which of the following is the magnitude of the maximum force done by the person stretching the spring?
e: Since pulling a spring gets tougher with every inch, your peak force equals twice the work divided by that stretch.

q: Placodonts, which lived during the Triassic Period, were a group of:
e: These chunky reptiles were marine animals that loved paddling through prehistoric oceans, crunching shellfish with their flat, cozy teeth.

q: Two sounds of the same intensity will be perceived by the human ear to have the same loudness if:
a: The two sounds have the same pitch
The two sounds have the same pitch and the same timbre
The two sounds have the same timbre
The two sounds are below 100 Hertz
e: Our ears are picky listeners! Two sounds only feel equally loud if they share both the same musical note and the same instrument flavor.

q: Which of the following extends farthest from the Sun?
e: The Oort cloud is a giant, icy bubble drifting way out at the very edge of our solar neighborhood, farthest from the Sun.

q: Gallium arsenide would most likely be found in which of the following?
e: Gallium arsenide loves catching sunshine! This special semiconductor material works inside solar photovoltaic cells to turn bright beams into speedy electric power.

q: Which of the following is NOT a discovery attributed to Edwin Hubble?
a: The redshift observed in light spectra from distant galaxies is proportional to their distance from Earth
The Andromeda nebula is a separate galaxy from the Milky Way
The existence of the asteroid 1373 Cincinnati
e: Another clever sky-watcher actually spotted galactic redshifts first, though Hubble later used those stretched-out light waves to show our universe is expanding.

q: A magnet would NOT attract which of the following substances?
e: Unlike iron, aluminum refuses to join the magnetic party, so fridge magnets just slide right off soda cans.

q: Which of the following are proper units for entropy [EN-troh-pee]?
e: Entropy measures how heat spreads out, so we count energy in joules shared across each degree of temperature in kelvin.

q: What is the speed of a particle that has a Lorentz factor of 3.0?
e: When relativity stretches things out by three, Einstein's cosmic speed math shows this zippy particle travels at two root two over three.

q: Which of the following countries has the highest percentage of its electricity produced by nuclear power?
e: France loves atomic energy, using bustling nuclear power plants to bake most of the country's electricity with glowing atoms.

q: Brookhaven National Lab researchers are using electron diffraction to image structural details of crystalline materials. Which of the following is closest to the ratio of the wavelength of these electrons to that of x-rays used in x-ray diffraction?
e: Tiny, super-fast electrons have wave ripples about a tenth the size of X-ray light waves, making the ratio roughly zero-point-one.

q: What arises in space, thought to be from particle pairs that blink into existence and promptly annihilate?
e: Empty space is secretly bustling! Ghostly pairs of particles pop into existence and vanish in a flash, buzzing with vacuum energy.

q: During an El Nio event, what wind pattern falters, causing cold, nutrient-rich water to be trapped underneath warmer waters?
e: When the trusty trade winds take an unexpected nap, ocean breezes weaken and warm water traps the chilly sea below.

q: Which of the following is the approximate distance in kilometers covered by a photon in one year?
e: Light never hits the snooze button, racing through space fast enough to cover a mind-boggling nine trillion kilometers in a single year.

q: The NOvA [nova] collaboration is performing an experiment in which neutrinos [new-TREE-noze] generated at Fermilab are sent to a detector 500 miles away in Minnesota. Which of the following best describes how the neutrinos travel between these facilities?
a: Neutrinos travel on a curved path over the surface of the Earth
Neutrinos oscillate, preventing them from traveling in straight lines
Neutrinos interact very little with matter, enabling them to travel through the ground
Neutrinos are reflected off the stratosphere
e: Neutrinos are cosmic ghosts that barely touch anything, letting them zoom straight through solid Earth from one lab to another.

q: Which of the following is the BEST explanation of why Population One stars have a high metal content:
a: old stars lose their metals as they age
old stars convert their metals to non-metals
