young stars acquire metals when they form from previous stars that created the metals
all stars accumulate metals early in their development
e: Younger stars are born from dusty leftovers of older exploded stars, inheriting all the shiny heavy metals their stellar ancestors cooked up.

q: SLAC [slack] National Accelerator Lab scientists are studying the physical properties of trimethylamine [try-meth-il-ah-meen]. Which of the following is closest to the pKb [p.k.b.] of this compound?
e: This stinky fish-smelling chemical is a moderate base, which neatly lands its base-strength score, or pKb, right around four.

q: An electromagnetic wave goes into a block of glass with an index of refraction of n = 1.1. In terms of the speed of light C, which of the following is closest to the speed at which the wave propagates inside the glass medium?
e: Entering the glass slows light down just a little bit, dividing its speed so it travels at about zero-point-nine C.

q: Which of the following stellar reactions would be the dominant pathway by which a star of similar mass as our Sun converts hydrogen to helium?
e: Inside our cozy Sun, friendly hydrogen protons smash together step-by-step in the proton-proton chain to build helium.

q: Which of the following adjacent pairs of thermodynamic processes are a part of a Carnot [CAR-noh] cycle?
e: A Carnot engine works by first stretching warmly at steady temperature, then smoothly continuing into isentropic expansion.

q: When a resistor, inductor, and capacitor are connected in series to an AC generator, the current through the capacitor must be in phase with the voltage across which of the following?
e: Because the same electric current flows through the whole chain, it dances in perfect lockstep with the resistor's voltage.

q: The Sun's temperature is highest at its core and decreases with increasing distance from the core until its temperature reaches a minimum and increases throughout the Sun's atmosphere. Which of the following layers of the Sun is closest to where this minimum occurs?
e: Right at the bottom of the chromosphere, the fiery Sun hits its coolest spot before sizzling back up into a blazing outer coat.

q: A golf cart and a fire truck collide. Which vehicle experiences a greater force in the collision?
a: Both vehicles experience the same force
Depends on the speeds of the vehicles
e: Even though the little cart gets squished more, both vehicles push back against each other with the exact same forceful bump!

q: Researchers at SLAC [slack] developed a microscopic rake that enables better mixing of deposited materials on surfaces, resulting in more efficient solar cells. Which of the following solar cells benefit from this invention?
e: That tiny rake neatly combs long, bendy plastic chains inside polymer cells, helping them catch sunshine much better.

q: A 10,000-kilogram truck is rolling at 2 meters per second when 5000 kilograms of cargo is dropped into it. Which of the following, in meters per second, is closest to the truck's speed afterwards?
e: Piling on heavy cargo slows the rolling truck down to about 1.3 meters per second because extra weight is harder to push.

q: A box is sitting on a ramp with a coefficient of static friction of 0.7. Which of the following is closest to the smallest ramp angle for which the box will begin to slide down the ramp?
e: The ramp has to tilt up to about 35 degrees before gravity finally beats the sticky friction and sends the box sliding!

q: Which of the following BEST describes how one would compute the speed for a sound wave through a liquid:
a: the square of the density of liquid divided by its bulk modulus
the square of the bulk modulus of the liquid divided by its density
the square root of the density of liquid divided by its bulk modulus
the square root of the bulk modulus of the liquid divided by its density
e: Sound zips through liquids by balancing springiness against heaviness, calculated by the square root of bulk modulus divided by density.

q: What are the two kinds of motion displayed by the motion of a bowling ball?
e: As it glides down the lane, the ball happily rolls forward while spinning around, showing both translational and rotational motion.

q: Chemists at Ames Lab are using powder X-ray diffraction to study novel hetero-structures. Which of the following photon wavelengths is closest to the one they used for their diffraction experiment?
e: To peek between tiny atoms sitting close together, scientists use X-rays with teeny wavelengths of about one angstrom.

q: Uniform circular motion is achieved by applying force in what direction?
a: Away from the center of rotation
e: To keep whirling in a neat circle, you must always be gently tugged right toward the center of the spin.

q: Which of the following would not be considered a balance-of- system component for a stand-alone wind power system?
e: The spinning turbine is the main star making the electricity, while all the balance-of-system parts just play supporting roles.

q: Which of the following best explains how and why galaxies in the universe are moving relative to each other?
a: Most galaxies are moving away from each other because space is expanding
All galaxies are moving toward each other because space is contracting
Most galaxies are moving away from each other because space is contracting
All galaxies are moving toward each other because space is expanding
e: Like raisins in rising bread dough, most galaxies drift apart because the space between them is constantly stretching out.

q: The messenger particles of weak interaction are which of the following?
e: Three busy little helper particles—the Z, W+, and W- bosons—deliver all the messages for the weak force.

q: Given that nuclear reactions are a great source of energy, which of the following represents one of the main concerns about nuclear energy production?
a: The expense of building and maintaining safe nuclear power plants
Lack of knowledge about the technique
e: Nuclear power makes lots of energy, but leftover radioactive waste piles up and stays dangerous for thousands of years.

q: Which of the following is closest to the length of time, in years, it takes Earth to complete one cycle of its orbital eccentricity variation?
e: Earth takes a grand, patient journey of 100,000 years to slowly stretch its circular orbit into an oval and back.

q: The resistance of a hot tungsten filament is about 10 times the cold resistance. What is the resistance, in ohms, of a 100 watt and 200 volt lamp filament when not in use?
e: When hot and glowing, the filament has 400 ohms of resistance, so resting cold, it drops down to 40 ohms.

q: Which of the following BEST describes how planets are distinguishable from stars in the night sky?
a: Planets have periods of retrograde motion while stars do not
e: Unlike steady stars, planets wander across our night sky and sometimes look like they are playfully looping backward!

q: If yellow light has a wavelength of 550 nanometers, which of the following colors and associated wavelengths of light in nanometers is most energetic?
e: Shorter light waves pack more punch, so green light at 500 nanometers carries more energy than longer red waves.

q: Three hundred-millibar charts are used to visualize the dynamics of jet streams. Lines on these charts correspond to places that are equal in which of the following properties?
e: Because the air pressure stays fixed at 300 millibars everywhere on the chart, the lines show your changing altitude.

q: In a nuclear plant, 1 kilogram of mass is converted to energy. Given c = 3 x 108 meters per second, how much energy would be produced?
e: Einstein showed matter holds giant secrets, unlocking one kilogram of mass into a whopping 90 petajoules of energy!

q: Which of the following properties of felsic melts makes them more viscous than mafic melts?
e: Packed with sticky silica, this lava links together like melted marshmallow, making it thick and slow to flow.

q: A lady in a spacecraft travelling away from the Earth at 4/5 the speed of light gives birth to a child at 1:00 p.m., which, according to the spacecraft's clock, is only 3 hours after the spacecraft departed from the Earth. Assuming constant acceleration during those 3 hours, what is the child's birth time according to a stationary clock on the Earth?
e: Zooming near light speed makes the ship's clocks tick slow, so four Earth hours pass while only three tick inside, making it 2:00 p.m.!

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of an ichnofossil?
e: Trace fossils are just leftovers like footprints or burrows, but a shiny shell was an actual piece of the creature's own body.

q: The atomic matter converted into energy by the atomic bomb in World War II at Hiroshima weighed about as much as a:
e: Believe it or not, a tiny pinch of matter weighing no more than a shiny penny unleashed all that gigantic, explosive energy.

q: Which of the following classes of objects is distributed around the Sun with spherical symmetry?
e: Long-period comets swoop in from the giant, round Oort cloud, surrounding our sun like a giant, fluffy bubble of icy snowballs!

q: The rest frame lifetime of a muon is 2.2 microseconds. Muons are produced in the upper atmosphere by collisions with cosmic rays. The light travel time from the upper atmosphere to the ground is about 150 microseconds. Nevertheless, a substantial fraction of muons produced in the upper atmosphere are observed on the ground. For an observer on the ground, which of the following principles best explains this phenomenon?
e: Because these tiny muons zoom so close to light speed, time stretches out for them, letting them live long enough to reach Earth!

q: Which of the following statements best reflects our current understanding of the past and present of Mars' atmosphere?
a: It has always been about as thick Earth's atmosphere today
It has always been much thinner than Earth's atmosphere today
It was thick shortly after formation, but has since thinned due to solar wind
It was thin shortly after formation, but has since thickened due to volcanic outgassing
e: Young Mars wore a cozy, thick blanket of air, but rowdy solar winds slowly blew it away into space over billions of years.

q: Which of the following quantities has an inverse-cubic relationship with distance?
a: The magnitude of the gravitational force between two point masses
The electric potential energy for a point charge
The magnetic field strength at an axial point from the center of a current loop
The speed of a satellite in circular orbit around the Earth
e: A loop of electricity acts like a tiny magnet, so its invisible pull fades extra fast, shrinking with distance cubed as you back away.

q: Which of the following laws expresses the increase in redshift of a galaxy's spectral lines with distance?
e: Hubble discovered that distant galaxies are speeding away like runaway balloons, stretching their starlight red the farther out they run.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are studying medical imaging scintillators that absorb high-energy light and release lower-wavelength light that can be detected with a camera. In what type of imaging are these materials most likely used?
e: X-rays pack crazy energy, so cameras use special glowing crystals to turn those invisible beams into gentle light we can actually see!

q: The liquid-drop model of the nucleus was originally proposed based on what observation?
e: Just like raindrops big and small pack water together equally tightly, every atomic center shares nearly the exact same crowded density.

q: Which of the following BEST describes the zenith:
a: the point in the sky that is at 180 degrees of inclination to the horizon
the opposite position on the ecliptic to an observer
the point on the celestial sphere directly overhead of an observer
e: If you look straight up at the sky, right above your nose, you are gazing right at the magical point called the zenith!

q: In a wild shot, Guido flings a pool ball of mass m off a 0.68 meter high pool table with downward spin, and the ball hits the floor with a vertical speed of 6.0 meters per second. How fast was the ball moving vertically in meters per second when it left the pool table?
e: As gravity pulls the falling ball downward, it speeds up, meaning it started off rolling over the edge at about 4.7 meters per second.

q: Scientists at the Joint Genome Institute are using 16S rRNA sequencing to profile bacterial populations. What is the typical purpose of this sequence in the bacterium?
a: Transferring amino acids from the tRNA to the nascent peptide
Binding the codon at the A site
e: Inside the busy cell, this helpful RNA grabs onto a special docking spot called the Shine-Dalgarno sequence to kick off protein making!

q: Changing which of the following will NOT result in a change in the voltage induced in a rotating wire coil?
e: The magnetic dance only cares about the spin and coil size, so changing the wire's resistance never changes the voltage sparked inside.

q: Which of the following characteristics make universal motors attractive for home appliances?
e: Your trusty vacuum loves these spunky little motors because they spin super fast and pack lots of muscle to tackle tough chores!

q: Which of the following regions of an active galactic nucleus is the most distant from the supermassive black hole?
e: While other gas huddles close to the hungry black hole, the narrow line region drifts far away in the cool outer cosmic suburbs.

q: The period of oscillation of a given simple pendulum on a grandfather's clock here on earth is 1 second. What would be the period in seconds of the same pendulum on another planet where the gravitational acceleration is 1/4 that of the earth?
e: Weaker gravity gives the swinging pendulum a gentle, lazy pull, doubling its round-trip time from one second up to two seconds.

q: Which of the following geometries is inconsistent with a flat universe?
e: A horn shape curls and flares with negative curvature, so it bends space in ways a perfectly flat universe never could!

q: Which of the following does NOT help explain why the theoretical yield of cellular respiration is never actually achieved?
a: Pyruvate [py-ROO-vayt] must be actively transported out of the mitochondria [my-tuh- KON-dree-uh]
Phosphate is actively transported into the mitochondria
ADP and ATP are actively exchanged across the inner mitochondrial membrane
The inner mitochondrial membrane leaks protons
e: Cellular powerhouses actually pull pyruvate inside to make energy instead of pushing it out, so that statement is completely backwards!

q: The rate at which temperature decreases with increasing altitude is known as the:
e: As you climb higher up a chilly mountain, the air cools down at a steady tempo that scientists call the lapse rate.

q: Two objects of masses m1 and m2 with speeds v1 and v2, where v2 = 0, suffer collision, stick together, and move off with speed V. Which of the following equals the ratio v1/V?
e: When a rolling cart scoops up a resting buddy, their combined mass slows them down, making the starting speed ratio one plus m2 over m1!

q: Which of the following cells cannot be recharged?
e: Think of primary batteries like one-way adventure tickets: once their energetic chemicals finish their job, they simply cannot be recharged.

q: What is an object's average angular acceleration, in degrees per second per second, if it transited 72 degrees with an initial angular velocity of 8 degrees per second and a final angular velocity of 10 degrees per second?
e: As this spinning dancer speeds up from eight to ten across seventy-two degrees, physics shows she steadily gains one-fourth of a degree per second squared.

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are developing hardware for training artificial neural networks. One important aspect of a neural network is the activation function. Which of the following functions best approximates the "all-or-none" behavior of a neuron?
e: Just like flipping a bedroom light switch instantly on or off, a step function hops between two choices without any halfway values.

q: The helium flash occurs in what stage of stellar evolution?
a: Tip of the red giant branch
e: Right at the very tip of the red giant stage, an aging star gets so hot that its helium core suddenly bursts awake!

q: Scientists at Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility are trying to form protons that are squeezed into a configuration smaller than their typical one. Which of the following is closest to the typical radius of the proton, in meters?
e: Protons are unbelievably tiny building blocks, measuring just ten to the minus fifteen meters across, which is far smaller than any dust speck.

q: When using a psychrometer and the two temperatures read are nearly identical, what conclusion would you reach?
a: A change in temperature is forecast
The air has a high relative humidity
The dew point temperature is very low
e: When both thermometers match, water cannot evaporate to cool them off because the air is already packed full of moisture!

q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of using LEDs over incandescent light sources?
e: These clever little lights are amazing, but they are grumpy about heat; their performance changes and drops if they get too warm.

q: In the ray approximation in optics, which of the following is NOT true for a converging lens:
a: a ray parallel to the optical axis passes through the focus
a ray passing through the center of the lens is bent parallel to the optical axis
an object at infinity is imaged at the focus
a ray passing through the focus is bent parallel to the optical axis
e: A beam of light marching right through the very center of a lens never bends; it simply zips straight through without changing direction!

q: Which of the following is the device in a galvanic cell that completes the electric circuit by connecting the two sides of the cell with an inert electrolyte:
e: A salt bridge acts like a friendly tunnel between both sides, letting ions march across to keep electricity flowing smoothly.

q: An asteroid with linear momentum is gravitationally captured by a planet. Which of the following best explains where the linear momentum of the asteroid went?
a: Conserved in the asteroid's orbital velocity
e: Nothing gets lost in space; the incoming asteroid’s forward shove simply nudges the whole planet-asteroid team together across the cosmos.

q: Seismologists believe that Earth's inner core rotates faster than the rest of the planet. What evidence do they cite?
a: The fastest route for s-waves is shifting eastward over time
The fastest route for s-waves is shifting westward over time
The fastest route for p-waves is shifting eastward over time
The fastest route for p-waves is shifting westward over time
e: Deep earthquake p-waves take a speedy shortcut through Earth's center, and that path is slowly shifting eastward as the inner core spins ahead.

q: Which of the following colors of light would give the highest resolving power of a compound light microscope:
e: Ultraviolet light has super short, tight waves, allowing it to squeeze into tiny spaces and reveal the sharpest pictures under a microscope.

q: If you were using a 50-millimeter camera lens and changed the lens aperture from 8.0 to 5.6, about how much LESS light would the lens be allowing to pass through it:
e: Shifting between these f-stops changes the lens opening by one full step, which cuts the incoming light by fifty percent.

q: Scientists at SLAC National Accelerator Lab are exploring theories involving supersymmetry. Which of the following best describes supersymmetry?
a: Symmetry of reversing the direction of time
Correspondences between fermion and boson particles
e: Supersymmetry imagines a cosmic buddy system where every matter fermion particle has a matching partner among the force-carrying bosons!

q: A galaxy shows a strong bar and very loosely-wound spiral arms. Which of the following would most likely be its class?
e: In galaxy naming, the letters SB mean a barred spiral, while the c shows its swirling stellar arms are loosely unwound.

q: Sophie is plotting the kinetic energy of a 5-kilogram mass on the y-axis and its speed on the x-axis. If she uses a log-log plot, which of the following curves would best fit her data?
e: Because kinetic energy depends on speed squared, graphing the powers of both numbers creates a straight line with a slope of two.

q: Which of the following is NOT considered a practical source of biodiesel?
e: Essential oils are made for sweet smells rather than bulky fats, making them far too pricey and impractical for powering engines.

q: Which of the following statements BEST describes why protons in the nucleus do NOT fly apart due to coulomb repulsion?
a: The negative charges of the orbiting electrons neutralize the positive charges of the protons
The coulomb force does not manifest within the nucleus
The strong force between quarks dominates
e: Even though positive protons push apart, the mighty strong force between their quarks hugs them together with an unbeatable nuclear embrace!

q: Under what circumstances could the relative humidity exceed 100% without producing condensation in the air?
e: Floating water vapor needs tiny dust specks to grab onto, so without those condensation seeds, clouds cannot form even in soaked air.

q: What is the speed of light in meters per second for monochromatic light of 780 nanometers in glass with a refractive index of 1.55:
e: Glass acts like thick mud for zooming light beams, slowing them down to about 1.9 times ten to the eighth meters each second.

q: Which of the following best describes the absorption characteristics of dust in the interstellar medium?
a: Its effects are strongest in radio wavelengths
It absorbs light at all wavelengths with about the same efficiency
It preferentially absorbs optical light at redder wavelengths
It preferentially absorbs optical light at bluer wavelengths
e: Hungry space dust loves snacking on shorter blue light waves, letting the longer red ones slip safely by.

q: Which of the following particles has the least penetrating power?
e: Big, bulky alpha particles run out of puff so fast that a single sheet of paper completely stops them.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding a wheel rolling along a surface?
a: If the wheel is rolling smoothly, the only friction acting on it is static friction
When rolling down a ramp, the force of static friction on the wheel is directed down the ramp
When rolling on a flat surface, the force of static friction on the wheel is directed in the opposite direction as the motion of the wheel
For a wheel rolling down a ramp, the normal force is perpendicular to the ramp
e: When a wheel rolls downhill, friction actually pushes up the ramp to keep it spinning instead of sliding like a sled.

q: Which of the following is the most common location of young blue and white stars in a spiral galaxy:
e: Shiny young blue stars love crowding inside the swirling spiral arms, where cozy gas clouds build fresh new suns.

q: Which of the following events occurred in the Late Mississippian?
e: Long ago, giant land masses Gondwana and Laurasia slowly bumped into each other like sleepy bumper cars to build a mega-continent.

q: Whose equation describes the relationship between the concentration of an electro-active species and electric potential?
e: A clever scientist named Nernst figured out the secret recipe connecting chemical crowds to electric zap.

q: Scoria is most typically described as having which of the following textures:
e: Scoria rock is vesicular because fizzy volcanic gases leave it full of tiny, bubbly pockets like an airy sponge.

q: Which of the following will increase the entropy [EN-troh-pee] of a system?
a: Changing the phase from a liquid to a solid
e: Giving particles extra room lets them wander everywhere, creating much more playful mess and disorder inside the bigger space.

q: Which of the following is generally NOT true regarding diffraction of light:
a: when white light is passed through a diffraction grating, shorter wavelengths are diffracted the most
if laser light is passed through a diffraction grating it will produce an interference pattern as a series of dots on a screen
white light passing through a diffraction grating is spread into a rainbow of colors
e: Long light waves actually bend the most around tiny obstacles, so shorter waves never get spread out the furthest.

q: A solid, spherical object is floating in equilibrium in water with two-thirds of the object's volume submerged. The object is then pushed down until it is completely submerged. What is the ratio of the magnitude of the buoyant force on the object to the magnitude of the force of gravity on the object while it is submerged?
e: Pushing the whole ball under makes the water shove back with extra muscle, three-halves as strong as gravity.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of laser light?
e: Laser light loves staying in tight, neat lines together, so it definitely does not spread out and scatter.

q: A light wave travels a distance of 3 10-7 meters in a medium of refractive index n 1.5. How much time does this trip take?
e: Because the medium slows light down, this super tiny trip takes just 1.5 times ten to the minus six nanoseconds.

q: Scientists at the Joint Genome Institute are studying giant viruses like Pandoravirus [pan-DORE-ah virus]. How many base pairs are in the genome of Pandoravirus?
e: This giant virus packs a huge backpack of life instructions, holding an impressive 2.5 million base pairs inside.

q: Scientists are using the Advanced Photon Source to study the gumboot chiton [KYE-tun]. This organism's teeth contain what element found in santabarbaraite?
e: These cool little creatures wear mouth armor made of iron, giving them super tough teeth to scrape tasty algae off rocks.

q: Which of the following best describes the luster of cut diamonds?
e: We call a diamond's brilliant sparkle adamantine because it catches the light with breathtaking, fiery shine.

q: When a wave passes into a new medium, the sudden change in which of the following properties of the wave is responsible for causing refraction?
e: When a wave enters a new home, its speed suddenly changes, causing it to trip and bend like a running puppy.

q: Paul is simulating a moving object, and can adjust its speed, density, and volume. He wants to cut its speed in half while keeping its kinetic energy constant. Which of the following other changes could he make to keep the kinetic energy constant?
a: Double both the volume and the density
Double the volume and quadruple the density
e: Cutting speed in half slashes energy by four, so doubling both volume and density gives it back four times the mass.

q: What is the wavelength in nanometers of a photon of period 3.33 10-18 seconds?
e: Traveling at light speed in that tiny split-second tick, the photon's little wave stretches out to exactly one nanometer.

q: Which of the following is the BEST description of a Cepheid variable star:
a: a pulsating variable varying in brightness in a very regular time period of 1 to 50 days
a short pulsating variable with a very regular period of 1 to 4 minutes
a binary star system with an eclipsing partner
a small k-type star with a very regular period of 1 to 3 weeks
e: These stars puff in and out like glowing cosmic hearts, brightening and dimming on a steady rhythm of 1 to 50 days.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a native element?
e: Pure gold and diamonds like to stand all alone, but a ruby is actually a cozy mineral blend of aluminum and oxygen.

q: Which of the following best represents a closed system?
a: A 2-liter bottle filled with aquatic plants, a fish, water, and a bit of air, sealed with a tight lid and placed in a window
A terrarium with a closed lid, some plants, and a live boa constrictor
e: The universe holds absolutely everything, so not a single crumb or beam of light can sneak in or out!

q: Elastic deformation is BEST described as:
a: the linear portion of a stress/strain curve
the ultimate strength of a material
e: Like a playful rubber band stretching smoothly and springing back, elastic deformation shows up as a neat, straight line on the graph.

q: What percentage of the world's geothermally produced electricity is produced in the United States?
e: Earth's underground heat bubbles with power, and the United States grabs a giant thirty percent slice of the whole planet's geothermal electricity!

q: According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, which of the following sectors consumed the most energy in the United States in 2014?
e: Hungry factories and busy builders in the industrial sector worked overtime, gulping down more energy in 2014 than anyone else!

q: The Coriolis effect causes northward flowing air currents in the Northern hemisphere to veer off course:
a: in the direction opposite to rotation
e: As our spinning planet whirls eastward, northward winds get nudged sideways to follow along in the exact direction Earth is rotating.

q: A 1 kilogram object is travelling to the left at 3 meters per second when it explodes into 2 equal pieces. One piece is travelling at 7 meters per second to the left after the explosion. What is the velocity in meters per second of the other piece after the explosion?
e: To balance the big blast that shot one half zooming left, momentum politely nudges the other half one meter per second to the right.

q: If object A and object B are in thermal equilibrium, and object B and object C are in thermal equilibrium, then object A and object C are also in thermal equilibrium. This situation is an example of what law of thermodynamics?
e: When two friends share warmth with a third, they all match, which is the famous rule called the zeroth law.

q: What is the standard SI unit for luminous intensity?
e: Shining like a cozy flame, the candela measures brightness just like a single glowing birthday candle!

q: Which of the following BEST describes where the zodiacal light is brightest to a stargazer at mid-northern latitudes:
a: within about 20 degrees of the ecliptic
at the western horizon at sunrise
at right angles to the Milky Way
e: Space dust gathers along the solar system's flat highway, so this lovely glow shines brightest within twenty degrees of the ecliptic line.

q: A current-carrying wire changes diameter from larger to smaller gauge. In which of the following locations would the current be greater?
a: At the location where the wire changes diameter
It would be the same at all points
e: Electric current is like an eager parade of charges; even through skinny wire squeezes, the same amount marches past every single point.

q: Which of the following is the abbreviated name of the most common field effect transistor in modern electronic circuitry:
e: Tucked inside almost every tiny computer chip, the MOSFET works tirelessly as the world's most popular electronic switch.

q: The area under the curve of a velocity versus time graph represents:
e: Multiplying your speed by the ticking clock fills in the graph, showing your total displacement from start to finish.

q: Sinuous [SIN-yoo-us] rilles on the Moon are thought to have been created by which of the following?
e: Long ago, fiery rivers of melted rock carved out winding tunnels, leaving behind smooth lava flows that shaped those moon grooves.

q: Which of the following statements most accurately describes Einstein's first postulate of special relativity?
a: The speed of light in a vacuum is the same in all inertial reference frames
The laws of physics are the same in all inertial reference frames
It is impossible for an observer to travel at the speed of light in a vacuum
An observer cannot discern between inertial acceleration and acceleration due to gravity
e: Einstein realized nature plays fair everywhere, so the laws of physics work the exact same way for anyone gliding smoothly through space.

q: Which of the following statements is true about the relationship between a BTU and a kilocalorie?
a: A BTU has about one tenth the energy of a kilocalorie
A BTU has about one fourth the energy of a kilocalorie
A BTU has about the same amount of energy as a kilocalorie
A BTU has about 251 times the energy of a kilocalorie
e: A little BTU packet of heat holds only about one fourth the cozy energy of a bigger kilocalorie snack!

q: Which of the following sources of energy is derived from the gravity fields of the Sun and the Moon?
e: As the Moon and Sun play gentle tug-of-war with Earth's oceans, their pulling gravity creates rise-and-fall ocean tidal power.

q: After combing your hair, the comb becomes electrically charged. You then use the comb to pick up electrically neutral bits of paper, without making contact between the comb and the paper. What process allowed you to pick up the paper bits?
e: The comb's charge gently shuffles the charges inside the paper bits without touching them, an invisible tug called polarization.

q: Chemists at Brookhaven National Lab are studying the protein BADC [bad C], which inhibits the rate-limiting step of fatty acid synthesis in plants. BADC inhibits this process when levels of fats in the cell are already high. In glycolysis [glye-KAWL-eh-sis], which of the following has the role most analogous to BADC?
e: When a cell has plenty of fuel, busy citrate steps up to say slow down, hitting the brakes just like BADC does.

q: Which of the following is the MOST likely ultimate fate of the universe if mass in the universe is less than the critical density and there is no dark energy:
a: it will eventually stop expanding and maintain a constant size
it will stop expanding and collapse
it will expand at an accelerating rate and then nearly collapse, then expand again and continue to oscillate this way forever
e: Without enough heavy gravity to pull the brakes, space has all the freedom it needs to keep coasting and expanding forever.

q: Which of the following provides the most accurate description of carrying capacity?
a: Population below the carrying capacity will increase primary succession
Population above the carrying capacity cannot be sustained indefinitely
Population above the carrying capacity will always run out of space
Population above the carrying capacity will always result in excessive CO2 levels
e: When a forest hosts too many hungry critters beyond its limit, the snacks run out, so that crowd simply cannot survive forever.

q: Princeton Plasma Physics Lab researchers are exploring the use of lithium metal as a plasma-facing component in the devices they are building. Which of the following devices uses a plasma-facing component?
e: A tokamak is a giant magnetic donut that traps super-hot, starry plasma right against its tough inner walls.

q: A dart is shot from ground level over level ground with a speed of 30 meters per second at an angle of 30 above the ground. Assuming no air resistance, what is the vertical speed in meters per second of the dart when it hits the ground?
e: The dart leaped upward at fifteen meters per second, so gravity politely returns it down at that exact same vertical speed!

q: What is the arc length, in miles, traveled by a rocket along a circular path whose angle measures 0.2 radians with a radius of 80 miles?
e: To find the rocket's curve, you just multiply its eighty-mile radius by point two radians to get sixteen thrilling miles!

q: If the tension in a stretched string is multiplied by a factor of 9, the speed of the transverse wave is multiplied by what factor?
e: Waves love square roots, so pulling the string nine times tighter makes the wiggle travel three times faster.

q: A room has a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 tesla, directed into the floor. A 2.0-meter copper rod parallel to the floor and with one end pointed toward you is moving to the right with a speed of 100 meters per second. What is the motional electromotive force in volts, and which end (near or far) is at higher potential?
e: Multiplying field, speed, and length gives one hundred volts, while magnetic force pushes positive charges toward the far end.

q: The habitable zone in our solar system ranges from approximately the orbit of Venus to the orbit of Mars. Which of the following best explains why astrobiologists are optimistic about the habitability of Jupiter's icy moon Europa, which is far outside the habitable zone?
a: It is rich in organic carbon molecules
It has a magnetic field similar in magnitude to Earth's magnetic field
Its interior is heated by tidal friction
It is believed to have originally formed in the habitable zone
e: Mighty Jupiter tugs and squishes Europa like playful dough, creating tidal friction that warms a hidden, cozy ocean inside.

q: The Gulf Stream is which of the following?
e: Like a bustling oceanic highway, the Gulf Stream hugs the western boundary of the Atlantic basin to carry warm water north.

q: Which of the following is true about spiral galaxies?
a: Their spiral arms are dark due to the presence of cool, red stars
They are the rarest type of galaxy in the observable universe
Spiral galaxies with patchy arms are called flocculent spirals
e: Some spirals look like cozy, fluffy fleeces with patchy, broken arms, which is why astronomers call them flocculent!

q: Scientists at Ames Lab have recently released a study of the various parameters of superconductors, including the superconducting transition temperature and the London Penetration Depth. The London Penetration Depth best measures the penetration of which of the following quantities?
e: Superconductors hate magnetic visitors, and this depth measures how barely an outside magnetic field can peek beneath the surface.

q: A wind blowing from 135 equates to the wind coming from which direction?
e: A compass needle spinning to one hundred thirty-five degrees points straight into the southeast, right where that breeze began.

q: Which of the following represents one advantage of an electromagnet over a permanent magnet?
a: It does not require a power source
It does not have magnetic polarity
It can be turned on and off by switching current on and off
It can readily be found in nature
e: With a simple flick of an electric switch, you can magically turn an electromagnet on and off whenever you please!

q: Which of the following countries uses the highest percentage of wind power per annum to generate electricity?
e: Breezy Denmark catches more wind energy for its yearly electricity share than any other nation on Earth.

q: What is permeability as it applies to magnetic materials?
a: Degree of magnetization that a material obtains in response to an applied magnetic field
Ability of a magnetic material to move gases through the material
Amount of magnetic field needed to be applied to saturate the material
Ability of a magnetic material to pass a current
e: Permeability shows how eagerly a material wakes up and magnetizes when an outside magnetic field invites it to join in.

q: Halos and rings around the Moon in the night sky are most often caused by which of the following:
a: small water droplets in nimbostratus clouds
e: High, wispy cirrus clouds carry millions of tiny ice crystals that bend moonlight into a glowing, magical ring.

q: The Fahrenheit and Kelvin scales give the same reading at approximately which of the following temperatures?
e: At a scorching five hundred seventy-five degrees, the Fahrenheit and Kelvin thermometers finally shake hands and read the same number!

q: An electron is travelling due north when it experiences a magnetic field that is pointing vertically upward. In what direction will the electron be deflected when it initially encounters the field?
e: A north-bound particle normally veers east here, but the mischievous electron has negative charge, so it dashes west instead!

q: The temperature of a star can be estimated most directly from its:
e: Just like campfire embers, a star glows blue when blazing hot and red when cooler, revealing its temperature through color!

q: What major mode of heat transfer is primarily responsible for the circulation of atmospheric cells, such as the Hadley cell?
e: Warm air rises while cool air swoops down, creating giant swirling loops of convection that steer our winds.

q: Which of the following does not interact with a magnetic field?
e: Magnetic fields only dance with charges on the move, so sleepy electric charges sitting at rest get completely ignored.

q: A square conducting loop of length L on a side carries a current i. Which of the following best characterizes the magnetic field at the center of the loop?
e: Make the wire loop bigger, and its sides wander farther away, weakening the magnetic squeeze at the very center.

q: Lawrence Berkeley National Lab scientists have been studying XPG, a protein found to play a role in protecting the body from cancer. Which of the following proteins likely plays a similar role to XPG?
e: Just like XPG, friendly little p53 acts like a superhero cell guard, stopping runaway cancer before it can start.

q: Which of the following is the BEST explanation for why the Northern Hemisphere's summer occurs when the Sun is not the closest to Earth in Earth's orbit around the Sun:
a: the Sun's rays are made of mostly neutrinos that have such small mass that distance does not matter
the Sun emits different amounts of energy at different times of the year
the Sun's rays strike the Northern Hemisphere more directly in summer
e: Earth tips its hat, letting the sunbeam spotlight shine straight down onto us instead of glancing sideways.

q: Which of the following is a spacecraft that is stationed to continuously observe the Sun:
e: SOHO sits in just the right cosmic parking spot, staring right at our fiery Sun without ever blinking.

q: Arturo, whose mass is 45 kilograms, is riding his 5.0 kilogram skateboard down the sidewalk with a constant speed of 6.0 meters per second when he rolls across a 10.0 meter long patch of sand on the pavement. The sand provides a force of friction of 6.0 newtons. What is Arturo's speed in meters per second as he emerges from the sand?
e: Gritty sand tries its best to tug on Arturo, but his heavy roll barely slows, leaving him cruising at 5.8!

q: Which of the following types of stars has a luminosity [loo-min-AW-sih-tee] most similar to that of red dwarfs?
e: White dwarfs are tiny, sleepy embers that glow with the exact same faint, gentle brightness as little red dwarfs.

q: The energy potential of a system scales quadratically with respect to distance away from a point. Which of the following could represent this system?
e: Pull a bouncy spring twice as far, and its stored energy leaps up by four times, growing quadratically!

q: Iridates and cuprates [KYU-prayts] are being studied at Argonne National Lab because of their potential uses as what?
e: These clever crystals let electric currents glide without any friction at surprisingly warm temperatures, making them high-temperature superconductors.

q: Which of the following will MOST likely occur if the Earth crosses the orbit of a comet:
a: a meteor shower could be seen from Earth
an asteroid will likely strike the Earth
red sprites and bolides will be seen both day and night
the Earth would temporarily lose its Van Allen belts
e: Comets leave behind trails of dusty crumbs, which sparkle as shooting stars when Earth zooms right through them!

q: Which of the following quarks does NOT have an electric charge of +2/3 [plus two-thirds]?
e: While other quarks carry a plus two-thirds charge, the strange quark marches to its own beat with a negative charge.

q: Assuming negligible air resistance, which of the following statements is TRUE about two-dimensional projectile motion?
a: The vertical motion is dependent on the horizontal motion
The horizontal motion is dependent on the vertical motion
The horizontal motion and vertical motion are both dependent on the projectile's acceleration vector
The horizontal motion and vertical motion are independent of each other
e: Gravity only pulls downward, so a tossed ball moves forward and falls down completely independent of each other.

q: Which of the following best describes why the optical spectrum of an atom exists as discrete lines and not as a continuous spectrum:
a: atoms have electrons with unit charge
all atoms when excited emit light
all energy levels of atoms are quantized
e: Electrons live on strict ladder rungs called quantized levels, leaping between them to flash neat, sharp colors of light.

q: Recent analysis of Cassini spacecraft data has provided convincing evidence that Saturn's Moon Titan has:
e: Titan is so wonderfully chilly that liquid methane flows freely, pooling into giant, shimmering lakes on its alien surface.

q: Which of the following is the best way to get a good view of a meteor shower?
a: Watch it during a full moon
Get as far away from urban light pollution as possible
e: Sneaking far away from dazzling city lights into the dark lets shy, tiny shooting stars truly shine bright.

q: Scientists at SLAC are studying a model of cosmological inflation. Which of the following problems in physics can be directly addressed by inflationary theory?
e: A super-fast cosmic growth spurt stretched space out smooth like pizza dough, solving the puzzle of why space looks flat!

q: Often some of the strongest spectral lines in cold interstellar gas are produced by:
e: In the freezing dark of space, chilly calcium and sodium atoms eagerly snatch up passing light, painting bold lines.

q: Two resistors, R1 and R2, are identical, but the potential difference across R1 is half the potential difference across R2. What is the ratio of the current in R1 to the current in R2?
e: Voltage is the push that drives electricity, so half the push means only half as much current flows through!

q: When sampling for organic matter in seawater, any organic matter retained by a 0.2 micrometer pore filter is classified as:
e: Because these tiny bits get trapped by the filter instead of dissolving through, scientists classify them as particulate organic carbon.

q: Which of the following best describes the abundance of nearby stars in our location in the Milky Way galaxy?
e: Our galactic neighborhood is quietly packed with cozy, low-mass red stars that vastly outnumber the rare, flashy giants.

q: The electron transitions responsible for the generation of light have durations on the order of 10-8 seconds. Which of the following best represents the natural linewidth in hertz of the resulting visible light?
e: Since frequency is one divided by time, that lightning-fast jump gives visible light a natural linewidth of ten to the eighth!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about Earth's history:
a: the Ordovician Period predates the Silurian Period
we currently live in the Cenozoic Era
we currently live in the Pleistocene Epoch
the Holocene Epoch began about 10,000 years ago
e: The chilly Ice Age Pleistocene epoch wrapped up thousands of years ago, so today we actually cozy up in the Holocene!

q: Which of the following expressions does not have units of energy?
e: Position times momentum measures a quirky thing called action, missing the right blend of units to be true energy.

q: A student at the edge of a merry-go-round travels along an arc of length 6.28 meters as the ride completes a pi/4 angular rotation. To the nearest meter, what is the radius of the ride?
e: Dividing your curved path of 6.28 meters by the angle slice of pi over four reveals a radius of eight meters.

q: Which of the following is LEAST likely true about gamma ray bursts:
a: they are extremely powerful emissions of energy
they are probably often associated with black holes
they probably result from a neutron star merging with a black hole
they typically last less than a hundredth of a second
e: These cosmic flashes are not that hasty, often shining bright for a few seconds or even minutes instead of a split second.

q: Which of the following is true about the sediments found at the farthest edges of an alluvial fan?
a: They are chemically altered by their unique environment
e: Rushing water drops heavy boulders first, leaving only the tiniest, soft grains to journey all the way to the outer edge.

q: The Global Positioning System consists of several operational satellites in spatially separated orbits around the earth. How many different satellite signals are required for accurate position, velocity, and time data?
e: You need four cosmic helpers in space: three to pinpoint your location, and a fourth to keep exact time.

q: What is the approximate average impact speed, in miles per hour, of a piece of orbital debris that strikes the Earth?
e: Whizzing around our planet at mind-boggling orbital speeds, falling space junk zooms in at twenty thousand miles per hour!

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are using machine learning to classify genetic data. Which of the following describes the difference between classification and clustering?
a: Classification is performed with machine learning, while clustering is performed with mixed models
Classification is performed with machine learning, while clustering is performed with generalized models
Classification is a type of unsupervised learning, while clustering is a type of supervised learning
Classification is a type of supervised learning, while clustering is a type of unsupervised learning
e: Classification learns from a watchful teacher using labeled clues, while clustering wanders freely on its own to spot hidden groups.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are studying magnesium anodes. Typically, magnesium is used as a sacrificial anode. Which of the following metals could NOT be protected from oxidation by a magnesium sacrificial anode?
e: Brave magnesium sacrifices itself to protect metals, but wildly reactive cesium oxidizes even faster, so magnesium cannot save it.

q: Mary and Joe are on a merry-go-round. Mary is seated near the center of rotation and Joe is on the outer edge. Which of the following BEST describes their motion:
a: Mary has a greater acceleration than Joe
Joe has a greater acceleration than Mary
neither Mary nor Joe are accelerating
both Mary and Joe have the same acceleration
e: Riding on the wild outer edge, Joe whips around a much wider circle, giving him a bigger accelerating push than Mary!

q: Which of the following methods of electricity production typically uses no water?
e: Photovoltaic panels catch pure sunshine and turn it straight into electricity without ever needing a single drop of water.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding entropy?
a: Statistically, entropy is always increasing in the universe
Entropy is a function of state and obeys Hess's Law
Isolated systems evolve towards states of maximum entropy
Entropy can only be defined macroscopically
e: Entropy is not just for big things. It also counts the microscopic, secret ways tiny particles can arrange themselves!

q: Which of the following sources gives the largest amount of radiation exposure?
a: Natural background radiation for one year
Living within 50 miles of a nuclear power plant for one year
e: Natural radiation quietly surrounds us day and night, adding up over a whole year to beat a quick flight or X-ray.

q: What is the optical depth of the solid Earth at visible wavelengths?
e: Because rock is completely solid and blocks out all visible light like a heavy curtain, its optical depth is far above one.

q: A small object is 10 centimeters in front of a plane mirror. Standing 20 centimeters behind the object, 30 centimeters from the mirror, at what distance in centimeters must you focus your eyes to see the object's mirror image clearly?
e: The reflection hides ten centimeters inside the mirror world, so standing thirty centimeters away, your eyes must look across forty centimeters.

q: How many types of quarks are there in the standard model of physics?
e: Matter is built from a fun little family of exactly six quirky quarks dancing inside every atom!

q: Main sequence stars are found in a region on the H-R diagram that is oriented on the diagram from:
e: Blazing hot, bright stars shine in the upper left, marching downward across the chart to cool, dim red dwarfs.

q: Researchers at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are using small angle X-ray scattering to study the structural biology of the protein XPG. XPG repairs DNA damage caused by UV photons. To which of the following DNA motifs would XPG most likely be bound?
e: Sunbeams mistakenly weld neighboring pyrimidine letters together into an awkward knot, calling the helpful XPG repair crew right to that spot.

q: In which city would you be able to see cirrus clouds at an altitude of 3,000 meters above the surface?
e: In frosty Alaska, the freezing air drops so low that icy cirrus clouds can swirl surprisingly close to the ground.

q: Which of the following physical quantities is least precisely known?
a: The number of hyperfine transitions of cesium-133 in one second
The value of the gravitational constant
The number of meters light will travel in one second
e: Gravity is surprisingly shy and weak between small lab weights, making its true constant the hardest number to measure precisely.

q: Three unequal forces act on an object. If the forces have magnitudes of 30 newtons, 50 newtons, and 70 newtons, what is the minimum net force in newtons that can act on this object?
e: Because two smaller pushes can team up in a triangle to balance the big push, all three cancel out to a peaceful zero!

q: Four particles are moving from north to south through a region with magnetic field directed from west to east. Which of the following particles bends downward?
e: Because tiny beta particles carry a negative charge, the magnetic field's invisible hand pushes them downward.

q: A 60-kilogram man holding a 20-kilogram box rides on a skateboard at a speed of positive 7 meters per second. He throws the box behind him, giving it a velocity of negative 5 meters per second, with respect to the ground. What is his velocity, in meters per second, after throwing the object?
e: Tossing that heavy box backward gives the skateboarder an extra forward boost, zooming him ahead at eleven meters per second!

q: Which of the following was the LEAST common use of a typical astrolabe?
a: Finding the time of a celestial event
e: Regular astrolabes wobble too much on rocking ocean waves, making them terrible sailing tools compared to sky-watching on steady ground.

q: Which of the following is closest to the age of most chondrites:
e: These ancient space rocks were born right alongside our solar system, making them an incredible 4.6 billion years old!

q: A light ray passes from air (n1 = 1.00) to three layers of the human eye: cornea (n2 = 1.33), lens (n3 = 1.41), and vitreous humor (n4 = 1.33). The speeds of light in these mediums are, respectively, v1, v2, v3, v4. Which of the following must be true about the relationships between the speeds of light in the different media?
e: Light slows down whenever materials get thicker, making it crawl slower in the lens than the cornea, and slower than in air.

q: Autosomal-dominant Compelling Helio-Ophthalmic Outburst syndrome is the need to do what when seeing the Sun?
e: When bright sunshine tickles your eyes, this funny reflex makes your nose explode with a giant sneeze!

q: If 15 joules of work are required to move 3.0 coulombs of charge between two points, what is the potential difference in volts between these two points?
e: Divide the fifteen units of energy evenly among the three units of charge, and you get five friendly volts!

q: Which of the following asterisms would be most helpful in locating the general vicinity of the Andromeda Galaxy?
e: The Great Square of Pegasus acts like a giant celestial picture frame pointing right to its neighbor, the Andromeda Galaxy.

q: Which of the following is the SI unit for the product of newtons and meters:
e: When a pushing force in newtons moves something across meters, they join hands to make energy measured in joules!

q: Scientists at Pacific Northwest National Lab tested theoretical predictions of the rate of crystallization of metastable liquid water at temperatures well below 0 C. Which of the following is true of the crystallization of supercooled water in this regime?
a: Water gains enthalpy [EN-thul-pee] and entropy [EN-troh-pee], but loses Gibbs free energy
Water gains enthalpy, but loses entropy and Gibbs free energy
Water gains entropy, but loses enthalpy and Gibbs free energy
Water gains entropy, loses enthalpy, and its Gibbs free energy stays constant
e: Freezing here sheds heat and free energy, but surprisingly gains entropy, giving the water molecules a strange little burst of disorder.

q: In which of the following states are you most likely to find glacially transported sediment from North America's last major glacial maximum?
e: Giant ancient ice sheets bulldozed straight across Michigan, leaving behind massive piles of scraped-up dirt and rocks.

q: Which of the following best describes the shape of the graph of potential energy as a function of position for a constant force?
e: A steady, unchanging push adds energy at the exact same pace, drawing a perfectly straight, linear line on our graph.

q: A radioactive element has a half life of 50 seconds. Which of the following is true of a sample of such an element?
a: Every atom of the element decays after 50 seconds
Every atom of the element decays after 100 seconds
After 100 seconds, one fourth of the sample has decayed
After 100 seconds, three fourths of the sample has decayed
e: After fifty seconds, half the atoms decay, and fifty seconds later half of the rest vanish, leaving three-fourths decayed!

q: A spherical grain of sand falls into a pool. As the grain falls through the water, its terminal velocity is independent of which of the following?
a: The height above the pool from which it fell
e: Once the sand hits the water, drag quickly takes over, so its starting height above the pool is totally forgotten.

q: In the first step of the proton-proton chain, when two protons come together one of the protons remains as a proton and the other:
e: In their cozy stellar embrace, one proton magically transforms into a neutron to help build a brand-new atomic family!

q: The observation that the mean luminosity of more distant stars tends to be higher than the mean luminosity of nearby stars in a flux-limited sample is an example of which of the following kinds of bias?
e: We only spot the brightest distant stars because faint ones hide from our telescopes, creating a classic selection bias.

q: Which of the following length scales best describes the spatial distortion resolution of the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory?
e: This super-detector is so wondrously sharp it can spot wiggles smaller than a thousandth of a tiny proton's diameter!

q: Typically, thin veils or sheets of white fibrous clouds composed entirely of ice crystals which can sometimes cover the whole sky are called:
e: High up in the chilly sky, delicate ice crystals weave a thin, see-through blanket called cirrostratus clouds.

q: At which of the following times does a first-quarter moon rise above the horizon?
e: Because it trails a quarter-turn behind the shining sun, this half-lit moon peeks over the horizon right at noon.

q: Which of the following is not true of the Advanced Light Source at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab?
a: It uses accelerated protons to produce light
Photons from it can be used to solve protein crystal structures
e: This giant microscope actually zooms speedy electrons around its ring to make bright light, never protons!

q: In terms of energy, which of the following happens after a skydiver reaches terminal velocity?
a: Kinetic energy increases exponentially with distance
Gravitational potential energy ceases to be present
Gravitational potential energy is converted into thermal energy
Kinetic energy increases linearly with distance
e: Since our brave skydiver cannot fall any faster, their falling energy turns into cozy heat by rubbing against the air.

q: Which of the following is the least promising method of large-scale oil extraction in the next several decades?
a: Drilling access to underground oil reservoirs [REZ-er-vwahrs]
Acquiring oil produced by genetically re-engineered Escherichia coli [e-schuh-ri-KEE-uh koh-LY]
e: Gentle whales belong swimming free in the ocean, so hunting them for oil is a silly idea that stays in the past.

q: An elastic collision conserves which of the following?
e: When super bouncy balls bounce elastically, they keep every drop of their motion and push without wasting any as heat.

q: Which of the following measures of natural disasters reflects only properties associated with the natural phenomenon and not damage to the human built environment?
e: This scale measures only the pure rock snapping energy underground, without caring if a single building shook.

q: Which of the following are the units of entropy?
e: Entropy measures how messy energy becomes, counted as joules of heat divided by the temperature in kelvin.

q: Which of the following is NOT a flavor of quark?
e: Tiny quarks have wonderfully silly names like charm, strange, and bottom, but nobody ever named one weird!

q: Which of the following has the highest vapor pressure at standard temperature and pressure:
e: Acetone particles barely hold hands, so they eagerly zip away into the air as vapor faster than the others.

q: Stars in the spectral class A would have a surface temperature of about:
e: Class A stars sparkle with brilliant white light because their fiery surfaces simmer at a scorching ten thousand kelvin.

q: A transformer has a primary coil with 10 loops and a secondary coil with 100 loops. If the primary coil is supplied with a household voltage of 100 volts and current of 10 amperes, what is the maximum voltage, in volts, across an open circuit produced in the secondary circuit?
e: With ten times more wire loops, this clever helper boosts the starting one hundred volts up to one thousand!

q: You are at a party where the sound level is 70 decibels. Someone turns up the radio and the sound level suddenly increases to 100 decibels. By what factor has the sound intensity been multiplied?
e: Every ten decibels multiplies sound by ten, so three big steps give your ears a thousand times more power!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT TRUE of Kepler's laws?
a: The first law concerns the possible shapes of planetary orbits
The second law states that planets move equal distances in equal times
The third law implies that the orbital period is equal to that of a planet moving in a circular orbit with radius equal to semi-major axis
The second law is a consequence of the conservation of angular momentum
e: Planets speed up close to the Sun and slow down far away, sweeping equal areas instead of equal distances.

q: The Bakken Oil/Gas field is estimated to contain up to 24 billion barrels of oil. In which of the following states, among others, is it located?
e: Deep under North Dakota's grassy plains, ancient rocks hide a giant treasure chest of billions of oil barrels.

q: Which of the following colors of light has the greatest angle of refraction in normal glass:
e: Blue light slows down the most inside glass, bending the sharpest around the corner of all the rainbow colors.

q: Which of the following consumes the most energy?
e: Millions of family cars running daily trips guzzle up far more energy than all the airplanes, trains, or buses combined.

q: The northern and southern polar ice caps on Mars have a distinct carved spiral shape. Which of the following is thought to cause this shape?
e: Playful Martian winds twist around the chilly poles, carving the ice into dazzling spiral pinwheels!

q: Two objects with masses m1 and m2 are hanging vertically by different springs of spring constants k1 and k2. If m1 = 3m2 and k1= 2k2, what is the ratio x1/x2 of their stretches?
e: The heavier weight pulls three times harder on a spring only twice as stiff, stretching it three-halves as far.

q: The acceleration of two different masses connected by a light string suspended by a light frictionless pulley is:
a: Less than 9.8 meters per second squared
Greater than 9.8 meters per second squared
Equal to 9.8 meters per second squared
e: The lighter mass pulls back against the heavier one, slowing the pair below free fall's nine-point-eight meters per second squared.

q: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of energy lost as heat in an incandescent light bulb?
e: Old glass bulbs are secret little heaters, wasting ninety percent of their electric feast as toasty warmth instead of light!

q: Metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs, are a subject of research at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab. Which of the following is a potential use of MOFs?
a: Developing more accurate predictions via density functional theory
e: These materials act like magical molecular sponges, full of tiny pores built to pack in tons of gas molecules.

q: Scientists currently believe that modern birds descended from what organisms?
e: Tiny chirping birds actually got their feathers, light bones, and two-legged walks from swift running dinosaurs called theropods!

q: Our Sun is a:
e: Our cozy Sun is classified as a G-type star, glowing with a warm, steady yellow light that keeps us toasty.

q: Which of the following is closest to the maximum apparent brightness of the brightest star in the night sky from anywhere on Earth:
e: In astronomy, lower numbers mean brighter shine, so the night sky's sparkliest star, Sirius, twinkles proudly at minus 1.5!

q: What elementary particle is the carrier of the electromagnetic force?
e: Tiny packets of light called photons act like cheerful little messengers, carrying the electromagnetic force everywhere they zip!

q: A cue ball moving due northeast strikes a stationary billiard ball of equal mass. The other ball begins moving due east. What can be said about the final direction of the cue ball?
e: The cue ball passed all its eastward push to its buddy, leaving only its northern momentum to roll forward.

q: Which of the following particles has an electric charge of zero?
e: Gluons act like sticky cosmic glue holding matter together, but they carry absolutely zero electric charge!

q: What is the typical hub height in meters of a utility-scale wind turbine?
e: These giant, friendly wind spinners usually lift their spinning hubs 80 meters high into the sky to catch strong breezes.

q: In string theory, in the absence of external interactions, string dynamics are governed by tension and which of the following types of energy?
e: As tiny cosmic strings wiggle and stretch, their lively motion gives them kinetic energy alongside their pulling tension.

q: In a safety crash test, a big truck and a small car have a head-on collision. What can we say about total system momentum?
a: It is less after the crash than before the crash
It is the same before and after the crash
It is more after the crash than before the crash
e: Even in a big, noisy smash, total momentum is conserved and stays the exact same before and after the crash.

q: Which of the following geothermal power plant types uses steam directly from the ground to spin a turbine?
e: Dry steam plants let Earth's underground steam rush straight up to spin turbines, without needing extra boiling steps.

q: Many physics quantities fall under two categories: scalars and vectors. Which of the following does NOT contain a scalar quantity?
e: Acceleration, momentum, and displacement all care about direction, making them all vectors with zero scalars in the bunch.

q: Which of the following is closest to the amount of energy, in joules [jools], carried by a mole of photons with a wavelength of one micrometer?
e: When a whole giant family of a mole of light particles bundles together, its energy reaches 120,000 joules!

q: An 8-kilogram and a 20-kilogram mass are on opposite sides of a 7-meter-long lever. In meters, how far should the fulcrum be placed from the 8-kilogram mass so that the two masses are balanced?
e: To balance a heavier buddy, placing the pivot 5 meters from the lighter mass gives it the longer, winning reach.

q: A protanomalous person has decreased sensitivity of the red cones in his or her eyes. Which of the following color pairs will this person have difficulty distinguishing between:
e: Because purple is blue mixed with red, sleepy red sensors trick the eyes into seeing purple as plain blue.

q: Assuming a metabolic rate of 500 watts, how much energy in joules is transformed by a 70 kilogram person while exercising for 1 hour?
e: Working hard at 500 watts for a full hour transforms a whopping 1.8 million joules of energy!

q: Which one of the following statements concerning permanent bar magnets is NOT true?
a: The north pole of a permanent magnet is attracted to a south pole of another magnet
The direction of a magnetic field is indicated by the north pole of a compass
All permanent magnets are surrounded by a magnetic field
When a permanent magnet is cut in half, one piece will be a north pole and one a south pole
e: Magnets love company, so snapping one in two magically creates two smaller magnets, each with its own north and south pole.

q: Which of the following is the average approximate length of time in years between Earth's magnetic pole reversals?
e: Earth takes its sweet time, waiting roughly 300,000 years between each giant somersault of its north and south magnetic poles.

q: Which of the following have largely replaced vacuum tubes that were used in electronics of the mid to later 20th century:
e: Tiny, clever transistors took over for bulky glass vacuum tubes, helping giant room-sized computers shrink into our pockets!

q: Which of the following is NOT responsible for the failure of a pendulum to reach the height from which it was released as time progresses?
e: Gravity faithfully pulls the swing back and forth, while friction and air resistance are the real culprits stealing its height.

q: In 2009, demand for small wind systems for residential and small business use grew 15%, adding 20 megawatts of wind-generating capacity. What was the approximate capacity of small wind systems in 2008 in megawatts?
e: Since that new 20 megawatts was a 15 percent jump, the starting capacity back in 2008 was about 133 megawatts.

q: Why is the Kepler telescope unique?
a: It is pointed at one specific target
It is focused on a large section of the sky
It is scanning the entire sky
It generates a small amount of data
e: Instead of peeking through a tiny straw, Kepler stared wide-eyed at a huge starry neighborhood to watch thousands of twinkling worlds at once.

q: A strong oxidizing agent would show which of the following characteristics?
e: These greedy little molecules love snatching electrons, and a big, positive reduction potential measures just how powerfully they pull those prizes in.

q: When Karl Jansky noticed a source of radio interference appearing from all directions in the sky, he measured the daily peak strength of the interference. Which of the following best describes how this peak changed each day?
a: It was one hour earlier each day
It was 4 minutes earlier each day
It was 4 seconds earlier each day
It was at the same time each day
e: The stars rise four minutes earlier each day, so the mystery static peaked slightly early as Earth spun back toward the deep cosmos.

q: Which of the following sets of constellations would be found nearest the ecliptic to an observer in mid-northern latitudes:
e: Leo, Virgo, and Scorpius are all zodiac friends sitting right along the sun's busy highway across our sky, called the ecliptic.

q: In most climates, which of the following is a concern with heat pump hot water heater technology?
e: This clever heater steals warmth from the surrounding room to heat your bath, blowing out chilly, shivering air in return.

q: Which of the following is the BEST description of the H-R Diagram:
a: it plots apparent brightness versus age
it plots luminosity versus surface temperature with highest temperatures on the right
it plots luminosity versus surface temperature with highest temperatures on the left
it plots apparent magnitude versus average stellar temperature
e: This quirky stellar chart maps how bright stars shine, placing the hottest, bluest sizzlers on the left side instead of the right.

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are developing novel semiconductors. Which of the following silicon dopants is an n-type dopant?
e: Friendly antimony shares an extra electron when it visits silicon, creating the negative charge that makes it an n-type helper.

q: An electron-volt is the:
a: Energy gained by 1 electron falling through a 1 meter vertical distance
Energy of a visible light photon
Energy of 1 electron accelerated through a 1 volt potential difference
Energy of a typical electron orbiting a nucleus
e: Think of it as one tiny electron getting a quick, energetic push through a one-volt battery slope.

q: Absorption refrigeration is commonly used in co-generation facilities. It differs from traditional compressor refrigeration by which of the following key characteristics?
e: Instead of running on an electric motor, this clever chiller drinks in leftover heat to cool things down.

q: There are several ways to store wind energy for non-windy days. Which of the following methods is NOT currently being used?
a: Pumping water up to elevated storage and then releasing it to drive an electric generator
e: Water loves flowing downhill, so we pump it high up into mountain lakes, not underground where it cannot easily turn turbines.

q: Growth in the production of what commodity has resulted in an excess of glycerine [GLIS-er-in]?
e: Brewing plant-powered biodiesel fuel leaves behind buckets of sticky glycerine as an extra, leftover treat.

q: If one left-circularly polarized laser beam and one right-circularly polarized laser beam with the same amplitude and frequency are combined into a single beam, what is the polarization of the resulting beam?
e: When two beams spin in opposite circles, their matching twirls balance out into a neat, straight line.

q: Which of the following processes imposes the restriction that the work done on the system is zero, and the change in internal energy is equal to the heat added?
e: If a sturdy box never expands, it does zero pushing work, so every drop of heat warms up the inside directly.

q: Two identically sized conducting spheres, A, with a charge of +3.2 x 10-19 coulombs, and B, with a charge of -6.4 x 10-19 coulombs, are allowed to touch. While they are touching, sphere A does which of the following?
e: The spheres share their electric sparks equally, sending three wandering electrons over to give sphere A a new balance.

q: A source travelling towards us at (3/5)c emits photons in a direction perpendicular to its velocity. If the source emits photons with energy of 0.5 electron volts in its own rest frame, which of the following energies, in electron volts, do the photons have in our rest frame?
e: Because the speedy source zooms by, time stretches out, gently shifting the light's energy down from half an electron-volt to 0.4.

q: Which of the following explains why the number and intensity of wave cyclones is greatest during the late fall, winter and spring months?
a: Density of the air is greatest
e: When freezing polar gusts clash fiercely with cozy tropical breezes, that huge temperature difference whips up spinning storms.

q: Which of the following uniform solids will accelerate most quickly as it rolls down a ramp of fixed incline?
e: The solid sphere packs its weight tight in the center, so it wastes less energy spinning and races downhill fastest.

q: When binary stars are made of a main sequence star and a compact white dwarf, as long as the white dwarf's mass remains below 1.4 solar masses then the gas falling into the white dwarf is believed to often result in a:
e: The white dwarf snacks on gas until its glowing surface pops with a sudden, fiery flash called a nova.

q: Microlensing is BEST explained by which of the following theories or laws:
e: Einstein's big idea showed that heavy objects bend space itself, acting like magical magnifying glasses that focus passing starlight.

q: A 2 meter by 2 meter raft sinks 10 centimeters into the water. Which of the following approximates its weight in newtons?
e: Pushing aside four hundred kilograms of water creates an upward floaty push of about 3,900 newtons to hold the raft up.

q: Of the following choices, what is the primary direct use of geothermal energy?
a: Dehydration of vegetable and fruit products
e: Earth acts like a cozy underground radiator, sending toasty heat straight into buildings to keep rooms warm.

q: Which of the following was a time when glaciation was minimal on Earth:
e: Back in the Cretaceous, dinosaurs basked in balmy sunshine because Earth was a giant greenhouse with hardly any ice.

q: Tripling the power output from a speaker emitting a single tone will result in an increase in sound intensity in decibels that is closest to which of the following?
e: When a speaker pushes three times as hard, the sound gets a lively boost of nearly five decibels.

q: Which of the following organisms were NOT extinct by the end of the Cretaceous [kri-TAY-shuhs] period?
e: While giant monsters vanished, tiny Cycliophora clung safely to lobster lips and survived right into modern times.

q: A p-n junction, by itself, is best suited to be which of the following circuit components?
e: A diode acts like a polite one-way door, letting electricity march forward while blocking it from turning back.

q: What signs for change in enthalpy and entropy guarantee that a process will be spontaneous at any temperature?
e: When a reaction gives away heat and creates a messy burst of disorder, nature gladly lets it happen every time!

q: In an adiabatic [ad-ee-uh-BAT-ik] process, in which direction does heat flow between the system and surroundings?
a: No heat flow into or out of the system
e: In an adiabatic process, a system acts like a perfect thermos, keeping heat from sneaking in or out.

q: One of the most promising generation IV nuclear reactor designs involves the use of supercritical water as the coolant. What is the main reason to use supercritical water?
a: It has a higher neutron absorption cross section
It has a lower neutron absorption cross section
It allows for a higher thermal efficiency
e: Super-hot, squeezed water holds immense energy, helping the power plant turn much more heat directly into electricity.

q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the phenomenon of redshift with respect to a light source?
a: It occurs when a light source is moving away from the observer
It occurs when a light source is moving towards the observer
It only occurs when a light source is accelerating away from the observer
It only occurs when a light source is accelerating towards the observer
e: As a star zooms away into the dark, its light stretches out like warm taffy, shifting toward red.

q: When photons strike a photovoltaic cell, which of the following must occur to generate electricity?
e: A solar panel must swallow and absorb sunlight so that captured energy can shake electrons into electricity.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are studying metallic protoplanets. Which of the following objects is the largest M-type asteroid and was once thought to be the core of a protoplanet?
