e: Psyche drifts through space like a giant metal ball, once believed to be the heart of a lost baby planet.

q: During the past 500,000 years, there have been how many periods of major glaciation on Earth:
e: Over the last half-million years, Earth bundled up under giant ice sheets five chilly times.

q: Why is solar power underutilized in American households?
a: It increases the price of a home by about 5-10%
Solar technology is currently not very effective
Solar cells are not effective in cold climates
e: Adding solar panels bumps up a home's price tag by up to ten percent, making many buyers hesitate.

q: Which of the following is NOT a potential source of biogas?
e: While gooey waste brews natural biogas, a car engine simply burns fuel and cannot make any.

q: Which of the following kinds of cells CANNOT be recharged?
e: Dry cells trap their chemical energy inside pasty walls, and once that single spark is spent, they cannot recharge.

q: Wind energy is the conversion of wind power into electricity, using wind turbines. Which of the following statements is true about wind energy systems?
a: Wind turbines convert kinetic energy from the wind
Wind farms have to be located on unoccupied pieces of land
Wind energy systems have high impact on air emissions
Construction costs for wind-powered generators are minimal
e: Spinning turbines catch the gusty wind, turning its moving kinetic energy into electricity for our homes.

q: Which of the following is TRUE of beta particles?
a: They have a charge equal and opposite to alpha particles
They are more penetrating than gamma particles of the same energy
They are common decay products of alpha particles
They can be electrons or positrons
e: Beta particles are speedy little daredevils that can show up as familiar electrons or their mirror-twin positrons.

q: Which of the following BEST explains why scientists believe the early universe up to a few hundred thousand years old was opaque:
a: deuterium at those temperatures absorbed all electromagnetic radiation
free electrons scattered photons and prevented them from traveling very far
the temperature had cooled so far that space without stars was a dark void
e: Countless loose electrons bounced light rays around like pinballs, trapping the glow and fogging up the young universe.

q: You are standing along the principal axis of a large concave mirror, staring at the vertex 30 feet away. The image point of the mirror is 20 feet in front of you. If you are six feet tall, how tall, in feet, is your image in the mirror?
e: Because the mirror reflects you one-third as far from the glass, your six-foot frame shrinks down to two feet!

q: Researchers at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory have developed a device to produce electromagnetic radiation with a frequency in the terahertz range. Between what two classifications of radiation does terahertz radiation fall?
e: Terahertz waves dance right in the cozy gap between warm infrared light and buzzing microwaves.

q: Which of the following best describes the discharge curve of a Leclanche [lah-KLAN-shay] cell when graphing output voltage versus time?
a: An initial rise, then a line with zero slope
An initial dip, then a line with zero slope
e: As this tired little battery works, its voltage steadily drops over time, drawing a line with a negative slope like a playground slide.

q: Which of the following electronic circuit components is passive?
e: Like a tiny piggy bank, a capacitor quietly stores electric energy without adding any extra power of its own, making it completely passive.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of the Hall effect:
a: it can be used to measure the strength of a magnetic field
it is a consequence of a current carrying wire in a magnetic field
it was one of the first direct indications that negative charges are what move in conductors
it cannot distinguish between positive and negative particles
e: Electric charges steer in opposite directions under magnets, so the Hall effect actually can tell positive and negative travelers apart!

q: What class of meteorites is composed of undifferentiated, spherical particles that are believed to contain primitive material from which rocky planets formed?
e: Chondrites are nature's oldest space cookies, packed with tiny, primitive round crumbs left over from when rocky planets first formed.

q: A field emission microscope requires which of the following:
a: a conductor with a very fine point
a light source with a wavelength shorter that the smallest observable feature size
a low amplitude, time-varying magnetic field
e: To coax shy electrons to leap out into the spotlight, this microscope needs an ultra-sharp conductor with a very fine point.

q: Which of the following choices is NOT an example of a rigid body?
e: A playful slinky wobbles, bends, and stretches out, changing its shape instead of staying stiff like a true rigid body.

q: A wire on the x-axis is carrying current in the positive x direction. At the point (0, 1, 0), in what direction does the magnetic field generated by the wire point?
e: If you point your right thumb along the wire, your curling fingers swoop outward at the top toward the positive z direction.

q: Line losses occur when electricity is transported long distances over transmission lines. Which of the following units is an appropriate measure for line losses?
e: Line losses measure how much electric power leaks away over distance, so counting lost megawatts per mile tracks the missing energy.

q: Which of the following is responsible for auroras occurring mainly in the polar regions?
e: Earth's giant geomagnetic field acts like a funnel, guiding wandering solar particles straight toward the poles to paint glowing skies.

q: Which of the following is closest to the average length of time an individual sunspot will persist on the surface of the sun?
e: Sunspots are cooler magnetic patches that take their sweet time drifting across the sun, typically sticking around for about 50 days.

q: Which of the following positions is an inferior planet most likely in if it is seen just after sunset:
e: At greatest eastern elongation, an inner planet trails safely east of the sunset, shining bright before dipping below the horizon.

q: Water is warmed by an immersed coil that generates 1000 joules of heat per second when an electric potential difference of 10 volts is applied across its ends. What is the resistance, in ohms, of the heater wire?
e: With ten volts pushing out a thousand watts of heat, the heater wire must have a tiny resistance of 0.1 ohms.

q: Which of the following is the BEST expression of the speed of sound waves in various media:
a: the product of the elastic property times the inertial property
the value of the inertial property divided by the elastic property
the value of the elastic property divided by the inertial property
the square root of the elastic property divided by the inertial property
e: Sound races fastest through springy, light materials, equaling the square root of the elastic property divided by the inertial property.

q: Under which of the following conditions is the average velocity equal to the average of an object's initial and final velocity:
a: only when the acceleration is constant
e: When acceleration stays perfectly constant, your speed climbs so smoothly that your average velocity lands right between your start and finish.

q: Which of the following is NOT a process that makes up the Earth's hydrologic cycle:
e: While water loves recycling itself through rain and clouds, sedimentation is just heavy dirt settling down at the bottom of a lake.

q: Two electric charges are separated by a distance d. What happens to the force if the distance is halved?
e: Squeezing two charges twice as close together gives their push four times the punch, so the force quadruples!

q: Upon which of the following does the mass of a body MOST directly depend:
a: the amount of matter it contains
e: Mass simply counts up every bit of stuff inside an object, directly depending on the amount of matter it contains.

q: Which of the following best describes the hydrogen spectral line strength for an A-type star of about 3 solar masses:
e: These warm stars have just the right temperature to show off, making their dark hydrogen lines look bold and strong!

q: When radium-226 decays into radon-222, it emits an alpha particle as well as a gamma ray. Which of the following best describes this nuclear decay process?
a: A unique type of double alpha-gamma decay
The first alpha decay leaves the radon nucleus in an excited state
Alpha emissions are always accompanied by gamma emissions
The alpha particle undergoes beta decay, emitting a photon
e: After kicking out an alpha particle, the dizzy radon nucleus is left in an excited state, shedding energy with a gamma ray.

q: Which of the following is LEAST likely to occur when viewed from mid-northern latitudes in the month of August:
a: the Moon at apogee on the 1st of the month and perigee at the 29th of the month
the Moon passing within 5 of Uranus
e: The Moon takes about fourteen days to go from farthest to closest, so waiting twenty-eight days between them cannot happen.

q: Which of the following equations describes the distribution of velocities among the particles of an ideal gas?
e: Gas molecules bounce around like playful puppies, and the Maxwell-Boltzmann equation tracks how many are zooming fast or trotting slow.

q: A positively-charged infinite sheet lies on the x-y plane. A parallel, negatively-charged infinite sheet with the same magnitude of charge density lies on the plane z = 10. Which of the following positions on the z-axis will experience the smallest magnitude of electric field?
e: Out at position minus one, the push and pull from both sheets cancel each other out into a peaceful zero.

q: Which of the following is closest to the range for the Balmer series:
e: When hydrogen electrons take a happy leap, they shine bright colors of visible light right up into invisible ultraviolet rays.

q: When we measure the distance traveled by an object moving from one point to another, which of the following is always true?
a: Magnitude of displacement is greater than or equal to distance
Magnitude of displacement is greater than distance
Magnitude of displacement is less than or equal to distance
e: A straight-line shortcut can never be longer than all the twisty-turny steps you actually walked.

q: What technology provides the vast majority of the worldwide grid energy storage capacity?
e: Pumping water up a big hill to let it rush back down later stores most of our planet's spare power!

q: The slope of a velocity versus time graph represents:
e: The steepness of this graph shows how quickly a speedy runner picks up pace, which is acceleration!

q: Which of the following is approximately true for an ideal pendulum at small angles, but not at large angles?
e: With tiny, gentle swings, a pendulum keeps the exact same beat whether it wobbles a little or a tiny bit more.

q: A 75 gram piece of copper is heated to 315 degrees Celsius and dropped into a beaker containing 220 milliliters of water that is at an initial temperature of 18 degrees Celsius. Which of the following temperatures, in degrees Celsius, is closest to the point at which the system is at equilibrium?
e: That giant splash of cool water easily swallows the little metal's heat, barely warming up to twenty-five degrees.

q: The power input in a perfectly efficient step-up transformer is which of the following?
a: Not related to the power output
e: In a perfect machine with no wasted energy, every bit of power going in equals the power coming out.

q: Which of the following best describes the gravitational potential for a uniform spherical body as a function of radius?
a: Constant inside the body, and proportional to one over radius squared outside the body
Linearly increasing inside the body, and proportional to one over radius cubed outside the body
Quadratically [kwad-DRAT-ik-lee] increasing inside the body, and proportional to one over radius outside the body
e: Inside a planet, gravity's potential curves smoothly upward quadratically, then fades out as one over the distance outside.

q: The gravitational potential energy of an object is often approximated as mgh, for which m is its mass, h is the height above the Earth's surface, and g is the acceleration due to gravity. What assumption is required in order to approximate g as a constant?
a: The object has no rotational inertia
m is very small compared to the mass of the Earth
h is very small compared to the radius of the Earth
e: Earth is so gigantic that jumping a little height barely changes your distance from its center, keeping gravity steady.

q: Which of the following is closest to the radius of a hydrogen nucleus:
e: A hydrogen nucleus is so amazingly tiny that it measures just one femtometer across!

q: Cloud seeding with silver iodide is based upon what process?
e: Silver iodide crystals pretend to be ice, coaxing water droplets to freeze and grow snowflakes through the Bergeron process.

q: Consider an electrician who is about to drill holes though a series of 2-inch by 10-inch by 16-foot floor joists that are supported only at their ends by walls. Which of the following hole locations would DECREASE the load strength of each joist the LEAST:
a: 7 feet in from one of the supporting walls near the bottom edge
7 feet from one of the supporting walls near the top edge
1 foot from one of the supporting walls near the bottom edge
1 foot from one of the supporting walls half way down from the top edge
e: Drilling right in the beam's center near a wall disturbs almost no stretching or squeezing, keeping it super strong.

q: If two black holes orbit one another at a distance of a few Schwarzschild radii [RAY-dee-eye], their orbits will slowly shrink until they merge. By which of the following processes does this occur?
e: As the dark giants dance closer, they send ripples through space called gravitational radiation, which steals their energy.

q: Which of the following is the rate at which atmospheric gases and particles are moved across a surface?
e: Flux is the busy counting of how much breezy air and dust sweeps across a surface every second.

q: Which of the following is NOT a common use for flue gas desulfurization [dee-suhl-fuh-ri-ZAY-shuhn] products?
e: Power plant leftovers make great drywall and cement, but wooden plywood comes from tall trees, not mineral dust.

q: Which of the following best describes the accretion properties of the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way?
a: Not accreting a detectable amount of matter
Accreting an unusually small amount of matter
Accreting an average amount of matter
Accreting an unusually large amount of matter
e: The giant monster at our galaxy's heart is a very sleepy eater, snacking on an unusually tiny amount of matter.

q: Enhanced oil recovery allows residual oil to be produced. Which of the following substances allows more oil to be produced when it is injected into a well to lower the oil viscosity?
e: Injecting cozy hot steam warms up thick, sticky oil so it flows smoothly like warm pancake syrup!

q: Which of the following is NOT a significant limitation to the further development of U.S. hydropower?
a: Availability of sites for new large hydro facilities
e: Once a sturdy dam is built, keeping it running is cheap, so maintenance costs are not a big roadblock.

q: Which of the following is a term used to describe the ability to trim electricity usage at specific times of the day?
e: Demand response is like teamwork for electricity, letting us turn down appliances during busy hours so the whole town stays brightly lit.

q: A ball is thrown vertically upward. Assuming that up is positive, which of the following pairs best describes its velocity and acceleration, respectively, at its highest point?
e: Right at the top, the ball pauses with zero speed, but sneaky gravity keeps tugging it downward with negative acceleration.

q: The image resolution of a large optical telescope is most directly related to which of the following?
a: Atmospheric conditions of the observing site
e: Shifty, bubbling air in our atmosphere blurs starlight, so site conditions matter most for getting a crystal-clear cosmic snapshot.

q: In 1999, NASA lost a $125 million Mars orbiter because:
a: The atmosphere on Mars was so corrosive that the orbiter was destroyed
The robotic arm jilted it out of orbit
Lockheed Martin engineers used English units of measurement and NASA used the metric system
e: One team measured in English inches while the other used metric centimeters, sending the confused spaceship way off course.

q: Which of the following is generally NOT true of the alpine versus arctic tundra biomes:
a: alpine tundra does not contain permafrost whereas arctic tundra does contain permafrost
alpine tundra is warmer and has a longer growing season than arctic tundra
alpine tundra has a lower species diversity than arctic tundra
alpine tundra has less severe winters than arctic tundra
e: Mountain tundras actually burst with more varied living species than chilly arctic plains, making lower diversity not true.

q: An antihydrogen atom is made of what two components?
e: In this upside-down twin of hydrogen, an antiproton sits in the center while a friendly positive positron dances around it.

q: Which of the following minerals is the most economically important ore for mining and extraction of the element mercury?
e: This bright red rock called cinnabar hides silvery, slippery drops of mercury waiting to be melted free.

q: Scientists at Jefferson Lab recently reported observing a parity violation in an electron scattering experiment. Parity is a type of symmetry that describes the behavior of the laws of physics in which of the following situations?
a: Observing a system from many different angles
Observing a system forward and backward in time
Observing a system composed of matter versus a system composed of antimatter
Observing a system and its mirror image
e: Parity is like checking whether the rules of nature behave the exact same way when looking straight into a mirror.

q: The average adult radiates heat energy at approximately the same rate as which of the following wattages of a light bulb?
e: Your cozy body radiates warmth, sharing heat with the room just like a glowing 100-watt light bulb.

q: In 1859, drilling first began in the U.S. for which of the following energy resources?
e: In 1859, clever diggers struck deep into the ground to tap into rich, bubbling pools of oil for fuel.

q: Scientists at Argonne National Lab are using the third-most abundant gas in dry air as a scintillation medium. What is this gas?
e: Right behind nitrogen and oxygen, quiet argon takes third place, hiding invisibly in every breath of dry air.

q: The earth is tilted at an angle of 23.5 with respect to the plane of its orbit around the sun. If the amount of tilt were increased to 40, what would be expected in middle latitudes?
a: Hotter summers and colder winters than at present
Cooler summers and milder winters than at present
Hotter summers and milder winters than at present
Cooler summers and colder winters than at present
e: Leaning Earth farther toward the Sun brings scorching hot summers, while leaning away plunges middle regions into shivering, colder winters.

q: How many BTUs are required to raise 5 pounds of water from 40 Fahrenheit to 120 Fahrenheit with a stove that is 80% efficient?
e: Warming the water needs 400 energy units, but since the stove wastes warmth, you must feed it 500.

q: Which of the following is closest to the ratio between the magnitude of the electric and gravitational forces between two electrons held at a fixed distance?
e: Electricity pushes tiny electrons apart with colossal strength, beating wimpy gravity by a mind-boggling number with forty-two zeros.

q: Which of the following recently gave what many think as irrefutable evidence for the existence of dark matter:
a: the discovery of gravitational waves at the LIGO facility at Pacific Northwest National Lab
Chandra X-ray images of hot gases during a violent merger of the "bullet cluster" of galaxies
creation of quark-gluon plasma at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider
the finding that neutrinos account for more mass of the universe than all the stars in the universe
e: Pictures of the colliding Bullet Cluster showed mysterious dark matter zooming right past trapped gas clouds.

q: If the Sun had the same mass but one-half its current radius, by which of the following factors would the radius of Earth's orbit be multiplied?
e: Because the Sun keeps all its heavy mass, its gravity stays unchanged, leaving Earth's orbit multiplied by 1.

q: A wire of radius A carries a uniform current I. The total magnetic energy per unit length contained within the wire is which of the following?
e: No matter how chubby or skinny the wire grows, its internal magnetic energy stays completely independent of its radius.

q: Scientists at SLAC National Lab recently began construction on the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment, or DUNE, in South Dakota. What property of neutrinos are scientists at DUNE trying to measure?
e: These tiny ghost particles zip through solid rock while clever underground scientists try to weigh them to find their mass.

q: A lightning bolt is seen and its accompanying thunder is heard 15 seconds later. This means the storm is most likely how many miles away:
e: Sound takes five slow seconds to travel one mile, so waiting fifteen seconds means the storm is three miles away.

q: What is the main difference between transverse and longitudinal waves?
a: Direction of the medium displacement with respect to the direction of wave propagation
e: The difference comes down to direction, like whether the wave wiggles side-to-side or pushes forward along its traveling path.

q: Which of the following is equivalent to 10 centimeters?
e: Ten centimeters stretches just as far as ten to the eighth nanometers, holding hands in an invisible, microscopic line.

q: A non-relativistic electron in a uniform magnetic field is moving in a circular orbit. Which of the following best describes how its orbital period changes if the kinetic energy of the electron is increased?
a: Depends on the direction of the magnetic field
e: Even when our spunky electron zooms faster, its wider circle means each loop takes the exact same time!

q: Which of the following is not a logical corollary to special relativity?
e: Spacetime only bends when heavy gravity shows up in general relativity, so it doesn't belong to special relativity!

q: In a tug-of-war, each person on a team pulls with an average force of 500 newtons. What is the tension in the center of the rope if there are 10-man teams on each side:
e: Ten teammates tug with five thousand newtons together, so the rope's middle feels that exact five-thousand-newton pull.

q: Which of the following is the most common term for the general type of wave that results from the vibration of a physical medium:
e: Mechanical waves love company, needing real stuff like water or air to wiggle through as they travel along.

q: Which of the following is the most common instrument used for measuring gas pressure:
e: A friendly manometer uses a balancing puddle of liquid to see just how hard trapped gas is pushing.

q: Which of the following materials would mostly likely be used for a radiant heat barrier?
e: Shiny aluminum acts like a mirror, bouncing sizzling heat rays right back before they can warm your room.

q: A motor has a DC resistance of 5 ohms. The motor operates on 220 volt AC, and when running at full speed, it generates a back electromotive force of 200 volts. What is the current, in amperes, drawn when the motor operates at top speed?
e: The motor pushes back two hundred volts, leaving twenty volts across five ohms to drive four tidy amperes.

q: If 500 joules of energy are required to move a 20-coulomb charge from point A to point B, what must be the potential difference, in volts, between A and B?
e: Sharing five hundred joules across twenty traveling charges gives each little friend a boost of twenty-five volts!

q: One of Maxwell's equations states that the divergence of any magnetic field is zero. Which of the following statements is a direct corollary to this expression?
a: When traveling at relativistic speeds, some part of a magnetic field will appear as an electric field
Any moving electric charge induces a magnetic field
Any changing magnetic field induces an electric field
No magnetic field lines have endpoints
e: Magnetic field lines never have endpoints because they always chase their own tails in endless, unbroken loops!

q: Which of the following times of day BEST corresponds to a decrease in ionization of particles in the ionosphere?
e: When the cozy night arrives and sunlight sleeps, excited sky particles calm down and lose their electric charge.

q: A liquid metal fast reactor (LMFR) is an advanced type of nuclear reactor that uses liquid metal as a primary coolant. Of the following metals, which one is NOT most commonly used as a primary coolant in LMFRs?
e: While metals like sodium happily cool reactors, greedy lithium absorbs too many neutrons to be a common coolant.

q: You have three equivalent resistors with which to make a circuit. Which of the following combinations would have the least total resistance?
a: Two resistors in series to each other and in parallel with the third
Two resistors in parallel to each other and in series with the third
e: Wiring three resistors in parallel gives electricity three easy pathways at once, creating the least total resistance.

q: The photoelectric effect reveals what property of photons?
e: Light acts like tiny billiard balls knocking electrons right out of metal, showing off its bouncy particle-like nature.

q: Two balls are dropped one second apart from a tall building. Given g as 10 meters per second squared and neglecting air resistance, what is the approximate distance in meters between the two balls three seconds after the first ball is dropped?
e: After three seconds, the first ball falls forty-five meters and the second falls twenty, leaving twenty-five meters between them.

q: Which of the following numbers is the best estimate for the number of kilowatt hours of energy used by an average U.S. home in 2014?
e: A typical cozy home hums through about eleven thousand kilowatt-hours each year, powering everything from toasters to lamps.

q: Only two forces are acting on a large rigid body: one is 5 newtons upwards, and one is 5 newtons downwards. However, the object is not at equilibrium. Which of the following could be the reason why?
a: External forces are acting on the object
The object had a non-zero initial speed
e: Even with balanced opposite forces, pushing on different spots creates an unbalanced torque that makes the object spin!

q: Scientists at Pacific Northwest National Lab are using mass spectrometry to study beta amyloid proteins. Which of the following is NOT true regarding beta-amyloid proteins?
a: Beta-amyloid proteins are commonly seen in plaques in patients with Alzheimer's
Treatments reducing beta-amyloid plaques have been successful in alleviating Alzheimer's symptoms
There are multiple forms of beta-amyloid proteins, including some that are soluble
Beta-amyloid proteins are produced from the proteolytic processing of a transmembrane protein
e: Clearing those sticky protein plaques has sadly not cured Alzheimer's symptoms, making that hopeful statement false.

q: What type of stream only bears water during and immediately after a rainstorm:
e: An ephemeral stream is a fleeting pop-up brook, flowing for a brief dance only when fresh rain falls.

q: Which of the following is the most accurate description of charging by induction?
a: It depends on putting two objects in actual physical contact with each other
It depends on the use of friction
It depends on the use of a ground to redistribute charges
It depends on gain of electrons during chemical reactions
e: By letting charges escape safely into the ground without touching, induction neatly leaves behind a brand-new electric charge.

q: Pacific Northwest National Lab scientists are studying the virus that causes Middle East respiratory syndrome. This virus is most closely related to the virus that causes what other disease?
e: MERS and SARS are like sneaky virus cousins that wear the exact same spiky crown, making SARS its closest family match.

q: Which of the following correctly describes a magnifying glass?
e: A magnifying glass is just a single lens curving outward like a round belly, bending light to make tiny critters look giant!

q: What type of feature is the Moon's Rupes Recta?
e: Rupes Recta is a fault where the dusty Moon's crust cracked and slipped downward, leaving a giant, dramatic cliff.

q: The index of refraction for a medium is:
a: the ratio of the angles of refraction of red light and blue light in the medium
the angle of refraction for monochromatic light in the medium
the ratio of the speed of light in the medium to the speed of light in a vacuum
the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in the medium
e: Light dashes fastest in empty space, so this compares that top cosmic speed to light's slower crawl inside a material.

q: Which of the following physical quantities is equal to the rate of change of momentum?
e: Whenever something gains or loses momentum over time, a push or pull called force is making that change happen.

q: Water flows at 2.0 meters per second through a tube of radius 1 centimeter. The dynamic viscosity of the water is 1.0 10-3 pascal seconds. Which of the following best represents the Reynolds number and the nature of the flow, given that the density of water is 1.0 103 kilograms per cubic meter?
e: With a Reynolds number of 40,000, this speedy water churns wildly in a tumbling, messy dance called turbulent flow.

q: A positively-charged particle is traveling in the positive-x direction as it experiences a uniform magnetic field pointing in the positive-y direction. In which of the following directions will the particle initially be deflected?
e: Following the right-hand rule, this speedy little positive charge gets shoved straight into the positive-z direction by the magnetic field.

q: A slingshot stretched by a distance x gives a pebble speed v. What is the speed of the same pebble if a slingshot, obeying Hooke's law, is stretched by a distance 2x?
e: Pulling the rubber band twice as far stores extra snap, shooting the pebble out twice as fast at 2v!

q: The cost of generating electricity has many different components. Fuel, maintenance, and transmission are examples of which of the following costs?
e: Because bills for fuel and wire repairs go up and down depending on how much power you make, they are variable costs.

q: Which of the following statements is false about photovoltaic cells?
a: N-type silicon is doped with phosphorus
Phosphorus gives the silicon a positive character, and the tendency to attract electrons
P-type silicon is doped with boron
Boron gives the silicon a positive character, and the tendency to attract electrons
e: Phosphorus actually brings extra negative electrons to the party, so saying it gives silicon a positive character is completely false.

q: The process in which an atom reradiates a photon after interacting with an incident photon of the same energy is called:
e: In Thomson scattering, an atom catches a photon and playfully tosses it right back out with the exact same energy.

q: Which of the following stars has a positive apparent magnitude?
e: In space, dimmer stars get positive brightness numbers, making North Star Polaris positive while flashier stars stay negative.

q: Which of the following will cause adiabatic warming?
a: Heat being added to the volume of air
e: Squishing air with increasing pressure forces its little molecules to bump together faster, warming them up without adding outside heat.

q: Which of the following nuclides is both fissile and fissionable only with high energy bombardment?
e: Tough Uranium-238 refuses to split unless you strike it with super high-energy particles to force its heavy nucleus apart.

q: Proxima Centauri [PROK-suh-muh sen-TAWR-y], the closest star to the sun, is nearest which of the following distances from the sun?
e: Even though Proxima Centauri is our Sun's nearest stellar neighbor, its twinkling light still takes about 4 light-years to reach us.

q: Which heavy metal element, used in photovoltaic thin films, has raised concerns about ecological bioaccumulation due to its high toxicity?
e: Cadmium helps solar panels catch sunshine, but this heavy metal is dangerously toxic and can build up inside living creatures.

q: Which of the following BEST describes an air mass that originates in northern Mexico, moves into the Great Plains and stagnates, resulting in severe drought:
e: Baking over warm, dry land makes this continental tropical air mass bring thirsty, rain-free droughts wherever it wanders.

q: Which of the following meteorological sensors is not part of the suite of sensors on the Mars Rover Curiosity?
e: The rover checks Martian wind, heat, and air pressure, but it left the psychrometer off its weather tool belt.

q: Planck resolved the ultraviolet catastrophe for black bodies by postulating the quantization of photon energies to derive an expression showing that the modal energies obey which of the following statistical distributions?
e: Photons love to herd together, so their quantized energies follow the team-player rules of Bose-Einstein statistics.

q: Which of the following is a type of inland fog that occurs more often in spring when warm, moist air is cooled below its dew point as it moves over a cooler surface:
e: When cozy, moist air glides horizontally across chilly spring ground, it cools down and creates a blanket of advection fog.

q: A bucket of hot oil weighing 50 newtons is lifted at constant velocity up a castle wall that is 10 meters high. It takes 20 seconds to raise the bucket up the wall. How much power was used to raise the bucket?
e: Lifting five hundred joules of energy over twenty speedy seconds means the castle winch worked at twenty-five watts of power.

q: A waning gibbous [JIH-bus] moon describes which of the following parts of the lunar cycle?
a: Third quarter moon to new moon
Full moon to third quarter moon
First quarter moon to full moon
New moon to first quarter moon
e: After shining completely full, the moon slowly shrinks toward its third quarter phase, which we call a waning gibbous.

q: Two balls are thrown perfectly horizontally off a cliff on Mars, where the acceleration due to gravity is 3.7 meters per second squared. If ball 1 lands 30 meters further than ball 2, which of the following statements is correct about their initial velocities?
a: The velocity of ball 1 is 30 meters per second greater than the velocity of ball 2
The velocity of ball 2 is 30 meters per second greater than the velocity of ball 1
The velocity of ball 1 is 30 times larger than the velocity of ball 2
The exact relationship cannot be determined without knowing the height of the cliff
e: Without knowing the cliff height, we cannot tell how long the balls fell, so their speeds stay a mystery.

q: A cord making a 60o angle with the floor pulls on a crate with a tension of 100 newtons along a 10 meter distance. How much work, in joules, is done on the crate by the pulling cord?
e: Because the rope pulls sideways at an angle, only half its pull counts, making exactly five hundred joules of work.

q: Which moon is the only satellite in our solar system to possess a dense atmosphere?
e: Saturn's giant moon Titan snuggles under a cozy, thick blanket of orange smog, unlike any other moon!

q: A torque [tork] integrated over an angle describes which of the following quantities?
e: Twisting something through an angle is just rotational pushing, which means all that spinning effort adds up to work!

q: The statement that magnetic monopoles do not exist in classical physics is most equivalent to which of the following statements?
a: The magnetic field has a divergence of zero
The electric field has a divergence related to total charge density
A changing magnetic field will induce an electromotive force in a closed loop
A moving charge will induce a magnetic field
e: Since magnet ends never live alone, magnetic lines always make unbroken loops, meaning their divergence is zero.

q: Fatty acid synthesis uses which of the following kinds of metabolic pathways?
e: To build up long fats, tiny cell workers repeat the same chemical loop, winding along like a growing spiral staircase.

q: According to the equipartition theorem, by what factor of the Boltzmann constant does each translational degree of freedom of an ideal gas contribute to the heat capacity?
e: Each way a gas atom can zip through space gets an equal one-half share of heat energy.

q: What is the term for a crescent-shaped sand dune with horns pointed downwind?
e: When the desert breeze gently pushes sand into smiling crescents pointing with the wind, a barchan dune is born!

q: A gold leaf electroscope is negatively charged by touching it with a negatively charged conductor. You then bring a positively charged glass rod close to, but not touching, the top of the electroscope. Which of the following occurs?
a: The leaves first spread further apart, then move closer together
e: The positive rod charms negative charges up to the top, leaving the leaves less negative so they snuggle closer together.

q: If the fundamental frequency of a pipe open at both ends is 70 Hertz, what will its next two harmonics be in Hertz?
e: Pipes open at both ends sing in whole-number steps, so double seventy makes one hundred forty and triple makes two hundred ten!

q: Which of the following would best approximate the temperature, in kelvins, of a star with very strong Balmer absorption lines?
e: Stars need to be just the right coziness of ten thousand kelvins for their hydrogen atoms to show those bold lines.

q: Roughly, which of the following BEST represents the solar energy intensity in watts per square meter incident on the Earth?
e: High above the clouds, our cozy sun beams down about fourteen hundred watts of warmth onto every square meter.

q: What will occur if a white dwarf in a binary exceeds its Roche [ROSH] lobe?
a: Its companion will transfer mass to it until it shrinks below its Roche lobe
It will form a planetary nebula
It will continue to expand and ablate onto its companion
It will transfer matter to its companion until it shrinks below its Roche lobe
e: When a little white dwarf puffs up too big for its space, it spills extra gas onto its partner star until it fits again.

q: If a soldier wants to shoot a projectile as far into enemy territory as possible over level ground, at what angle from the ground should the projectile be shot?
e: Aiming halfway between straight up and flat out at forty-five degrees gives the best balance to travel farthest.

q: Marine sediment in the North Atlantic is primarily calcareous [kal-CARE-ee-us] ooze, while marine sediment in the North Pacific is primarily pelagic [peh-LAJ-ik] clay. Which of the following best explains why?
a: The North Pacific has a higher pH than the North Atlantic
The North Pacific is deeper than the North Atlantic
The North Pacific has a lower pH than the North Atlantic
The North Pacific has more dissolved oxygen than the North Atlantic
e: The North Pacific water is more acidic with a lower pH, so it dissolves delicate shells before they can settle into ooze.

q: At about 10 PM in late summer of 2006, an observer at about 35 degrees north latitude would most likely see the stars Altair, Deneb and Vega in which of the following places in the sky:
a: about half way up in the northern sky
e: On warm summer nights, these three bright starry friends climb high to sparkle almost directly above your head!

q: Which of the following conditions is sufficient for describing a system in unstable equilibrium?
a: Net force is at a minimum
Potential energy is at a strict minimum
Potential energy is at a strict maximum
e: Perched at the very top of an energy hill, maximum potential energy means any tiny wobble sends things tumbling away.

q: Which of the following numbers corresponds to the approximate temperature in kelvins of red stars?
e: Glowing with a sleepy red ember light, these cooler stars simmer right around three thousand kelvins.

q: Which of the following percentages is closest to the percent of energy used in Texas in 2014 that was generated by wind?
e: Giant windmills danced in the Texas breeze, spinning up about ten percent of the state’s electricity back in 2014!

q: DOE scientists have recently been studying the material properties of graphene. Which of the following pairs of characteristics did they discover regarding graphene?
e: Graphene is mighty strong like an invisible shield, but it has low toughness, meaning a tiny crack makes it snap easily.

q: When a tennis racket hits a tennis ball, how do the forces on each object compare?
a: The force on the tennis ball has a greater magnitude than the force on the racket
The force on the racket has a greater magnitude than the force on the ball
The magnitude of the force on each object is the same
The forces depend on the level of impact
e: Whenever two playful things collide, they push back equally, giving both the racket and the ball the exact same force!

q: The unit formed by multiplying pounds-force times seconds can be used to measure which of the following quantities?
e: Multiplying a pushing force by time measures momentum, which is the unstoppable roll of an object on the move.

q: The Meissner effect is most directly associated with which of the following:
e: Superconductors get so super-chilly that they kick out magnetic fields, magically floating magnets in the famous Meissner effect!

q: A steadily increasing force is applied to a box that remains at rest for some period of time and then begins to accelerate. Which of the following appropriately describes what happens to the frictional force during the experiment?
a: The frictional force remains constant throughout the experiment
The frictional force increases throughout the experiment
The frictional force increases and then suddenly drops to a lower, non-zero value
The frictional force increases and then suddenly drops to zero
e: Friction pushes harder and harder to keep the box still, then suddenly drops to a lower grip once it slides.

q: Scientists at Fermilab are building devices to perform quantum teleportation of qubits [CUE-bits] over long distances. Which of the following is a unique property of qubits, compared to classical bits?
a: Are less error-prone than classical bits
Are cheaper to produce than classical bits
e: Unlike ordinary bits, qubits can become entangled, linking up like cosmic best friends that mirror each other across space.

q: A proton initially at rest is accelerated through a potential difference of 1 megavolt. What is its final kinetic energy in electronvolts?
e: Zooming through a million-volt gap gives the tiny proton one million, or ten to the sixth, electronvolts of lively energy!

q: If Omega is exactly one, which of the following is TRUE about the universe?
a: It will expand forever at an accelerating rate
It will expand forever, but the speed of its expansion will slowly approach zero
It will eventually collapse upon itself
It will eventually be destroyed by a black hole
e: On this cosmic tightrope, space keeps expanding forever, but it gently slows down until its speed nearly touches zero.

q: In quantum physics, which of these theorised sub-atomic particles has yet to be observed?
e: The shy graviton is supposed to carry gravity's pull, but no scientist has ever caught one peeking out!

q: How does the intensity of light passing through an absorbing medium change as a function of optical depth?
a: It decreases exponentially with the optical depth
It decreases as the sixth power of the optical depth
It decreases as the cube of the optical depth
It decreases as the square of the optical depth
e: As light sneaks into a shadowy cloud, its brightness fades exponentially, dimming quickly as optical depth grows thicker.

q: Which of the following is TRUE of a sound wave traveling in dry air at STP at a constant velocity:
a: if frequency increases, wavelength stays the same
e: When a sound chirps at a higher frequency, its traveling ripples bunch closer together, making each wavelength shorter.

q: Which of the following capacitor configurations for four identical capacitors would yield the largest stored charge for a given voltage?
a: All four capacitors connected in series
Two parallel branches of two series capacitors
Three capacitors in parallel, in series to a fourth
All four capacitors connected in parallel
e: Connecting all four capacitors side-by-side in parallel lets them team up to store the largest mountain of charge!

q: The Moon always turns the same face toward the Earth, yet small variations in the visibility of its features appear to take place, such that it appears to rock slowly backward and forward. What effect accounts for this observed behavior?
e: That shy little wobble is called libration, letting the Moon playfully rock so we can peek around its edges!

q: Which of the following is true regarding capacity factor for an electric power producer?
e: A power plant cannot make less than zero power or beat its top limit, keeping this factor strictly between zero and one.

q: An electron and positron collide and annihilate [uh-NY-uh-layt] one another. Which of the following is nearest the energy released, in mega electronvolts?
e: When these tiny opposites collide and vanish, their combined mass turns into a bright spark of about one mega electronvolt!

q: A wire carries a current of 2 amperes vertically upward. What is the magnitude and direction of the magnetic field in teslas produced by the wire 4 millimeters to the North of the wire?
e: Using the right-hand rule, the upward current swirls the field West, measuring one times ten to the negative fourth teslas.

q: Which of the following is illustrated on Maunder's diagram:
e: Maunder’s famous diagram tracks sunspots dancing across the Sun over time, creating patterns that look like butterfly wings!

q: Which of the following occurs when a glass tube is rubbed with a silk cloth:
a: protons are transferred from the silk to the glass tube
protons are transferred from the glass tube to the silk
electrons are transferred from the silk to the glass tube
electrons are transferred from the glass tube to the silk
e: Rubbing them together tickles tiny electrons right off the glass tube, sending them hopping onto the silk cloth.

q: Which of the following is nearest escape velocity on the surface of the Earth, in miles per hour?
e: To break free from Earth’s hug, a brave rocket must zoom at an astonishing twenty-five thousand miles per hour!

q: Remnants of the energy released by the Big Bang are now distributed across the Universe as which of the following?
e: The universe's very first baby picture cooled down over billions of years, stretching into gentle microwaves that still whisper softly everywhere today.

q: Which of the following is closest to the average number of years between reversals of the polarity of Earth's magnetic field?
e: Earth's invisible magnetic compass loves to flip upside down, swapping north and south roughly every 200,000 years.

q: What kind of trajectory will a comet follow if it has the minimum amount of energy needed to escape its star?
e: With just enough energy to escape its star forever, our brave little comet glides away along an open, U-shaped parabolic curve.

q: Which of the following occurs as a rapidly advancing cold front overtakes a closed off warm front?
e: When a speedy cold front zips ahead and scoops cozy warm air right off the ground, meteorologists call that chilly squeeze an occlusion.

q: A mass spectrometry experiment is performed with a magnetic field of 0.2 newtons per ampere meter and an electric field of 3.0 105 volts per meter. What is the speed of the ions?
e: Balancing the electric push against the magnetic tug sends these zippy little ions racing at an astonishing 1500 kilometers per second!

q: What is the source of the annual Perseid (read as: PER-seed-id) and Leonid meteor showers?
a: The Earth passing through an asteroid belt
e: When traveling comets shed trails of dusty crumbs along their path, Earth sweeps through them to create dazzling meteor showers!

q: The rostral bone evolved to allow for the powerful beak-like bite characteristic of what dinosaur group?
e: Beaked ceratopsian dinos grew a special rostral bone at the tip of their snouts, giving them a super-strong chomping beak.

q: What is the SI derived unit for electrical conductance?
e: When scientists measure how happily electric currents flow through a material, they track that friendly conductance in units called siemens.

q: Water tank A has width W1 and tank B has width W2, where W1 > W2. The two water tanks are the same height, H. If both tanks are completely filled with water, which of the following is true about the water pressure at the bottom of the tank?
a: The pressure is greater in tank A
The pressure is greater in tank B
Both tanks have the same pressure
e: Water pressure only cares about how deep it goes, so two tanks with the same height push down with the exact same pressure.

q: Which of the following is the MOST common term for a galaxy that is emitting a large amount of radiation from a black hole at its center:
e: A galaxy is called active when its hungry central black hole gobbles up gas and shines with brilliant, glowing energy.

q: All the elements that are more massive than iron were formed by what astronomical phenomenon?
e: When a giant star ends its life with a dazzling supernova blast, it cooks up all the elements heavier than iron!

q: Which of the following is the part of an electric motor that functions as an electromagnet:
e: Inside an electric motor, a spinning coil called the armature acts as an electromagnet, delightfully turning electricity into round-and-round motion.

q: Which of the following is the magnitude of the focal length of a spherically curved convex mirror in air, where R stands for the radius of curvature:
e: A curved mirror focuses light halfway to its center point, which is why the focal length equals the radius divided by two.

q: If you heat a container of gas at a higher temperature than its surroundings to twice its prior absolute temperature without changing the temperature of its environment, you have done which of the following?
a: Increased the system's enthalpy and decreased its entropy
Increased the system's enthalpy and entropy
Decreased the system's enthalpy and entropy
Decreased the system's enthalpy and increased its entropy
e: Warming up the trapped gas gives its particles more heat energy and randomness, increasing both the system's enthalpy and entropy.

q: Which of the following countries has lost the greatest land area of forest to deforestation over the past decade?
e: With its enormous Amazon home, Brazil has sadly lost the most total forest area over the past decade.

q: In what cloud type does hail generally form?
e: Mighty cumulonimbus storm clouds juggle raindrops high into the freezing air, turning them into icy hailstones before dropping them down!

q: Which of the following BEST describes the most common functions for which most transistors are used:
a: to switch on and off or amplify electronic signals
to allow electric current to pass in only one direction while increasing or decreasing the voltage
to regulate the frequency of electrical sine waves
e: Transistors work like speedy little light switches in your gadgets, flipping electronic signals on and off or boosting them louder.

q: Which of the following is the double-degenerate model for Type Ia supernovae [soo-per-NOH-vee]?
a: The cores of a binary system undergo common envelope evolution collapse and explode after iron fusion
A red giant overflows its Roche [ROHSH] lobe and dumps matter onto a white dwarf until the white dwarf exceeds the Chandrasekhar [chun-druh-SAY-ker] mass
Two white dwarfs collide to create a new object, which exceeds the Chandrasekhar mass
A main sequence star overflows its Roche lobe and dumps matter onto a white dwarf until the white dwarf exceeds the Chandrasekhar mass
e: In this cosmic tango, two white dwarf stars smash together to form an overweight giant that dramatically bursts into a supernova!

q: Which of the following colors of light has the most energy?
e: Violet light wiggles in super-fast, tiny waves, packing more lively energy than any other color of the rainbow!

q: Two pipes of diameters 1 and 2 are connected. What is the ratio of kinetic energy per unit volume (k1/k2) of water flowing through these pipes?
a: 24 [open parenthesis d2 over d1 close parenthesis to the power of 4] 1
22 [open parenthesis d2 over d1 close parenthesis to the power of 2] 1
14 [open parenthesis d1 over d2 close parenthesis to the power of 4] 2
12 [open parenthesis d1 over d2 close parenthesis to the power of 2] 2
e: Narrower pipes speed up water, making the kinetic energy ratio equal the second diameter over the first, all to the fourth power.

q: Which of the following would have a Widmansttten Pattern:
e: When an iron meteorite cools super slowly in space over millions of years, it grows beautiful crisscrossing metal stripes hidden inside.

q: What is the magnitude of the force, in newtons, experienced by a 1 coulomb charge travelling 10 meters per second at a 30-degree angle with respect to a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.1 tesla?
e: Multiplying the charge, speed, magnetic field, and that gentle thirty-degree angle tilt leaves our tiny particle with half a newton of push.

q: A force is conservative when the work done by the force:
a: On a closed path is zero
On an open path is zero
e: If a force is conservative, walking in a full loop brings you back with zero total work done along the way.

q: Which of the following statements is true about kaolinite [KAY-uh-luh-nyt]?
a: It has a high cation exchange capacity [KAT-eye-uhn]
e: Unlike greedy clays that swell up like sponges, kaolinite keeps its layers tightly glued together, so it refuses to expand when wet.

q: Which of the following terms best describes the albedo of a planet:
e: Think of albedo as a planet's mirror score, showing how much bright sunlight bounces right off its shiny face!

q: Scientists from Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are studying volatile organic compounds, or VOCs, released from the upper canopy in the Amazon Rainforest as part of the "Go Amazon" project. Understanding VOC production by trees involves understanding the variables that control it. Which variable is NOT important to the study?
e: High up in the sunny canopy, daily weather drives the leafy scents, making a tree's age surprisingly unimportant to the study.

q: Which of the following materials could be used as a moderator in a nuclear reactor?
e: Graphite acts like a polite bumper, gently slowing down speedy neutrons without swallowing them up so the reactor keeps humming safely.

q: Which of the following glacial features can result from calving?
e: When a giant glacier reaches the chilly sea and cracks, colossal chunks break off to become floating icebergs!

q: A girl runs up one flight of steps. Which of the following factors does NOT affect the work done by the girl against gravity?
a: Height of the flight of steps
e: Gravity only cares about lifting your weight to the top, not whether you zoomed up like a rocket or strolled slowly.

q: Which of the following planets has the longest year?
e: Being farthest out, chilly Neptune has the longest cosmic track to travel, taking almost 165 Earth years for one single birthday!

q: Scientists at Argonne National Lab are using x-rays to probe porosity in 3D-printed titanium alloys. Which of the following best explains why porosity is undesirable?
a: A large range of pore sizes reduces printing resolution
Porosity limits the size of the structures that can be printed
e: Tiny hidden air pockets weaken metal over time, making it tire out and crack when it gets bent repeatedly.

q: The closest distance at which Gina can properly focus is 100 cm from her eye. The distance of normal vision is 0.25 m. Find the power in diopters [dy-OP-ters] of the converging lens for her eyeglass.
e: To nudge blurry words from a meter away to a cozy quarter-meter, her lens needs three diopters of focusing power.

q: The Sun has already completed nearly one half of its main sequence stage. Which of the following will occur next?
e: When our cozy yellow Sun finishes its core fuel, it will puff up into an enormous, glowing red giant!

q: Which of the following experimental approaches was used by scientists to discover that the atomic nucleus held most of the atom's mass and a positive charge:
a: directing alpha particles at thin metal strips
finding the amount of magnetic deflection in cathode rays within a well-evacuated tube
exposing photographic film to certain radium salts
using a crude cyclotron to disintegrate large nuclei
e: Firing tiny particles at thin gold foil revealed that a few bounced right back, uncovering the atom's dense positive center!

q: A 100 watt current of heat flows via conduction between two stable temperature reservoirs through a material of length 5 centimeters and cross-sectional area 0.5 square meters. If the length of material is extended to 1 meter and the cross-sectional area increased to 1 square meter, what is the new heat current in watts?
e: Stretching the path twenty times longer slows heat down so much that doubling the thickness still leaves just ten watts.

q: Which of the following experiments provided evidence in favor of the wave theory of light?
e: Beaming light through two tiny slits created ripple patterns like splashing water, proving light travels in dancing waves.

q: Some quasars exhibit multiple images. What phenomenon explains this observation?
e: A heavy galaxy bends space like a giant funhouse mirror, splitting one quasar's light into multiple glowing copies!

q: The Coriolis effect causes objects moving in the Northern Hemisphere to veer in which of the following ways?
a: To the right, or clockwise when viewed from above
To the left, or counterclockwise when viewed from above
e: Because Earth spins underneath everything, things traveling across the north gently curve to the right like a giant merry-go-round.

q: The curve that the position of the Sun at noon traces on the sky over the course of a year most closely resembles which of the following?
e: Earth's cozy tilt and oval orbit make the midday Sun dance in a graceful figure eight across the yearly sky.

q: Which of the following lavas does not have a modern analog?
e: Komatiite lava needed baby Earth's super scorching heat to melt, so our cooler modern world cannot brew it anymore.

q: A common device used to study extreme forms of matter is the magneto-optical trap. Which of the following explains how the trap works?
a: It heats magnetically contained matter with lasers
It oscillates matter through dipole interactions
It uses both magnetic fields and lasers to cool matter
It magnetically accelerates matter through optical lens systems
e: Like tiny traffic cops, clever lasers and gentle magnets work together to slow down zooming atoms until they chill out completely.

q: The Moon's composition is most similar to which layer of Earth?
e: Our rocky Moon is made of the very same lightweight stuff as Earth's outer crust, like a cosmic crumb tossed into space.

q: Which of the following values, in kelvins, is closest to the temperature of the Sun's photosphere?
e: The sun's glowing yellow face beams at a toasty 5,800 kelvins, warm enough to shine bright across the entire solar system.

q: Which of the following is an example of an action that demonstrates negative work?
a: Throwing a book to the ground
Gently lowering a book to the ground
e: When you lower a book gently, your hands push up while it moves down, stealing its energy with negative work.

q: Which of the following is not equivalent to the second law of thermodynamics?
a: Heat cannot flow spontaneously from a colder object to a hotter object
No heat engine can have an efficiency exceeding that of the Carnot engine
No thermodynamic process can decrease the entropy of the universe
It is impossible for a thermodynamic system to return to the same state twice
e: Systems can happily reset to their starting state, like a bouncy piston, so returning to the same state twice is totally allowed.

q: A wire is carrying current directly towards you. Which of the following describes the orientation of the magnetic field generated by this wire?
a: In a counter-clockwise loop about the wire
In a clockwise loop about the wire
e: Point your thumb toward you, and your fingers curl around the wire in a merry, counter-clockwise magnetic dance.

q: In a DC/DC converter, the electrical energy is stored in which elements of the circuit?
e: Capacitors and inductors act like tiny electrical piggy banks, storing buzzing energy in electric and magnetic fields until it is needed.

q: A family sits on an 8 meter long see-saw. The daughter, massing 20 kilograms, sits at the left end of the see-saw, and the father, massing 80 kilograms, sits at the middle of the right portion of the see-saw. Where must the mother, massing 60 kilograms, sit in order to make the see-saw in static equilibrium and level with the ground?
e: Mom must sit four-thirds of a meter left of the pivot, adding just enough tipping power to balance the playful seesaw.

q: In general, the probability of flooding decreases when there is an increase in the amount of which of the following?
e: When thirsty soil drinks up rainwater through infiltration, less water puddles on top, keeping neighborhood streets safe from floods.

q: Which of the following metals reacts violently with water?
e: Dropping eager little lithium into water makes it fizz, pop, and zoom around with fiery, bubbling excitement!

q: What region of the country has the greatest percentage of homes heated with heating oil?
e: Up in the chilly Northeast, historic homes still rely heavily on cozy heating oil to stay toasty all winter long.

q: As an object falls to the Earth with air resistance present, what happens to the acceleration of the object?
a: It remains a constant 9.8 meters per second squared
It increases from 0 to 9.8 meters per second squared
It remains at a constant 0 meters per second squared
It decreases from 9.8 to 0 meters per second squared
e: As rushing air pushes back, the falling object stops speeding up as quickly, dropping its acceleration from 9.8 right down to zero.

q: You are observing an object traveling away from you approaching the event radius of a black hole. Which of the following would you expect to see?
a: The object slows down and turns redder as it approaches
The object slows down and turns bluer as it approaches
The object speeds up and turns redder as it approaches
The object speeds up and turns bluer as it approaches
e: Strong gravity stretches the light and warps time, making the daring traveler look frozen in place and glowing redder.

q: A box of proper length l, proper width w, and proper height h is falling right-side up without tumbling toward the ground. The Lorentz contraction predicts that which of the following dimensions will be contracted?
e: Because the box zooms straight down, relativity only squishes it along its path of travel, shrinking just its height.

q: Which of the following is true regarding all members of our solar system?
a: They were formed thousands of years ago from elements that have always existed
They were formed millions of years ago, when the elements and each body were created at the same time
They were formed billions of years ago from elements that were created in many previously existing stars
e: Billions of years ago, stardust recycled from ancient exploding stars gathered together to build our entire sun and planetary family.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are studying protists that consume bacteria and have pseudopodia. What taxonomic group are these protists part of?
e: These wiggly Amoebozoa stretch out blobby false feet called pseudopodia to scoop up and gobble down yummy bacteria.

q: Researchers are using the DOE's Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory to study the distribution of metabolites produced during nitrogen-fixation via MALDI-TOF [mawl-dee-tawf]. MALDI-TOF is a variation of what family of techniques?
e: MALDI-TOF belongs to the mass spectrometry family, which weighs tiny molecules like luggage to discover who they really are.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of tropical forest soils in relation to temperate forest soils?
a: Tropical forest soils are richer in nutrients
Tropical forest soils experience more intense leaching
Temperate forest soils retain more organic matter
e: Heavy rains wash away nutrients quickly in tropical forests, leaving behind surprisingly poor soil rather than rich dirt.

q: The Fermi [FUR-mee] energy of semiconductors lies in which of the following regions?
e: In semiconductors, the Fermi energy sits right in the quiet band gap between the crowded lower and upper electron levels.

q: If the viscous force acting on an object moving through a liquid or gas is modeled as F = -bv, where F is the resistive force, v is the velocity, and b is a constant, which of the following types of equation will need to be solved in order to determine the acceleration as a function of time?
e: Because acceleration depends on changing speed, you need a differential equation to solve this smooth, slowing-down puzzle.

q: At what point in time is a CFL's [C-F- elz] energy consumption greatest, compared to its light output?
a: After being turned off for 15 minutes
e: When first clicked on, this sleepy bulb gulps extra electricity to wake up before it can shine its brightest!

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are researching the balance between liquid water and ice within clouds in the Arctic, in which temperatures range from -3 to -8 degrees Celsius. Liquid water droplets within these clouds are said to be in what state?
e: Even below freezing, these chilly drops stay liquid instead of turning to ice, making them supercooled daredevils!

q: Which of the following classes of stars does NOT have radiative zones?
e: Tiny M-class stars churn heat from their cores like bubbling soup, with no calm radiative zone to slow them down.

q: A child learns that mixing approximately equal amounts of the paint colors orange and green produces brown. This is an example of:
e: Each squirt of paint steals away different colors of light, subtracting them until all that reflects back is muddy brown!

q: A DOE geothermal research project has established the effectiveness of enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) for utilizing geothermal energy for the generation of electricity. Using this approach, which of the following percentages of total U.S. current generating capacity could be generated with EGS?
e: Earth holds so much trapped underground heat beneath our feet that it could power half of the whole country!

q: Unstable particles muons [MYOO-ons], pions [PY-ons], kaons, and sigmas have half-life times in the range of which of the following?
e: These speedy little particles vanish in a flash, surviving only ten to the minus six down to minus twenty-three seconds.

q: Brookhaven National Lab researchers are studying leaf properties that change with age of the leaf. Which of the following accurately describes how oak leaves change in their near-infrared absorption over time?
a: It increases over the first half of the year, then decreases
It decreases over the first half of the year, then increases
e: Young leaves soak up more infrared light as they grow thick, then absorb less as they dry out in autumn.

q: A person spearfishing from the shore sees a fish located 3 meters from the shore at an approximate depth of 1 meter. To spear the fish, the person should aim in which of the following directions?
e: Water bends light like a magic trick, making the fish look higher up than where it is actually swimming!

q: What is the power generated by a circuit with a total current of 6 amperes running through two resistors in parallel, of 2 and 6 ohms?
e: With six amps sharing two parallel paths, their teamwork creates one point five ohms, pumping out fifty-four watts of glowing power!

q: On the Beaufort Scale of wind force, what wind name is given to number 8?
e: When the wind throws a mighty temper tantrum at level eight, sailors call that roaring blow a gale!

q: Excluding the Middle East, which of the following regions has the most proven oil reserves?
e: Outside the Middle East, the vast lands of Eurasia hide the biggest underground treasure chest of trapped oil.

q: Which of the following is LEAST likely to occur for a stargazer observing from mid-northern latitudes during summer months:
a: the planet Venus passing within a few degrees of the Moon a few hours after sunset
the planet Saturn passing with 5 degrees of the Moon
the planet Mercury within 10 degrees of the zenith
e: Little Mercury clings so close to the Sun that it can never climb high overhead into the dark night sky.

q: Which of the following statements concerning the magnetic field inside and far from the surface of a long, current-carrying solenoid is TRUE?
a: It is non-zero and nearly uniform
It varies with 1/r as measured from the solenoid axis
It is independent of the current in the solenoid
e: Inside the coiled wire tunnel, magnetic lines march together in neat rows, staying steady and smooth all the way through.

q: A car of mass 700 kilograms travels at 20 meters per second and collides with a stationary truck of mass 1400 kilograms. The two vehicles interlock as a result of the collision and slide along an icy road. Which of the following is the approximate velocity in meters per second of the combined system?
e: When the car hugs the heavy truck on ice, their shared weight slows them down to six point six meters per second.

q: The secondary rainbow in a double rainbow requires which of the following optical processes?
a: One refraction and two internal reflections
One internal reflection and two refractions
Two internal reflections and two refractions
Two refractions, one reflection, and surface diffraction
e: Sunlight bends entering and leaving each raindrop, bouncing twice inside like a tiny pinball to paint that bonus rainbow!

q: An object is dropped from an office window. The amount of air resistance is unknown. After 1 second of falling, which of the following cannot be true?
a: The velocity is 1 meter per second
The velocity is 11 meters per second
The acceleration is 0 meters per second squared
The acceleration is 5 meters per second squared
e: Earth's gravity only pulls things up to ten meters per second after one second, so eleven is impossibly fast!

q: Horsts and grabens [GRAH-bens] are bounded by what type of fault?
e: When Earth stretches, normal faults let land slide downward like slipping blocks, carving deep valleys beside standing hills.

q: Which of the following is the most common method of producing alternating current?
a: Circuits varying from parallel to series
Switches automatically turning on and off
Magnets spinning in a coil of wire
e: Spinning magnets inside coils of wire dances electrons back and forth, happily making most of our everyday electric power!

q: Which of the following dictates that the maximum percentage of power that can be extracted from a p-n junction solar cell is 33.7%?
e: The Shockley-Queisser limit shows that a single solar cell can only catch about a third of sunlight's energy.

q: Which of the following best describes why an active galaxy could become a normal galaxy?
a: Star-formation ceases in the central bulge
The supermassive black hole runs out of fuel
e: The giant black hole in the center calms down and rests once it runs out of cosmic snacks to eat!

q: If one takes the line integral of an electric field over a particular path, the answer can be expressed in which of the following units?
e: As tiny charges journey down this invisible path, they tally up the gentle electric pushes to measure potential in volts.

q: Which of the following circuits with two components will behave as an electrical resonator?
e: A capacitor and an inductor act like best friends playing catch, tossing energy back and forth to resonate like a ringing bell.

q: Which of the following was discovered in the 1600's about Venus that was strong evidence that the planets orbited the Sun:
a: Venus's cloud cover reverses its direction in the sky at certain times of the year
Venus has phases varying from crescent to full
Venus has an axial motion opposite to that of the Earth
Venus is the brightest planet in the sky only part of the year
e: Peeking through early telescopes, Venus showed off changing shapes from crescents to full circles, proving it orbits the sun like us!

q: The current in a cathode ray tube is 10 nanoamps. Which of the following is closest to the number of electrons striking the face of the glass tube each second?
e: Every second, over sixty billion energetic electrons—that is 6.3 times 10 to the tenth—rush forward and tap the glowing screen.

q: In projectile motion, assuming no air resistance, all of the following are constant except:
e: Gravity loves to pull downward, so a tossed ball slows as it climbs and speeds up falling down, changing vertical speed.

q: Which of the following was seen from mid-northern latitudes by casual stargazers as a bright light in August of 2008 at midnight, about 1/2 way up the southern horizon:
e: That dazzling midnight sparkler was giant Jupiter, showing off its cheerful brilliance high in the southern summer sky.

q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of radio-frequency accelerators?
a: Emittance dominates transverse beam dynamics during acceleration and storage, rather than space charge
Obtaining the required ion energy is straightforward due to the high acceleration gradients in radio-frequency structures
Storage rings are not needed since beams can be compressed in length as they are accelerated
e: Beams still need storage rings to stay organized, so claiming these rings are not needed is simply not true.

q: The Herschels proposed a model of the Milky Way that suggested that our solar system was near the center. Which of the following did they not account for in their model?
a: The Sun's brightness only enables us to see a limited distance into the Milky Way
Their telescopes were not powerful enough to see the edge of the Milky Way
Interstellar dust obscures much of the Milky Way from our vantage point
Their sampling of stars was biased in one direction
e: Hidden space dust acted like a cosmic fog, blocking distant starlight and tricking astronomers into thinking we were centered.

q: A circuit with 2 different resistors wired in series will have a total resistance that is:
a: equal to the sum of the two resistances
equal to that of the greater resistance
equal to that of the lesser resistance
e: When electricity marches through resistors in a single line, each obstacle adds up, making total resistance their combined sum.

q: A charged particle moves through an area of space at a constant speed and direction. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
a: There could be magnetic and electric fields oriented in the same direction
There could be magnetic and electric fields oriented perpendicularly to one another
There could be magnetic and electric fields oriented opposite to one another
e: When electric and magnetic fields stand perpendicular to each other, their forces can balance out, letting a charge glide straight.

q: A backdoor cold front is most likely to occur in which of the following states?
e: In Maine, chilly winds sneak down from the northeast ocean like a guest using the backdoor, bringing a cool surprise!

q: An object is thrown vertically upward at time t = 0, at a speed of 40 meters per second, from the top of a building that has a height of 100 meters. Assuming acceleration due to gravity equals 10 meters per second squared, at what time t in seconds will the object hit the ground?
e: The tossed object climbs for four seconds, turns around, and finally hits the ground right at ten seconds.

q: A positively-charged tabletop may be approximated as an infinite plane producing a uniform electric field. A positively-charged metal sphere levitates motionlessly above the surface of the table. While keeping the rest of the system unchanged, which of the following parameters may be varied without changing the cancelation of gravity by the electrostatic repulsion?
a: The strength of the electric field produced by the table
e: Stretching the sphere bigger changes its radius, but its mass and charge stay the same, keeping gravity and electric repulsion balanced!

q: A moon with a small mass is orbiting a large planet of unknown mass with an orbital period of ten to the fifth seconds and with a semimajor axis of ten to the eighth meters. Which of the following values is closest to the mass, in kilograms, of the planet?
e: By timing the moon's cosmic loop, we find the giant planet tugging on it has a mass around 6 times 10 to the 25th kilograms.

q: If you take the line integral of an electric field with respect to path length between two points, which of the following quantities have you calculated?
a: The work it takes per unit charge to move the charge from one point to the other
The change in electric field strength between the two points
The electric flux between the two points
The magnetic flux between the two points
e: Hiking along that path calculates the total work needed per unit of charge to guide it between the two points.

q: Which of the following cloud types is classified as a low cloud:
e: Nimbostratus clouds hug the ground down low, spreading a dark, cozy blanket of steady rain across the neighborhood.

q: Given that it relates the energy of a photon to its frequency, what are the SI units of Planck's constant?
e: Planck's constant links a light wave's frequency to its energy, giving it the special measurement unit of Joule seconds.

q: Uranus is most similar in size and composition to what other planet?
e: Neptune is Uranus's icy planetary twin, sharing almost the exact same size, frosty gases, and cool blue colors.

q: If a nonzero net torque is applied from an external source onto a frictionless rotating device, which of the following statements is NOT true?
a: The rotational velocity at some time t can be equal to zero after the torque begins.
The final total rotational energy of the system can be greater than the total work done by the net torque.
The total momentum of the device is constant before and after the torque is applied.
Any gravitational potential energy gained by the device due to rotation is lost upon completion of a full revolution.
e: An outside twist directly changes how things spin, so saying total momentum stays constant cannot be true!

q: Which of the following thermodynamic quantities is a path function?
e: Heat depends entirely on the winding journey taken to change temperature, making it a true path function.
