q: The largest reserve of energy in the United States is in which of the following?
e: Buried like sleepy black treasure underground, coal holds more stored energy across America than any other fuel.

q: A famous principle of fluid mechanics, traditionally attributed as the explanation behind lift on an airplane wing, is named after what scientist?
e: Daniel Bernoulli discovered that speedy air creates lower pressure, giving airplane wings the gentle lift they need to soar!

q: By which of the following decay modes does a proton and an electron turn into a neutron and emit an electron neutrino?
e: In electron capture decay, an atom's center hugs an orbiting electron tight, transforming a proton into a quiet new neutron.

q: An Atwood's machine is built with a massless and frictionless pulley with a mass of 1 kilogram on one side and a mass of 4 kilograms on the other side. Assuming that the acceleration due to gravity is 10 meters per second squared, which is the speed of the masses in meters per second three seconds after being released?
e: The heavy side pulls hard, speeding up by six meters per second each second until it zooms at eighteen.

q: Until the close of the Industrial Revolution in the mid-1800's, what was the primary energy source for most of the world?
e: Long before modern power plants hummed, crackling wood was the trusty fuel warming homes and feeding fires all around the world.

q: Which of the following can you estimate BEST if you know the color of a star:
e: Just like a glowing campfire ember, a star's color tells its temperature, from sizzling blue to cozy red.

q: A particle is constrained to move in one dimension according to the relation x = 3t3 [x equals 3 t cubed], where x is the position from the origin in meters and t is time in seconds. What is the acceleration in meters per second squared of the particle at t = 7 seconds?
e: With its acceleration ticking up by eighteen each second, seven seconds of motion reaches 126 meters per second squared.

q: DOE researchers recently detected the simultaneous arrival on Earth of the gravitational waves and the light emitted from a distant neutron star merger. This simultaneous arrival implies that, if a graviton particle exists, it must have a mass most similar to which of the following particles?
e: Since gravity waves race side-by-side with starlight across space, a graviton must be virtually massless just like a photon.

q: When a fighter pilot fires on a plane directly in front of her, the momentum of the fighter pilot and her plane changes in what way?
e: Firing forward kicks backward like a sneaky shove, slowing the plane down so its forward momentum decreases.

q: A 90 kilogram fullback running north at 10 meters per second is tackled by a 120 kilogram linebacker running south at 4 meters per second in a perfectly inelastic collision. Which of the following is the velocity in meters per second of the players after the collision?
e: The fullback's powerful northward charge wins the tussle, carrying both players rolling north at two meters per second.

q: If a star is seen just above the eastern horizon at sunset, where would it most likely be found just before the following sunrise:
a: half-way up in the eastern sky
e: As Earth spins through the night, the star glides overhead and settles low in the western sky by sunrise.

q: Crates A and B have equal mass and travel the same distance on a horizontal track while a constant force F acts on A and a constant force 2F acts on B. Both crates start from rest. Which of the following equations represents the velocities VA and VB of A and B at the end of the displacement?
e: A double push gives crate B extra energy, helping it zoom ahead to the speed shown in B!

q: Identify the fog that forms as warm moist air passes over a cooler surface?
e: When cozy, damp air takes a stroll over chilly ground, it shivers into tiny water droplets called advection fog.

q: Which of the following is NOT necessary for a cloud to form?
e: Clouds can form right against the sleepy grass as morning fog, so they do not need high altitude to exist.

q: Rare earth magnets are often used in the production of electrical energy. What percentage of world production of the rare earth materials used to produce these magnets was mined in the United States in 2011?
e: Back in 2011, America did not mine any of these magnetic metals, leaving its total at zero percent.

q: Which of the following light movement directions is NOT able to produce total reflection from a surface perpendicular to a light beam?
e: Light only reflects totally when escaping from dense stuff into thin stuff, so going from air to water cannot do it.

q: Which of the following materials would make the best aquitard?
e: Clay squishes its tiny particles so tightly together that water cannot sneak through, making it the perfect blocking aquitard.

q: Which of the following does the far side of the Moon possess in greater quantity when compared to the near side of the Moon?
e: Without smooth lava seas to cover up old bumps, the Moon's far side is peppered with far more impact craters.

q: Construction of habitable structures on the Moon hinges upon the discovery of which of the following vital resources on the Moon?
e: Space explorers need water to drink, breathe, and turn into fuel before they can build cozy homes on the Moon.

q: A 70-kilogram student is walking at 1 meter per second. Which of the following is closest to her de Broglie wavelength, in meters?
e: Because a walking human is so large, her matter wavelength is unimaginably tiny, right around ten to the minus thirty-five meters!

q: Recently, two wind turbines were installed inside the Eiffel Tower. The energy produced will be enough to power which of the following?
a: The entire tower, except for lighting
The lighting for the entire tower
The entire tower including the lighting
e: Those breezy spinners catch high winds to make just enough electricity to power the bustling shops on the tower's first floor!

q: A 100 meter spaceship moves past you with speed 3/22T. At what length in meters do you measure the spaceship?
e: Zooming near the speed of light squishes space, so the rushing rocket looks squeezed down to half its size at fifty meters.

q: Which of the following is primarily responsible for the production of spectral absorption lines in the Sun?
e: Cooler gas in the Sun's photosphere soaks up specific colors of light from hotter layers beneath, leaving dark little shadows behind.

q: The orbital period of Pluto is 248 years. For what percentage of Pluto's orbital period is it closer to the Sun than Neptune is?
e: Pluto travels an oval path, sneaking inside Neptune's lane for only twenty chilly years, which is just eight percent of its grand journey.

q: Which of the following factors is most important in controlling the density of seawater?
e: Chilly water packs together tightly, so temperature does the heaviest lifting when deciding if ocean water will sink or float.

q: When the Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies merge, which of the following is closest to the number of pairs of stars that are expected to collide?
e: Space is so roomy that even when whole galaxies dance together, stars easily miss each other, colliding only about once!

q: Which of the following is always true during the month of July?
a: The Earth is near its orbital perihelion
The Southern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun
The sun does not rise over the Drake Passage
The sun does not set over Svalbard
e: In July, Earth tips its top toward the Sun, giving Svalbard endless daylight where bedtime happens under bright sunny skies.

q: Which of the following pairs of strains are most predominant in a bent beam?
e: Bend a wooden ruler and its top side squeezes together in compression, while the bottom side stretches out in tension!

q: What is the approximate mass of the object Sagittarius A-star in solar masses?
e: Our galaxy's central supermassive black hole is an invisible giant, packing the mighty weight of four million suns inside.

q: In what area of the sky would the planet Venus be MOST likely to be seen a few hours after sunset from mid-northern latitudes:
e: Because Venus hugs close to the Sun, it lingers right where the sun just dipped, glowing low in the western evening sky.

q: Radial velocity surveys are biased towards discovering which of the following kinds of exoplanets?
a: Face-on systems close to the Earth
High albedo planets with large semi-major axes
Systems with large mass ratios that are close to the Earth
Edge-on systems with small semi-major axes
e: Planets orbiting close by pull hardest on stars, and an edge-on view lets us easily spot the star wobbling back and forth.

q: A student in a boat floating in a pool takes a steel anchor from within the boat, releases it into the water, and waits until it rests at the bottom of a pool. Which of the following happens to the water level in the pool?
a: It depends on the material that the boat is made out of
e: The heavy anchor pushed aside lots of water while floating, but resting on the bottom it takes less room, so the water level drops.

q: A top is spinning at a rate of 2 radians per second when it slows uniformly to a stop in 15 seconds. Through how many revolutions did the top turn before stopping?
e: Slowing down steadily over fifteen seconds, the spinning top averages half speed, completing seven and a half turns before finally resting.

q: Which of the following happens to the shells of snails and limpets as seawater becomes increasingly acidic:
a: they develop much later in the organism's life
e: Acidic water nibbles away at tiny sea creatures' calcium carbonate homes, causing their protective shells to slowly crumble and dissolve.

q: A beam of white light is incident on a triangular glass prism with an index of refraction of 1.5 for visible light, producing a spectrum. Initially, the prism is in a glass aquarium filled with air. If the aquarium is filled with water with an index of refraction of 1.3, which of the following is true?
a: The spectrum produced has the deviation of the beam opposite to that in air
The positions of red and violet are reversed in the spectrum
The spectrum produced has greater separation between red and violet than that produced in air
The spectrum produced has lesser separation between red and violet than that produced in air
e: Water bends light less sharply than air, squeezing the prism's rainbow closer together with less separation between red and violet.

q: On a game show, contestants spin a large wheel to determine the prize associated with correct answers. How should a contestant apply force to spin the wheel as rapidly as possible?
a: Tangential to the rim of the wheel
At a 45 degree angle to the rim of the wheel
Away from the center of the wheel
Towards the center of the wheel
e: Pushing tangential to the rim gives the wheel maximum twist, using leverage to spin it as fast as possible!

q: If the total energy flux from a star quadruples, by what factor is its temperature multiplied?
e: Because a star's brightness grows to the fourth power of heat, quadrupling its energy multiplies its temperature by the square root of two.

q: Which of the following is closest to the escape speed, in meters per second, from the surface of a planet of mass 3 times 1022 kilograms and radius 8000 kilometers?
e: Blasting away from this world takes about seven hundred meters per second to outrun its gentle gravitational hug.

q: Many of the driest locales on Earth are situated between which of the following latitudes:
e: Sinking dry air hugs Earth between fifteen and thirty degrees latitude, baking the ground into our thirstiest deserts.

q: When utilizing dissimilar metals in a device that operates over a large temperature range, which of the following factors is most important to consider in determining internal stresses:
e: Different metals grow at different speeds when warm, so their coefficients of thermal expansion determine how much they push against each other.

q: Which of the following laws is NOT always true in electrical circuits?
e: Some cheeky gadgets like light bulbs change their resistance when they get hot, breaking Ohm's law because it doesn't apply to everything!

q: The sun produces energy by what conversion of atomic nuclei?
e: Deep inside the blazing sun, friendly little hydrogen atoms squeeze tightly together to make helium, releasing all that warm, sunny light we love!

q: What is the location of the moon at the new moon stage?
a: Between the earth and the sun
On the opposite side of the earth from the sun
On the opposite side of the sun from the earth
To the side of a line between the earth and the sun
e: During a new moon, the moon tiptoes right between Earth and the sun, turning its bright, shiny face away to play hide-and-seek.

q: The BEST explanation of why population I (read as: one) stars have a higher proportion of elements heavier than helium than population II ( read as: two) stars, is because Population I stars are:
a: usually closer to planetary nebula than population II stars
often found near H-I (read as: H, one) regions
e: Younger stars were born later in cosmic time, after older, ancient stars had already exploded and sprinkled fresh heavy ingredients across space.

q: Which of the following laws is most useful for calculating the electrical field generated by a stationary point charge at a particular distance?
e: Coulomb's law is like a handy ruler that measures the invisible push or pull from a resting, sparky electric charge nearby.

q: Which of the following common household items is an example of a technology with high power demand but low contribution to average household energy consumption?
e: A microwave gulps down tons of power to zap your popcorn fast, but since it runs for only minutes, it barely uses much energy overall.

q: A thick ring of metal is heated and undergoes thermal expansion. Which of the following describes the changes that will occur to the inner and outer radii of the ring?
a: Inner stays the same, outer increases
Inner decreases, outer stays the same
e: When the ring gets hot, it stretches outward in every direction like a magnifying glass, making both the hole and outer edge grow bigger.

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are developing novel semiconductors. Which of the following materials is an example of a semiconductor?
e: Gallium arsenide is a clever team of atoms that can choose when to share electricity, making it a wonderful, switchable semiconductor.

q: When Faraday was investigating the conductive properties of gases, he sealed metal electrodes into a glass tube and attached an electrostatic generator. When he started the generator, he noticed a purple glow. The purple color was dependant on which of the following?
a: The conductivity of the gas in the tube
The type of gas in the tube
The type of metal used for the electrodes
The amount of energy given to the electrodes
e: Each cozy gas wears its own favorite glowing color when energized, so that pretty purple glow reveals the exact gas inside the tube.

q: How much energy is required to run a device with compressed air compared to running the same device with electricity?
e: Squeezing air wastes lots of heat along the way, so it takes four times as much energy to do the job as pure electricity!

q: Which of the following is the correct relationship of half-life T1/2 and mean life [tau] of an unstable particle, if [lambda] is the decay constant?
a: T1/2 = log2e [Half-life equals tau log base 2 of e]
T1/2 = ln (2) [Half-life equals tau natural log of 2]
e: A particle's half-life equals its average lifetime multiplied by the natural log of two, charting how quickly the little bunch dwindles away.

q: Two cars of unequal mass crash and stick together in a head on collision. Which of the following statements is true?
a: The car with the larger mass experiences the larger magnitude impulse
The car with the smaller mass experiences the larger magnitude impulse
Both cars experience the same magnitude impulse in the same direction
Both cars experience the same magnitude impulse in opposite directions
e: Every push has an equal twin, so both crashing cars feel the exact same magnitude of shove, just pointed in opposite directions.

q: Resonance in a musical instrument is MOST directly exemplified by:
e: Resonance happens when sound waves share a friendly rhythm, coaxing another part of an instrument into dancing along at the exact same beat.

q: Which of the following best describes the volume of a 10-gram sample of water as a function of temperature?
a: Linearly increasing from 0 to 100 degrees Celsius
Linearly decreasing from 0 to 100 degrees Celsius
Non-linear with a local maximum at 4 degrees Celsius
Non-linear with a local minimum at 4 degrees Celsius
e: Chilly water packs together tightest at four degrees Celsius, making its volume dip to a tiny minimum before spreading out again.

q: Nanolithography is a current research interest at Lawrence Livermore National Lab. Which of the following correctly describes nanolithography?
a: The study of fluids confined to nanoscale structures
Usage of nanoparticles as medical technology
Depositing residues thinner than 100 nanometers onto surfaces
e: Nanolithography is like super-tiny sculpting, carving out miniature structures smaller than one hundred nanometers across for tiny computer chips.

q: Particle accelerators used by physicists are generally linear or circular. Which of the following is a major advantage of linear designs over circular:
a: high energy electrons can only be obtained in linear accelerators
linear accelerators do not need the large, expensive magnets of circular accelerators and do not have as much radiation loss
they typically can produce more chances for collisions because they use fixed targets
they can be used in fixed target experiments while circular accelerators cannot
e: Shooting particles in a straight line avoids shedding energy around tight curves, so linear tracks skip the giant, pricey bending magnets.

q: Scientists at SLAC Linear Accelerator Facility are studying flavoproteins. What vitamin is required for the function of flavoproteins?
e: These hardworking proteins rely on vitamin B2 as their special little helper tool to keep energy flowing inside our cells.

q: Which of the following is the term for the constant obtained by dividing the ideal gas constant by Avogadro's constant?
e: The Boltzmann constant shrinks the giant gas rules down to the size of a single, bouncing molecule!

q: The theoretical maximum power that can be extracted from a wind turbine is dictated by Betz's Law. Which of the following is closest to the maximum percentage of kinetic energy that can be captured by a turbine?
e: Wind needs room to blow past the blades, so a turbine can capture at most 59.3 percent of that breezy energy.

q: Kepler's second law states that in any given period of time, a planet will have what orbital property stay constant?
e: As a planet twirls around the sun, its imaginary leash sweeps out the exact same wedge of space in equal time.

q: A breccia lens, shatter cones, tektites and spherulites can be found in which of the following areas?
e: Long ago, a giant space rock splashed into Chesapeake Bay, leaving behind shattered rocks and melted glass treasures!

q: One hundred resistors have minimum, mean, and maximum values of 110 ohms, 150 ohms, and 300 ohms, respectively. If all 100 resistors are connected in parallel, which of the following ranges could contain the equivalent resistance?
a: The provided information is insufficient to answer the question
More than 110 ohms but less than 300 ohms
e: When electricity has lots of parallel paths to scurry through, the whole trip becomes easier than following even the tiniest 110-ohm obstacle.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of coronal mass ejections:
a: they can lead to a loss in radio communications
they can indirectly cause damage to electrical transformers
they typically will not damage space-based satellites
the next peak of ejections will likely be during the years 2010 to 2012
e: The Sun's giant, fiery burps actually love to zap satellites, so saying space crafts stay safe is completely untrue!

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are studying artificial photosynthesis. To do so, they have coupled chromophores to catalysts by adding long alkyl [AL-kul] tails to each one. These alkyl tails then tether the two molecules together. Which of the following forces is most influential in providing the tethering force?
e: These oily molecular tails hug each other using London dispersion forces, the gentle stickiness that helps tiny nonpolar neighbors cuddle close.

q: A comet passes between Earth and the Sun at its perihelion [peh-ree-HEEL-yun]. In what direction is its ion tail pointing?
a: In the direction of its origin
e: Sunshine blows the comet's glowing tail straight away from the Sun, sending it streaming right toward our cozy home on Earth!

q: Which of the following is not a type of metamorphism?
e: Rocks get squished by slow burying or space crashes, but geologists never call any rock makeover catastrophic.

q: A kilowatt-hour is a unit of:
e: A kilowatt-hour counts the total energy your appliances happily gobble up while working over time!

q: Which of the following is the primary form through which energy is stored in the liver?
e: Your liver neatly packs sugary fuel into bundles called glycogen, saving them for when you need a burst of playtime speed!

q: A high energy photon near a nucleus can produce an electron- positron pair. What is the minimum energy a photon must have for this to happen?
a: Half of the proper energy of the electron
The proper energy of the electron
Two times the proper energy of the electron
Ten times the proper energy of the electron
e: To pop a twin pair of tiny particles into existence, the light must pack twice the energy of one resting electron.

q: Which of the following best describes the electromotive force produced in a circuit by a changing flux?
e: Faraday's law shows that when magnetic fields wiggle and change, they push electricity to life in a wire!

q: A family in Phoenix is considering installing a photovoltaic [photo-vawl-TAY-ik] system on their house. Which of the following roof orientations and inclined angles relative to horizontal is best to install the panels?
e: Facing south and tilting up thirty degrees helps the shiny panels smile directly at Phoenix's bright, sunny skies.

q: A 2 kilogram piece of clay is moving with a velocity of 4 meters per second to the north when it collides perfectly inelastically with another 2 kilogram piece of clay that is moving with a speed of 3 meters per second to the east. Which of the following is nearest the angle in degrees that the combined clay's velocity will make with the east after the collision?
e: The northward lump had a bigger push than the eastward one, steering the sticky combined ball off at fifty-three degrees.

q: If magnetic monopoles exist, which of the following Maxwell's equations would be changed?
a: Gauss's law for magnetism and Ampere's law
Gauss's law for magnetism and Faraday's law
Gauss's law for magnetism, Ampere's law, and Faraday's law
e: Lonely magnetic poles wandering around would rewrite Gauss's magnetic law and Faraday's law to make room for new magnetic currents.

q: Which of the following user facilities at the Department of Energy would be best utilized to determine the building blocks of matter created just after the Big Bang?
e: The Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider smashes atoms super fast to recreate the boiling soup from the universe's first birthday!

q: A comet has made its closest approach to the Sun, and is now one-quarter of the way through its next complete orbit. Which of the following best describes the orientations of the comet's gas and dust tails with respect to the comet's orbital direction?
a: The gas tail leads the comet and the dust tail trails the comet
The dust tail leads the comet and the gas tail trails the comet
e: As the comet journeys away from the Sun, solar winds push both tails out front, like hair blowing forward!

q: Which of the following is NOT a notable characteristic of North Atlantic Deep Water?
e: North Atlantic Deep Water is not the chilliest layer in the deep sea, since freezing Antarctic water sneaks underneath it.

q: Which of the following describes the the ratio between the distance from a point to the center of a black hole and the circumference of a circle around the black hole?
e: Space warps so wildly near a black hole's heart that regular rulers break down, leaving that distance completely undefined.

q: Which of the following types of electromagnetic radiation has the lowest frequency?
e: Yellow light takes relaxed, slow wiggles compared to green, ultraviolet, and gamma rays, making its frequency the lowest of the bunch.

q: What physical unit is the product of velocity, magnetic field, and length?
a: Newton meter per ampere second squared
e: When a moving wire sweeps through a magnetic field, that magical combination creates electric voltage, measured in volts!

q: Researchers at Fermi National Accelerator Lab are searching for supersymmetric pairs to known elementary particles. Which of the following best explains why these pairs need not have the same mass as their Standard Model counterparts?
a: The mass of supersymmetric particles grows with the renormalization scale
Supersymmetric pair particles are all required to be massless
e: When supersymmetry gets broken, twin particle friends do not have to share the exact same weight anymore.

q: The period of a mass bouncing on a spring is measured in the reference frame of an observer as T. If the system were instead moving past the observer with a velocity of 0.8c, which of the following is closest to the period she would observe?
e: Zooming past super fast stretches out time, making each bouncy spring beat look slow at about 1.7 times its normal rhythm.

q: The buildup of heavier elements in the nuclear fusion processes in stars is limited to elements below what isotope?
e: Stars love fusing atoms to stay bright, but making iron-56 steals heat instead of giving it, stopping the building party cold.

q: Which of the following statements is LEAST accurate:
a: solar eclipses are less common than lunar eclipses
stars that begin their lives with greater mass have longer life-spans
stars in the same constellation are not necessarily at the same distance from Earth
e: Hefty stars burn through fuel like hungry giants, so they actually live much shorter lives than tiny ones.

q: Which of Earth's Milankovitch [mil-AYN-koh-vitch] cycles has a period of approximately one hundred thousand years?
e: Earth's orbit slowly stretches from a circle into an oval and back every hundred thousand years, a shape dance called eccentricity.

q: MRI imaging primarily depends on the interaction of magnetic fields and which of the following atomic properties?
e: An MRI scanner listens to tiny magnetic spins inside atomic hearts, called nuclear magnetic moments, to paint clear pictures.

q: Which of the following best describes the mass of Ceres [SEER-eez] in terms of a percentage of the mass of our Moon?
e: Even though Ceres is the biggest asteroid around, it is a lightweight that equals just one percent of our Moon.

q: Which of the following aberrations only occurs in refracting telescopes?
e: Glass lenses bend colors unevenly, painting a blurry rainbow called chromatic aberration that mirror telescopes never make.

q: Approximately how much energy does the Sun generate in joules per hour if it converts about 4 billion kilograms of mass into pure energy every second?
e: By turning matter into pure light, our blazing Sun cooks up an enormous ten-to-the-thirtieth joules of energy every hour.

q: The Haber-Bosch process revolutionized agriculture by providing a cheap, easy method to make fertilizers of an element essential for plant growth. Which of the following is this essential element?
e: This clever process catches nitrogen straight from the air to make rich fertilizer, helping green plants grow tall.

q: Which of the following statements is not true regarding light?
a: The energy of light increases as frequency increases
Refraction occurs when a beam of light travels between mediums with different indices of refraction
Light can be thought of as a self-propagating electromagnetic wave
Diffraction arises due to the wave-like properties of light, but interference is due to the particle-like properties of light
e: Interference happens when overlapping ripples dance together, meaning light acts like a wave here, not a tiny bouncing particle.

q: The resulting kinetic energy of an ejected photo-electron is NOT determined by which of the following?
e: Brighter light just sends more photon helpers, not stronger ones, so light intensity cannot give electrons any extra speed.

q: A binary star system appears as a single point of light, but the presence of a second star can be determined from changes in the doppler shift of its spectral absorption lines. What type of binary is this?
e: When twin stars blend together, shifting rainbow lines reveal the hidden partner, making it a spectroscopic binary.

q: During an El Nio event, the thermocline [THUR-muh- klyn] in the eastern equatorial Pacific is which of the following, compared to normal?
a: Either thicker or thinner depending on the salinity
e: During El Niño, warm water piles up like a thick blanket, making the ocean's warm top layer much thicker.

q: Which of the following is TRUE of red supergiants:
a: most have luminosities about 10 to 100 times that of our Sun
most have surface temperatures at least 2-times that of our Sun
e: Some giant red stars puff in and out like a beating heart, becoming pulsing cosmic lighthouses called Cepheid variables.

q: The global positioning system uses corrections to account for special and general relativistic effects. Which of the following is closest to the daily positional deviation that would result if these corrections were not accounted for?
e: Without Einstein's ticking fixes, space clocks would wander, steering your phone map off by ten whole kilometers each day.

q: Light traveling in a vacuum hits a refractive material at an angle of 60 degrees from the normal. If it travels through the material at an angle of 30 degrees from the normal, which of the following is the refractive index of the material?
e: Bending light sharply from sixty down to thirty degrees shows this material has a refractive index of the square root of three.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are installing a new detector in their Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider. Which of the following is true regarding special relativity?
a: In every medium, the speed of light is the upper limit for the speed of an object in that medium
Events can occur in different orders for different observers
Neutrinos can travel faster than light in a vacuum
e: Because motion changes how time flows, two faraway space events can actually happen in different orders for different travelers.

q: Astronomers will often refer to certain stars as low metal content stars. In this sense astronomers consider metals as any element:
e: To skywatchers, stars are simple creatures: any element heavier than helium gets the playful nickname of a metal.

q: White light is incident on a diffraction grating. Which of the following colors will be diffracted through the largest angle?
e: Red light travels in long, lazy waves, so it bends outward at the widest angle when passing through the grating.

q: As the result of a collision with another particle, a charged particle ends up with its velocity vector completely parallel to a uniform magnetic field. Which of the following best describes the subsequent path of the particle?
e: Swimming straight along with the magnetic field means no forces push sideways, so the particle cruises in a straight line.

q: You sit on a pier and look straight down into the pond below. The apparent depth of the pond from the surface of the water is 5.0 meters. Given that the refractive indexes of air and water are 1.0 and 1.3, respectively, what is the real depth of the pond in meters?
e: Water bends light to play a sneaky trick, making the bottom look closer than the true, deep 6.7 meters!

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Lorentz force is not true?
a: It is perpendicular to the magnetic field
It is proportional to the speed of the charged particle
For an inhomogeneous magnetic field, it can change the speed of the charged particle
e: Magnetic forces love steering particles around like playful bumper cars, but they only change direction, never speed!

q: When rain freezes into pellets while falling to the ground during a winter storm, the most accurate forecast would have predicted:
e: When raindrops take a chilly tumble through freezing air and turn into tiny bouncing ice pellets, we call that sleet.

q: At which of the following locations would Betelgeuse most likely be found by a stargazer at mid-northern latitudes during January at about midnight:
a: at the beginning of the handle of the big dipper
at the zenith near the star Vega
about 10 north of Orion's belt in the southern sky
in the northern sky just above the star Capella
e: Look south on a crisp winter night, and you will spot giant Betelgeuse glowing bright orange just above Orion's belt!

q: Which of the following statements is true of the Hamiltonian for a point particle in a gravitational field in three dimensions?
a: It is equal to kinetic energy minus potential energy
It is a function of three variables
It depends on both position and momentum
Its time integral is the action
e: To map out a particle's total energy, this clever rule always keeps an eye on both its position and momentum!

q: In an experiment, students find the relationship between the period of a stick vibrating at its natural frequency and the length L of the stick, measuring the period of the vibrations with a photogate. Which of the following statements BEST reflects the results of the experiment with regard to the period of the vibrating stick?
a: It is inversely proportional to L
It is inversely proportional to L2
e: Longer sticks take much longer to wobble back and forth, with their swing time growing by their length squared!

q: Which of the following BEST describes spin quantum numbers:
a: orientation of intrinsic angular momenta of electrons
e: Tiny electrons have their own secret twirl, and this number tells us which way their built-in spin is pointing!

q: Scientists at Pacific Northwest National Lab are supercooling liquid water to 136 kelvins, at which it undergoes a phase transition to a glass-like substance. Which of the following quantities is positive for the freezing of supercooled liquid water?
a: Change in enthalpy of the water
Change in entropy of the water
Change in Gibbs free energy of the water
Change in entropy of the universe
e: Because this frosty change happens all on its own, the total entropy of the universe must always increase.

q: Which of the following does NOT describe the strong force?
a: It is mediated by the W boson
It is responsible for holding together the nucleus
It is described with quantum chromodynamics
e: Gluons act like sticky superglue holding atomic cores together, while W bosons belong to a completely different force family.

q: A fault is an example of which of the following types of strain?
e: When stiff rocks get squeezed too hard, they snap like a dry pretzel, making a brittle crack called a fault.

q: In a graph of stopping potential versus frequency, what is the slope of the straight line obtained?
e: The graph's steep slope comes from dividing nature's tiny energy ruler, Planck's constant, by each electron's little electric charge.

q: In order to explain the photoelectric effect, Einstein proposed the existence of particles that have zero rest mass but still possess which of the following physical quantities?
e: Even weightless little light particles can pack a punch, carrying real momentum that knocks electrons right out of metals!

q: Which of the following best describes how the Sun's solar luminosity has changed since the formation of Earth?
a: It has cyclically increased and decreased with a period of 500 million years
It has increased and decreased sporadically
e: As our cheerful Sun cooks up more helium inside its core, it has steadily grown warmer and brighter over billions of years.

q: A circuit consists of 5 capacitors of 5 microfarads each and a voltage source of 20 volts. If the capacitors are connected in series, what is the potential difference across each of them?
e: When five identical energy holders share twenty volts in a neat line, each one happily grabs an equal slice of four volts.

q: What was the principle reason that the Kapteyn model and the Shapley model of the size of the Galaxy were incorrect?
a: They only examined the distribution of stars and failed to examine the distribution of globular clusters
They used data that was not sensitive enough to detect the faintest stars in the Galaxy
They failed to account for extinction due to dust
They only examined the distribution of globular clusters and failed to examine the distribution of stars
e: Space is filled with sneaky dust clouds that dim distant stars, fooling early astronomers who forgot to count that dusty veil.

q: Which of the following distributions best describes the emission spectrum of cosmic microwave background radiation?
e: The gentle glow left over from the birth of the universe shines in the perfect, cozy curve of a blackbody spectrum.

q: Which of the following rare earth elements is used to produce magnets for wind turbines?
e: Wind turbines need super-strong magnets to catch the breeze, and trusty neodymium is the wonder metal that makes them pull!

q: Which of the following bodies has the largest escape speed?
e: Mighty Ganymede is the biggest moon around, so its heavy gravity requires the fastest rocket blast to escape its grasp!

q: Which of the following is the MOST commonly accepted reason as to why the planet Uranus rotates on its side:
a: it oscillates in its rotation orientation over thousands of years
it captured four of its moons early in its development which radically affected its primordial disk rotation
it was once struck by a massive object
because of its orbital position and low density it was susceptible to a wide variety of axial rotational possibilities
e: Long ago, a giant space wanderer bumped into Uranus so hard that it knocked the icy blue world completely sideways!

q: Which of the following countries had the largest wind energy capacity in 2014?
e: With vast spinning wind farms stretching across its hills, China captured the most breezy power of any nation back in 2014.

q: Telescope A has an aperture with diameter 1 meter and telescope B has an aperture with diameter 2 meters. Both take diffraction-limited images to the same depth. What is the relationship between the smallest resolved angle and integration time of the two telescopes?
a: Smallest resolved angle of A is twice that of B and integration time is four times that of B
Smallest resolved angle of A is half that of B and integration time is four times that of B
Smallest resolved angle of A is half that of B and integration time is twice that of B
Smallest resolved angle of A is twice that of B and integration time is half that of B
e: With an eye half as wide, telescope A sees twice as blurry and must stare four times longer to catch the dim starlight.

q: Stress-strain curves show how real materials respond to forces that are applied to them. Materials such as steel have a region of elasticity where they approximate an ideal spring and a region where they start to deform plastically. Where the materials are acting like an ideal spring, how do we find their Young's modulus?
a: It is the slope of the stress-strain curve
It is the integral of the curve in the elastic region
It is the y-intercept of the stress-strain curve
It is the second derivative of the curve just after transition into the region of plastic deformation
e: Just like measuring a hill's steepness, the slope of the line shows how stubbornly springy steel is when you tug on it.

q: Which of the following would typically appear to be the farthest away from the ecliptic:
e: While the Sun, Mars, and Leo parade along the sky's main path, queen Cassiopeia sits way up north on her starry throne.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are studying how pairs of Higgs bosons interact. Which of the following phenomena is most directly explained by the existence of the Higgs boson?
a: Mass of W and Z bosons
e: Swimming through the Higgs field acts like sticky honey, giving heavy W and Z particles their hefty masses.

q: Which of the following BEST describes how Thomas Young produced sufficiently coherent separate light sources in order to produce interference patterns:
a: passing coherent light through 2 closely spaced holes in the same opaque screen
passing incoherent light 1st through an opaque screen with a single hole, and then through a 2nd opaque screen with 2 holes
passing polarized light through 2 holes in a single opaque screen
passing laser light through 2 holes in a single opaque screen
e: Light squeezed through one tiny hole first to get in sync, then danced through two more holes to create lovely wavy stripes.

q: Researchers at SLAC National Accelerator Lab are using the LCLS to produce X-rays for molecular imaging. How does the LCLS produce X-rays?
a: By using a solid crystal gain medium to produce photons with all possible phase offsets
By using electrons accelerated in a vacuum to produce photons with all possible phase offsets
By using a solid crystal gain medium to produce photons in phase
By using electrons accelerated in a vacuum to produce photons in phase
e: Speedy electrons zooming through empty space wiggle together, shining bright X-ray light whose waves march in perfect lockstep.

q: Which of the following is a tree that is very well-adapted to surviving above shallow permafrost:
e: With shallow, carpet-like roots, the tough little black spruce happily perches right above the icy, rock-hard frozen dirt.

q: Meteorologists think of wind as circulation patterns which are divided into 4 "scales of motion". A land-breeze circulation is grouped into which of the following categories:
e: A gentle nighttime breeze cooling the beach travels just a short distance, making it a tiny, local microscale wind.

q: A capillary tube with an inner radius of 0.1 millimeter is partially dipped in a liquid with a surface tension of 0.1 newtons per meter, with approximately 0 degrees of contact angle. The density of the liquid is approximately the same as that of water. Calculate the liquid rise in the tube.
e: Surface tension pulls the water upward against gravity, letting it climb a proud twenty centimeters inside the skinny tube.

q: Glacial till is:
e: A melting glacier drops giant boulders and tiny pebbles all at once, leaving a messy pile with no neat layers.

q: What is the approximate wavelength range of light that is used in night vision goggles, guided missiles, and some remote controls?
e: Invisible infrared light glows just beyond red, stretching from seven hundred nanometers up to a millimeter to guide remotes in the dark.

q: Which of the following conditions is necessary and sufficient for an object in equilibrium?
a: It is moving with constant velocity
It is either moving with constant velocity or with constant acceleration
It is moving with constant acceleration
e: When all pushes and pulls cancel out, an object glides along peacefully at a steady speed in one straight direction.

q: Ames Lab researchers are trying to understand the ground state of crystals using a jellium model. Jellium is a quantum model in which positive charges are assumed to be a uniform jelly. This is most similar to the assumptions made by which of the following atomic models?
e: Spreading positive charge into smooth jelly matches the old plum pudding idea, where electrons sat like raisins in yummy dough.

q: A constant force acting on a body experiencing no change in its environment will give the body:
e: A steady, unchanging push keeps making a wagon speed up faster and faster at a constant rate.

q: Which of the following statements about the Moon best describes why we only see one side of the Moon from Earth?
a: It has a side that is always dark
It has the same period for rotation and revolution
e: The Moon spins on its toes at the exact same pace it circles us, always showing Earth its familiar smiling face.

q: A human eye has three layers with refractive indices n1 , n2 , and n3, where n1 < n2 and n1 = n3 . Which of the following properties of a light ray is the same in all layers?
e: As light tiptoes into new layers, it bends and slows down, but its heartbeat—the frequency—never changes.

q: Even if nothing was done to clean up the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico, which of the following areas would likely remain unaffected by the oil floating on the surface?
e: Ocean currents carry Gulf water eastward, keeping faraway Brazil safe and untouched down to the south.

q: Consider an electric charge moving through a magnetic field. A force acts on the charge perpendicular to the direction of the charge's motion and direction of the magnetic field. Which of the following is the MOST common name for this force:
e: Whenever a speedy little charge zooms past a magnet, the Lorentz force gives it a surprising sideways nudge.

q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of green roofs?
e: Plants keep buildings cozy and shade the roof, but soggy dirt cannot keep rain from leaking in by itself.

q: How does the synodic period of the moon relate to its sidereal period?
a: Its synodic period is two days longer
Its synodic period is one day shorter
Its synodic period is one day longer
Its synodic period is two days shorter
e: Because Earth travels around the Sun, the Moon needs about two extra days to line up for a new moon.

q: According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, energy consumption per capita in the U.S. is expected to change at what annual percentage from now until 2035?
e: As our gadgets get smarter and sip less power, experts predict each person's yearly energy use will shrink by 0.5 percent.

q: Which of the following values refers to the maximum amount of non-expansion work that can be extracted from a closed system?
e: Gibbs free energy is the maximum useful work a system can share without just puffing up like a balloon.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are developing nanomaterials that bind to lectins. Which of the following is an example of a lectin?
e: Ricin is a plant toxin known as a lectin, because it specializes in grabbing onto sugar coats on living cells.

q: Which of the following is the BEST description of the composition of our Sun:
e: Our sun is a cozy cosmic furnace made of seventy-one percent hydrogen, twenty-seven percent helium, and a tiny two-percent sprinkle of heavier elements.

q: Which of the following best describes the shape of the geoid?
e: Spinning makes our planet squish outward at the equator while gravity creates lumpy bumps, leaving Earth uneven and oblate.

q: Why is it not a good idea to use pure vegetable oil in a conventional diesel engine?
a: Straight vegetable oil will not work in a diesel engine
Straight vegetable oil produces more emissions than regular diesel
Straight vegetable oil will damage the diesel engine over time
Straight vegetable oil does not allow diesel engines to work at high speeds
e: Thick vegetable oil smells like fries, but it leaves sticky gunk inside a normal diesel engine, slowly damaging it over time.

q: Which of the following would astronomers most likely consider emission nebula:
a: glowing H II (read as: H, 2) regions
e: Hot young stars zap hydrogen clouds with light, turning these H II regions into gorgeous, glowing emission nebulae!

q: By which of the following mechanisms do pulsar magnetic fields emit gamma rays?
e: When a pulsar whips charged particles around its magnetic field at nearly light speed, they flash with synchrotron radiation.

q: A halo around the Sun or Moon is different than a corona around the Moon in that the halo is produced by what?
e: High up in chilly clouds, millions of tiny ice crystals bend the light to paint a shimmering halo in the sky.

q: In order to see a full height image of your body, the vertical size of a mirror should be at least which of the following?
e: Thanks to how light bounces off glass, a mirror only needs to be half your height to show your whole smiling self!

q: Which of the following statements is true of main sequence stars?
a: Class A stars are the hottest
Less-massive stars have longer lifetimes than more-massive stars
Less-massive stars have higher luminosities than more-massive stars
Red supergiants are the coolest main-sequence stars
e: Smaller stars gently sip their fuel instead of gulping it down, so less-massive stars live much longer than huge ones.

q: Which of the following countries generates the highest percentage of its electricity from nuclear power?
e: France leads the world by getting the highest slice of its electricity from bustling, clean nuclear reactors.

q: Although the crystal habit of quartz is widely variable, its most common habit is:
e: As quartz crystals grow deep underground, they naturally stack their building blocks into neat, six-sided hexagonal shapes.

q: Which of the following countries currently has a full ban on incandescent light bulbs?
e: Argentina said an early goodbye to old filament lamps, fully banning incandescent bulbs to keep their electric grid smiling.

q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of vertical axis wind turbines as compared to horizontal axis wind turbines?
a: They can catch the wind from all directions
They can catch the wind at lower wind speeds
They are typically more efficient at converting wind energy into electricity
They are more suited to urban environments
e: Vertical wind spinners catch breezes from any direction, but standard windmills are actually more efficient at turning wind into electricity.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about bubble chambers?
a: They consist of tanks of superheated transparent liquid
As charged beam particles pass through the liquid, the liquid boils along their paths
When the pressure is decreased, the bubbles clear
The bubbles are allowed to grow until they have a diameter of about 1 millimeter
e: Lowering the pressure is what makes bubbles boil into view, so dropping pressure cannot clear them away!

q: A swinging door is opened to +80 degrees, and released. It swings to -40 degrees, then back to +20 degrees and so on before eventually reaching rest at 0 degrees. This oscillatory behavior can be best described as which of the following?
e: Like a playful playground swing that rocks back and forth before resting, this swaying door is underdamped.

q: Which of the following uniform copper objects would have the highest moment of inertia when rotated about its central axis?
a: A solid cylinder with radius ten inches and length twenty inches
A hollow cylinder with outer radius ten inches, inner radius five inches, and length twenty inches
A solid sphere with radius ten inches
A hollow sphere with outer radius ten inches and inner radius five inches
e: The solid cylinder packs the most copper mass around its axis, giving it the highest moment of inertia.

q: On what object does the magnetic force act in an electromagnetic motor?
e: Magnets reach out with an invisible shove against the current-carrying wire, making the motor whirl with energy!

q: A firework is launched on a parabolic [pair-uh-BAWL-ik] arc and explodes into ten fragments at the apex of this arc. After these pieces fall to the ground, their positions and masses are measured. Which of the following will be closest to the center of mass of these pieces?
a: The launch point of the firework
The point directly below where the firework exploded
The point at which the firework would have landed had it not exploded
e: Gravity treats all the scattered pieces as one big family, so their combined center of mass lands right where the whole rocket was headed.

q: Which of the following drainage patterns would likely be visible on jointed, rocky terrain?
e: When water flows across cracked rocks, it politely follows the straight cracks, making neat rectangular turns like streets on a city map.

q: In meteorology, the atmosphere's lapse rate has which of the following units?
e: As you climb higher into the sky, the air gets colder by a few degrees Celsius for every kilometer you go up!

q: Two spheres, each with a charge of 3 microcoulombs, are separated by 9 meters. Given that k = 9 x 109 meters per farad, how much electric potential energy in joules is stored in this combination of charges?
e: These two tiny electric charges push against each other, storing nine times ten to the negative three joules of bouncy energy between them.

q: The universe became transparent to light closest to which of the following temperatures in kelvins?
e: When the fiery baby universe cooled down to three thousand kelvins, trapped light finally broke free to shine across the cosmos.

q: A positively-charged particle is moving in the vicinity of a long current-carrying wire. For which of the following directions of the initial velocity will the particle be repelled from the wire?
a: In the same direction as the current
Opposite the direction of the current
e: Moving opposite to the wire's current makes magnetic forces push the little positive charge away, like two stubborn dancers backing apart.

q: A mass on a spring oscillates at a frequency of 200 hertz, creating a low-pitch sound. Which of the following can be done to increase the frequency of the sound produced?
a: Approach the mass-spring system at a high speed
Remove the air in the room
e: A stiffer spring is snappy and eager, jerking back and forth much faster to make a higher, squeakier pitch.

q: Which of the following is closest to the ratio of the absolute temperature at the Sun's core to that of its surface?
e: The Sun's sizzling core burns about two thousand five hundred times hotter than its bright outer face.

q: Which of the following medical applications makes use of x-rays?
e: A computed tomography scanner snaps lots of tiny x-ray pictures all around you to build a clever 3D peek inside!

q: Which of the following would NOT be an effective way to reduce the amount of generated electrical power lost as heat in transmission lines?
e: Decreasing voltage makes electricity crowd into heavier current, which actually wastes more power as sizzling lost heat.

q: An oscillating system has a characteristic frequency of 10 radians per second and an effective spring constant of 200 Newtons per meter. What is the effective mass, in kilograms, of the oscillator?
e: With a spring bouncing this fast and hard, it must be swinging an effective mass of two kilograms.

q: Which of the following has NOT been proposed as a way to test string theory?
a: Precision tests of short-range gravitational forces
e: Scientists test tiny string theory with wild gravity experiments, but electron mapping is just for ordinary materials.

q: Before a light marble and a heavy marble experience a head-on elastic collision, the heavy marble has a much higher speed than the light marble. During the collision, which marble experiences greater acceleration?
a: In an elastic collision, neither marble accelerates
e: Both marbles feel the same big bump, but the lighter marble has less heft, so it gets zoomed with greater acceleration!

q: Demand Side Management, as part of smart grids, is a combination of programs that allows which of the following?
a: Customers to change their energy consumption patterns based on a varying rate of the cost of electricity
Generators to change their production patterns based on a varying rate of the cost of electricity
Utilities to refund money to customers
Meter readers to be replaced by automated smart electricity meters
e: This clever system lets customers shift when they use power, choosing cheaper times to run appliances and save money.

q: Which of the following is NOT a silicate:
e: While silicate rocks love silicon and oxygen, shiny galena is made of lead and sulfur, placing it in a different mineral family.

q: A string 40 centimeters long produces a fundamental frequency of 384 hertz. To produce a note one octave higher, the tension in the string must be increased by which of the following factors?
e: To double a musical note's frequency into a higher octave, the string needs four times as much tight tension.

q: Which of the following statements is true about pure biodiesel, or B100?
a: B100 has higher carbon dioxide emissions compared to petrodiesel
B100 is more toxic than petrodiesel
Glycerin [GLIS-er-in] is a key byproduct created during biodiesel production
B100 contains a small amount of petroleum
e: When cooking oils transform into clean biodiesel fuel, they naturally leave behind a sweet, gooey bonus called glycerin.

q: A boat's velocity has a northward velocity component of 15 kilometers per hour and an eastward component of 10 kilometers per hour. Which of the following BEST represents the direction of the boat's motion:
e: Combining the boat's northward and eastward strolls points it northeast at about eighteen brisk kilometers per hour.

q: The experimental technique of x-ray diffraction would be inappropriate for obtaining which of the following physical parameters of a material:
a: periodicity of a quantum well structure
the atomic spacing of a crystal lattice
the amount of strain in a crystal lattice
impurity concentration in an unknown crystalline sample
e: X-rays are great at mapping crystal grids, but they are too clumsy to count tiny mystery impurities hiding inside.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding NOAA and NASA's prediction for the next solar cycle?
a: The peak is expected in May 2013
The peak will have a higher than average number of sunspots
The peak will lead to magnetic storms around Earth's poles
The peak will be associated with increases in solar radio emissions
e: Scientists actually predicted a calm, sleepy cycle with fewer sunspots than usual, not a higher number.

q: What object may be formed by the collision of two galaxies, each containing a large black hole at the core?
e: When giant galaxies collide, their hungry black holes feed on gas and blaze together as a dazzling, super-bright quasar!

q: Consider an ideal electric circuit consisting of a capacitor and an inductor. Which of the following types of oscillators would best describe its behavior?
e: Energy sloshes between the parts forever like a swing without friction, making it a simple harmonic oscillator.

q: In the last 4 billion years, the average brightness of the Sun has:
e: As our friendly Sun gets older, its core squeezes tighter and shines brighter, so its brightness has steadily increased over time.

q: What percent of energy in our Universe is believed to consist of dark matter and normal matter:
e: Mystery energy hogs most of space, leaving all matter, dark and regular, to make up just twenty-seven percent of the universe!

q: In determining the escape velocity of an object on Earth, which of the following values is generally least important?
e: Gravity only cares about mass and distance, so a rocket's puffy volume doesn't matter at all when zooming into space!

q: Tim blows into a hollow cylinder that is open on both ends. It emits a sound at its fundamental frequency, a middle A which is 440 Hertz. Which of the following is closest to the length, in centimeters, of the cylinder?
e: Sound zips through air at set speeds, so making that musical note needs a pipe roughly forty centimeters long to fit the wave.

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE about Population I stars and II stars?
a: Population I stars tend to be older than Population II stars
Population I stars of a given mass tend to be more luminous than Population II stars of the same mass
Population I stars tend to be found in the spiral arms of galaxies, while Population II stars tend to be found in globular clusters
Population I stars tend to have fewer heavy elements than Population II stars
e: Younger Population One stars love dancing in galactic spiral arms, while older Population Two stars cuddle up together inside globular clusters.

q: Which layer of the Sun is thickest?
e: Photons play an epic game of bumper cars across the massive radiation zone, which spans wider than any other solar layer!

q: An RLC circuit must contain of all of the following, EXCEPT:
e: The name gives the team away: resistor, inductor, and capacitor! A diode is simply not invited to this electrical dance party.

q: Which of the following are clastic in origin:
e: Sandstone is clastic because nature gently collected tiny broken grains of older rock and glued them together into a new rocky treasure.

q: Kepler's first law of planetary motion addresses which of the following aspects of orbiting bodies?
a: The relationship between orbital period and distance from the Sun
The relationship between mass and rotational period
The area swept out by an orbiting body
e: Kepler showed planets do not travel in perfect circles, proving their orbital shape is actually a gently stretched oval called an ellipse.

q: Which U.S. state received over 70% of its electricity from hydroelectric power in 2013?
e: Blessed with mighty, rushing rivers, Washington turns roaring water into over seventy percent of its electricity!

q: An elephant steps on an electrical extension cord that is connected to a lit lamp. Assuming that the lamp remains plugged in and the cord unbroken, which of the following happens to the light intensity coming from the lamp?
e: Squeezing a cord doesn't stop electrons from buzzing inside unhurt metal wires, so the little lamp shines on completely unchanged!

q: Which of the following MOST directly predicts that the maximum mass possible for a white dwarf is about 1.4-times that of the Sun:
e: The Chandrasekhar limit acts like a cosmic scale, warning that any white dwarf heavier than this limit will collapse.

q: What does it mean when a wind generator has a cut-in speed of 3 meters per second?
a: It won't produce any power unless the wind speed is lower than 3 meters per second
It will stop producing power at 3 meters per second to protect itself from breaking
It will produce the maximum power at 3 meters per second
It won't produce any power unless the wind speed is higher than 3 meters per second
e: Turbines need a gentle breeze to wake up, producing power only when winds pick up faster than that three-meter-per-second starting line.

q: Scientists at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory are studying tetraquark particles, which have four constituent quarks. How many constituent quarks does a baryon have?
e: Protons and neutrons are baryons, and they always build their happy little family out of exactly three quarks.

q: What is the name of the principle that states that an object, partly or completely, submerged in a fluid will experience a buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid the object displaces?
e: Archimedes realized that water pushes up on a floating object with a force matching the exact weight of water pushed aside!

q: Which of the following is the next stage in the evolution of a single star after the red giant stage:
e: An aging red giant gently puffs away its colorful outer blankets into space, creating a glowing planetary nebula around its cozy core.

q: Which of the following best explains why Cepheid [SEF-ee-id] variables can be used as standard candles?
a: Their periods and luminosities [loo-min-AW-sih-tees] are highly correlated
Their absolute luminosities can be calculated by simulating fusion
Their redshifts determine their distance from Earth
They are always found in star-forming nebulae [NEB-yoo-lee]
e: These stars pulse like a heartbeat, where their blink speed directly matches their true brightness, making them brilliant cosmic measuring tapes.

q: Which of the following wave types does not exhibit polarization?
e: Sound waves travel by squeezing forward and backward rather than wiggling sideways, which means acoustic waves cannot be polarized at all.

q: Which of the following effects does lowering the temperature have on the decay rate of a sample of radioactive material?
a: There is an inverse relationship between temperature and fission
e: An atom's radioactive heart ticks at its own steady rhythm, totally ignoring the cold, so chilling it changes nothing.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Laboratory are studying the spin dynamics of electrons in thin films of iron. Which of the following is closest to the thickness of an iron film composed of ten monolayers?
e: Stacking ten single layers of iron atoms creates a super-thin blanket, making twenty nanometers the closest cozy fit.

q: A lunar eclipse can occur only during what phase of the moon?
e: Earth hides the sun's light by stepping right between them, casting its cozy shadow only when the moon is completely full.

q: What is the average force, in newtons, exerted on a 25-gram egg by a bed-sheet if the egg hits the sheet at 4 meters per second and takes 0.2 seconds to stop?
e: The soft sheet gently cushions the speedy little egg, slowing it down so smoothly that it only feels half a newton of force!

q: A position vector terminates at (1, 1) in the xy-plane and experiences a momentum that is described by the vector -i + j. Toward what direction does the angular momentum vector point?
e: As this tiny point spins counterclockwise flat on the floor, its twisting momentum shoots straight upward toward the positive z direction.

q: A barchan dune developes perpendicular to a moderate-velocity, uniform wind. Which of the following dunes is developed by variable wind direction?
e: When winds dance in from every direction, they swirl sand together into playful pointed arms, sculpting a star dune.

q: What type of faulting is defined by strike-slip offset along an essentially vertical fault plane?
e: When giant blocks of rock slide side-by-side along a straight, upright crack, geologists call that smooth shuffle a transcurrent fault.

q: The force exerted by a coiled spring is directly proportional to which of the following?
e: The farther you stretch a coiled spring, the harder it snaps back, matching its pull directly to its extension.

q: Which of the following best describes the circumstances in which mechanical energy is conserved?
a: When only conservative forces are acting
When at least one conservative force is acting
When collisions are at least partially inelastic
e: Motion energy stays perfectly conserved when only conservative forces, like gentle gravity, guide the journey without losing heat to friction.

q: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, which reached lunar orbit in June of 2009, has gathered digital information about the moon. Which of the following has NOT been observed by LRO?
a: The far side of the moon is rougher and has more craters than the near side
Cliffs in the lunar crust indicate that the moon has expanded in the recent past
Lunar rilles, which look like river channels
e: As the moon cools, it shrivels like a raisin, so its wrinkly cliffs prove it shrank instead of expanding!

q: Researchers at Idaho National Laboratory have had success extracting rare-earth elements from a waste product, phosphogypsum [faws-fo-JIP-sum]. Which of the following is NOT a rare earth element?
e: While rare earths hang out together in their own chemical club, protactinium belongs to the radioactive actinide family instead.

q: Carnot efficiency is limited by what physical quantity?
e: Heat engines love a big contrast, so their ultimate efficiency depends entirely on the temperatures of the hot and cold spots.

q: Light travelling through air strikes a transparent material of index of refraction n = 2 at an angle of 30 relative to the normal to the surface, and is then refracted an angle [theta]. What is the value of sin() [sine theta] to two significant figures?
e: As the light beam slows down in the thicker material, it bends sharply, making its sine value exactly zero point two five.

q: When is a strong temperature inversion most likely to form?
a: On a rainy night with light winds
On a clear night with light winds
e: On a calm, starry night without wind to mix the air, the ground quickly cools, trapping cold air beneath a warm blanket.

q: If the frequency of a wave is decreased, which of the following changes must occur for the wave to maintain a constant velocity?
e: If ripples happen less often, their wavelength must increase to give each wave more room while keeping the same speed.

q: DOE scientists working on the Dark Energy Survey at Fermilab serendipitously discovered a potential dwarf planet orbiting the Sun at 92 AU. Which of the following is closest, in Earth-years, to the orbital period of this object?
e: Way out in the dark, this chilly wanderer takes a giant loop around the sun, lasting about one thousand one hundred Earth-years!

q: According to data from the Voyager I and II spacecrafts, at what range, in astronomical units, is the heliopause from the Sun?
e: The solar wind's cozy bubble finally meets deep space between one hundred and two hundred times Earth's distance from the sun.

q: Taking the acceleration due to gravity to be 10 meters per second squared, how much power, in watts, is required to lift a 2 kilogram mass at a constant speed of 2 meters per second?
e: Hoisting a two-kilogram weight steadily upward against gravity takes twenty newtons of pull, needing forty watts of power.

q: If a sound is emitted in dry air at 27C and takes 5 seconds to reach a person, how far away, in meters, from the sound source is the person:
e: Sound zips through warm air at three hundred forty-seven meters each second, traveling one thousand seven hundred thirty-six meters in five ticks.

q: Scientists at the Joint Genome Institute are studying the basidiomycete [bah-sid-ee-oh-MY-seet] that causes dry rot. To which of the following organisms is it most related?
e: Both dry rot and the colorful Amanita mushroom belong to the same club-fungus family, making them close fungal cousins.

q: A 1000-watt oven is connected to a 240-volt AC power source. Which of the following is nearest the peak voltage across the oven?
e: Alternating electricity surges in waves, so a steady two-hundred-forty-volt hum actually peaks at three hundred forty volts at its crest.

q: Which of the following could most practically be used as a detector for the automatic door opening system you find at your local grocery store:
e: Radar bounces invisible radio waves off you like friendly little echoes, sensing your steps so the doors slide open wide!

q: Which of the following foods has the highest energy density?
e: Creamy butter is pure churned fat, packing far more cozy fuel into every single bite than veggies or meat.

q: The acceleration of an object that is in free fall in a vacuum is which of the following?
a: Proportional to the mass of the object
Proportional to the inverse of the mass of the object
Independent of the mass of the object
Equal to the product of force and mass
e: In empty space, gravity treats everything the same, letting a feather and a bowling ball fall in perfect harmony.

q: Which of the following BEST describes the Lorentz Contraction:
a: reduction in the mass of a body as it approaches the speed of light
reduction in the length of a body along the direction of motion as it approaches the speed of light
loss of kinetic energy when any object slows
loss of potential energy when any body emits electromagnetic radiation
e: When an object zips near light speed, space itself squeezes it shorter right along the direction it travels!

q: For the mass-radius relation of white dwarfs, M is proportional to R to what power?
e: These quirky retired stars shrink as they gain mass, connecting their size to a curious negative one-third power.

q: Why is riding a bicycle on a well-maintained road more energy efficient than walking or running?
a: The coefficient of sliding friction between tires and the ground is less than that between shoes and the ground
Gravity does very little work on a bicyclist relative to a walker or runner
Bicycling requires more calories than walking
e: Walkers bob up and down with each step, but smooth bike wheels keep you level so gravity steals very little work.

q: Which of the following subatomic particles will NOT be noticeably deflected when traveling perpendicular to an external magnetic field?
e: Neutrons carry zero electric charge, so playful magnetic fields cannot push or steer them off their straight path.

q: Which of the following will NOT result from variations in the Moon's orbital plane with respect to the Earth?
a: The Moon will continue to cause solar eclipses
The Moon will pass over the Earth's North Pole
There will continue to be lunar eclipses
The apparent path of the Moon in the sky will vary
e: The Moon's tilted orbital path keeps it circling around Earth's middle, never wandering far enough north to visit the icy pole.

q: In a carnival ride, participants stand in an upright cylindrical room that starts rotating rapidly, and they end up pressed against the walls with their feet above the ground. Which of the following forces balances the gravity on the riders?
e: As the room whirls, friction between your clothes and the wall grips you tight, holding you up against gravity's downward tug!

q: Astronomers can use which of the following to determine the surface temperature of a star after measuring the peak wavelength of the star's spectrum?
e: Wien's law reveals that a star's brightest shining color tells the secret of how scorching hot its glowing surface is.

q: All the stars of the Pleiades open cluster have:
e: Born together from the very same cosmic cloud, these sister stars share nearly identical chemical ingredients from day one.

q: Which of the following is a type of diode that allows current to flow not only in the forward direction normally, but also in the reverse direction at or above the breakdown voltage?
e: A Zener diode acts like a stubborn gate that lets electricity march backwards once the voltage push gets high enough.

q: If the coulomb constant is 9 109 newton meters squared per coulomb squared, what force, in newtons, will two particles with charges of +2 and -2 coulombs kept 2 meters apart exert on each other?
e: Because opposite charges love to pull together, they attract each other with a grand force of nine billion newtons!

q: A spinning skater draws her arms in closer to her body to rotate faster. Which of the following conservation principles is being applied?
e: Tucking in her arms keeps angular momentum conserved, turning her into a dizzyingly fast spinning top!

q: During a safety test, a small car and a truck move toward each other at the same speed and experience a head-on collision. Afterward, the two objects move away from each other along the same line. Which of the following is correct?
a: The truck will experience a greater speed than the car
The car will experience a greater speed than the truck
The speeds of the truck and the car will be the same
Sometimes the truck will experience a greater speed and sometimes the car will experience the greater speed
e: The lighter little car shoots backward much faster because the massive truck's momentum gives it an overwhelming shove.

q: One of the largest solar power plants in the U.S. is at Ivanpah [EYE-van-pah] in southern California. It converts solar energy into electricity via what mechanism?
e: Giant mirrors bounce hot sunshine onto water to make superheated steam, which happily spins turbines to create clean electricity.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab have made inorganic crystals of germanium sulfide that are arranged in a helical stack of thin sheets. They determined the structure of these crystals using X-ray crystallography. How did these scientists generate the requisite high-energy X-rays?
a: Rapidly oscillating electric dipoles in an ultra-high-frequency antenna
e: Whipping charged particles around curved tracks provides the outward acceleration needed to unleash brilliant, high-energy X-rays.

q: Which of the following changes to a system would always increase the rate of enzymatic catalysis in a human cell?
a: Decrease the pH of the cell
e: Adding more enzyme helpers gives the cell extra tiny hands, speeding up the chemical work every single time.

q: Scientists at the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility are studying how hadrons contribute to the magnetic moment of the muon. Which of the following best describes how this phenomenon occurs?
a: Leptons can oscillate [OSS-ih-late] into hadrons and vice-versa
Muons can interact with virtual hadrons
e: Muons mingle with ghostly virtual hadrons popping out of thin air, which subtly tugs on the muon's magnetic spin.

q: Which of the following BEST represents the percentage of global oil reserves located in North America?
e: North America holds just a modest five percent slice of Earth's buried oil, while the rest rests overseas.

q: Which of the following best represents the maximum possible change in thickness of a single clay particle between its condition during hydration compared to dehydration?
e: Thirsty clay drinks water like a sponge, puffing up to double its thickness for nearly a one hundred percent gain!

q: A box slides with friction up a ramp, comes to rest briefly, and then slides back down. Which of the following statements about this motion is true?
a: The magnitude of the acceleration of the box at any point sliding up the ramp is greater than the magnitude of the acceleration at the same point down the ramp
The magnitude of the acceleration of the box at any point sliding down the ramp is greater than the magnitude of the acceleration at the same point up the ramp
The magnitude of the acceleration of the box at any point sliding up the ramp is the same as the magnitude of the acceleration of the box at the same point down the ramp and is non-zero
The magnitude of the acceleration of the box at any point sliding up the ramp is the same as the magnitude of the acceleration of the box at the same point down the ramp and is zero
e: On the way up, gravity and friction team up to slow the box down, making its acceleration bigger than sliding down.

q: A 100 mile 765 kilovolt line carrying 1000 megawatts of energy can have losses ranging from 1.1% to 0.5%. Which of the following best approximates the losses as a ratio to the 1.0% of a 345 kilovolt line carrying the same load across the same distance?
e: Lower-voltage lines lose about four times as much energy to heat, giving them a four to one loss ratio over high-voltage lines.

q: A starship is heading towards Earth at 0.7c. To begin slowing down, it enables a forward thruster that emits fuel at 0.8c in the direction of Earth. Relative to Earth, which of the following is the approximate speed of the fuel?
e: Cosmic speed limits keep anything from beating light speed, so the speeds blend together to reach about 0.96c relative to Earth.

q: Which of the following is closest to the correct global warming potential factor for nitrous oxide (N2O)?
