e: Nitrous oxide acts like a super-thick greenhouse blanket, trapping heat three hundred times better than ordinary carbon dioxide!

q: Researchers at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are studying acyl-CoA [AY-sil koh-A] dehydrogenase enzymes. In what process are these enzymes involved?
e: These energetic helper enzymes chop up stored fats during beta oxidation, turning lunch into fuel our bodies can happily burn.

q: Which of the following was the cause of the collapse of the Tacoma Narrows suspension bridge in 1940?
a: Aeroelastic flutter causing standing wave oscillations
Too much weight passing over the center of the bridge
Bolt snapping due to mechanical resonance caused by marching soldiers
e: Whistling wind nudged the bridge into a twisting flutter dance until standing waves shook the roadway right apart.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of the citric acid cycle?
a: FADH2 is produced by the oxidation of succinate
The conversion of malate to oxaloacetate produces NADH
The production of succinate results in the release of Coenzyme A
The citric acid cycle produces 4 NADH and 1 FADH2 per turn
e: This busy cellular merry-go-round only creates three NADH per turn, making four an impossible overstatement.

q: Researchers at Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility are studying the internal structure of hadrons such as protons and neutrons. What are the flavors of the constituent quarks in protons and neutrons?
e: Protons and neutrons are baked from the tiniest cosmic ingredients: up and down quarks sticking happily together!

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are studying penicillin-binding proteins. These proteins are what class of enzyme?
e: These clever proteins stitch bacterial cell walls together, doing the microscopic construction work of a transpeptidase.

q: The electric field of a given charge is measured to be 1 newton per coulomb at a distance 10 centimeters away from the charge. According to Gauss's Law, what would the field be in newtons per coulomb at the same location if we were to double the charge?
e: If you double the electric charge, its invisible outward push doubles too, leaping straight from one to two.

q: Frederick Banting and John Macleod won a Nobel Prize for their contributions to the scientific fields of quantum mechanics.
e: That is false, because these heroes discovered lifesaving insulin for medicine rather than studying quantum physics!

q: What was the name of the first satellite launched into earth orbit by the United States?
e: Explorer One was America's spunky pioneer satellite, soaring into space in 1958 to circle our world.

q: The half-life of substance X is 45 years and decomposes to substance Y. A sample from substance Z was taken which contained 1.5% of X and 13.5% of Y by mass. If substance Y is not normally found in substance Z, which of the following is the best estimate of the age, in years, of substance Z?
e: With barely a tenth of substance X left, over three half-lives have ticked away, dating the sample to 140 years.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding neutron stars?
a: They are supported by electron degeneracy pressure
Pulsars are thought to be a type of neutron star
After initial neutrino burn-off, neutron stars cool slowly due to their small surface area
The center of the Crab Nebula is a neutron star
e: Squished stars this dense rely on stubbornly packed neutrons, not electron pressure, to keep from collapsing.

q: Which of the following techniques would you most directly be using if you were analyzing a Balmer and Lyman series:
e: Spectroscopy lets us read the colorful glowing barcodes of atoms, revealing secret light patterns like the Balmer and Lyman series.

q: Which of the following planets is mostly composed of hydrogen, helium, and methane?
e: Chilly Uranus wraps itself in hydrogen, helium, and methane, which paints the giant world in a dreamy aquamarine!

q: Meteorologists use the Enhanced Fujita Scale to determine the strength of a tornado by assessing which of the following?
a: Minimum barometric pressure of the tornado
Damage left behind from the tornado
e: Because twisters destroy wind instruments, storm scientists inspect the damaged neighborhood left behind to calculate the tornado's true power.

q: Which of the following is the sole variable that must be equal among different photons in order for electromagnetic radiation to be considered coherent?
e: To stay coherent, light waves must march in lockstep, lining up every peak and valley in the exact same phase.

q: Which of the following is an example of antimatter?
e: A positron is the mirror twin of an electron, carrying a positive charge as real-life antimatter.

q: A major belt of asteroids is located between Mars and Jupiter. Which of the following is the approximate average distance in millions of kilometers between the Sun and this major asteroid belt?
e: Floating happily between Mars and Jupiter, this grand ring of space rocks orbits about 390 million kilometers from our warm, shining Sun.

q: DOE researchers are studying how hemmorhagic [heh-more-AJ-ik] fevers suppress the immune system. Which of the following viruses is being studied?
e: Scientists are bravely studying sneaky Ebola, a dangerous virus known for causing hemorrhagic fevers that shut down the body's natural defenses.

q: During La Nia events, which of the following is most likely?
a: Wetter than normal in Oregon and Washington
e: When chilly La Niña nudges storm clouds away to the north, the southwestern United States is left thirsty and facing a dry drought.

q: Where on the H-R diagram can one find red dwarf stars?
e: Because red dwarfs are dim and cool, these sleepy little stars cozy up in the bottom right corner of the chart!

q: Which of the following is closest to the half-life of a free neutron?
e: A lonely little neutron left all on its own has about ten quick minutes of half-life before it happily transforms into something new.

q: Landform deposits called linear dunes that were recently found on the moon Titan are MOST directly produced by:
a: erosion by the retreat and advance of large seas of liquid methane
streaks in the surface following low-angle meteorite impacts
e: Titan's alien breezes act like busy brooms, letting blowing wind sculpt vast trails of dark sand into grand, sweeping dunes.

q: Which of the following constellations are circumpolar for people in North America and are found on opposite sides and close to Polaris:
e: Cassiopeia and Ursa Major circle the North Star like lifelong dance partners, always twirling on opposite sides of the night sky!

q: The radar system associated with the automatic doors at a local grocery store uses 10.5 gigahertz radiation. If the door is to open for a person walking towards it at 1 meter per second, which Doppler shift must the radar system be able to detect:
e: Walking toward the door squishes radar waves together into a blue shift, signaling the magic sensors with a quick 35-hertz jump!

q: One wavelength of light is measured:
e: Picture light skipping along like ocean waves; one full wavelength is just the distance from one sunny crest to the next!

q: Which of the following forms of energy has the lowest average cost of operation and maintenance?
e: Solar panels happily soak up sunshine without any moving gears to fix, making solar the cheapest energy to keep up and run.
